AC receivables collected; 5 of last 8 quarters negative

segments.name: Air conditioners
segments.commentary: Management said AC is about two-thirds of revenue and was the weakest margin category under the new regulations; Q1 AC sales were up about 50% in the company's outlet KPI and AC shipments rose in April-May ahead of the summer.

segments.name: Refrigerators
segments.commentary: Launched the 654-litre Luxuriem side-by-side with triple evaporator and Intelli Crisper, priced against INR 70,000-80,000 competitor side-by-sides; company previously had no presence above 500-600 litres, and Pune plant began shipping in July.

segments.name: Washing machines
segments.commentary: Washer sales grew over 80% in the quarter per management; Dynamix dispenser now on 50% of the range, and 11 kg top-load launched in Juniper Green. Top-load segment described as highly competitive.

segments.name: Kitchen appliances (Elica)
segments.commentary: Elica revenue and profit growth were cited as strong; management said there is no remaining minority stake to buy and the holding sits with Pralhad Bhutada.

guidance_outlook: No full-year FY27 revenue or margin guidance; management said predicting it is 'close to zero' accuracy.
July-September 2026 expected to be the weakest quarter, with margins lower than April-June but not as low as the year-ago period.
Management aims for above 10-20% AC growth over the next two years, pacing growth to avoid channel stock build-up.
Management expects war-related and e-waste headwinds to ease if resolved, with an equitable e-waste solution sought from government.
Company aims for 10% share of top-load washers in time; 12-15 months of new product launches planned.
capex_capacity: Pune plant started production in July 2026, shipping Luxuriem refrigerators, with INR 245 crore invested in the facility (as stated).
Faridabad plant delivered record manufacturing output in Q1 FY27 despite war and heat-wave supply constraints.
Current utilisation of about 70-75% on an annual basis; management said no immediate capex need in the next 6-12 months.
Capex is an ongoing process; management said cash is not a constraint and capital goes to projects with strong ROI.
demand_pricing: Price increases taken in April and May 2026 only partly offset war-led and regulatory cost increases, creating a net under-recovery.
Management said the company led hikes only in April and May and avoids unilateral moves that could cost share, citing 2022 experience.
Competition in top-load washers has intensified; the company lost share in that segment while gaining elsewhere.
Distribution is near 10% share in some regions versus about 3% in smaller ones; not present at Croma, Vijay Sales or Reliance Digital (per analyst question).

qa_highlights.question: Parent refinancing and plans for the remaining stake; the cash on the balance sheet.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the parent, Whirlpool Corporation, holds 39.75% and it does not discuss parent matters. The board is examining capital use across manufacturing expansion, automation and inorganic opportunities, with no decision announced.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year revenue growth and margin expectations, including whether OPM could be flat year on year.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide; it said the outcome depends on war, forex and regulatory developments, and that margin protection is a focus.

qa_highlights.question: Whether industry can pass on further price hikes, and the elasticity of a 10% increase.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price coordination is illegal and that it decides pricing independently; a 5% price move equals about INR 1,000 per unit, and not all cost inflation will be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the about 400 bps margin compression between war, regulation and P4G actions.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the war impact (oil and forex) was larger than the regulatory impact; P4G savings were largely offset as input-supply constraints limited negotiation leverage, and fixed costs were held flat as a percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Sale of services to the parent (INR 250 crore in FY25) and ESOP vesting terms.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the transitional services agreement runs to 2029 on a cost-plus, arm's-length basis; ESOPs were issued at market value with performance-linked vesting and a 3-year cliff.

risks_watch: Oil-linked input costs (MDI, polyol, EPS, plastics) and rupee at about 95-96 per dollar; about 30% of raw materials imported and several Middle East-sourced items are single-sourced.
E-waste accounting provision: management is seeking an equitable industry solution and said the impact is significant.
July-September weakness in AC, which is about two-thirds of revenue.
Price competition in top-load washers and whether the company can hold share while raising prices.
Parent Whirlpool Corporation at 39.75% stake and undisclosed capital-allocation plans.
500238|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and new launches, but cautious on margins; management repeatedly declined to quantify full-year outcomes and attributed the margin squeeze to war, forex and regulation. Evasive on the parent's capital plans and the remaining stake.
key_quotes: Revenue is up 26% and profits are up 22%.

500241|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 14.151 bn, but FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 13.7% amid SPP UK service-mix shift and Rs 389 mn labour-code charge.
500241|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 10% YoY to Rs 14.151 bn with EBITDA of Rs 2.093 bn (14.8% margin) and PAT of Rs 1.121 bn. Full-year revenue was flat-to-marginally up at Rs 45.380 bn (+1%), with EBITDA of Rs 6.213 bn (13.7%) and PAT of Rs 3.772 bn. Domestic revenue fell 3% for FY26 while Q4 grew 3%; international grew 7% for the year and 25% in Q4. Management attributed the year's shortfall to JJM funding delays, a foundry ERP transition, and a Rs 389 mn labour-code charge classified as exceptional. Order books grew strongly: domestic Rs 24.680 bn (+30%) and international Rs 14.808 bn (+21%).

segments.name: Domestic (standalone)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 28.281 bn (-3%); Q4 Rs 9.091 bn (+3%). Order growth led by building and construction, marine and defence, oil and gas, power and water; JJM is about 4-5% of revenue but hit water-sector shipments.

segments.name: International - SPP UK
segments.commentary: EBITDA fell from Rs 95 crore to Rs 58.1 crore (Rs 37 crore drop), driven by a shift from high-margin services to products as UK industrial customers idled on power prices above Rs 30/unit.

segments.name: International - SPP US
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs 540 crore versus Rs 300 crore in FY22; about 35% from fire pumps and 25% from data centres. EBITDA down about Rs 3 crore per management.

segments.name: International - other entities
segments.commentary: Dutch, South African and other entities grew; South Africa margin % lower but absolute EBITDA higher. Management said Q4 was a slower first quarter for some entities due to prior-year spillover timing.

guidance_outlook: Management will strive for double-digit revenue growth in FY27 in both domestic and international businesses, but cited war and gas-supply risks.
SPP UK margins expected to realign toward the target level by roughly the calendar Q3 2026, with full-year margins targeted back to desired levels.
Labour-code impact of Rs 389 mn in FY26 (Rs 258 mn in Q4) treated as exceptional; estimates may be revised as rules are notified.
Final dividend of Rs 7 per Rs 2 share (350%) recommended, subject to AGM approval.
Management expects JJM-related disruption to ease over the next few quarters; AMP8 inquiries are expected to convert from next quarter.
capex_capacity: Foundry ERP (SAP) transition at Kirloskarvadi caused temporary disruption; management says the system has largely stabilised.
Company has five foundries; the largest was the focus this year, and in-house electricity capacity was added to hedge gas shortages.
Eight US data-centre packages were on the shop floor at the US plant as of the call.
Nuclear: full-scale primary heat transport pump prototype is to be delivered to NPCIL on schedule; budgetary quotes given for all pump types; Bharat SMR (200 MW) quotes sought.
demand_pricing: Standalone order inflow growth came from building and construction, marine and defence, oil and gas, power (coal and nuclear), and water and irrigation.
Company says it earns premiums against multinationals on lifecycle cost and efficiency, and enforces advance payment or LC for small and medium pumps; retail sold on cash.
Management says it can pass on raw-material price rises; Hormuz-related disruption raised costs.

SPP US competes with Amstel, Taco, Grundfos and Xylem in data-centre cooling; management says it is not cheaper but offers plug-and-play containerised packages with 18-24 month data-centre lead times.
US distributors rose to about 46 from 12 four years ago; roughly 10 states have no coverage.

qa_highlights.question: Where are the strong standalone orders coming from, and what else is disrupting execution beyond JJM?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth from building and construction, marine and defence, oil and gas, power and water. Execution was hit by the foundry ERP transition and JJM fund-release delays at the state level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did international margins fall despite strong order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Kirloskar said the SPP UK mix shifted away from services because UK industrial customers idled on power prices above Rs 30/unit. Margins are expected to realign by about calendar Q3 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Would FY26 have grown at double digits without the disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Kirloskar said Q4 sales exceeded last year's Q4 and growth should resume, but war and gas uncertainty remain. He declined to give a precise FY27 figure beyond striving for double digits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nuclear opportunity and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Company has indigenously designed primary-side pumps, with budgetary quotes given. Orders are expected step by step as NPCIL and DAE constraints clear; SMR prototype orders are expected once the design is finalised.

qa_highlights.question: How diversified is the US business, and what is the 3-year plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Fire is about 35% of US business and data centres about 25%; the rest is municipal and booster packages. Focus is HVAC, municipal markets and AMP8-style programmes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profit fall across international entities in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Kirloskar said Q4 is seasonally slower for some entities due to prior-year spillover, and that year-on-year all entities except SPP UK improved.

risks_watch: SPP UK service mix and margin recovery timing (calendar Q3 2026 target).
JJM second-phase tendering and state-level fund release; no meaningful tendering pickup yet.
Geopolitical shocks (Middle East war, gas and fertiliser supply), with management citing cost pressure.
Foundry ERP stabilisation and dispatch conversion of the Rs 24.7 bn domestic order book.
Data-centre demand, where management acknowledged a mild US delay; ECA financing is a dependency.
Further labour-code revisions could change the Rs 389 mn exceptional charge.
500241|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on order book, nuclear and data-centre opportunities, but cautious and evasive on FY27 growth, citing wars and gas shortages. Management was candid that FY26 margins and volumes were hit by SPP UK mix and operational transitions. Several questions on order-book breakdown and aftersales share were declined.
key_quotes: the double-digit growth that we expected was actually impacted by the first quarter, second quarter and third quarter.
So we do expect that we will get back to that level.
We're not cheaper, but we changed the model before to a modular model, and we provide a container system to them.

500241|2026-06.headline: Kirloskar Brothers Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% YoY to Rs.11,049 million, but EBITDA grew only 2% at an 11.8% margin.
500241|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to Rs.11,049 million and consolidated EBITDA rose 2% to Rs.1,306 million, a margin of 11.8%. Standalone domestic revenue grew 9% to Rs.6,738 million, EBITDA 16% to Rs.920 million, and PAT 15% to Rs.540 million. International revenue grew 19%, but international EBITDA margin fell to 5.1% on lower high-margin services revenue at SPP UK and weak Rodelta execution. Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27 on both standalone and consolidated bases, while acknowledging that a large order slipped and foundry modernisation delayed some dispatches.

financial_highlights.change: driven by SPP USA and Kirloskar Brothers Thailand
moderated due to lower services contribution

segments.name: Standalone domestic (KBL)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs.6,738 million (+9%), EBITDA Rs.920 million (+16%), PAT Rs.540 million (+15%). Domestic pending order book Rs.25,577 million excluding small pump order book.

segments.name: International (overseas)
segments.commentary: Revenue +19% YoY, led by SPP USA and KBT Thailand. EBITDA Rs.207 million at 5.1% margin. Overseas pending order book Rs.15,045 million.

segments.name: SPP USA
segments.commentary: Growing 20-plus% in the quarter, driven by data centers, fire and HVAC projects; a multi-year framework with a large US data center operator is near signing (under NDA).

segments.name: SPP UK / Rodelta (Netherlands)
segments.commentary: SPP UK margin pressure from lower services revenue as chemical/petrochemical service contracts idled; management expects services recovery from Q2 FY27 for SPP UK and Q3 for KBL. Rodelta losses widened on delayed execution; improvement expected over the next two quarters.

segments.name: KPML (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Margin fell from 12.5% to 7.3% after merger of loss-making TKSL (steel castings) into KPML; management expects TKSL to turn profitable.

guidance_outlook: Double-digit revenue growth in FY27 over FY26 for standalone business, reiterated.
Management will strive for double-digit consolidated revenue growth in FY27.
Services business expected to recover from Q2 FY27 at SPP UK and from Q3 at KBL, lifting blended overseas margins.
Rodelta execution expected to improve over the next two quarters; all entities expected to be profitable with better-than-prior-year numbers.
About two-thirds of the domestic order board (~Rs.2,500 crore) expected to execute in FY27.
Capex expected to be roughly equal to depreciation, focused on modernisation, debottlenecking and quality.
Management asks investors to assess performance half-yearly or annually rather than quarterly.
capex_capacity: Foundry modernisation programme completed; management says it will enable higher revenues and faster execution, though it delayed some dispatches in Q1.
Capex guided at roughly equal to depreciation for FY27, mainly modernisation, debottlenecking and quality.
Nuclear primary circuit pump development is close to order placement; metallurgical trials in European and Indian foundries expected to conclude by mid-to-late August.
Pump-based IoT devices now in second version; deployed base is in the hundreds in India.
demand_pricing: Standalone order intake grew about 5.4% YoY per management's corrected figure; consolidated order intake +4% to Rs.13,954 million. A large order was delayed into later quarters.
Price increases of about 10% taken since January, which management says is sufficient to cover raw material cost increases; gross margin improved on product mix and price.
Oil and gas: petrol pump order booking of about Rs.217 crore cumulative to Q1-end; Rs.74 crore dispatched in the quarter.
Power order book grew about 30%; nuclear primary circuit pump orders of about Rs.70 crore and secondary circuit orders of about Rs.40 crore received in Q1.
Industry order book was Rs.1,497 million (the Rs.556 million figure quoted was marine & defence), per the corrected print.
Data centres: hyperscale package USD7.5-10 million excluding intake water system; about 4,000 operating US data centres plus 2,000 with planning permission.

qa_highlights.question: Why are inventories and advances rising and is dispatch being withheld, hindering double-digit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory built up during the foundry upgrade, which is now complete; some orders were half-finished, so full shipments slipped. Improvement was seen in the current month and is expected in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: When will the services expansion lift SPP UK margins, and what is the outlook for Rodelta?
qa_highlights.answer: SPP UK services expected to restart in Q2 FY27 (Q3 for KBL) as power plant and water utility contracts ramp. Rodelta delays are due to consolidating Dutch entities; improvement expected in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why was consolidated margin down from 13% in Q4 to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said standalone EBITDA margin was 13.7% vs 12.8% last year; the drop was mainly SPP UK. Management agreed margins should recover as services revive from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the domestic order book executes in FY27, and what drove the power order book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds of the ~Rs.2,500 crore domestic order book expected in FY27. Power growth is largely nuclear, with primary and secondary circuit orders received in Q1 and new thermal plants.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the KPML margin fall from 12.5% to 7.3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to the merger of loss-making TKSL into KPML; management expects TKSL to turn profitable on BHEL and KBL demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is normally equal to depreciation, used for modernisation, debottlenecking and quality. No specific figure was given.

risks_watch: Inventory and advances rising sharply (per annual report, inventory WIP 180 to 241; advances Rs.32 crore to Rs.91 crore) with dispatch timing dependent on customers accepting goods.
Overseas EBITDA margin at 5.1%; recovery depends on SPP UK services contracts and Rodelta execution over the next two quarters.
Finance cost up 31% and other expenses up 21% YoY; other expenses rising from digitalisation and advertising spend.
Large order delays (domestic orders, petrol pump dispatch subject to end-customer acceptance) make quarterly numbers lumpy.
Nuclear primary circuit pump metallurgical qualification and tender outcome expected within weeks.
key_quotes: Inventory has gone up as we had explained in the previous quarter, we were improving our foundries. And that exercise is complete.
We remain confident of delivering double-digit revenue growth in FY '27 over FY '26 for our standalone business.
Normally our capital expenditure is equal to depreciation and it is mainly used for modernization, debottlenecking and quality requirements wherever they are.
So, drop is observed in the SPV UK business and that's why the consolidated numbers are lower.
500241|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on FY27 growth: management reiterated double-digit standalone revenue growth and said it will strive for double-digit consolidated growth. Cautious on timing, attributing the inventory build and dispatch slippage to the foundry upgrade and deferring overseas margin recovery to Q2/Q3 FY27 services restarts. Evasive on specifics, declining to quantify the nuclear share of the power order book, the FY27 capex figure, and the SPP UK and Rodelta margin path beyond qualitative timelines.

500245|2026-06.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q1 FY27: castings sales up 18% to 41,345 t, tube sales down 14% to 41,512 t, and power and fuel costs rose about INR58 crore YoY.
500245|2026-06.overview: Pig iron and castings output rose in Q1 FY27, while tube output and sales fell on weaker high-value oil and gas and export orders. Power and fuel costs rose sharply, with about INR58 crore of the INR100 crore YoY jump in other expenses coming from power and fuel, half of it from rate increases. A change in green-power rules (8 hours instead of 17) and the end of power trading (about INR10 crore a year) cut the expected solar and wind savings to about INR80 crore a year from about INR100 crore. Management guided to recovery in pricing and volumes from Q2, and said Q1 EBITDA margin was 12-13%.

financial_highlights.change: -3% YoY vs 132,392 t; management attributed to higher internal consumption
Company level; steel and tube margins cited at 14-17%

financial_highlights.metric: Power and fuel cost increase in other expenses
financial_highlights.value: INR58 crore of ~INR100 crore YoY jump
financial_highlights.change: About INR50 crore sequential jump in other expenses; about INR30 crore from rate increases

segments.name: Castings
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,345 t, up 18% YoY; pricing passed through to customers, with further price increases still being concluded. Rajpura foundry is fully sold out at about 2,200 t per month.

segments.name: Tubes
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,512 t, down 14% YoY, with a weaker product mix as more line pipe was sold in place of high-realising export and oil and gas tubes. Management is in a wait-and-watch stance due to Chinese dumping and subdued demand.

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: Realisation improved YoY and QoQ (about INR42,400/t vs INR39,000/t base, as cited on the call); about 30,000 t exported at slightly better than domestic prices. Pig iron EBITDA is expected to support the company margin.

segments.name: Steel (alloy)
segments.commentary: Management expects external sales of 100,000-110,000 t this year vs about 84,000 t, but cost pass-through is still under discussion.

guidance_outlook: Castings volumes expected to rise to about 162,000 t gross sales and then about 188,000 t, implying roughly 17-20% growth.
Overall volume growth of at least 15% across products in the remaining three quarters, with tube volumes up at least 10% YoY and steel external sales up more than 20%.
Pig iron output close to 700,000 t this year, possibly slightly less.
Price-increase and cost pass-through benefits expected from Q2 and Q3 onward.

Medium term: about INR14,000 crore revenue aspiration with 300,000 t castings, 300,000 t casting sales and 400,000 t tube sales. Management said castings reach 270,000 t realisable capacity in this year plus two more years, with tubes at 350,000 t in 3-4 years.
Capex of INR600-700 crore this year, rising in the following years; about INR3,000-3,500 crore over the next four years.
capex_capacity: 35 MW solar plant in commissioning stage; 12 windmills of 2.1 MW each; both expected to be commissioned between June and September 2026.
Solapur two-part (no-bake) foundry, 15,000 t per annum, with commissioning expected by October 2026. Management said it has capacity of about 1,250 t per month.
Rajpura expansion: first phase to 40,000-50,000 t per annum within about 8 months; second phase to 70,000 t per annum. Total realisable castings capacity across six foundries is 270,000 t per annum.
Koppal oxygen plant and enhanced pulverised coal injection in blast furnaces 1 and 2, expected to complete by February-March 2027. Hiriyur pig iron upgrade to 360,000 t, taking about nine months.
Jejuri rolling capacity to rise from 15,000 t to 25,000 t per month (about 3 lakh t per annum), with about 240,000 t saleable; about 18-month timeline.

Premium couplings plant in Baramati, order expected within weeks. Koppal steel plant (about 2 years) and Baramati expander mill (2 years to build) are at early stages. Iron ore mines and pelletisation at Koppal are in progress.
One blast furnace to move to steelmaking, with government clearances in place; decision expected within 2-3 months, commissioning in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: Castings demand described as strong across tractors, automobiles, earthmoving equipment and stationary engines; management expects realisation improvement.
Tube demand subdued by oil and gas slowdown and export disruption; Chinese dumping is pressuring pricing. Management expects the tube market to recover.
Coke dumping into India has reportedly eased, which supports domestic pig iron prices. Pig iron exports are running at about 30,000 t.
Fuel costs rose sharply: LPG cost in Solapur roughly doubled versus pre-war levels. Coking coal cost is expected to peak in June-August because of a three-month coal inventory.
Monthly pig iron sales plan of about 58,000 t including internal sales (about 48,000 t external); foundry grade about 20,000-25,000 t of that.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal (Unique PMS): what drove the ~INR100 crore YoY and ~INR50 crore QoQ jump in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR58 crore of the increase is power and fuel, split roughly INR28-29 crore rate-driven and INR28 crore volume-driven, with Rajpura castings volumes and a full-month Jejuri run versus last year's shutdown. Power trading (about INR10 crore a year) has stopped and green power use is now limited to 8 hours instead of 17.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal: does the regulation change hit the solar and wind savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, savings fall to about INR80 crore a year from about INR100 crore, and payback stretches from 3 years to 3.6-3.7 years. Battery storage at MW scale is being examined, with some power expected through batteries shortly.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal: what is the INR350 crore contingent liability for forest development fee?
qa_highlights.answer: Karnataka levied forest development fees in 2016; the company won in the High Court, the state appealed to the Supreme Court, and the matter is sub judice after hearings with orders reserved. The company provides at 8% and discloses it as a contingent liability.

qa_highlights.question: Vipul Mody (individual investor): will the company move into subassemblies, machined components and high-end castings, and what is the status of 3D printing?
qa_highlights.answer: Machine shops at Koppal, Solapur and Rajpura already supply fully machined components, including a 6-cylinder head to an OEM. Maximum casting size after expansion is about 3 tons, the 2-part foundry is about 1,250 t per month, and the company is not yet in mining or wear-resistant parts. Prototyping is near serial production, with 50 cylinder blocks bought via the proto route.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor (Kapoor & Co): what is Q1 EBITDA margin and how will it trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Q1 company EBITDA at 12-13%, with steel and tube margins at 14-17% and pig iron weighing on the blend. Castings target about 15% plus or minus 1%, with pricing upside, and tubes are in a wait-and-watch phase due to Chinese dumping. Management expects company margin to improve on pig iron support and pass-through from Q2-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: what are current pig iron realisations and how much did raw-material costs absorb?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation moved from a base of about INR39,000/t to about INR42,400/t QoQ. Management said dollar rates and coal costs are pressuring costs, but realisation still improved slightly net of cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Dhruvesh Kanakia (Antique): what volumes are expected for the remaining nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Pig iron close to 700,000 t this year, possibly slightly less. Castings gross sales to rise from about 162,000 t to about 188,000 t (17-20% growth). Steel external sales of 100,000-110,000 t vs about 84,000 t, and tube volumes up at least 10%, with overall volume growth of at least 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Manish Goyal (Thinkwise): timeline for INR14,000 crore revenue aspiration, seventh foundry, and ONGC/OIL tube order execution?
qa_highlights.answer: Castings realisable capacity of 270,000 t is targeted in this year plus two years, with 300,000 t in 3-4 years; tubes to 350,000 t in 3-4 years after the expander mill (2 years to build); steel external sales of 240,000 t in about 2 years. Blast furnace 1 conversion to steelmaking is expected to be decided within 2-3 months, with commissioning in about 2 years. The 23,000 t tube order should complete in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Sanghvi (Monarch): will coking coal costs rise further next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company holds about 3 months of coal stock, so the high-cost coal flows through June-August, which will be higher than April-June. Peaks may be partly mitigated as coal prices ease and blending improves.

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Sanghvi: is pig iron realisation a blend of foundry and steel grade, and what is capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly pig iron sales plan is about 58,000 t including internal sales (about 48,000 t external), a mix of grades with foundry grade about 20,000-25,000 t. Capex is INR600-700 crore this year, rising in later years, with about INR3,000-3,500 crore over four years. Green power capex is set to slow, with battery storage starting at 50-70 MW.

qa_highlights.question: Anurag Patil (Quest): what is the net impact on annual power cost after solar, wind and power trading changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the 70 MW solar to yield INR70-80 crore a year, the 35 MW solar about INR30 crore, and the windmills (equivalent to 55 MW) to add more, with the combined solar and wind benefit at about INR70-80 crore. Seasonal wind benefit is about 70% in June-September. Koppal is self-sufficient on waste-heat power, but Maharashtra fuel costs need a strategy and power trading is not likely to return without battery storage.

risks_watch: Power and fuel cost inflation: about INR58 crore of YoY increase, LPG in Solapur roughly doubled, and coking coal peaking June-August; watch whether castings and alloy steel price pass-through actually lands in Q2-Q3.

Tube volume recovery: tube sales down 14% YoY with a weaker mix; Chinese dumping and subdued oil and gas and export demand; the INR100 crore-ish order book from ONGC/OIL is expected to finish within two quarters.

Green power economics: regulatory limit cut from 17 to 8 hours, power trading (about INR10 crore a year) stopped, and solar and wind savings cut to about INR80 crore from about INR100 crore; payback moved to 3.6-3.7 years.

Execution of capex: INR600-700 crore this year against INR3,000-3,500 crore over four years; Solapur 2-part foundry by October 2026, solar and wind commissioning June-September 2026, Koppal oxygen and PCI by February-March 2027.
Pig iron pricing and exports: realisation up to about INR42,400/t from INR39,000/t; about 30,000 t exported; a dollar and coal cost squeeze could offset gains.
Contingent liability of about INR350 crore on Karnataka forest development fee, sub judice at the Supreme Court with no timeline.
key_quotes: There's no understanding in the market for price escalation. So we have to really get the increase from the market for the tubes.
I think we are on this direction though still the aggregates could be a little far away.
So I would say that I'm optimistic and we should look for improved performance in the coming quarters.
We can't push too much of line pipes into market.
There is a negative impact, but we continue to progress because still there is benefit.

500257|2026-06.headline: Lupin Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 8,277 crore and EBITDA hit INR 2,464 crore (30% margin), but management guided to a sharper US slowdown ahead.

500300|2026-03.headline: Grasim Q4 FY26: Birla Opus revenue up 52% YoY like-to-like, Pivot revenue more than doubled; paint price hikes staggered into Q1 FY27 on crude-linked input cost spike.
500300|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as a record year, with consolidated revenue of INR1,75,431 crores and standalone revenue of INR41,039 crores. Birla Opus grew 52% YoY like-to-like in Q4 and crossed 10% revenue market share in March 2026 on its own, while Birla Pivot's Q4 revenue more than doubled YoY and is close to its INR8,500 crore annual guidance. Raw material costs linked to crude derivatives rose sharply, with management citing up to 20-25% of COGS, prompting two further paint price hikes staggered into Q1 FY27. Cellulosic fibre and cement (UltraTech) contributed strong profit growth, and Grasim announced a INR10 final dividend.

financial_highlights.change: FY26 revenue roughly doubled vs FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Caustic soda sales volume Q4 FY26

segments.name: Birla Opus (paints)
segments.commentary: Q4 like-to-like revenue +52% YoY; revenue market share up ~90 bps QoQ and 370 bps in FY26, now No.3 in organised decorative paints and crossed 10% share in March 2026. Installed capacity 1,332 MLPA (24% of industry); Kharagpur plant commercialised in Q3 FY26. Network at 11,500 towns, 50,000+ dealers, 1,200+ franchise stores; 218 products.

segments.name: Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue more than doubled YoY; close to INR8,500 crore annual revenue guidance. Delivers to 5,000+ pin codes across 400+ cities. Management targets EBITDA break-even exit in FY27, possibly sooner.

segments.name: UltraTech (cement, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Crossed 200 MTPA grey capacity in April 2026, targeting 240+ MTPA by March 2028. UltraTech declared INR240 per share dividend, implying about INR4,000 crore cash inflow to Grasim before tax.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR4,614 crores (+14% YoY), EBITDA INR588 crores. Harihar Lyocell Phase 1 of 55,000 tpa under way within a total 110,000 tpa expansion. China operating rates at 92% in Q4 versus 87% a year ago.

segments.commentary: Chlor-alkali capacity 1,505 KTPA moving to 1,530 KTPA. Specialty chemicals revenue +5% YoY, but higher ECH input prices hit profitability. Specialty chemicals 27% and chlorine derivatives 22% of revenue mix.

segments.commentary: Board approved a INR4,000 crore preferential equity raise; Grasim to invest INR2,880 crores to keep its 52.3% fully diluted stake.

segments.commentary: Porcelain capacity held flat with productivity focus only; polymer long rods sold out after recent expansion; hollow composite expansion being evaluated. Sales and EBITDA no longer disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management expects industry paint growth to move from single-digit to double-digit in FY27, with Birla Opus targeting high double-digit growth.

Birla Opus priorities in order: become No.2 decorative paints player, reach INR10,000 crore revenue in the third year of full-scale operations (FY26 treated as year one), then profitability. Paint EBITDA losses to narrow quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year.
Birla Opus dealer network to exceed 15,000 towns by end of FY27 from 11,500 currently.
Birla Pivot targets EBITDA break-even exit in FY27.
Two further paint price increases announced April 2026, staggered into Q1 FY27; consumer impact expected in second half of Q1 and all of Q2 FY27.
Capex guidance for FY27 to be shared next quarter.
Grasim intends to keep above 50% stake in UltraTech and Aditya Birla Capital (current position, not a long-term policy).
capex_capacity: UltraTech above 200 MTPA grey capacity (April 2026); 240+ MTPA target by March 2028.
Harihar Lyocell: Phase 1 of 55,000 tpa in progress, total 110,000 tpa expansion; Phase 2 to be announced.
Birla Opus Kharagpur (sixth plant) commercialised Q3 FY26; average distance travelled per product down over 30%.
Chlor-alkali capacity 1,505 KTPA to 1,530 KTPA; additional capacity under evaluation.
Insulators: no plans to add porcelain base capacity; incremental investment in polymer long rods and hollow composites.
demand_pricing: Paints: dealer price hikes of 2-6% in Jan-Feb 2026 were absorbed; primary and secondary sales stayed strong in Q4 and April 2026 primary sales were in line with March.
Paints: input costs rose to as high as 20-25% of COGS due to crude-linked raw materials, packaging and rupee depreciation; management says raw material prices remain unstable.
Paints: 10% free-paint consumer scheme continues despite price hikes; institutional channel grew 43% QoQ and 212% YoY, with a pipeline of 45,000 sites.
Paints premium and luxury products at 65% of value; 75% of products rated No.1 in blind tests by applicators (company claim).
Cellulosic fibre: management says cellulosic fibres are growing at roughly 2x the CAGR of other fibres in India; benign pulp prices supported margins.
Specialty chemicals: ECH input price increase compressed profitability.

qa_highlights.question: How much growth in paints will come from distribution expansion and tinting machines versus throughput?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth from both numerical dealer expansion (11,500 towns to 15,000+) and throughput gains by adding product ranges to existing dealers. Older dealers over 18 months show 25-50% higher counter share and throughput comparable to legacy players.

qa_highlights.question: Is paint profitability improving from scale, and is FY26 the first full year for the INR10,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed FY26 as the first full operating year internally. Fixed costs (sales and service force, brand spend) were front-loaded and should be covered by growth; variable-cost levers include better procurement, plant and logistics optimisation, and adding second and third raw material suppliers. Paint contribution improved significantly in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How close is Birla Opus to the No.2 position in decorative paints?
qa_highlights.answer: Birla Opus plus Birla White putty is roughly at the level of the current No.2 on a decorative-only basis for Q4 FY26. The ambition is for Birla Opus alone to become No.2 in decorative paints, excluding industrial.

qa_highlights.question: Dealer throughput versus industry benchmarks?
qa_highlights.answer: Throughput is in line with market presence across A/B/C/D dealer classes. Top dealers stock 2-2.5x the bottom dealer and generate 4-5x its throughput. The market leader is estimated to have 20-25% more dealers and a richer A-class mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan after the UltraTech dividend, given about INR2,900 crores for ABC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the INR2,900 crore use (ABC stake maintenance) as a one-off for FY26. Cash is being used for Grasim's dividend, maintaining the ABC stake, and supporting the two new businesses. Capex guidance for FY27 will come next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Pivot profitability path and when will segment disclosure start?
qa_highlights.answer: Pivot aims to exit FY27 at EBITDA break-even and may get there sooner. Paints EBITDA losses are on a glide path to narrow each quarter. Management said segment reporting for paints and Pivot would start shortly.

qa_highlights.question: Will paint EBITDA losses (about INR300 crores per quarter) come down materially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management answered 'Yes, it will come down' without quantifying the timing.

qa_highlights.question: Insulator capacity, sales and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Porcelain capacity is flat, with productivity focus; polymer long rods are sold out after expansion; hollow composite expansion is being evaluated. Insulator sales and EBITDA are no longer disclosed.

FY27 capex guidance is pending and will be shared next quarter; capital allocation (dividend, ABC stake maintenance, support for new businesses) was described as a one-off for FY26, not a long-term policy.

This VUCA situation makes demand forecasting difficult and we need to closely monitor the situation as impact of price rise will slowly be felt by consumers and contractors in second half of quarter one and entire quarter two FY '27.

500300|2026-06.headline: Grasim Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR48,716 crore, up 21% YoY, with standalone EBITDA more than doubling to INR1,094 crore.
500300|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached a record INR48,716 crore (up 21% YoY), the 24th consecutive quarter of YoY growth. Standalone revenue rose 28% to INR11,795 crore and standalone EBITDA rose 107% to INR1,094 crore. Birla Opus revenue grew 64% YoY to INR1,661 crore after an 8.8% cumulative price increase to offset a raw material cost shock, and Birla Pivot grew 75% to INR2,548 crore. Management also disclosed a new 0.25% of standalone revenue brand royalty payable to Birla Holdings from June 2026, and a planned Renewables equity infusion below INR1,000 crore in FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated net debt to TTM EBITDA

segments.name: Birla Opus (paints)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,661 crore (+64% YoY, +17% QoQ); market share up 30 bps QoQ to a number-three position, with 8.8% cumulative price increase in Q1. Premium and luxury portfolio is about 65% of sales value; institutional sales up 85% YoY.

segments.name: Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,548 crore (+75% YoY), annualised run rate above INR10,000 crore. Management reiterated EBITDA break-even by exit of FY27; private labels more than doubled YoY off a low base.

segments.name: Cellulosic fibres (VSF/CSF)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR4,530 crore (+12% YoY) on volumes down 4% YoY; specialty fibre rose to 27% of sales mix from 21%. EBITDA roughly doubled, helped by a low base and specialty mix.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,640 crore (+10% YoY); ECU realisation INR37,955/t (+6% YoY); caustic share of revenue fell to 49% and specialty chemicals rose to 30%. EBITDA INR491 crore (+16%). Volumes softer on plant maintenance.

segments.name: Cement (UltraTech, consolidated)
segments.commentary: Sales volume 41.31 Mt (+12% YoY); gray capacity 205.5 Mt after adding 8.7 Mt in the quarter; EBITDA INR5,146 crore (+12%). Green power mix 45.6%; 5,802 retail outlets.

segments.name: Aditya Birla Capital (financial services)
segments.commentary: Lending portfolio grew 32% to nearly INR2,20,000 crore; housing finance crossed INR50,000 crore (+50%). Grasim invested INR2,880 crore at INR356/share to maintain its fully diluted stake.

segments.name: Other businesses
segments.commentary: Renewables revenue +59% YoY; textiles +26% YoY; insulators serving the power sector expansion.

guidance_outlook: Birla Opus: continues to target INR10,000 crore revenue by FY28 and guides over 50% YoY revenue growth for FY27; expects to become profitable once it reaches INR10,000 crore.
Birla Pivot: on track for EBITDA break-even by exit of FY27 (earlier guidance tied break-even to about USD1 billion or INR8,500 crore revenue; timeline shifted slightly).
Standalone FY27 capex planned at INR3,157 crore (about 45% growth); Q1 spend INR375 crore (about 12% of budget).
Net debt to EBITDA to be kept below 2x for the entire year; Renewables equity contribution below INR1,000 crore in FY27; transaction expected to complete around December 2026.
Chlorine integration expected to reach 68% by exit of FY27 as CPVC is commissioned and ECH commissioning happens in Q2 FY27.
Opus Q2 FY27 expected to be weaker on monsoon seasonality and reversal of Q1 dealer stocking; management expects market stock to normalise by Q3.
capex_capacity: Lyocell Phase 1: INR1,350 crore, 55,000 TPA, detailed engineering and civil work progressing.
Lyocell Phase 2: INR3,094 crore, 110,000 TPA, approved and moving through environmental clearance.
Birla Opus manufacturing capacity 1,332 million litres per annum across six plants; Q1 was the highest-ever production with utilisation improving.
UltraTech: gray cement capacity 205.5 Mt including overseas after 8.7 Mt added in the quarter; renewable power capacity 1.4 GW.
demand_pricing: Birla Opus: raw material COGS up 20-25%, or 10-14% of revenue depending on month; price increases were phased, cumulative 8.8% in Q1 with part flowing into Q2. Management said Q1 was boosted by dealer channel stocking ahead of industry price hikes.
Birla Opus distribution: 12,100+ towns, 55,000+ dealers billed, 1,450+ exclusive franchise outlets, 228 products and 1,945 SKUs, about 11,000 institutional project sites billed in the quarter.
Birla Pivot: volumes supported by demand timing as customers bought at measured rates during Middle East volatility; repeat purchases and new buyer additions reported as rising.
CSF: China supply described as disciplined; management said Indonesian and other high-cost capacity closures are positive for global supply-demand balance.
Caustic: SE Asia caustic soda exited the quarter at USD483/t vs USD468/t a year earlier; management expects domestic prices to trade at import parity.

qa_highlights.question: Is Birla Opus's sequential growth of 17% in line with listed peers, and how should profitability and revenue be prioritised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 industry revenue was inflated by channel stocking ahead of double-digit price hikes; as a new entrant, Birla Opus lacks that stocking power. It will keep the INR10,000 crore revenue target and judge revenue over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: Will Birla Opus turn profitable on a full-year FY28 basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stand is unchanged: profitability begins once Birla Opus reaches INR10,000 crore revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 64% YoY growth give confidence on FY27 growth above 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to over 50% YoY revenue growth for FY27; annual dealer loyalty and year-end schemes are expected to add sales in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 0.25% royalty to Birla Holdings and its impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Applicable from 1 June 2026 on standalone revenue, capped at INR225 crore. Management estimated about INR100 crore impact for standalone; on INR50,000 crore revenue it would be about INR125 crore. Subsidiaries pay on their own revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How will Grasim fund the Renewables equity contribution and what is the net debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Grasim's contribution in FY27 is under INR1,000 crore, with a cash impact of less than INR1,000 crore; GIP is also investing. Net debt to EBITDA will stay below 2x through the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for chemicals margins and caustic pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 margins will face pressure from higher-cost inventory bought in Q1, and it is pricing near daily against commodity prices. It sees domestic caustic trading at import parity and new PVC-linked capacity as small.

qa_highlights.question: Are VSF margins sustainable, and what is the impact of Lenzing exits?
qa_highlights.answer: VSF operating rates in India are close to 100% excluding maintenance. Management said competitor exits are small, high-cost capacity and that Indonesian capacity cuts help global supply-demand balance.

qa_highlights.question: When will Birla Pivot break even, and what share of sales comes from UBS stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Pivot is set to exit FY27 at EBITDA break-even, slightly later than earlier guidance. Retail is 15-20% of mix, and UBS is 70-75% of retail revenue.

Renewables (AB Renewables) capital needs and debt levels; a separate analyst session has been promised with the company team.
Birla Pivot EBITDA break-even timing, which has already slipped slightly versus earlier guidance.

Birla Pivot remains on track to achieve EBITDA break-even by exit of FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Indian agrochemical market growth of ~6-8% in FY27 and seeds in the mid-to-high single digits excluding cotton, which is expected to decline significantly; the company does not expect cotton seed growth this year.

demand_pricing: Demand was weak in Q1: heatwave, delayed monsoon, farmer crop switching, cotton acreage loss and illegal HTBT cotton spread. Kharif sowing was down ~23% YoY at end-June; by 5 July acreage was still ~21% below last year.
IMD forecasts below-normal monsoon at ~90% of LPA (±4%), with El Niño risk; rainfall was ~15% below normal as of 8 July.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further price increases, and how much of the input cost increase has been passed on?

qa_highlights.question: How should one view FY27 execution, and when will volumes recover?

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost fall sharply?

qa_highlights.question: What are the timelines and utilisation for the MENA projects?
qa_highlights.answer: The LSAW/HSAW plants can be done in 18-24 months and the seamless plant in 18-20 months. Management assumes about 50% utilisation and peak utilisation in 2-3 years from FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Nashik seamless run-rate outlook after the API reinstatement?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation should dip for about a quarter and improve from September-October. Quarterly volumes are expected to be about 70,000-80,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin pressure bottoming, and will H2 improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are under pressure from low utilisation and fixed-cost absorption. Management expects H2 to improve over H1, though Q2 may look similar to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What peak term debt is expected after the projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Term debt is about INR500-plus crores now and is estimated at about INR3,500 crores once the projects are complete. Working capital is additional.

risks_watch: The Strait of Hormuz blockade remains unresolved after the mid-June peace talks collapsed. Shipments to MENA are suspended and the Saudi job-work solution is still under discussion.
Pending JJM fund release and state title scrutiny continue to weigh on domestic DI demand.
Margin pressure is expected to persist into Q2 until utilisation recovers.
Working capital will rise as operations pick up.
The Delhi High Court order in the Jindal ITF vs NTPC matter is expected within about two months.
Seamless Nashik ramp-up depends on API orders following the licence reinstatement.
Watch whether MENA financial closure, the Abu Dhabi and Saudi projects and the peak-debt build-up stay on schedule.

500378|2026-09.headline: Jindal Saw Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT fell to INR35 crores (from INR91 crores in Q1) as EBITDA dropped to INR312 crores on MENA disruption and water-segment softness.
500378|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 0.8% QoQ to INR4,523 crores and 6% YoY, but EBITDA fell to INR312 crores from INR420 crores in Q1, and PAT fell to INR35 crores including a INR27 crore tax credit. Management attributed the weakness to delayed Saudi job-work shipments, logistics cost inflation, coking coal costs in DI pipes, low utilisation in water pipes, Abu Dhabi DI plant underutilisation, and pellet margin pressure. Standalone net debt declined to INR2,245 crores from INR2,346 crores. Management guided H2 to be better than H1, with margins expected to move toward double digits from Q3/Q4 as oil and gas orders ramp.

500380|2026-03.headline: JK Lakshmi Cement guided FY27 capex of INR1,500-1,700 crore and sees Q1 FY27 cost pressure of INR100-130/t with limited price pass-through so far.
500380|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 industry demand growth of about 7% to roughly 480 million tonnes, with March softening to about 5% amid Middle East conflict and May sluggish before showing green shoots from 15 May. Industry capacity additions of 64 million tonnes pushed utilisation to about 69%, limiting price hikes; non-trade prices rose but trade prices lagged. Company-specific: FY26 clinker production 92.26 lakh tonnes, blended cement ratio 62%, Surat plant utilisation above 60%, and Assam limestone mining rights cancelled (INR325 crore intangible derecognised). Management expects Q1 FY27 cost inflation of about INR120-130/t, with INR300/t energy cost impact more likely in Q2, and gave no firm FY27 EBITDA/t guidance.

500380|2026-06.headline: JK Lakshmi Q1 FY27: realisation up ~8-9% QoQ on geo-mix and non-trade price gains, but management guides to a sharp Q2 cost squeeze from fuel and packaging.
500380|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 demand was reasonable, with industry growth around 8%, and the company's realisation rose roughly 9% sequentially, driven mainly by a 20 km reduction in lead distance (to 368 km from 388 km) and higher non-trade prices in Gujarat, Mumbai, East and North. Fuel cost per Kcal rose to INR1.65 from INR1.54 in Q4, and management expects Q2 fuel cost of 1.8-1.85 plus packaging inflation of INR3.5-4 per bag, with July-September demand cyclicality compounding the pressure. Management reiterated 30 MTPA by FY30 and a net debt/EBITDA ceiling of 2.5x, stretching to 2.75x at peak. Management also described the proxy-advisor-driven AGM voting outcome and an Assam PIL affecting the Northeast project.

segments.name: Novelis
