guidance_outlook: Novelis: Oswego hot mill to restart in the next few weeks; current-year headwinds expected to substantially recover in FY27; long-term $600/t EBITDA target intact.
Novelis cost programme: FY26 exit run-rate savings raised to $200 million (from $125 million target); 3-year structural cost cut of $350-400 million by FY28 exit.

Novelis Bay Minette 600 KT greenfield plant: cold mill commissioning started, hot mill commissioning from next month, commercial coils in FY28, 18-24 month ramp; start-up costs of about $100-150 million annually expected below EBITDA.
India copper TC/RCs: more than 85% contracted at benchmark; expected close to zero or slightly negative for FY27.
India copper EBITDA: Q1 FY27 similar to Q4 (INR900 crore range) but management guided INR600-700 crore per quarter for Q2 and Q3.

India capex FY27 about INR12,000 crore (later framed as INR15,000-17,000 crore for the next year); Novelis FY27 capex $2.3-2.4 billion, mainly Bay Minette; consolidated net debt peak INR80,000-90,000 crore over next 2 years; net leverage around 2x.
Aluminium market: deficit now 1.5 million t for CY26 (from 0.3 million t), tightest in Q2-Q3 CY26.
Renewable capacity 470 MW at year end, rising to 523 MW by end Q1 FY27.
capex_capacity: Aditya smelter: first 180 pots by December 2027, next 180 pots by December 2028; management says timelines look firm.

Captive coal: Chakla box cut expected in next 2 months, first coal possibly Q4 FY27; Bandha box cut done but first coal only in FY28 due to high strip ratio; Meenakshi (strip ratio under 1) expected to add substantial volumes in FY29; Chakla Stage 1 forest clearance received.

Downstream: Aditya FRP ramping up; battery enclosure at full ramp-up; Aditya battery foil commissioned; Taloja AC fin facility commissioning; specialty alumina precipitate hydrate commissioned, under customer approval.

Copper: inner grooved tubes (35 KT) in customer qualification; 50 KT Pakhajan e-waste recycling plant to commission in August; copper smelter about 3 years out; battery grade copper foil scaled down to a smaller capacity in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: Aluminium prices strengthened in the quarter; West Asia conflict disrupted supply; global market now seen in 1.5 million t deficit for CY26.
India Q4 FY26 aluminium demand about 1.6 million t, +9% YoY; India copper demand 402 KT, +10% YoY.
Q4 FY26 hedges: aluminium 64% at INR2,807/t; currency 26% at INR88/$. FY27 hedges: aluminium 29% at $3,013/t; currency 14% at INR90.13/$.
Sulfuric acid prices high due to Middle East conflict and China export restrictions; management expects Q1 FY27 to be slightly above Q4 but could correct if Strait of Hormuz reopens.
Global concentrate TC/RCs at record lows around -$0.21 to -$0.25/lb; expected to stay negative through FY27.
Alumina sales 211 KT in Q4 FY26; Q1 FY27 guided at about 170 KT.
Midwest premium at about $380/t due to 50% US tariffs; Japan premium up on supply tightness and freight. Domestic vs export realisation gap narrowed; exports may be slightly higher in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Does Q4 copper EBITDA reflect the full sulfuric acid price surge, and how sustainable is the INR900 crore run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 expected in the same range given high sulfuric acid, but management guided INR600-700 crore per quarter for Q2 and Q3 and cautioned that Hormuz reopening could correct sulfur prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the India and consolidated capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: India FY27 capex about INR12,000 crore, rising to INR15,000-17,000 crore in the following year; Novelis FY27 capex $2.3-2.4 billion, falling sharply in FY28 after Bay Minette. Consolidated capex expected to be lower than current levels; FY28 detail deferred to Q3/Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt breakdown and peak?
qa_highlights.answer: India gross debt INR12,200 crore, cash INR18,000 crore (net cash INR6,000 crore). Novelis gross debt INR75,000 crore, cash INR11,000 crore (net debt INR63,000 crore). Consolidated net debt peak INR80,000-90,000 crore over the next 2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is $600/t Novelis EBITDA assuming current scrap spreads and start-up costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management does not assume current spreads or metal prices; start-up costs sit below EBITDA. The $600/t target is seen as sustainable, not reliant on current tailwinds.

qa_highlights.question: How do coal captive mines change costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Chakla and Bandha expected at similar cost to market coal; Meenakshi substantially lower. Captive mines expected to flatten the cost curve over 15-20 years; meaningful captive volumes only from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will Novelis avoid shipping to Canada given tariffs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is mitigating tariffs by using US cold mill capacity, including additional capacity secured at Logan; Kingston (Ontario) mill longer-term planning still pending.

risks_watch: Oswego hot mill restart timing and the resulting Novelis volume recovery in Q1 FY27.
Tariff exposure (Midwest premium, US-Canada flows) and possible relief from governments.
Input cost inflation: Q1 FY27 cost guided about 5% higher, driven by furnace oil; CP coke and pitch also rising.
Sulfuric acid and TC/RC normalisation could reduce copper EBITDA from the current run-rate if Hormuz reopens.
Captive coal ramp-up delays (Bandha high strip ratio) and Aditya smelter timelines.
Net debt rising toward INR80,000-90,000 crore; net leverage target around 2x.
Battery-grade copper foil and battery demand in India slower than expected.
500440|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on India operations and cost leadership, and on Novelis recovery in FY27, but cautious on near-term macro, sulfuric acid normalisation and copper beyond Q1. Management declined to guide copper EBITDA beyond Q1 and gave ranges rather than firm figures on some capex and start-up costs.
key_quotes: Our quarterly copper EBITDA stood at a record INR907 crores, up 48% year-on-year on account of better realization in byproducts and operational efficiencies.

So, I think that Q1, to be fair, will also be in the same range because sulfuric prices are high. But I'm not going to stick my neck out to Q2 and Q3. I would still go back to the 600, 700 per quarter there.
So consolidated net debt peak should be between INR80,000 crores and INR90,000 crores over the next 2 years.
We have not factored in current scrap spreads. I mean these current scrap spreads and the current scrap market conditions; we take it as not sustainable.
So, I think that Novelis is heading to a recovery year in FY 27.

500440|2026-06.headline: Hindalco Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 58% YoY to INR13,481 crore and PAT 75% to INR7,013 crore, led by record India upstream EBITDA of INR7,390 crore.
500440|2026-06.overview: Consolidated business segment EBITDA rose 58% YoY to INR13,481 crore and PAT rose 75% to INR7,013 crore, with Hindalco India EBITDA up 73% to INR8,606 crore. India upstream aluminium posted a record INR7,390 crore EBITDA (USD2,331/t, 55% margin) on higher LME and favourable macros, while copper delivered a record INR918 crore despite a planned smelter shutdown. Novelis volumes fell 5% YoY to 916 kt and adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to USD516 million, but the Oswego fire outage and elevated US tariffs (USD70 million) weighed on the quarter. Management guided volumes higher in Q2 for downstream aluminium and copper, and said sulphuric acid prices will stay near Q1 levels in Q2.

segments.name: India upstream aluminium
segments.commentary: Shipments up 3% YoY and revenue up 44% YoY; record EBITDA of INR7,390 crore. Hedged about 29% of FY27 aluminium at USD3,004/t and 18% of FX at INR91.63/USD.

segments.name: India downstream aluminium
segments.commentary: Shipments up 3% YoY to 104 kt; EBITDA INR298 crore, up 30%, on volume, mix and premiumisation. Management sees a sustainable downstream margin nearer USD250/t than the USD300 seen in Q1.

segments.name: India copper
segments.commentary: Metal shipments 105 kt, down 16% YoY on a planned smelter shutdown; CCR volumes 96 kt, down 8%. Record EBITDA of INR918 crore; ex-shutdown EBITDA/t would have been around USD1,000.

segments.name: Novelis
segments.commentary: Shipments 916 kt, down 5% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA USD516 million including an $18 million net positive from Oswego fires and $47 million insurance proceeds. Cost savings run-rate at USD225 million against a USD350-400 million target by FY28 exit; Oswego mill restarted in June.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 sulphuric acid prices expected to stay near Q1 levels; management hopes for no tapering in H2.
Q2 volumes expected higher for both India copper and India downstream aluminium.
India cash cost expected to rise 5-6% QoQ in Q2 on northern-region coal prices during monsoon.
Novelis net leverage expected to fall below 4x, with a level of about 4.5x around end-September; Novelis net debt/EBITDA to start declining in Q4.
Novelis working capital release of USD300-400 million over the next couple of quarters.
Novelis long-term EBITDA/t guidance of USD600 unchanged; Oswego net cash impact seen at about USD600 million after all insurance recoveries.
Consolidated net leverage to remain around 2x; India net debt/EBITDA not expected to change materially as FY27 is a high-capex year.
Aditya refinery and first 180 kt smelter phase commissioning Dec 2027; second phase Dec 2028; meaningful contribution in FY29. Captive coal: Chakla about 1 Mt and Bandha about 0.5 Mt in FY28.
capex_capacity: Aditya alumina refinery and aluminium smelter expansions progressing on track; strategy to double upstream capacity.
Captive coal mines: Chakla, Bandha and Meenakshi under development. Chakla about 1 Mt and Bandha about 0.5 Mt expected in FY28.
Renewables: 470 MW operational; 414 MW solar/wind and 90 MW RE-RTC pumped storage to be added in FY27, taking the portfolio to 884 MW solar/wind/hydel and 125 MW RE-RTC.
Novelis Bay Minette 600 kt greenfield rolling and recycling plant on track for completion in 2026, with initial commissioning underway.
Aditya Battery Foil and Taloja AC Fins commissioned last quarter and in customer qualification; specialty alumina (precipitated hydrate) nearing commercialisation.
Copper smelter expansion, Pakhajan scrap melting project (commissioning this year, IRR in high teens) and copper smelter timing under review, with smelter output expected in FY29.
demand_pricing: LME aluminium moved from about INR3,150/t before the Middle East conflict to a peak near USD3,850/t, then eased to USD3,200/t after the ceasefire; management expects a 2026 deficit of about 1 Mt.
India aluminium demand about 1.5 Mt in Q1 FY27, up about 3% YoY; flat-rolled products up more than 10%; electrical segment weak on deferred contractor-led projects.
Indian refined copper demand 359 kt, down 9% YoY; TC/RC at -26 to -30 cents/lb; concentrate tightness expected to persist through 2026.
Alumina prices around USD330-340/t, slightly up from historic lows, and expected to stay in this range until Middle East smelters return.

Novelis faces US Section 232 tariffs of about USD70 million in Q1 (versus USD24 million last quarter) as it imports metal while Oswego is down; management expects some tariff cost for the next couple of quarters.
Japan/Korea MJP premiums elevated due to Middle East supply disruption; expected to ease next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Novelis tariff impact of USD70 million excludable to show EBITDA/t above USD600, and why did it rise from USD24 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Novelis Steve Fisher said it was not excluded from adjusted EBITDA and advised against adding it back; tariffs stem from importing metal while Oswego is down and will persist for a few quarters. Dev Ahuja said third-party costs sit below the line as fire costs, while own-network imports do not, and declined to give specific guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the brand royalty to Birla Group Holdings affect Hindalco?
qa_highlights.answer: Satish Pai said both Novelis and Hindalco will pay a royalty of 0.25% of revenue to Birla Group Holdings, capped at INR225 crore per year, which is below Hindalco's materiality threshold and does not affect dividend or capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the USD300/t downstream aluminium EBITDA sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Pai said USD250/t is a more sustainable level for the rest of FY27, with the longer-term aluminium downstream target still above USD300/t; more clarity on total downstream (including copper) is due next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will Novelis leverage fall well below 4x?
qa_highlights.answer: Dev Ahuja said Novelis will be below 4x, helped by insurance recoveries, working capital release, lower ABL borrowings and higher EBITDA run-rate, after about 4.5x at end-September.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Oswego insurance recovery outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Dev Ahuja said cumulative cash impact so far is about USD1.4 billion net of recoveries, of which USD300 million has been recovered; the net cash impact is expected to settle at about USD600 million, with a couple of hundred million possibly slipping into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedging position for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Pai said 21% of FY28 aluminium is hedged at USD3,160/t, with a target of about USD3,200/t; no further FY27 hedging is being added due to deep backwardation.

risks_watch: Novelis tariff costs (USD70 million in Q1) persist until supply chains are reconfigured; cash impact of Oswego fire pending insurance recovery.
India copper concentrate tightness and negative TC/RC keep pressure on smelter economics; copper smelter expansion is capital-intensive.
Elevated coal, sulphur and MJP costs; India cash costs seen rising 5-6% QoQ in Q2.
Related-party royalty (0.25% of revenue, capped at INR225 crore per year) under SEBI LODR disclosure.
USMCA status is uncertain; management does not expect a material impact.
Exceptional items of about INR300 crore at consolidated level (Ind AS vs US GAAP) expected to fall away as Oswego recovers; watch Q2 for confirmation.
500440|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on India upstream and downstream profitability and Novelis recovery, but noticeably evasive on tariff quantification, royalty terms and the consolidated exceptional-item treatment, deferring details offline or to next quarter.
key_quotes: Our quarterly EBITDA was a record INR7,390 crores, up 81% year-on-year.
We view the impact of the outage largely as a timing issue rather than a structural one.
Our long-term EBITDA per ton guidance of $600 remains unchanged.
I would say more around USD250 is a more sustainable number.

500459|2026-03.headline: PGHH FY26 sales flat at about Rs 4,300 crore while PAT rose 19% to about Rs 850 crore on savings-funded reinvestment.
500459|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of targeted investment: sales were flat at about Rs 4,300 crore, while PAT grew 19% to about Rs 850 crore, helped by a Rs 86 crore savings programme. The call focused on the Integrated Growth Strategy, with Whisper Period Panties, Whisper Nights and Vicks launches cited as proof points. Management acknowledged category growth has been uneven, with feminine hygiene at 7-10% and healthcare at 2-3%, and flagged West Asia-linked commodity and resin cost pressure. Incoming CFO Srividya Srinivasan takes over on July 1. Few hard guidance numbers were given, and several questions on buybacks, investment plans and manufacturing were declined.

financial_highlights.metric: Structural operating margin improvement in FY26
Net profit margin expansion over 10 years

segments.name: Feminine Care
segments.commentary: Category growing 7-10%, with growth coming from varied sub-segments; Whisper is the market leader. Whisper Period Panties sold over 10 crore units and tripled the business in FY26 (as stated); Whisper Nights is about half of pad users' choice and growing ahead of the category.

segments.name: Personal Healthcare (Vicks)
segments.commentary: Category growing about 2-3%, volatile through the year and linked to monsoon timing. Vicks VapoRub returned to double-digit growth within 6 months of its all-night relief relaunch. Vicks Cough Drops offtake growing double digits this year, with volume and volume share up on a past-3-month basis.

guidance_outlook: Management expects some near-term challenges to continue, citing macro headwinds, West Asia conflict and inflation.
Feminine hygiene category expected to grow at late single digits this year; long-term category growth expected at mid to high single digits.
Multi-year savings master plans being built for each business unit, intended to fund reinvestment and margin expansion.
Management said it would not guide on price-sensitive matters; no quantitative FY27 sales or margin guidance was given.
capex_capacity: No capacity, capex or utilisation figures were disclosed on the call.
Manufacturing footprint and future investment plans were raised in Q&A but were not answered.
demand_pricing: Crude and resin prices have risen 30-50% due to the West Asia conflict; the company said it has not gone out of stock.
Rural consumption still exceeds urban, but a softening trend is visible due to inflation; non-food inflation is below the RBI 4% medium-term target.
More than 50 new players have entered feminine hygiene in the last 10 years, including regional and D2C brands.
Healthcare category has declined for many quarters post-COVID, with early signs of recovery in recent quarters.
Qcomm: one in four consumers buying period products are choosing panties, where Whisper is #1.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue growth slowed over the last 5 years despite ad spends, distribution expansion and launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited fast-changing consumer needs, shifts in media and retail, and very high competitiveness; it said it is investing in innovation, communication and Nights and Panties segments.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company not launching new-age products in feminine hygiene?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to its Nights and Period Panties launches and upgrades to existing lines across benefits and sizes, with Whisper Period Panties positioned as the segment leader.

qa_highlights.question: Are margins being optimised at the expense of growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said flat sales came after reinvestment and that savings are used to fund product, package and demand generation; green shoots are visible in focus portfolio areas.

qa_highlights.question: How are West Asia-linked cost pressures being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said crude and resin prices are up 30-50%, supply continuity has been maintained, and savings programmes are being accelerated to offset costs.

qa_highlights.question: Questions on CEO/CFO turnover and management tenure.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said strategy has stayed constant across leadership changes and that a grow-from-within talent model ensures succession continuity.

qa_highlights.question: Questions on buybacks, parent company investment and manufacturing expansion.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to answer, citing unpublished price-sensitive information.

risks_watch: Top-line stagnation: FY26 sales flat despite investments; watch whether volume growth returns in FY27.
Commodity and resin cost inflation from the West Asia conflict, which could erode the margin gains.
Intensifying competition from regional and D2C players in feminine hygiene and healthcare.
Monsoon timing affecting healthcare category growth.
CFO transition effective July 1, 2026 (Srividya Srinivasan) and leadership change narrative.
Softening rural and urban consumption from inflation.
500459|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on strategy and productivity but cautious on near-term demand; management openly acknowledged flat sales and category challenges. It was evasive on guidance, buybacks, capex and manufacturing expansion.
key_quotes: We know that the results have been mixed.
Our Integrated Growth Strategy is working for us.
Whisper Period Pants has sold 10 crore units in the last year!
Despite these significant disruptions, we have not gone out of stock or made compromises on product performance.

500463|2026-03.headline: Black Box targets INR12,000 crore organic plus INR6,000 crore inorganic revenue by FY30 (~$2bn), with 10% EBITDA margin; order book ~$800m.
500463|2026-03.overview: This was a Capital Markets Day held June 1, 2026 (transcript filed June 7), not a quarterly earnings call, so no Q4 FY26 quarterly P&L was presented beyond FY26 annual figures. Management said the turnaround is complete and set a FY30 target of INR12,000 crore organic revenue (~$1.3bn, 17% CAGR from ~INR6,000 crore) plus ~INR6,000 crore (~$0.7bn) from acquisitions. FY26 EBITDA was INR570 crore at a 9% margin, up from 4.3% in FY23, and the order book reached ~$800m. Growth is pinned on hyperscale data centre fit-out, enterprise GSI services, the TPS products business (~$90m to $200m) and rest-of-world, including India.

financial_highlights.change: Expanded by 470 bps (as stated; likely margin expansion context)
From INR269 crore and 4.3% margin in FY23
Up from ~$500m; ~60% growth cited; $1bn booked in FY26

financial_highlights.value: Over 9x growth in last three years

financial_highlights.change: Total capital raised ~INR600 crore in the period

financial_highlights.value: Receivables up ~INR580 crore QoQ; payables up ~INR300 crore; receivable days ~90+ vs 60-75 normal
financial_highlights.change: Driven by 38:62 revenue skew to March quarter

segments.name: Hyperscale data centre / GSI
segments.commentary: Data centre share of order book ~25%, guided to rise to 35-40% in coming quarters. Seven dedicated sites for one hyperscaler (three more allocated); GSI headcount ~1,500, with 400 in data centre practice and 2,100 hires planned in 12 months, mostly in the US.

segments.name: Technology Product Solutions (TPS)
segments.commentary: Current business ~$90m, targeted at ~$200m by FY30 with ~40% gross margin and a 10% EBITDA target. Seven verticals addressed, ~$3bn TAM; R&D in Bangalore and Limerick, Ireland; flagship product line Emerald.

segments.name: India / Rest of World
segments.commentary: India is 6-7% of revenue (~$50m), targeted at 8-10% of a $2bn business (~$200m). India is a low-margin geography per management; 300+ partnerships and 17 offices / 35 delivery centres cited.

segments.name: Financial services (anchor client)
segments.commentary: A large US bank client has been served for 27 years at ~$100m annual spend, ~$1bn lifetime revenue crossed in the last 10 years, 68% growth since 2016.

guidance_outlook: FY30 target: INR12,000 crore organic revenue (~$1.3bn, ~17% CAGR) plus ~INR6,000 crore inorganic (~$0.7bn), totaling ~INR18,000 crore (~$2bn). Computed at INR95/$.
EBITDA margin: 10% overall target, reached in FY27 per management (9% currently); FY30 EBITDA margin target of 10%+.
Order book expected to reach $1.3-1.4bn by March 2027 (guided 50%+ growth in FY27 bookings); average order age 15-18 months.

Acquisitions: ~$200-250m of revenue acquired per year, targeting 2-5% EBITDA margin targets bought at 6-8x and turned to 9-10% in 90-120 days; 70% upfront, 30% earn-out. Brazil (2S) acquisition recently announced.
Debt-to-equity could rise to ~1:1 after the acquisition programme; otherwise debt to stay broadly flat with internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Data centre workforce: 2,100 hires planned in next 12 months (mostly US) to go from ~4,000 total employees to ~7,000.
GCC in Bengaluru to grow from ~600 to ~1,000 people.
Centralised resource management in Plano, Texas; estimating tools Accubid and P6 Primavera; separate project controls team.
Training: 600 people trained on AI; 36 hours of learning per person per year vs 28-hour industry average; 1,500 certifications in data centre business.
Capital allocation priorities: people and training, AI-enabled platforms, working capital, and acquisitions in Europe, APAC, India and Latin America.
demand_pricing: Management says demand outweighs supply in data centre work; prices have 'considerably increased', with cost increases passed through; margins claimed to improve modestly with execution.
Mike Carney stated no business is won on price; win depends on execution and relationships.
Hyperscaler data centre contracts: mainly time-and-materials / design-build; ~25% of project value is unknown at outset; change orders agreed, e.g. ~$2.5m change orders on a $10m initial scope.
US skilled labour market is constrained; inflation expected. Talent on Tap programme trains trade-school hires (~3 weeks) to address it.
Management claims ~0.2% share of the $200bn networking and connectivity opportunity; India data centre market from 1.3 GW to 8 GW (42% CAGR), India IT $171bn (9.2% CAGR per Gartner).

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory for non-TPS businesses, and how acquisitions will be funded (~$200m a year).
qa_highlights.answer: Target is 10% EBITDA across all businesses; management expects to reach 9% to 10% in FY27 with scale. Acquisitions funded mainly by internal accruals plus some debt; ~$200-250m of revenue acquired per year.

qa_highlights.question: Share of hyperscaler exposure in order book and margin difference vs enterprise.
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres ~25% of order book, rising to 35-40%. Margins are stated as not varying by customer type; India is a low-margin geography and data centre operators/multi-tenants carry higher margins than general contractors.

qa_highlights.question: Contract structure for data centre projects (time-based vs fixed price).
qa_highlights.answer: Mix of annuity contracts, fixed-price small projects and cost-plus for large multi-year projects; management says 15-20% of projects are expected to convert to annuity as the business scales to $2bn.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rising and receivable outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: The March quarter revenue skew (62% in March vs 38% in first two months) raised receivables by ~INR580 crore; management expects receivable days to revert to 60-75 from ~90+ as the skew normalises to 45:55.

qa_highlights.question: Hiring split by geography and rupee sensitivity.
qa_highlights.answer: The 4,000 headcount is ~2,000 US, ~1,200 India (500-550 India business, balance GCC), ~300 Europe, ~400 Latin America; hiring is revenue-based and the US accounts for most growth. Plan computed at INR95/$; currency moves affect INR revenue, margin percentages unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Risks to the FY30 plan.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited talent and attrition, unforeseen events and geopolitics; said currency is naturally hedged (earn and spend in same currency) and the main risk is project execution.

risks_watch: Execution on large, multi-year data centre projects where ~25% of value is unknown at start and scope changes are common.
Talent: 2,100 US hires in 12 months in a constrained labour market; wage inflation and attrition.
Working capital: receivable days at ~90+ and the March-quarter revenue skew; watch normalisation toward 60-75 days.
Acquisition integration and the INR6,000 crore inorganic target, funded partly with debt; D/E could rise to ~1:1.
Tax rate normalising from ~10% to 18-20% after about two years, which will weigh on PAT.
Order book conversion: target of $1.3-1.4bn by March 2027 and new hyperscaler wins.
500463|2026-03.management_tone: Highly confident and promotional, with aspirational targets described as a 'dream' and 'plan A'. Specific numbers are given for FY30 and order book, but several claims (market sizes, share, margins) are loosely supported and the Q&A on margin, tax and funding was answered in detail.
key_quotes: So, this is our organic plan, primarily the aspiration to go to INR12,000 crores from current INR6,000 crores, almost like doubling that to a $1.3 billion revenue.
We are expecting that when we end this fiscal year, which is March '27, our order book will remain in the range of probably $1.3 -1.4 billion.
Without a hyperscaler being there, it won't happen, because they are the anchor tenants for most of the GPU data centers.
The focus now is the execution.

500463|2026-06.headline: Black Box Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR1,719 crore (+24% YoY) and EBITDA rose 38% to INR160 crore; FY27 revenue guided at INR7,800-8,000 crore.
500463|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR1,719 crore (+24% YoY), with EBITDA of INR160 crore (+38% YoY, margin 9.3%, up 90 bps) and PAT of INR56 crore (+18% YoY). The quarter included about two months of consolidation from the Brazilian acquisition 2S, which contributed about INR60 crore. Order bookings were US$339 million and the order backlog reached about US$950 million (up 83% since the transformation began). Management reiterated FY27 guidance, with FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 9.3-9.4%, and said growth would be weighted to H2 and spill into FY28.

financial_highlights.change: up 83% since start of transformation; company said up 83% YoY in opening remarks

segments.name: Hyperscale / data center
segments.commentary: Management expects hyperscale to grow about 25% in aggregate across the business, with data center tenures of 24-36 months. A new US hyperscaler order of US$131 million (about INR1,240 crore) was added, with work on site starting from November.

segments.name: Non-hyperscale enterprise
segments.commentary: Expected to grow at modest double-digit, about 10%, lagging the hyperscale cycle, with enterprise spend expected to follow with a lag.

segments.name: Product business (TPS / KVM, Emerald)
segments.commentary: Still loss-making at EBIT level as revenue grows; management expects about 20% growth in FY27 and says the segment is highly accretive once scale is reached.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue INR7,800-8,000 crore (+23-27% YoY).
FY27 EBITDA INR725-750 crore (+27-32% YoY); EBITDA margin 9.3-9.4% (about +30-40 bps). Medium-term aim is 10% or more at scale.

500480|2026-06.headline: Cummins India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR3,375 crore, but pre-exceptional PBT fell 0.7% to INR721 crore as commodity inflation hit margins.

Exports were flat YoY at INR521 crore, with high-horsepower exports up 16% but low-horsepower exports down 20%. Profit before tax before exceptional items was INR721 crore, marginally lower YoY, as steel, pig iron, aluminium and copper inflation, freight and West Asia disruption weighed on margins. Management took one price increase at the start of Q2 FY27 and said it had not yet been absorbed by the market; no price hike was taken in Q1. Data centres drove a large share of power generation growth.

qa_highlights.question: Lifespaces five-year vision and fit in the group?

qa_highlights.question: Can Bosch India become a low-cost export hub for the Bosch Group?

qa_highlights.question: How is JLR planning to reduce its breakeven volume to 300,000?

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected FY27 industry growth and TMPV's supply situation?

qa_highlights.question: Was there a prior-period item in Q4 PLI accrual?

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (aluminium, copper, petrochemical-linked inputs) of 5-6% of revenue with limited pass-through so far; margin depends on further price actions and cost savings.

500570|2026-06.headline: TMPV Q1 FY27: India volumes up 46% to 182,000 units, but 4.5% commodity hit held India EBITDA at about 4%; JLR PBT fell to GBP 109 million.
500570|2026-06.overview: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (formerly Tata Motors) posted Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 95,800 Cr, EBIT margin of 2.4% and PBT of Rs 1,600 Cr, down year on year. JLR wholesales fell about 10% (around 8,000 units) on Jaguar run-out, a supplier fire at Solihull and Middle East disruption, with JLR PBT at GBP 109 million versus GBP 351 million last year. India wholesales rose 46% to about 182,000 units and share rose 200 bps to 14.3%, but a 4.5% commodity hit in Q1 offset fixed-cost leverage and material savings, holding EBITDA margin at about 4%. Management says FY27 guidance for JLR is not changed.

segments.name: JLR
segments.commentary: Wholesales down about 10% YoY (about 8,000 units, around 3,000 below internal plan). Defender up YoY; Range Rover and Range Rover Sport hit by a chassis supplier fire early in the quarter. Retail down 14.5K YoY, with over 5,000 from Jaguar run-out and Middle East. China wholesales down 25%.

Group targets $1.7 billion of cost savings across ex-works cost, warranty and fixed costs; detail promised with Q2 results.

qa_highlights.question: Why only 1% price increase despite strong raw material headwinds?

qa_highlights.question: FY27 volume and margin outlook for India?

qa_highlights.question: How does rising EV mix affect JLR margins?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sierra supply outlook for the festive season?
qa_highlights.answer: Engine casting and sheet-metal constraints are easing over the next two months, with major capacity additions from October.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 margin outlook after the 3% commodity hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Net of price increase, cost reduction and the absence of Q1's 1% IPL seasonal impact, Q2 margins are expected to be flattish vs Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What JLR EV volume is expected in FY27?

500575|2026-03.headline: Voltas Q4 FY26 consolidated PBT fell to INR 181 crores from INR 343 crores as UCP margins were hit by commodity inflation and rupee depreciation.
500575|2026-03.overview: Consolidated total income rose marginally to INR 4,930 crores in Q4 FY26 from INR 4,847 crores, but PBT fell to INR 181 crores and net profit to INR 113 crores from INR 343 crores and INR 236 crores. For FY26, total income fell to INR 14,483 crores from INR 15,737 crores, PBT to INR 557 crores from INR 1,191 crores, and net profit to INR 377 crores from INR 834 crores. Management said March 2026 was a record sales month and April was close to that level, but margins were compressed by old-cost inventory, FX losses and commodity inflation, with price hikes only partly passed through so far.

segments.commentary: FY26 RAC volume was 2.25 million units; Voltas leads the No. 2 player by a 5.1% primary market share gap. Margins were hit in Q1-Q2 by channel overhang and in Q4 by commodity inflation and rupee depreciation. Chennai plant utilisation is ~1.2 lakh units/month against 1.5 million units annual capacity.

segments.name: Voltbek (within Segment A)
segments.commentary: Year-to-date market share of 8.6% in washing machines and 6.2% in refrigerators in a sluggish market. Sanand plant localisation is ongoing and management expects margin expansion over the medium term.

segments.commentary: Order book close to INR 6,200 crores at 31 March 2026, of which ~INR 4,500 crores is domestic. Pantnagar and Chennai facilities running at higher utilisation than last year.

Sanand plant localisation and scale-up for Voltbek is in progress.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1-Q2 margins were hit by a channel stock overhang from erratic summer and early monsoon, and that some pressures are structural (supply chain, currency). The aim is gradual improvement towards FY25 levels, through pricing and cost actions.

qa_highlights.question: Will cost inflation hit Q1 margins and could they dip significantly before price increases?

qa_highlights.answer: No client has invoked force majeure; Qatar's temporary contractor option was revoked. Price variation clauses cover 40-50% of the India MEP book and some international contracts, so margin risk is limited.

qa_highlights.question: What is channel inventory and Chennai utilisation, and what is the domestic share of the order book?

500620|2026-03.headline: GE Shipping posts best-ever quarterly profit and first-ever INR1,000 crore annual consolidated net profit, with INR35.10 full-year dividend per share.

The company announced its 18th consecutive interim dividend of INR 14.40/share, its highest quarterly payout. Management said it remains predominantly on the spot market (about 25-26% of capacity on time charter), is net cash, and is holding most cash rather than buying ships at peak prices.

500780|2026-03.headline: Zuari Industries guides net debt to about INR700 crores by FY26-end, dependent on ~INR850-900 crore Dubai inflows over six months.
500780|2026-03.overview: Sugar operations delivered record crushing of 159.7 lakh quintal and 101.7% capacity utilisation in FY26, with sugar realisation up to INR4,053/quintal from INR3,894. Standalone PAT turned to INR12 crore from a loss of INR37 crore, and consolidated PAT was INR105 crore versus a loss of INR94.4 crore. Management says the St. Regis Dubai project (98% complete, BCC received 21 May 2026) is the main deleveraging lever, with external borrowings of about INR1,900 crore expected to fall to about INR700 crore by year-end. Ethanol remains under pressure from stagnant prices and roughly 100% industry overcapacity, and the Envien bioethanol JV is still stabilising with OMC tenders delayed.

segments.commentary: Q4 income INR29.8 crore vs INR8.9 crore; FY26 income INR89.4 crore vs INR18.8 crore; FY26 EBITDA INR6.8 crore vs INR0.9 crore. About INR95 crore of projects under execution.

segments.commentary: Zuari Finserv FY26 income INR20.1 crore (up about 4.1%) and EBITDA INR5.6 crore (up about 60%). Zuari Insurance Brokers GWP INR99.4 crore (up about 9%), brokerage income INR10.2 crore (up about 40%).

segments.name: Envien bioethanol JV (ZEBPL)
segments.commentary: Plant commissioned 1 January 2026 and under stabilisation; OMC second and third round tenders have not yet been floated, with existing orders running to October.

guidance_outlook: Dubai inflows of about INR850-900 crore expected over the next six months, with the bulk in Q2 and Q3 FY27 per management; all proceeds to go to deleveraging.
Associate company inflow of about INR250-258 crore expected.
Management expects external borrowings of about INR700-800 crore (net debt about INR700 crore) at FY26 end, versus about INR1,900 crore currently.
Sugar closing stocks estimated at 5.6 million tonnes (vs 5.3 million tonnes), about two months of consumption; sugar prices expected stable near term.
No monetisation of Goa land (about 260 acres, book value INR163 crore) assumed in plans.
No new ethanol capacity expansion until overcapacity clears; ZEBPL 1,000 KLPD expansion on hold.
capex_capacity: Sugar crushing record 159.7 lakh quintal; capacity utilisation 101.7%, highest ever.

demand_pricing: Ethanol prices stagnant; management expects revision, citing industry representations. OMC bids about 1,800 crore litres against 1,050 crore litres tendered; overcapacity now about 2,000 crore litres.

qa_highlights.question: How certain is the Dubai inflow this quarter, and how much deleveraging is expected this quarter or next?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Banerjee said the BCC was received and demand letters are being raised; INR850-900 crore is expected over six months, with the balance of about INR800-850 crore in FY26-27 after retention money.

qa_highlights.question: What will net debt be after these inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Jatin Jain said external borrowings of about INR1,900 crore less about INR1,200 crore of deleveraging (Dubai plus associate) leaves about INR700 crore at year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dubai project profit and capital invested?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Banerjee said Zuari Infraworld's 50% JV share of estimated profit is about INR600 crore on capital invested of INR270-275 crore, giving about INR900 crore of cash back.

qa_highlights.question: What recourse exists if Dubai buyers default?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Banerjee said RERA in Dubai allows forfeiture of 40% of the apartment value and resale; the timeline could be about a year, but management sees no buyer inquiries or concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the value of strategic investments declined about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Athar Shahab said the holdings are performing operationally and management does not comment on share prices; Texmaco Rail is held as a strategic investment and not consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What drove lower sugar recovery and what can be controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Saxena said early-season crushing starting in late October lowered the weighted average recovery; the company ranked fourth of about 14 nearby units and is replacing the 238 variety.

risks_watch: Timing and collection of Dubai inflows (INR850-900 crore) amid West Asia conflict; retention money and buyer defaults could delay them.

Ethanol overcapacity (about 100%) and delayed OMC second and third round tenders affecting Envien ZEBPL utilisation.
Sugar recovery trend lower YoY; input cost inflation including chemicals.
Currency: management says rupee depreciation is favourable for Dubai receivables; forward covers if needed.
Goa land monetisation not factored in; Texmaco Rail provision of about INR700 crore reported by an analyst (not confirmed by management).
500780|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on operations and the Dubai cash flows, but guarded on deleveraging timing and evasive on share price and investment value questions. Management repeatedly deferred details (e.g., Texmaco, TIHL project) to other entities.
key_quotes: We achieved our highest ever crushing of 159.7 lakh quintal for the financial year.
So after considering the inflows from the Dubai project of around INR800 crores considering the exchange rate fluctuation and the inflows from our associate company of around INR258 crores.

This amount will be used entirely for deleveraging.

500780|2026-06.headline: Zuari Q1 FY27 standalone loss widened to INR9.5 crore PAT on sugar margin squeeze; Dubai St. Regis repatriation of INR142.58 crore received so far against INR900 crore FY27 target.
500780|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income rose 26% YoY to INR283.9 crore on higher sugar volumes and realisations, but EBITDA fell to INR31.3 crore from INR36.9 crore and PAT swung to a loss of INR9.5 crore from a loss of INR3.9 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to an 8% rise in UP cane SAP (INR370 to INR400 per quintal). Consolidated PAT was a marginal INR0.05 crore, supported by associate income, mainly Zuari Agro Chemicals. Management reiterated the INR900 crore Dubai repatriation target for FY27 and said that sugar prices are at record highs, which it expects to support the next quarters.

segments.name: Power

segments.name: Real estate (Zuari Infraworld)

segments.name: Engineering (Simon India)

guidance_outlook: Dubai St. Regis profit repatriation: INR900 crore expected in FY27; INR142.58 crore (AED55 million) received in Q1 and July–August, with about INR750-758 crore balance expected in FY27.
Zuari Agro Chemicals loan of about INR258 crore expected to be repaid in the current quarter (Q2 FY27).

Furniture division decision expected by the end of FY27 (revival or other action).

qa_highlights.question: How much Dubai St. Regis repatriation is expected in the current quarter and the next, and are there buyer challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: AED55 million (INR142.58 crore) received in the quarter; INR900 crore guided for FY27 with the balance on track; management said no buyer back-outs or discount demands so far.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY28 interest saving from repaying about INR1,100 crore of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Jatin Jain cited 9.73% average cost of borrowing; the analyst's INR100-110 crore saving estimate was accepted on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale and timing of buying Zuari International shares for INR150 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Transaction to be done in one or more tranches funded by an ICD approval; aim is to consolidate listed and unlisted group holdings into Zuari Industries and let the holding entities repay external debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Zuari Agro INR95 crore ICD get a six-month extension, and when will the INR258 crore be repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm any extension; said the entire INR258 crore outstanding is expected to be repaid in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will ethanol capacity expand, and are OMC tenders expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Next OMC tender expected in October 2026 and the company will participate; capex on hold due to overcapacity (1,050 crore litres tendered vs 1,800 crore litres offered), with investment only after demand clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone EBITDA fall despite revenue growth, and why did sugar segment profit drop?
qa_highlights.answer: UP cane SAP rose 8% (INR370 to INR400 per quintal); extra one lakh quintal of sugar sales from higher quota added about INR45 crore revenue, but segment profit fell to INR8.4 crore from INR12.3 crore on cane cost.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of earnings of sugar, power and ethanol over next 12-18 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the segments to recover in the next season, cites high sugar prices and a healthy UP cane crop, and expects a fairly decent quarters ahead.

qa_highlights.question: Concern over Texmaco share purchase at INR190 and shareholder value?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier Zuari International transaction was only an enabling resolution with no actual deal; future transactions will be at market price.

qa_highlights.question: Dubai repatriation, buyer payments and segment asset timing at Zuari Infraworld?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Banerjee said about 40-45% of customer collections remain; payment plan is 50-50 and demand notes were raised post completion certificate. Real estate segment assets of INR770 crore as on 30 June 2026, mainly INR400 crore Dubai receivables, expected to convert in one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Zuari Infra DM pipeline and GDV path to INR10,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book about INR6,000 crore per Alok Banerjee; GDV of projects in hand about INR4,900 crore per Athar Shahab, roughly halfway to the INR10,000 crore aspiration; Hyderabad and Bengaluru launches next month; plotted project cycle time 15-18 months.

risks_watch: Dubai repatriation: INR142.58 crore received against INR900 crore FY27 target; about INR750-758 crore balance must come in the remaining FY27 period, with buyer payments (about 40-45% of customer collections) still outstanding.

Goa land monetisation put on hold after new law and higher circle rates; furniture division decision due by end of FY27. Unresolved UP ethanol export fee exposure (INR507 lakh) with no provision.

500780|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on sugar prices, Dubai repatriation and real estate, but evasive on the Zuari International/Texmaco share transactions, the Zuari Agro ICD extension and the ethanol policy, where management declined to comment on rumours or quantify outcomes.

500790|2026-06.headline: Nestlé India says volume growth has been double-digit for recent quarters and ad spend is up ~40%, but gives no numeric FY27 guidance.
500790|2026-06.overview: This was an analyst and investor meet held virtually on 4 August 2026, not a formal Q1 FY27 results call, so no quarterly financial statements were presented. Management said volume-led growth has accelerated over the last four to five quarters, with double-digit volume growth in recent quarters versus a 4.2% five-year volume CAGR. Advertising investment has been raised by close to 40% in recent quarters, which management funds from cost-saving programmes (2.6% of cost base saved in 2025 versus a normal 1.8–1.9%). Management declined to give forward projections, said 40% ad growth will not persist every quarter, and flagged macro headwinds from energy, packaging, oil, shipping and currency.

financial_highlights.change: Management said it will not stay at 40% every quarter

segments.commentary: NESCAFÉ recorded its 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. NESPRESSO now has four boutiques in three cities; entry Rs.2 sachets to Rs.100 per espresso pod.

segments.commentary: Noodle penetration about 35–36% against ~100% monthly for biscuits; MAGGI is India's largest market globally. New MAGGI line capex about Rs.170 crore in the last calendar year.

segments.commentary: Management says the segment had good volume-led growth last quarter; CERELAC relaunched with a zero-added-sugar (ZAS) variant alongside the existing sugar-within-limit range. NAN EXCELLAPRO and LACTOGEN with probiotics launched.

segments.commentary: Management says it is gaining cat food share and the category is growing strongly; no revenue figures given.

Capex to continue to support volume growth; no forward capex amount given.

Household penetration in the mid-50s for key brands (annual); snacking: about 80% of the snacking market is below Rs.20 price point.
Q-commerce: management says e-commerce and q-commerce growth is well ahead of market; supplies about 6,000 dark stores of key q-commerce players; growth share data not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Can double-digit volume growth be sustained after ~11% FY26 volume growth, given chocolate and coffee strength?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined forward projections, citing a secular opportunity: noodles penetration ~35–36% versus biscuits ~100%; confectionery shares are small; coffee has 20 quarters of double-digit growth. Acknowledged quarters could be off.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be maintained or modestly improved over the medium term?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Nestlé has a track record of maintaining margins and efficiency programmes support this; management said it is not chasing growth at margin cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why has ad spend risen 40–50% for three quarters, and what happens to growth when the GST base gets high from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said spend is being raised behind brands with ROAS monitoring; 40% will not continue each quarter; base effects from GST tailwind will show in some quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MPN (nutrition) volume outlook and what initiatives have been added?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no new initiatives beyond the portfolio refresh (CERELAC ZAS variant, NAN EXCELLAPRO, LACTOGEN probiotics) and that volume growth in nutrition is expected to continue; no mid-to-high single-digit target given.

qa_highlights.question: How much reach expansion remains in rural and how big is the e-commerce contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rural reach is still about half of some peers' level and a long way to go; e-commerce/q-commerce contribution not quantified, with focus on category share rather than absolute growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A being considered and how is the parent portfolio being used?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said M&A is not imminent; 9 of 10 focus is on current businesses. Parent-group brands (Pops, Delight, Friskies, NESPRESSO) are being scaled in India.

500800|2026-06.headline: Tata Consumer Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12% to INR5,349 crore, with EBITDA up 19% and margin at 13.6%, up 70 bps.
500800|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 12% to INR5,349 crore (9% in constant currency), with India business UVG of 13%. EBITDA grew 19% and margin expanded 70 bps to 13.6%, while net profit rose 29% to INR427 crore (reported EPS INR4.31; adjusted EPS INR4.67). Growth businesses grew 47% and reached 36% of revenue, with Sampann, RTD and Capital Foods/Organic India leading. India tea revenue fell 4% despite 2% volume growth as tea prices were passed on, and India margins compressed sequentially on inflation, staggered pricing, higher A&P and FX losses.

segments.name: India salt
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7% on 7% volume growth despite June price increase (Tata Salt orange bag MRP INR30 to INR32); value-added salt grew 13%; market share close to 39%.

segments.name: India tea and coffee
segments.commentary: Revenue down 4% to INR1,200 crore as tea prices were passed on; tea volume +2%, coffee +24%. Unusually long summer and LPG shortage hit small restaurants and tea stalls in the south.

segments.name: Sampann and growth portfolio
segments.commentary: Sampann revenue +58%, volume-led; core pulses/spices/poha/vermicelli growing about 30%, with cold-pressed oil and dry fruits adding to growth. Sampann margin up 150-200 bps YoY.

segments.name: RTD (water and beverages)
segments.commentary: Revenue +41% on 38% volume growth; Tata Water Plus volumes up 35% with revenue +41%. Kombucha Zero launched in two variants.

segments.name: Capital Foods and Organic India
segments.commentary: Capital Foods INR232 crore (+40%); Organic India INR118 crore (+27%); combined gross margin close to 50%. Tata Soulfull grew 45%.

segments.name: International (incl. Starbucks India)
segments.commentary: Constant currency +3%, reported +16%. US +7% constant currency (seventh straight quarter of share gains); UK and Canada hit by warm weather; Starbucks revenue +11%. Non-branded and solubles/plantation declined on lower coffee prices.

guidance_outlook: Growth portfolio (30%+ growth) guided at 30% plus; Capital Foods and Organic India aspiration 25-30% growth.
Salt growth target 5-7%; ambition to cross 40% salt share quickly.
Tea volume guidance mid-single digit in the short to medium term; tea input inflation of 7-10% planned for.
Starbucks India expected to deliver high single-digit top-line growth going forward.
Full-year EBITDA margin expansion guided at 50-70 bps; management expects operating leverage to kick in as headcount stays broadly flat.
Management reiterated double-digit consolidated revenue growth as the norm, with some quarters at mid-teens and others at low double digits.
Medium-term aspiration: good India food business at 17-20% EBITDA margin; tea and salt gross margin 33-36%.
capex_capacity: Water business: adding capacity for next season, and possibly for the following season, after underestimating demand in some regions.
Capital Foods noodles capacity now in place; Cup Noodles launched and chilli oil expanded; a Korean noodle launch is coming soon.
Most Organic India and Capital Foods production is in-house; RTD is run by dedicated co-packers; Sampann relies heavily on outsourcing.
Management is evaluating bringing scale categories in-house; manufacturing capex for these categories is described as not heavy.
Water distribution reach about 40-50% of the 75% of the country where it is available; North and West are described as white space.
demand_pricing: Tea: input cost inflation of 7-10% seen so far, mainly at the lower end of the portfolio; pricing taken in June, with more to follow if inflation persists; buying is still early.
Salt: calibrated price increase from June 1; price hikes expected to settle in about a quarter.
Coffee: lower coffee prices helped the branded US business; the non-branded business is pass-through, so management calls the net effect positive.
Pulses: management expects to pass on any price rise; Sampann pulses about INR600-700 crore in a INR2.2 lakh crore pulses market with 6% branded penetration.
Non-branded business was down 10% constant currency; solubles down 12% and plantation down 8%.
Management says it has gained market share in tea in relative terms over the last couple of years, although Nielsen disclosure has been stopped.

qa_highlights.question: Whether growth businesses can invest in own capacity, pass on cost inflation in spices, dry fruits and edible oil, and reach a 35% growth norm for Capital Foods and Organic India.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most Capital Foods and Organic India production is in-house, and inflation will be passed on with a time lag. It set the Capital Foods and Organic India norm at 25-30% growth, with the go-to-market reset completed in February.

qa_highlights.question: Why India margins fell sequentially while international margins rose.
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Goenka cited input cost inflation, a timing gap between cost hikes and staggered pricing, higher A&P, and FX losses on hedges in India. International margins benefited from lower US coffee prices.

qa_highlights.question: Tea pricing outlook and inflation.
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil D'Souza said tea inflation is 7-10% so far, with buying still early; pricing will be reviewed after 15-30 days and taken up if needed to protect margins.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of margin expansion beyond salt pricing, and the path toward a 20% margin.
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers listed were full pricing impact, US coffee normalisation, cost saving drives, mix shift to Capital Foods and Organic India, water utilisation gains and operating leverage, with Sampann margins close to 12%.

500830|2026-03.headline: Colgate India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% to Rs 1,583 crore, with domestic growth at 9.2% and gross margin at 69.6%.
500830|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 net sales were Rs 1,583 crore, up 9% YoY, with domestic growth of 9.2% and growth broad-based across Core, Premium, toothpaste, toothbrush and personal care. Full-year FY26 sales were flat at Rs 5,984 crore, and full-year EBITDA margin was 31.2% including an 80 bps GST input-credit (IDS) impact. Q4 NPAT was Rs 353 crore, and excluding one-offs (restructuring, GST, prior-period tax refunds, labour code) management said profit grew about 9%. Management declared an interim dividend of Rs 48 per share and said it is still paying out virtually 100% of NPAT.

financial_highlights.change: excluding one-offs, management says profit grew about 9%
absolute spend up 10%; FY26 13.7% of sales
stated as improved on prior years despite GST-blocked capital

segments.name: Toothpaste (Core: Colgate Strong Teeth, Max Fresh)
segments.commentary: Max Fresh is described as the fastest-growing franchise in the portfolio, with a blue variant in testing and new Sensorials variants (berry added). Management said consideration for all sub-brands is flat or rising versus original levels.

segments.name: Premium (Colgate Total, Visible White, PerioGard)
segments.commentary: Premium mix is up 35% over the past two years per management. Visible White Purple was launched 18 months ago and is described as the most successful launch in Colgate's history; PerioGard franchise is said to be doubling YoY. Management did not disclose the premium share of sales; e-commerce is about 10% of business.

segments.name: Toothbrush
segments.commentary: Management says Colgate is 1.7x its nearest competitor in the entry tier. New launches include a Rs 10 brush with 16g to 20g of toothpaste offered in the pack and a PerioGuard brush.

segments.name: Personal care (Palmolive)
segments.commentary: Palmolive focus is hand wash and body wash. Management said foaming hand wash is the leader in the category and growing at double digits in key channels; body wash is a partnership-led watch item.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin is expected to stay in the range seen in recent quarters over the next two quarters despite commodity and currency headwinds, offset by the Funding the Growth programme.
EBITDA is not guided to a specific level or expansion; it will be calibrated to advertising investment, with top-line growth and absolute profit as the stated priorities.
A price increase to offset the post-West Asia inflation is expected to be taken within a few weeks; category price increases are expected to be in the low single digits.
Management targets balanced volume and price-led growth but gave no numerical growth target.
Management is pursuing GST input-credit mitigation through supplier duty representations, refunds in non-manufacturing states, and transporter rate changes.
Brand investment is expected to rise further from the Q4 level of 12.6% of sales; FY26 was 13.7%.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed in the call.
Direct outlets reach is 1.7 lakh; 2 lakh stores were added to reach in 2025.
Plant sustainability: recyclable tubes now fully adopted, renewable energy share moved from 40% to 60%, plastic neutrality at 101%, recyclable/reusable/compostable packaging at 95%.
demand_pricing: Q4 growth was balanced between price and volume, and management said Q4 volume was flat.
Post-GST price cuts have been lapped after the Q1 calendar 2026 anniversary, so the price increase is now needed for input-cost inflation.
Rural demand is recovering and is beginning to converge with urban growth, though rural is growing more slowly than in 2025.
Promotional intensity has not eased; management is using AI tools to cull promotions and redeploying the spend.
Premium portfolio is growing faster than the core; management cited the 130-140 index to the core as the premium threshold.
Quick commerce share is ahead of total e-commerce, which is ahead of the offline business.

qa_highlights.question: How has the QR-linked dentist recommendation programme helped premiumisation, and how is B2B sales to dentists growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4.5 million people were scanned, with around 20% of scans going to a dentist; the programme is being repeated and expanded to a virtual format via QR codes on 500 packs. B2B sales to the profession grew at about a 50-60% two-year CAGR, with a field force of about 150 people.

qa_highlights.question: Competitors have launched similar products (for example Purple); is the market expanding and what is the D2C threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Purple is accelerating and it aims to hold the largest share of the whitening segment. Most D2C brands are still small, and Colgate's quick-commerce share is ahead of its e-commerce share, so there is no loss of share.

qa_highlights.question: Is pricing growth in Q4 from the price increase, and will the West Asia-linked inflation be passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 growth was about half price and half volume, with the post-GST price cuts now lapped. A price increase for inflation is expected within a few weeks; gross margin should stay in range but EBITDA will depend on advertising.

qa_highlights.question: How should volume growth be viewed going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is balanced volume and price growth, not reliance on price as in the past, and not relying too heavily on volume.

qa_highlights.question: How is premium defined and what share of sales does it represent?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium is defined as products at a 130-140 price index to the core range and outside Active Salt, Max Fresh and Cibac. Premium's contribution has risen 35% in two years; management declined to disclose the premium share of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY26 EBITDA margin at a sustainable level, and is there room to expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin will keep improving through the Funding the Growth programme. It gave no EBITDA margin target, saying advertising spend is the key variable and top-line and absolute profit growth are the priorities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the GST inverted duty structure and how will it be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 80 bps (full year) and 160 bps (Q4) IDS impact stays in the baseline. Mitigation includes lower GST on transport services, refunds in non-manufacturing states, and supplier representations for lower input GST.

qa_highlights.question: Did higher-grammage packs drive Q4 growth, and what is the top-line growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said grammage increases of about 11% on a few packs were a pass-through of the GST cut, but were not the main driver of growth. 30-40% of SKUs are already higher-grammage. No numeric growth target was given; management stated top-line growth is a priority.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from commodity and currency costs, and the GST inverted duty structure (IDS) impact of 80 bps for FY26 and 160 bps in Q4.
Rising advertising intensity (Q4 12.6% of sales, FY26 13.7%) may keep EBITDA margins under pressure.
Competitive intensity in premium whitening, with copycat launches and D2C brands in toothpaste; promotional intensity has not eased.
Timing and size of the price increase for input-cost inflation; whether volume growth can be sustained alongside price.
Whether the rural demand recovery continues and whether the Q4 acceleration in growth holds.
500830|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the brand, premium portfolio and cash generation, but cautious on FY27 margins, with no EBITDA guidance. Management was evasive on the premium share of sales and on the timing and size of pricing.
key_quotes: We have seen over the last quarter a significant acceleration in net sales growth for Q4, our domestic
We are not at the moment seeing a slowdown. In fact, we are seeing an acceleration in the rate of growth of Purple
We are not seeing any let up in promotional intensity. The market continues to be competitive.
So, we obviously are looking to grow this company fast. Top-line growth remains a huge priority

500840|2026-03.headline: EIH Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue up 10% but EBITDA up only 1% on business mix, wage code and higher expenses; FY26 PAT hit by Rs 30 Cr wage code charge.
500840|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a very volatile year (Operation Sindoor, West Asia conflict, monsoon rains, December flight disruptions, late-February West Asia war) but said EBITDA was the highest in company history. Q4 consolidated revenue grew 10% while EBITDA grew 1%, with profit from operations down 5% on higher tax expense, business mix shift toward lower-margin OFS (flight catering), higher airport levy, repair and maintenance, CSR, legal and donation costs. For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 8% and EBITDA 3%; reported PAT fell on a one-time Rs 30 Cr wage code impact and the Mashobra fair-value charge from the prior year, and management said excluding these profit grew 2%. Management said April and May trends were better than expected, led by domestic demand.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated profit from operations, Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: +3% YoY; PAT lower on Rs 30 Cr wage code impact and Mashobra one-time charge

financial_highlights.metric: Own hotels FY26 room revenue / F&B revenue
Cash and funds balance, end FY26
financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,335 Cr vs Rs 1,051 Cr at end March 2025

segments.name: Oberoi hotels (luxury)
segments.commentary: Q4 RevPAR up 4.2% vs luxury segment 6%, dragged by Oberoi Rajgarh ramp-up; FY26 RevPAR up 10.4% vs Indian luxury 6.4%. RGI 204 in Q4 and 191 for FY26, both above last year.

segments.name: Trident hotels (upper upscale)
segments.commentary: FY26 RevPAR up 10.2%, against 5% for the upper upscale segment, on both occupancy and ARR gains versus competition.

segments.name: International hotels
segments.commentary: Q4 RevPAR up 13%, with Mauritius, Oberoi Zahra and Sahl Hasheesh the main contributors.

segments.name: OFS (flight catering)
segments.commentary: Q4 business about Rs 145 Cr, driven mainly by existing airlines with larger flight counts and market share; this segment carries airport levy costs that weighed on margins.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give forward numbers; said April and May were better than expected, led by strong domestic demand.
Foreign business (about 50% of Q4 business historically) hit by West Asia war; management expects the impact to be limited in summer months, with foreign travel peaking October to March.
Management expects a big summit in Q2 and Q3 FY27 to benefit demand, following AI Summit benefit in February-March.
Capex of about Rs 600-700 Cr a year to continue for the next one to two years, rising in FY29-30 when larger hotels open.
Oberoi Grand Kolkata partial opening still targeted for September 2026; Trident Vizag opens 2027; 825 owned/associate keys and 1,893 managed keys in pipeline by 2030.
Mashobra hotel O&M continues until October 2026; management awaits further developments.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about Rs 680 Cr: about Rs 330 Cr on Mumbai land conversion (leasehold to freehold), Rs 125 Cr on Oberoi Rajgarh, about Rs 100 Cr on ongoing renovations (Kolkata and others), remainder replacement capex.
Oberoi Rajgarh opened November 2025, total 3,800 keys in business with Rajgarh added in Q3; about 400 international keys.

Pipeline: 825 owned/associate keys by 2030, starting with Trident Vizag (2027) via EIH Associated Hotels; Hebbal mixed-use site (about 1.3 million sq ft development, including about 7.6 lakh sq ft commercial) by 2030.
Managed pipeline: 24 hotels, 1,893 keys; two new Trident management contracts added (Amritsar, 150 keys; Pawna, 150 keys), signed between Q3 and Q4.

Oberoi Grand Kolkata (about 200 keys) renovation under way with structural works; reopening targeted September 2026. Oberoi Grand Kolkata cited as timeline issue; separately, Oberoi Gandikota site delay moved from 2028 to 2030 due to site change.

Renovations: about 90 rooms at Oberoi Bangalore in 18-room blocks over summer; Trident Nariman Point 4 floors (six months); 4 floors at Oberoi Mumbai one floor at a time; F&B overhaul at Trident Bandra Kurla later in FY27.
demand_pricing: Q4 industry occupancy 67-69%, below last year on West Asia war impact; industry ARR up 6-8% and RevPAR up 5-7%. FY26 industry occupancy flat, ARR up 9-10%, RevPAR up 10-12%.

Occupancy weakened through Q4 with a sharp drop in March; ARR for EIH owned hotels rose from Rs 24,548 to Rs 28,198 in Q4. January RevPAR negative (about -6%), which management attributed to unexplained weak demand, possibly negative international press on air quality.
Delhi/NCR, Mumbai (T20 World Cup) and Bhubaneswar grew strongly; Bangalore hit by lower foreign bookings; Udaipur down on fewer weddings.
Room revenue: MICE and direct segments grew; corporate and leisure flat.
Management says India is significantly underpriced versus Europe, North America and parts of Asia at the top end; no reason to discount rates given rate premium strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What drove February ARR growth near 25% and why was January RevPAR negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said January was weak, with promotions having limited effect; the likely cause (unvalidated) was negative international press on North India air quality. February was strong, helped by the AI Summit, deferred winter travel and strong demand across leisure and city hotels.

qa_highlights.question: With few owned key additions in FY27-28, what drives growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Two levers: ARR (premium positioning, headroom if market stays buoyant) and cost elimination of waste rather than cuts. No specific growth guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 flight catering (OFS) revenue and was it new clients?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 145 Cr in Q4, mainly existing airlines expanding flights and market share, including some domestic airlines.

qa_highlights.question: Where do foreign tourist mix and Q4 FTA levels stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 foreign business about 50% historically; domestic share rose substantially in March and more than offset weaker foreign demand. Exact March quarter mix to be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a financial loss from geopolitical issues in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: No financial impact calculated; lower foreign room nights were offset by domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 20% in Q4 and will Mashobra O&M continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher expenses from business growth, higher airport levy on OFS, higher R&M, CSR, legal and donation costs. Mashobra case settled in June; hotel operated until October 2026.

risks_watch: Margin pressure: Q4 EBITDA only 1% growth as OFS mix rises and airport levy and wage code costs increase; watch for margin recovery in FY27.
Managed hotel project slippage (Trident Goa, Dehradun, Rishikesh and others); management says owners control timelines and delays are not significant, but 2027 pipeline looks thin.
Oberoi Grand Kolkata renovation: structural issues found, reopening target September 2026 still stated; any change would be updated to the board and investors.
Oberoi Rajgarh (Khajuraho) connectivity: only seasonal Delhi flights; no flights expected July-September unless IndiGo extends.
Geopolitical risk: West Asia war impact on foreign travel and occupancy; the company has not quantified the impact; March occupancy weakness may persist into Q1 FY27.
Supply risk in FY29-30 from new luxury keys in some micro-markets; management says the rate premium will be maintained rather than discounted.
500840|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and pipeline but cautious on near-term occupancy; management acknowledged a challenging year and avoided forward numbers, deferring several specifics (foreign mix, flight catering split, consolidated room revenue) to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: But that's not to undermine the fact that we had challenges in the year .
So, the full year occupancy for our own hotels was 76.8 or 77% for the year.
So overall, if you look at our investor update, we've almost spent 600 to 700 crores of CAPEX in the current year.
Foreign travel really picks up in October through to March , and with April being somewhat strong, maybe not as strong as the winter months, but still reasonable.

500840|2026-06.headline: EIH Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% to Rs 698 crore and PAT to Rs 120 crore, but EBITDA grew only to Rs 207 crore as margin fell on Rajgarh ramp-up and one-offs.
500840|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 15% YoY to Rs 698 crore (Rs 609 crore) and EBITDA rose to Rs 207 crore from Rs 195 crore, so margin compressed. Management attributed the gap to Oberoi Rajgarh ramp-up, about Rs 4 crore of extra marketing, IT/automation spend, power and fuel inflation from the West Asia conflict, and Rs 6-7.5 crore of renovation write-offs at Mumbai hotels. Growth was domestically led as foreign arrivals fell about 10% in Q1. Standalone numbers were stated to mirror consolidated. PAT of Rs 120 crore is not comparable with last year, which carried a Rs 110 crore Mashobra one-time impact.

financial_highlights.change: from Rs 195 crore YoY; margin about 29% as stated
not comparable; prior year had Rs 110 crore Mashobra one-time impact

segments.name: Oberoi brand (luxury)
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 8.2% vs luxury segment industry 13.2%; excluding Oberoi Rajgarh, RevPAR growth was 11.4%. Foreign-heavy mix was hit by West Asia conflict.

segments.name: Trident brand (upper upscale)
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 13.8% vs industry 9.2%; Mumbai TNP and BKC drove it, Trident RGI at 162 vs 155 last year.

segments.name: Flight catering (OFS)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 154 crore in Q1, driven by new domestic flights and direct international airline business; management said it was profitable and did not materially dilute margin.

segments.name: Oberoi Rajgarh (new, Khajuraho)
segments.commentary: Opened November 2025; in ramp-up, weighing on margins. Management expects about 3 years to stabilise and stronger winter months from October.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 business on books vs last year described as very positive; no full-year guidance given.
Industry expected to see ARR gains from limited supply and MICE events (BRICS, Aviation show) later in the year.
Foreign tourist arrivals expected to normalise in Q3 and Q4 FY27 if West Asia stabilises; Q2 foreign trend expected to remain weak.
Renovations to finish before October; no significant renovation in Q3 and Q4.
Oberoi Grand (Delhi/Kolkata-listed project in pipeline) expected to open September 2028 with 197 keys.

Shimla and Chandigarh showed the biggest RevPAR gains (base effect from Operation Sindoor); Jaipur fell on lower foreign arrivals; Hyderabad declined against the Miss World base.
Foreign guest arrivals were about 10% below last year in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Did flight catering mix and renovation, Rajgarh ramp-up drive the margin gap, and will these persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said renovations concentrate in lean months and Bombay renovations finish before October; Rajgarh should improve in winter. Flight catering was profitable and not a material margin drag.

qa_highlights.question: May and June RevPAR growth looked much higher than the quarter. Will that persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to forecast the full year; said Q2 business on books versus last year was very positive.

qa_highlights.question: Will large events like BRICS and the Aviation show boost RevPAR?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, large events have a ripple effect across cities, with Delhi and Mumbai benefiting from overseas visitors to Bengaluru's air show.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Kolkata Oberoi delayed and how firm is the new timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Heritage building restoration uncovered fire and structural safety work, plus a Kolkata construction halt after a fatal incident about two months ago; halt still in place pending building-by-building approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cost overrun on the Oberoi Grand from delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays add cost, the size depending on reasons, and the bigger impact is deferred revenue and profit from delayed market entry.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Mumbai outperformance continue, and what is foreign tourist trend in recent months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bombay market was strong and EIH beat it, but would not forecast 20% outperformance; Q2 foreign trend expected to stay weak.

qa_highlights.question: Rajgarh stabilisation timeline and winter outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3 years to stabilise for a leisure hotel, with winter months from October expected to do considerably better.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the base business margin fall after adjusting for Rajgarh and one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ex-Rajgarh margin was about 30.6% vs last year, with roughly Rs 9 crore YoY impact from power and fuel, Rs 4 crore marketing, IT and renovation costs. Management declined to disclose management fee income.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on Oberoi Rajgarh ramp-up; management guides about 3 years to stabilise and expects winter months from October to be considerably better.
Foreign arrivals were about 10% below last year in Q1 and management expects Q2 foreign trend to stay weak; normalisation in Q3-Q4 depends on West Asia stabilising.
Power and fuel costs rose due to the West Asia/Hormuz crisis; ex-Rajgarh impact about Rs 9 crore YoY, with cost pressure expected to persist.

Kolkata Oberoi timeline pushed to 2029 with construction halt still in place pending building-by-building approvals; Oberoi Grand opening Sept 2028 with management declining to give percentage completion.
Employee cost pressure from headcount, increments, labour code impact and working-hour reduction commitment; management declined to quantify Rajgarh revenue or management fee income.
