Answers on redevelopment selection and PTC were generic and qualitative.

503722|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose to a record Rs1,370 crore-scale year with EBITDA up 22.5% to Rs144 crore; FY27 guided to Rs1,450-1,500 crore.
503722|2026-03.overview: Banswara Syntex reported Q4 FY26 total income of Rs369.3 crore, with EBITDA up 46% YoY to Rs46 crore and PAT of Rs9.6 crore (up 87% YoY). For FY26, EBITDA was about Rs144 crore (margin near 11%) and PAT Rs28.4 crore (up 32.8%) after a one-time Rs9 crore labour code exceptional charge. Fabric and Garment grew, while Yarn volumes and revenue fell on labour shortages in spinning. Management guided to FY27 revenue of Rs1,450-1,500 crore and EBITDA margin of 10.5-11% over the medium term, with near-term margin pressure from raw material pass-through lag.

financial_highlights.value: Rs28.4 crore (after Rs9 crore one-time labour code expense)

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs456 crore a year earlier

financial_highlights.value: 20% on face value, total Rs3.42 crore

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs113 crore (vs Rs123 crore; management corrected the gap to Rs10 crore), FY26 Rs449 crore vs Rs460 crore (about -2%). Volume 46 lakh kg in Q4 and 194 lakh kg in FY26; utilisation 78% in Q4 and 77% for FY26. Realisations up about Rs30-35/kg.

segments.name: Fabrics
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs154 crore (vs Rs145 crore); FY26 record Rs569 crore, up 5%. Volume 62 lakh meters in Q4 and 230 lakh meters in FY26; utilisation 77% in Q4. Middle East exports affected.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs96 crore, up 40%; FY26 Rs324 crore, up 18%. Volume 11 lakh pieces in Q4 and 39 lakh pieces in FY26; FY26 utilisation 72% vs about 50% in FY25. Walmart added about Rs15 crore of Q4 revenue.

segments.name: Associate Tesca Textiles (40% stake)
segments.commentary: Management said Tesca had turnover of about Rs100 crore and PAT of about Rs10 crore, with Banswara's share about Rs4 crore. No plan to raise stake.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided to Rs1,450-1,500 crore, led by Fabric and Garment; FY26 was about Rs1,370 crore.
Management targets about 20% revenue growth in both Fabric and Garment in FY27; Garment division projects 18-20%.
EBITDA margin expected at 10.5-11% over the medium term; near-term margins may dip as raw material costs are passed on.
FY27 capex planned at Rs135-140 crore (an analyst cited Rs130-150 crore); Garment capex only Rs3-5 crore.
Long-term debt expected to rise in FY27 on planned capex and reduce from FY28 onwards; no reduction in total borrowings this year.
Management expects H2 FY27 growth to exceed H1; Garment momentum to improve from Q2 after a subdued Q1.
capex_capacity: Yarn and Fabric capacity was reshaped toward finer counts, Siro Compact yarn (about 200 tons per month) and worsted finishing machines; management says installed capacity fell YoY partly due to mix shift.
Garment capacity: about 70,000 pieces per month available vs 40,000-50,000 jackets used; could go to 80,000 with long runs.
Surat SEZ garment capacity (about 40,000-50,000 jackets and about 100,000 pants) awaits approval; timeline not given, file under process with Industries Commissionerate and Kandla SEZ.
Management said Garment expansion could start mid-year (Q2/Q3 FY27) and that Rs2,000 crore revenue is possible without significant capex, with no firm timeline.
Capex items: zero water discharge project, a 132 KVA power line application, and other infrastructure and sustainability spend.
demand_pricing: Polyester raw material costs up about 25% due to the Middle East conflict; yarn prices raised but not fully passed on.
Wool prices rose sharply, from Australia and China; management says customers take 6 months to 1 year to accept new prices.
Rupee depreciation of about 6-7% helped export realisations without price increases.
Walmart added as a Garment customer; JC Penney (Fabric) and Mango (Garment) already customers; Celio and Marks & Spencer cited as large relationships.
Middle East exposure about Rs100 crore; Rs8-9 crore of Q4 product could not ship on time; management expects Rs10-20 crore lower sales to the region in FY27.
US demand improving; company says it is more competitive than China in spun-synthetic segment.
D2C brand One Mile averages about Rs15 lakh per month; fundraising planned once it reaches about Rs1 crore per month.

qa_highlights.question: Have new export clients been added, such as Walmart?
qa_highlights.answer: Walmart is a new addition; it contributed about Rs15 crore of Q4 Garment revenue. Management aims for 20% growth in Garment and Fabric next year and sees no need for many more large clients.

qa_highlights.question: Why did installed capacity fall YoY despite investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Finer counts and worsted machines lower kg output; capacity is planned around realistic labour availability. Management says labour shortages persist into May.

qa_highlights.question: Is the labour shortage transient or structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says automation is not viable given many SKUs; focus is on scaling winning products and shifting from made-to-order to predictive analytics planning.

qa_highlights.question: How will the borrowings be reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said no reduction in FY27 as long-term debt rises on capex; long-term debt to reduce from FY28 on 5-7 year loan tenures. Working capital rise is linked to customer ready inventory; inventory above 90 days is watched.

qa_highlights.question: What are segment-wise margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give exact segment margins due to internal transfers (about 33% of yarn and 25% of fabric is internal). Segment margins are said to be close to company level; Garment was previously at breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East impact and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said polyester costs rose about 25%; price increases partly accepted, and export pricing benefited from rupee weakness. Middle East exposure is about Rs100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will FTAs (UK, EU) matter, and can Rs1,800 crore be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: UK FTA expected around September and EU by December end per management, with no certainty. Management hopes for Rs1,800 crore in the year after FY27 and is willing to accept 11% EBITDA to keep 20% growth.

risks_watch: Labour shortages in spinning and garments, particularly in April to June, could keep Yarn utilisation at 77-78%.
Raw material cost pass-through lag of 6 to 12 months may compress margins in H1 FY27.
Middle East logistics and demand; Rs10-20 crore lower sales to the region expected in FY27.
Surat SEZ approval timing is uncertain, and no firm Garment capacity expansion date was given.
Net debt rose to Rs483 crore; the long-term debt reduction only starts from FY28, while FY27 capex is Rs135-140 crore.
FTA benefits (UK, EU) are not yet certain; Q1 FY27 Garment orders expected to be subdued.
503722|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on Garment growth and export wins, but cautious on near-term margins, Q1 FY27 demand, and the Middle East. Management avoided firm timelines on Surat SEZ, FTAs and the Rs2,000 crore revenue target, and declined to give segment margins.
key_quotes: So, we are happy even if we get 11% EBITDA, but we grow 20% for this present financial year because we do not want to stifle the growth by jacking up the prices to an extent where the customers shy away.
Walmart has been definitely a new addition, and we saw the impact of that happening in our quarter four results in the Garment division, where we achieved INR96 crores turnover.
Near-term margins may go down as the raw material costs are being passed on.

503722|2026-06.headline: Banswara Syntex Q1 FY27 total income rose 4.1% to INR322.4 crores with PAT of INR4.4 crores versus a loss of INR1.4 crores; management reiterates FY27 revenue of INR1,450–1,500 crores.
503722|2026-06.overview: Total income grew 4.1% YoY to INR322.4 crores and EBITDA was INR29.5 crores (about 9% margin), with PAT of INR4.4 crores against a loss a year earlier. Fabric grew 25% YoY while yarn and garment revenues fell, mainly on labour shortages in spinning, higher internal yarn consumption and garment dispatches delayed by West Asia logistics. Management kept FY27 guidance of about INR1,500 crores revenue and 12% EBITDA, relying on a garment order book booked through November/December and a recovery in H2. Analysts pressed hard on the low top-line growth over a decade and on the pace of garment capacity additions.

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Revenue INR96 crores (vs INR110 crores YoY); sales volume 36 lakh kg at 70% capacity utilisation. Higher internal transfers to fabric and garments reduced external sales; labour shortage cut output.

segments.name: Fabric
segments.commentary: Revenue INR147 crores (+25% YoY); volume 59 lakh meters (+18% YoY) at 80% utilisation. Growth driven by value-added bi-stretch and wool blends; Q1 margin was in line with the 12–14% target. Roughly 50:50 export and domestic.

segments.name: Garment
segments.commentary: Revenue INR69 crores (vs INR75 crores YoY); 8 lakh pieces at 69% utilisation. West Asia logistics delayed dispatches; margin below target (8–10% expected) due to container availability. About 60% export, 40% domestic.

segments.name: Jackets (within garment)
segments.commentary: Q1 closed at about 135,000 jackets, soft demand. Run rate now upwards of 75,000 a month; FY27 target 800,000–900,000 jackets versus about 600,000 a year on average.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR1,450–1,500 crores maintained; management expects garment at about INR100 crores per quarter for the next three quarters and about INR375–380 crores for the year plus export incentives.
Consolidated EBITDA target of about 12% for FY27 versus 9% in Q1; segment targets: fabric 12–14%, garment 8–10%, yarn 8–10%.
Yarn expected to normalise progressively as labour availability improves; management expects visible improvement from Q2.
Surat facility targeted for DTA use by November/December 2026 and operations from April 2027; main impact in FY28. Restart seen adding about INR200 crores of runway for about INR50 crores investment.
Garment EU operationalisation with Mango, Celio and C&A targeted by end-December 2026/early January 2027.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR140 crores planned and sanctioned for this year across fabric, garment and common infrastructure.
Management targets about 20–25% garment expansion and about 20% fabric expansion in FY28, with a further 20% in FY28 as stated; yarn to be maintained or marginally grown.
Over the last three years, about INR350 crores invested: about INR150 crores in fabric and about INR130 crores in yarn; management said the modernisation phase is complete.
Surat facility shut to move into DTA; Daman capacity to be fully utilised this year.
demand_pricing: Garment order book fully booked through November and into December; fabric order book shows orders up to November end.
Demand healthy in US and domestic markets; Europe and Middle East softer in fabric.
India-UK FTA effective 15 July 2026; UK fabric exposure about INR70–80 crores a year; UK garment about INR20–25 crores, targeted to double to at least INR50 crores next year.
Two EU anchor garment customers (Mango and Celio) about INR100 crores of revenue; C&A onboarded with trial orders; new UK customers Haggar and NEXT added in fabric.
Domestic yarn realisations improved, partly offsetting lower volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export contribution for fabric and garments, and what are the jacket volumes and segment margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall exports 48%; fabric and garment together about 70% of export turnover. Jackets: about 600,000 a year average, FY27 expected 800,000–900,000. Segment margin targets given (fabric 12–14%, garment and yarn 8–10%).

qa_highlights.question: Why is the sequential drop so sharp in garment and yarn, and is the garment shortfall shipment timing or lost demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 weakness to a weak autumn/winter export season and seasonal domestic lull, plus delayed shipments. July garment sales were on target at about INR30 crores, with quarterly run-rate expected to reach about INR100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 12% EBITDA for FY27 on INR1,500 crores revenue; Q1 was 9%, with the rest expected to average out to 12% over the remaining three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue growth muted despite about INR500 crores of capex over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yarn capacity was under-used because of labour issues and the investments are now expected to lift top line and bottom line; fabric growth of about 20% a year is expected from its investments.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company different this decade, given flat revenue since FY19 and weak margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the dissolution of the French JV for lost sales a decade ago, said product mix is much better, and cited import substitution of Chinese goods and FTAs. Garment export share rose from about 20% to about 60%, with a target of 70%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any update on the Surat facility?
qa_highlights.answer: GIDC approvals and no-objection certificate received; customs duty clearance and SEZ debonding pending, expected within 3–5 months. Restart would involve fresh machinery, adding about INR200 crores of capacity for about INR50 crores.

risks_watch: Garment margin recovery (targeted 8–10%) depends on export mix and on timely container availability; Q1 garment EBITDA fell short.
Yarn utilisation (70% in Q1) depends on labour availability; labour shortages recur each festival and marriage season.
FY27 guidance needs about INR1,000 crores or more of revenue in Q2–Q4 at the stated quarterly run rate, with H2 weighted delivery.
Europe and Middle East fabric demand softer; West Asia logistics disruptions continue to delay shipments.
Surat restart timelines (DTA by Nov/Dec 2026, operations April 2027) and capex of about INR140 crores; benefits seen mainly in FY28.
Debt rising to about INR500 crores per analyst estimate; past capex has not yet translated into revenue growth.

segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 70% of consolidated EBITDA. Medium and long-term PPAs cover over 380 MW of 710 MW saleable capacity; about 330 MW of these are at SKS, at INR 5-6/unit. Small hydro output was hit by the delayed monsoon, and the company said it is roughly 1% below last year.

segments.name: Sikkim 113 MW hydro
segments.commentary: Shut from 18 June to 5 July 2026 after a transmission tower collapsed in heavy rain and landslide. Management said it is now running at full capacity, with about 5 days of July generation lost and the restoration cost covered by insurance apart from a minimal excess.

segments.name: Steel and ferro alloys (metals)
segments.commentary: Consolidated revenue fell QoQ on planned outages: a 30 MW captive unit replacement at Raipur (trial run now, commercial operation expected mid-August), a 23-day Vizag captive shutdown, and a 53-day Siltara ferro alloy furnace refurbishment. segments.name: Mineral wool (new)

Q2 expected to be better than Q1, driven by hydro generation and higher power prices. July IEX prices were about INR 5/unit versus INR 4.19-4.20 a year earlier.
FY27 IPP generation expected to exceed last year's 415 crore units, with the captive plant utilisation also improving after the 30 MW unit restarts.
Steel and ferro alloy prices expected to remain stable. Ferro alloy margins may firm as raw material prices soften; steel may rise after a West Asia settlement and after monsoon.
Real power tariffs expected at INR 5-6/unit for the year, rising with inflation and peak demand, especially for hydro.

Full-year FY27 pipeline: 50 MW captive solar expected by end of next quarter (after a railway right-of-way delay); 74 MW Chhattisgarh small hydro approvals on schedule; Arunachal 66 MW hydro detailed engineering to begin this year.

SKS 600 MW to 1,200 MW expansion: TOR submission in about 3 months, then public hearing and 6-8 months for EC, then 6-8 months to appoint a consultant. The new unit is targeted for FY31 completion (per management, asked on the last call).
capex_capacity: SKS thermal expansion from 600 MW to 1,200 MW is awaiting regulatory approval, and the company describes the brownfield project as capital-efficient, using existing land, water and evacuation infrastructure.
Waste heat recovery power plant at Vizag, about INR 300 cr, for energy efficiency; all expansion projects funded through internal accruals.

Coal mining: Shahpur West commissioning before end-FY27; Bartunga Hill by end of next financial year; Gare Palma IV/5, IV/7 and Senduri approvals in progress. Management said the Gare Palma IV/7 expansion from 1.8 Mt to 5 Mt is not in the immediate plan as new higher-grade mines take priority.
Shahpur West coal is high grade and is destined for sponge iron and ferro alloy plants, not the power plants.
Plans to quadruple mining capacity and double energy generation capacity, per management.
demand_pricing: India power generation grew 9.4% YoY to about 523 BU in the quarter; thermal grew 7.5%; solar generation rose about 45%; small hydro fell about 30% and large hydro about 7%.
Day-ahead market averaged INR 3.85/unit vs INR 3.92 a year earlier, but July prices rose to about INR 5/unit from INR 4.19. Management said peak hours have lengthened from 5 to 8-10 hours.
Indian coal index for June 2026 was about 21% above June 2025 and about 11% above March 2026.

504903|2026-03.headline: Rathi Steel FY26 total income rose ~41.7% to INR716 crore; Q4 PAT INR7.45 crore at 3% margin, with mills still only ~51-52% utilised.
504903|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 total income of about INR716 crore (+41.7% YoY), EBITDA of INR28.9 crore (+18.8%) and PAT of INR12.87 crore (+39.24%, excluding prior-year exceptional items). Q4 total income was INR244.57 crore (+63.3% YoY, +52.7% QoQ), EBITDA INR9.89 crore (+22% YoY, +54% QoQ) and PAT INR7.45 crore, with PAT margin of about 3%. segments.name: Steel melting shop (SMS)
segments.commentary: Capacity ~85,000 tons per annum, utilisation ~53% in FY26 (50-52% cited in opening remarks); about 40-45% backward integrated. Target is ~80% utilisation.

segments.name: Stainless steel vs TMT revenue mix
segments.commentary: Management estimated ~60% of FY26 revenue from B2B (mainly stainless) and ~40% from TMT bars, an approximate figure.

guidance_outlook: Rolling mill utilisation targeted at ~65-70% this year (fallback ~60-65%), up from ~51%.
Steel melting shop utilisation to move from ~50-52% towards ~80%.

Direct charging on the TMT mill expected to save ~INR3,000-4,000 per ton, or ~6-7% of TMT selling price including yield benefits, on the directly charged volume.
Capex of ~INR20 crore+ a year expected to continue for a few years, mainly replacement and debottlenecking; SMS expansion under study subject to approvals.
Refinancing talks under way with the existing lender at 16% cost of borrowing, with new lenders being explored at lower rates.
capex_capacity: Melting capacity ~85,000 tpa and rolling ~2,00,000 tpa at a ~12.5-acre NCR (Ghaziabad) site; FY26 utilisation ~51-52% for both divisions.
FY26 capex of INR20 crore+, mostly replacement and debottlenecking; the TMT restart cost ~INR5-7 crore in FY25.
Direct charging being implemented on the TMT mill, following its success in stainless wire rod.
SMS capacity expansion being evaluated at costs well below industry benchmarks; a larger melting unit is under consideration subject to demand visibility and statutory clearances.
Rooftop solar feasibility under study, indicatively 1-2 MW; open-access renewable power is over one-fourth of total power consumption.
demand_pricing: Management says domestic steel demand is healthy, with TMT and rebar pricing recovering after a prolonged soft patch.

Stainless steel pricing comes under pressure above a certain utilisation level; the company is shifting to a more balanced product mix to reduce reliance on any one category.
TMT sold mainly in NCR because freight limits longer-distance sales; stainless also sold in other states.

Single-lender dependence at 16% cost of borrowing; refinancing outcome is pending.
Unquantified GST input-credit disputes with adjudication and stays still pending.

Slow utilisation ramp (51% to 65-70% target) and the 550D premium-grade product push.
Plant ageing; ongoing replacement capex needed.

504973|2026-06.headline: Chola MS Q1 FY27 combined ratio rose to 120.4% with GWP up 6.7% to Rs 2,130 crore and motor OD loss ratio still elevated.
504973|2026-06.overview: Chola MS (general insurance arm of Cholamandalam Financial Holdings) reported GDPI of Rs 1,860 crore (+2.6% YoY) and GWP of Rs 2,130 crore (+6.7%), below management's expectations. Claims ratio rose to 85.6% (vs 81.3%) and combined ratio to 120.4%, driven by motor reserve strengthening, elevated motor OD claims and a large fire loss (Rs 12.4 crore net). Profit before tax was Rs 116 crore on operating profit of Rs 71 crore. Management said the OD loss ratio is unacceptable and targets a high-70s level first, while the Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment remains unprovided pending review.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Largest line (~70% of book per management); portfolio grew ~5.7% in Q1, mainly commercial vehicles. Mix: private cars 48%, two-wheelers ~9.5%, commercial vehicles ~42.5%. Motor combined ratio 128% in FY26 vs 123% in FY25; OD loss ratio now 80-86% range per analyst framing, not disputed by management.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: Portfolio declined 8.6% in Q1 vs industry fire decline of ~28%; Chola MS fire decline limited to 15.5%. Growth in marine, engineering and liability.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Growth moderate; decline driven by pricing corrections in PSU bank group platform and migration of business to retail platform. Claims settled within 30 days for 99%; NPS 73. Health is being rebuilt from the ground up.

guidance_outlook: OD loss ratio near-term target: bring it to high-70s, then progressively to mid-70s; management said it expects below 80% over time, with a couple of quarters needed for measures to show results.

Corrective measures across motor (new vs renewal mix, NCB focus, ACS control, repair vs replacement analysis) and health (product redesign, pricing revisions, SME push) expected to become visible over coming quarters.
Expects greater property pricing discipline after June NATCAT events; reinsurance market correction more likely at next renewal cycle.
Ind AS / IFRS transition effective April 1, 2027 (one-year IRDAI forbearance granted); no profitability impact estimate yet, preliminary observations possibly next quarter.
Industry CAT loss estimate of Rs 3,000-4,000 crore from multiple events in Gujarat, Assam, Jamshedpur and Maharashtra.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance capacity for fire and engineering secured at start of FY27, described as comparable to leading private players.
Motor issuance platform rolled out across bank channel; workflow enhancements under way in motor claims.
Health network exceeds 13,000 hospitals via PSU bank retail health partnerships.
Readiness work ongoing for Ind AS, Risk-Based Capital (RBC) framework and DPDP requirements.
demand_pricing: Industry GI premium growth ~8.3% in Q1 vs 8.9% a year earlier; motor and health led growth, fire under severe pricing pressure.
Industry combined ratio ~117.8% in FY26 vs 112.6% FY25; Chola MS 115.2% FY26 vs 110% FY25.
Motor TP is tariff-based; premiums do not keep pace with claims inflation and court award trends.
Inward reinsurance growth cited as a driver of GWP outpacing GDPI; sources are commercial-lines participation and group health.
GIFT City reinsurers cited as contributing to soft commercial-lines pricing; management expects limited sustainable lead-line capacity from them.

qa_highlights.question: Has any additional motor TP provision been made for the Supreme Court homemaker judgment, and what is the path for motor OD loss ratio?

OD loss ratio not accepted as the new normal; immediate target is high-70s, then mid-70s over time. Management said the 84.4% motor figure cited by analyst was not confirmed in the call, and said OD loss ratio below 80% is achievable over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did retail and group health decline when the industry is growing strongly?

qa_highlights.question: Is the claims ratio rise from new book or from reserve provisioning?

505010|2026-03.headline: Automotive Axles Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 18% QoQ to INR6,643 million, with PAT margin steady at 8%; FY26 revenue INR21,777 million (+5%).
505010|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR6,643 million, up about 18% QoQ and 18.5-18.7% YoY, with EBITDA of INR825 million (12.4%) and PAT of INR539 million (8%), matching Q4 FY25's PAT margin. 505010|2026-06.headline: Automotive Axles Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin rose to 13.6% (from 12.4% QoQ) on revenue of Rs 5,168 mn and PAT of Rs 455 mn.
505010|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 5,168 million, EBITDA of Rs 702 million (about 13.6%), and profit for the year of Rs 455 million (about 8.7%, EPS about Rs 30). Management described EBITDA as one of the highest margins the company has achieved, helped by mix, a one-off, and lower employee costs versus the high-volume Q4. Management now sees the FY27 M&HCV industry down 5-10% versus last year, against an earlier 15-20% decline assumption, with Q4 expected to be a peak quarter. Capacity expansion (Phase-1 and Phase-1(a)) is about 40% complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue growth since FY24 lagged the order wins of about INR4,000 crore, and were there internal factors?

qa_highlights.question: Why did forging Q1 growth lag and why has the forging guidance come down from earlier expectations of around INR400 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 hit by manpower shortages, LPG price spikes, lower BMW and GKN schedules and some orders taking time to move into execution; productivity dipped. Loss of Meritor business (INR30-40 crores p.a.) due to US tariffs is a key reason. Management said July was better than June and cited a INR500 crores, 5-year order book (about INR100 crores p.a.).

qa_highlights.question: Why did Marelli margins fall in Q1, and which segment will grow fastest in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower other income plus new manpower and shared rental costs; management expects margins to recover by year-end. Marelli is expected to grow 30-40% in FY27, forging about 20%, gaskets about 16-17%, and Talbros Marugo 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Is data-centre gasket margin different from the rest of the gasket business, and what is the EV revenue mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Same gasket product sold for a new application, with pricing unchanged; margins not split out. EV-related supply was INR12.5 crores in Q1 (about 3.27% of sales) versus INR10 crores in Q4 FY26 and INR9 crores a year ago; management targets around 5% in 2 years and a minimum of 5% over 5 years. JLR rubber EV components worth INR15-20 crores p.a. start in Q1/Q2 CY27.

risks_watch: Pass-through of steel, aluminium and labour inflation from OEMs has not yet happened; FY27 margin guide of about 17-17.5% depends on it.
Forging recovery depends on European demand, execution of the INR500 crores order book, and resolution of manpower and productivity issues; Q1 growth was only 4%.
Marelli JV: stake transaction still pending court proceedings with update expected by end-September; Q1 JV margin dip to be reversed by year-end.
Data-centre revenue (about 5% of gasket revenue) is concentrated in a single customer, Cummins, and depends on engine orders.
Lost Meritor business (INR30-40 crores p.a.) and Cummins America ramp-up timing (slow starter) could weigh on the forging and gasket revenue trajectory.
Export share at about 25% against a 35% FY28 target; EV share at 3.27% of sales against a 5% goal.
key_quotes: Talbros has delivered yet another record quarter, achieving its highest ever quarterly revenue and surpassing the previous high recorded in quarter 4 of '26.
But we are very positive that we will get these increases from the OEMs in the coming quarters.
We are pretty much single source to Cummins for this particular engine component.
Plus, we are supplying bushes to BMW of EV vehicles, where sale has gone up a little bit there.
505160|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on growth, order wins and the record quarter, but cautious on margins, which it says are under temporary inflation pressure. On forging and Marelli it was more guarded, with several answers deferred to later updates such as the end-September Marelli stake update.

505196|2026-06.headline: TIL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 86% YoY to INR117.1 crore, with EBITDA margin at 6.2% (vs 1.5%) and PAT at negative INR5.5 crore.
505196|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR117.1 crore included Tulip Compression (TCPL) only from 8 May to 30 June 2026, so the quarter is a partial-period read. Standalone revenue grew 25% YoY to INR78.6 crore, with EBITDA up to INR3.4 crore (4.3% margin vs 1.5%), but standalone PAT was negative INR7.2 crore. Management flagged that blended margins will stay volatile for the next six to eight quarters because of product mix and supply-chain localisation, and gave no near-term margin guidance. The company delivered nine ReachStackers and reported a current order book of INR211 crore against a pipeline of about INR373 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.1 crore (1.5%) in Q1 FY26; 9.6% in Q4 FY26 per analyst
+223% YoY vs INR1.1 crore; margin up from 1.5%

segments.name: Standalone TIL (cranes, material handling, defence)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR78.6 crore (+25% YoY), EBITDA margin 4.3%. Management said FY26 turnover was about 50% defence. Nine ReachStackers delivered in the quarter.

segments.name: Tulip Compression (TCPL)
segments.commentary: Consolidated from 8 May 2026 (part period). Order book INR328 crore, pipeline INR117 crore. FY26 revenue about INR278 crore per management. Management's medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin view is 14-15%.

segments.name: Aftermarket / services
segments.commentary: FY26 aftermarket about INR56 crore. Management's long-term aim is 40-45% of revenue; parts margins 25-35%, service margins slightly better.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a significant jump in FY27 turnover, but gave no numeric revenue guidance. Analyst's INR200 crore+ scenario was not confirmed.
Management expects no EBITDA margin harmonisation for the next six to eight quarters; medium-to-long-term TIL standalone EBITDA target 15-16%, timing 3-7 years.
Five-to-seven-year ambition to roughly triple turnover; no significant capex needed up to about INR700-750 crore turnover, beyond bridging capex of INR5-10 crore.
Debtor days target 60-75 days maximum; long-term aftermarket share target 40-45% of revenue.
Board approved up to INR50 crore equity infusion into Tulip; commitment to raise stake to 74% over a few years.
CarryKing 515 launch hoped for Q4 FY27, worst case Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: Kharagpur plant loaded only 30-35% with about 150 acres free; Kamarhati plant is old and fully loaded.
Bridging capex of INR5-10 crore per instance, mainly for the old Kamarhati plant.
Target to localise 75-80% in every product and above 90% overall, with Cummins engines for ReachStacker a key dependency.
Pick and carry crane (CarryKing 515) launch targeted Q4 FY27 with 520 configuration to follow.
demand_pricing: ReachStacker market share 38-40% after a comeback; CONCOR order described as one-time, first such order since 2014-15.
Rough terrain crane market share about 50%+; truck crane share now below 5% from over 95% a decade ago, lost to Chinese competition.
Order delivery timelines range from 60-90 days (retail ReachStacker) to 6-9 months (defence), with the bulk of the order book typically exhausted within nine months.
Chinese competitors have pricing and credit advantages; management said TIL will not compete on extended credit terms.
Tulip's market share is about one-third in India in a three-player market; clients include city gas distributors such as IGL, MNGL and IGL-type CGD operators.

qa_highlights.question: ReachStacker market share, competitors and whether the Q1 order is CONCOR.
qa_highlights.answer: Share is 38-40%, and the CONCOR order is one-time. Management expects ReachStacker sales to scale to a sizable number this year via retail and niche buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Can the current order book deliver more than INR200 crore this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the figure. It said the order book is exhausted over about nine months and new orders will add to it, and expects a significant jump in turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall from Q4 to Q1, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product mix and localisation drive volatility; Q4 had Air Force cranes and ReachStackers. No harmonised margin for six to eight quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Tulip's business, revenue, margin, and plans to raise stake.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 14-15% medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin, equity infusion up to INR50 crore, and a 74% stake target over a few years. Export to Nigeria has just begun.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtor days.
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors rose at end-FY26 due to a large IAF missile crane order in late March. Target is 60-75 days; TIL is now an MSME, which should speed customer payments.

qa_highlights.question: Chinese competition and pricing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TIL competes on reliability, durability, and aftermarket uptime commitments, not on credit terms.

risks_watch: Working capital and debt: management called the working capital cycle stressed; debtor days and debt reduction are the key items to track.
Margin volatility: EBITDA margins depend on product mix, and management gave no margin guidance for six to eight quarters.
Supply-chain dependence: localisation of European and US inputs (Cummins engines, gearboxes) depends on OEM and defence approvals and could take several quarters.
Execution: converting the INR211 crore standalone order book and the INR328 crore TCPL order book on time; the FY26 shortfall was attributed to geopolitics and logistics.
Governance and bandwidth: the Chairman plans to devote 40-50% of his time to TIL from next quarter, versus about 60% needed, and the Gainwell merger question was left open.
Tulip integration and TCPL full-quarter contribution in Q2 FY27.
505196|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term vision (tripling turnover, 15-16% margins, aftermarket targets) but cautious and explicit on near-term margins, which it said will not stabilise for six to eight quarters. It was candid on the stressed working capital cycle and declined to quantify FY27 revenue or Tulip profit projections.
key_quotes: Hence, we are looking at a few more quarters before we are really able to fix the margins.
You're right, working capital cycle at this stage in TIL looks stressed.

505200|2026-03.headline: Eicher Motors Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue INR8,280.6 mn? No: Q4 consolidated revenue INR6,080 crore? Transcript-stated EML Q4 revenue INR6,080, PAT INR1,520.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue (EML, as stated by Govind)
Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue (VECV, as stated by Srinivas)

segments.name: Royal Enfield (motorcycles)
segments.commentary: FY26 domestic motorcycle sales rose 23% to 1.1 million units; exports grew 20% to 120,634 units. Record FY26 total of 1.227 million motorcycles, with Brazil up 71% and now the largest international market. Apparel grew 21%, Genuine Motorcycle Accessories rose 32%, and spare parts grew 18%.

segments.name: VECV (commercial vehicles)
segments.commentary: FY26 volumes of 103,404 units, up 15%. Heavy-duty truck volumes were 25,155 with market share up to 9.1% from 8.4%... (stated as 14.1% growth with share improving to 9.1%); LMD trucks 46,195; buses 18,651; exports up 33.9% to 6,933 units; spare parts revenue up 13.9% to INR3,045.5 crore.

segments.name: Volvo Financial Services JV (proposed)
segments.commentary: Proposed 50:50 JV with Volvo Group for financing, leasing and other services, with EML investing up to INR750 crore for a 50% stake; the target company has assets under management of INR1,806 crore and has been operating for 10 years.

guidance_outlook: Management does not normally give numeric forward guidance; said the company is geared for a growth-led FY27.
Domestic motorcycle inquiry levels up 23% vs the previous period; booking rates at 7-8 days in May; bookings for 2025 vehicles described as strong.
Production capacity to be raised from 1.4 million to 1.6 million motorcycles per year by June-July 2026 via the 500 per day module, ahead of festive season.
Cheyyar brownfield expansion (INR958 crore capex) to add 2 million units of annual capacity by Q2 FY28.
Q1 FY27 material-cost headwind of 3% to 3.5% of material costs; 50% expected to be recovered via pricing and the rest via austerity and engineering savings, with projects kicking in by July-August.
Greenfield facility in Andhra Pradesh on 261 acres signed with the state government; typical 24-30 month window to become fully operational.
Medium-term: management expects the VECV trajectory to be upward; India's long-term drivers cited as infrastructure, logistics, e-commerce and cleaner mobility.
capex_capacity: Cheyyar (Tamil Nadu) brownfield expansion approved in February at INR958 crore, adding capacity from 1.6 million to 2 million units per year, targeted by Q2 FY28.
Current capacity of 1.4 million motorcycles per year, with a 500 per day module adding capacity to 1.6 million by June-July 2026.
Andhra Pradesh greenfield: 261 acres signed; MoU with state government; capacity to be planned beyond 2 million units.
JV investment capacity: up to INR750 crore for 50% of Volvo financing JV; target company net worth INR500 crore; management said it is adequately capitalised for the medium term.
Cheyyar land acquisition of 65 acres already in hand.
demand_pricing: Industry 250-750cc: management said FY26 domestic category sold 1.11 million motorcycles, up 23%; Q4 sales of 1.04 million, up 57% (as stated).
Inquiry levels up 23% vs previous period; no structural correction in demand per management.
Q4 price increase of 1.75% in April; Q4 margin pressure of 90 bps from costs, with 70 bps blended price increase taken in January and 20 bps offset by cost reduction and mix.
Premiumisation continuing; first-time buyers rising, with 30% of consumers under 25 years of age; GST reduction cited as a helper.
Europe continued to degrow; US tariff issues described as settled; US about 3% of total business.
VECV: entire FY26 broad-based growth; EV Pro X trucks delivered 2,452, incl. 726 EVs. Pro X named Debutant of the Year at Apollo CV Awards.
Supply disruptions in April-May from elections, manpower availability, LPG shortages and power issues described as temporary, lasting 1-2 weeks, with deliveries restarting.
Mid-size bike CAGR and inquiry momentum cited; no quantified category growth number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 retail outlook for the mid-size motorcycle category, and what are the expansion plans given thin dealer inventories?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 industry sales were 1.11 million, up 23%, with no structural demand correction; bookings are 7-8 days, temporary supply issues are expected to clear in a week to 10 days, and capacity is going to 1.6 million units by June-July with the Cheyyar expansion by Q2 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 3-3.5% material cost headwind is being passed on through pricing, and how much is being offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 50% of the 3-3.5% material cost headwind is recovered through the 1.75% April price increase, with the remaining 50% addressed through austerity measures and engineering savings; the Q4 margin hit was 90 bps, of which 70 bps was recovered in January pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Volvo financing JV see profit benefits and will it be a capital-hungry business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the JV will run independently with its own risk profile and that EML will invest up to INR750 crore for 50%; the target has INR1,806 crore AUM; management expects to grow AUM to INR9,000-10,000 crore over 5 years with no hurry to scale.

qa_highlights.question: What are the product pipeline and timelines, including the Bullet 650 and any plans below 350cc?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the project timelines shown at EICMA are on track; the Bullet 650 dispatch has started and the S6 was shown; the company focuses on 250-750cc, with platforms at 350cc, 450cc and 650cc.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the Andhra Pradesh greenfield plant and its capacity ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the land MoU was signed this week, with the 261-acre parcel to be acquired; a plant is typically 24-30 months from land to full operation; no greenfield capacity timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MHCV outlook and how are fuel price hikes and labour shortages affecting demand?
qa_highlights.answer: VECV management said it took about 2% price increases from 1 April, with pass-through lagging due to time-bound transporter contracts; labour and LPG disruptions lasted 2-3 weeks and supply is improving.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation: 3-3.5% material cost headwind in Q1 FY27 from the geopolitical situation, with only 50% expected to be recovered through pricing; watch Q1 gross margin.
Supply chain: elections, LPG availability, power issues and migrant labour movement disrupted production and deliveries in April-May; management expects normalisation within 1-2 weeks.
Fuel price hikes may hit transporter economics and the CV secondary market; VECV's pass-through is lagged by time-bound contracts.
Europe continued to degrow due to pre-registration effects of OBD2B, delaying billing; US tariff matters described as settled but still a drag.
Volvo financing JV: capital commitment of up to INR750 crore and dependence on a new business with a longer-term payoff.
Greenfield Andhra Pradesh plant: no timeline given beyond the 24-30 month window; the Cheyyar 2 million capacity target is set for Q2 FY28.
Replacement cycle yet to kick in; the digital platform's traction is slightly better but from a low base.
Q1 FY27 volume tracking to 1.6 million capacity by June-July; watch whether the capacity ramp meets festive-season demand.

505200|2026-06.headline: Eicher Motors Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% to INR 6,632 crore with record Royal Enfield volumes of 332,940 units.
505200|2026-06.overview: Eicher Motors posted its best-ever Q1 with consolidated revenue of INR 6,632 crore (up 32% YoY), EBITDA of INR 1,591 crore and PAT of INR 1,463 crore (up 21%). Royal Enfield sold a record 332,940 motorcycles (up from 261,326), and VECV recorded its highest-ever Q1 sales of 24,815 units (up 14.8%). Management flagged a tight dealer inventory of 10-12 days ahead of festive season, with capacity ramp-up at Cheyyar and a greenfield Tada (Andhra Pradesh) plant approved. Commodity inflation of 4-4.5% of costs was partly offset by price hikes and value engineering, and softening was noted.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1,203 crore in Q1 FY26 (highest ever)
+21% YoY from INR 1,205 crore; prior year included INR 168 crore share of VECV profit
vs INR 511 crore YoY; margin 8.4% vs 9.2%
1.2% price hikes, 1% international mix, 0.4% currency, 0.6% allied business; offset by lower value

financial_highlights.value: Above INR 1,000 crore, about 15.3% of revenue

financial_highlights.change: INR 30 crore timing (Q4 ad campaign and launches) plus INR 22 crore marketing control

segments.name: Royal Enfield (India)
segments.commentary: 301,174 motorcycles sold in India; management cites about 32% volume growth and 350cc models (Classic, Bullet, Hunter, Meteor) up about 34% YoY. 450cc and 650cc models are back to pre-GST price levels, with Guerrilla 450 at about 2,400-2,500 units per month and 650cc twins at about 4,000-4,200 per month.

segments.name: Royal Enfield (International)
segments.commentary: Global volume 31,766 motorcycles; Brazil is the largest overseas market (about every fourth exported motorcycle), with a planned CKD facility. Europe remains in a market adjustment phase; US shows early green shoots after a tariff cut.

segments.name: Flying Flea (EV)
segments.commentary: Flying Flea C6 launched and deliveries started this quarter; about 100+ units delivered in two months, with Bengaluru expansion to 10 touchpoints and about 6 further cities planned.

segments.name: VECV (commercial vehicles)
segments.commentary: Total 24,815 units (up 14.8%); Eicher heavy-duty 5,275 units (up 15.2%, 8.8% share); light and medium-duty 9,993 units; Eicher buses 6,126 units; Volvo trucks and buses record 598 units; exports 1,450 units (up 14.7%); spares sales INR 931.3 crore (up 15.3%).

segments.name: Allied / aftermarket
segments.commentary: Allied businesses about 15% of revenue; about 9 lakh service job cards per month (up about 20% YoY); accessories and apparel growing above 30%, with accessory attach rate at about 87% per management.

guidance_outlook: Management expects growth momentum to continue; no formal numerical guidance given. Commodity outlook not quantified because the situation is described as volatile.
Royal Enfield Cheyyar brownfield (INR 958 crore announced in Feb 2026) expected to reach 2 million units per year capacity by FY28.
Tada greenfield Phase 1 (INR 1,225 crore, approved today) adds about 4.5 lakh units per year at full utilisation, with completion expected in FY30; total capacity to reach 2.45 million units by FY30.
Next Cheyyar module expected to kick in by first week of October 2026.
Indonesia CKD decision expected within the current quarter.
capex_capacity: Current Royal Enfield build capacity about 1.5 million motorcycles per year after first Cheyyar module, which started in July 2026 (in time); delivery rate reached about 5,000+ per day.
June 2026 production about 1.16 lakh motorcycles, with about 4,500 per day rate; Oragadam and Vallam running three shifts since April.
Tada greenfield in Andhra Pradesh: INR 1,225 crore Phase 1, additional 4.5 lakh units per year at full utilisation, built in modules.
Depreciation rise attributed to about INR 346 crore increase in average gross block, mainly Flying Flea start of production and new capacity, plus tools and dies depreciation.
Indonesia: CKD assembly partner identified to get around 10,000-unit annual import quota limit; luxury tax about 160%+ applies to bikes above 250cc regardless of CBU/CKD.
demand_pricing: Royal Enfield India retail growth about 30-32% YoY in Q1; booking, walk-in and telephonic inquiries growing slightly faster than volumes.

Dealer inventory at about 10-12 days, described as lean; in-transit inventory about 5 days and depot inventory about 4-5 days additional, per Q&A. Management targets saving another 4-5 days via more direct billing (about 4.5-4.7x increase vs prior year).
Gross margin: commodity and input inflation net impact about 4-4.5% of costs in Q1; value engineering benefit about 0.4%; 350cc price hike of 1.75% from April 2026 gave about 1.2% benefit.
Hunter 350 first-time buyers about 50% share; overall RE customer mix about 70%+ upgraders, about 25% first-time buyers, about 5-6% repeat RE-to-RE.
VECV: spares growth 15.3%; Pro X SCV entry with 1,041 units including 172 EVs; PARIVARTAN fleet modernisation MoU for NCR targets over 2 lakh vehicles, implementation being finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the brownfield capacity ramp and what is channel inventory ahead of festive?
qa_highlights.answer: First module started July 2026, output about 5,000+ per day delivery; inventory about 10-12 days, lean; direct billing and vendor 3-shift planning aimed to build stock before festive; next module by October first week.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin bridge and the drivers of lower other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Net commodity/input impact about 4-4.5%, value engineering about 0.4%, price hikes about 1.2%, mix 0.2%. Other expenses down about 7%: INR 30 crore from Q4 timing (cricket ads, two launches) and INR 22 crore marketing cut. No forward commodity guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: What is demand outlook into the back half given high base from October?
qa_highlights.answer: Management points to strong funnel growth, a middleweight segment that grew from 70,000 to 1.2 lakh units per month in three years, planned launches, and a marketing ramp-up after scaling back in Q1 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue gap between standalone and consolidated and its sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Gap driven by subsidiary growth, mainly Brazil, with some offset from India-booked exports; international market size about 0.8-1 million units, Royal Enfield share 8-9%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ASP up and what is driving non-vehicle revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: ASP up 2.8% QoQ: price hikes 1.2%, international mix 1%, currency 0.4%, allied 0.6%. Allied about 15% of revenue, service job cards about 9 lakh per month.

qa_highlights.question: Any plans to list or hive off VECV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no crystallised plan; focus at Eicher level is on EV; VECV growth described as phenomenal across segments except heavy-duty buses.

risks_watch: Inventory tightness at about 10-12 days ahead of festive; ability of vendors to sustain 24/7 three-shift output and the October module timing.
Commodity inflation (aluminium, crude, steel, copper, precious metals) and logistics disruption; management declined to guide on Q2 commodity headwind.
Higher-cc (450cc/650cc) softness in Super Meteor, Himalayan and Shotgun in Q1 per analyst; management plans marketing and refreshes.
High base from October for the next 12 months after GST-related price cuts.
Europe and APAC still weak; Indonesia import quota and luxury tax constrain ASEAN growth; Flying Flea scale-up and EV economics still early.
505200|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes and demand, describing Q1 as exceptional for both businesses; more measured on commodity costs, which management called volatile and declined to quantify forward. Evasive on VECV listing, saying no crystallised plan exists.
key_quotes: There has been an exceptional quarter across both the businesses.
Currently, we are at a very low inventory.
We are cautiously bullish even in the international market.
So we are taking it in phases because the growth momentum is continuing.

505255|2026-03.headline: GMM Pfaudler FY26 revenue rose about 10% and EBITDA about 11% to INR 403 crore; Q4 gross margin fell, with no FY27 numeric guidance.
505255|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew about 10% and EBITDA rose from INR 361 crore to INR 403 crore, with full-year margin up about 1 percentage point. India was the standout, with revenue up about 12%, EBITDA up about 24% and PAT up about 40%. Q4 margins fell year-on-year and sequentially on a large HE (heavy engineering) shipment and higher gas and metal costs, which management called quarter-specific. FY26 order intake reached INR 3,714 crore (up about 20% from INR 3,100 crore) and opening backlog on April 1 was up about 34%. Management declined to give numeric FY27 guidance and said it would present a three-year plan to the market later.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 12%, EBITDA about 24% and PAT about 40% in FY26. Heavy engineering (Ahmedabad) did about INR 300+ crore revenue in FY26, and the Vatva facility (GMM Inox, Poland) grew double digits.

segments.name: Europe / International
segments.commentary: Execution was slow; international EBITDA margin cited at about 10%. German restructuring is expected to save INR 45 crore a year once fully absorbed. Europe order intake was much stronger in FY26, including large systems orders.

segments.name: Mixing / Edlon / SEMCO
segments.commentary: Edlon (semiconductor-linked high-purity linings) is now about USD 25 million revenue, which management called high margin. SEMCO (South America) won a USD 12-13 million agitator order in Q1 FY27; MixPro (Canada) is growing and profitable.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 guidance; management said it expects improvement in FY27 on a 12-month basis, citing order intake, backlog and restructuring.
Medium-term EBITDA margin aspiration of at least 15% at consolidated level, versus about 11.4-11.5% today.
Three-year strategy (growth, cost, organisation) prepared; market presentation targeted for August-September, possibly later given Middle East crisis.
Expects no significant one-off restructuring cost in FY27; the INR 45 crore German saving starts next year and fully materialises as staff retire.
Plans to repay about USD 20 million from group cash and reduce debt, but timing of the financing restructuring is not confirmed by end of FY27.
Target of at least double-digit revenue growth over about three years, but management said 20% growth in a year is unlikely to be planned for.
capex_capacity: GMM Inox (Poland, 51% owned, strong local partner) is full; two more sheds are needed as soon as possible to serve European sites with lower cost.
Vatva facility (GMM Inox) could reach about INR 700-800 crore revenue with small further investment; beyond that a new facility is needed.
UK and Hyderabad facilities shut; German factory downsized; Poland plant now operating.
Edlon and SEMCO acquisitions added intangibles and goodwill; split not given on call, to be shared offline.
demand_pricing: Order intake up about 20% to INR 3,714 crore; nearly 50% from non-traditional industries (semiconductors, defence, oil and gas, petrochemicals, metals and minerals, nuclear).
Two large systems orders (one US, one Eastern Europe) drove much of the increase; open systems opportunities could yield USD 20-30 million order intake per year.
Chemicals (especially agrochemicals and European chemicals) remain slow; pharma (CDMO, GLP drugs) improving; China business recovering in some segments.
Raw material pass-through depends on contract: long-term projects have a 5% expedition clause; fast-moving contracts absorb cost changes.
Q1 FY27 order intake continuing at a decent level, including an Edlon order of USD 8-9 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross and consolidated EBITDA margins (55.4% gross) drop, and what are sustainable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 to a large HE order shipped at lower margin and higher gas and metal costs that have since stabilised. It said quarterly margins are volatile and FY26 margin was up about 1 pp; it prefers 12-month views.

qa_highlights.question: Why no guidance for FY27, and what drives the growth and margin plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20% order-intake rise includes systems orders that convert over 2-3 years, so it avoided a bullish number. It plans a three-year strategy to be presented to the capital markets once confidence improves, targeting at least double-digit growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the German restructuring saving and will exceptional items recur?
qa_highlights.answer: The German restructuring saves INR 45 crore a year, starting next year. No significant one-off cost is planned for FY27, though future restructurings would be reported as one-offs. FY26 exceptional items were about INR 65 crore, including German severance and the India labour code impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the finance cost high relative to a small net debt, and how does the company plan to reduce it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited FX on an intercompany loan between Germany and Luxembourg, and a financing agreement in place until 2028, which it intends to restructure within the next year. It said the high cash balance is partly customer prepayments needed to finance large systems orders.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term margin targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to a 15% consolidated EBITDA margin in the medium term, as a minimum, versus about 11.4-11.5% today, and said it could come faster if initiatives work.

qa_highlights.question: Will the segment reporting change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reporting format will change from next quarter (Q1 FY27), with a new organisation aligned by product, vertical and industry, rather than mid-year.

risks_watch: Gross margin and mix volatility: Q4 margins fell and management said it is quarter-specific; watch whether FY27 margins recover.

Metals supply disruption: Middle East/Hormuz raw material shortfall; ~₹10 crore of metals sales not delivered on time in Q1. Q2 performance depends on second-half holding up.
Climate control weakness: sales ~₹3.9 crore; depends on government action (QCO, minimum import price) against Chinese dumping; no recovery expected before Oct-Nov.
Tax credit quality: ~₹4.75 crore one-off merger credit flatters Q1 PAT (~₹9.75 crore vs ~₹5.25 crore ex-credit); further ₹0.3-0.4 crore is subject to assessment.
Working capital and leverage: working capital rose on copper prices; debt to EBITDA ~3x with target of 2.5-3x by year end; cash flow expected to improve over next 2-3 quarters.
Management flagged a seasonal dip in automotive in Q3 after festive season and moderating automotive growth in Q3-Q4; monitor whether volume growth holds at ~20%.
key_quotes: So I'd say about 20 % is volume growth and the rest is, I would say value growth.

506395|2026-06.headline: Coromandel Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 3% YoY to INR761 crores on West Asia input-cost spike, while revenue rose 15% to INR8,215 crores.
506395|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 15% YoY to INR8,215 crores, helped by higher fertilizer realisations and non-subsidy growth, with NACL now consolidated. EBITDA declined 3% to INR761 crores and net profit fell to INR382 crores from INR502 crores as ammonia and sulphur costs outran NBS subsidy rates. Management said phosphate production was deliberately cut to 6.9 lakh tons (72% utilisation) to protect inventory economics, while Crop Protection (revenue +20%, EBIT +44%) and Retail (revenue +85%) carried the quarter. Management is pressing the government for a kharif NBS revision and says no near-term fertilizer capacity additions are planned.

segments.name: Fertilizers (phosphatic)
segments.commentary: Production cut to 6.9 lakh tons from 8.4 lakh tons (72% utilisation) to optimise inventory; phos acid output 1.2 lakh tons, flat YoY. Sales volume fell 9-10% to 10 lakh tons, but primary market share rose to 22% from 18%; point-of-sale up 13% to 7.9 lakh tons, 16% share.

segments.name: Specialty nutrients and organics
segments.commentary: Described as strong, aided by higher organics and micronutrient offtake; launched 3 new products. Management says this business grows 25-30% with about 20% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Crop Protection
segments.commentary: Record Q1: revenue +20% to INR870 crores, EBIT +44% to INR159 crores, with exports and B2B strong. New products are 32% of domestic B2C sales vs 23% last year.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Revenue +85% YoY; 76% of stores profitable vs 61% last year; 22 new stores take network above 1,200 outlets.

segments.name: Nano and bio products
segments.commentary: Nano business volumes +2% YoY with nearly 60% market share; UP and Maharashtra bans are restraining growth. Bio business steady, with 2 new products launched.

guidance_outlook: Phosphoric acid price for Q2 settled at $1,700/t vs $1,360/t in Q1, following higher DAP and raw-material prices.
Granulation project on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27; Crop Protection capacity expansion for key molecules expected by September 2026.

Management wants kharif NBS rates revised to the 6-month average policy formula; says the industry has taken a 25-30% price increase across grades, and that further price rises are not feasible without subsidy correction.
Sulphur expected to stay high for some time; management says the acid-backed production economics are unattractive until sulphur falls, with NACL-type steady-state EBITDA well below Coromandel.

No near-term fertilizer capacity additions planned; target is 4 million tons own fertilizer plus 1 million tons trading, with management citing 8-9 million tons of nutrient visibility for about 2 years.
Normal sustainable capex guided at about INR300 crores per year; ~INR7,000 crores invested over the last 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Phos acid and sulphuric acid plants commissioned; sulphuric acid at rated capacity and generating power; phos acid stabilising with a new rock-utilisation technology.
Granulation project on track for Q4 FY27 commissioning; new capacity is 750,000 tonnes, 50% to be sold via own retail and the balance into UP, Rajasthan, MP and Chhattisgarh.

Crop Protection key-molecule capacity to be commissioned by September 2026; further spending to focus on marketing and channel rather than assets; no new AI capacity planned given spare NACL capacity.
Senegal rock mining produced over 1.1 lakh tons in the quarter; BMCC operating close to 5 lakh tons/year target; evaluating a 100,000-150,000 ton SSP plant at $5-6 million.

Kakinada T-MAP plant and seaweed granulation plant progressing; Ankleshwar fluorination launch facility being set up; IIT Chennai research park planned; PA-SA plant gives about 60% acid self-sufficiency.
demand_pricing: Monsoon deficit was 23% through the quarter, moderating to 17% by late July; reservoirs at 34% of capacity vs 57% last year. Pulses acreage down 15%, oilseeds and cotton down 6%, and paddy back to normal.
Management says there is no fertilizer shortage; Urea and DAP stocks are comfortable for kharif, but industry production and imports must hold for two more months to build rabi carryover.
NP/NPK production and imports fell 21% and 38% respectively; management ties this to weak NBS subsidy for these grades.
Crop protection: domestic demand muted due to delayed sowing; export markets improving but cautious on price. Active ingredient prices are firmer than before because China keeps AIs low.
NACL export revenue hit by price moderation on molecules sold to global MNCs, while Coromandel passed input-cost increases through to exports.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a structural shift to NPK or a fertilizer shortage on the ground?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no shortage; the early-season pick-up of low-MRP packs was an advance purchase, and current uptake depends more on monsoon than on availability.

qa_highlights.question: How much did FX contribute to Crop Protection EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX is at most 5-6% of consolidated EBITDA, under a netting-based hedging policy.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the depreciation spike and how much is from new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental depreciation from new capex is about INR16-18 crores; the rest is mining overburden amortisation (about INR30 crores) and NACL intangibles amortisation (about INR20-21 crores).

qa_highlights.question: What is the ask from government and how is the EBITDA per ton outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants the 6-month average NBS rate applied, and says NP/NPK rates need significant correction; the target is nutrient EBITDA of about INR6,500/t from INR5,000/t, but not in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for the next 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided normal sustainable capex of about INR300 crores, but will consider higher spending for attractive-return projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dhaksha drone contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Coromandel bought 100-150 drones this quarter and targets a fleet of 500 during the year; management said Dhaksha is not a significant EBITDA drag.

risks_watch: Subsidy under-recovery on NP/NPK: sulphur and ammonia costs are not covered by NBS rates, and kharif revision is still pending.
Sulphur and phos acid pricing: phos acid up to $1,700/t in Q2; management says sulphur needs to fall to about $800/t for backward integration to pay.
Subsidy receivable of INR3,254 crores at June-end.
State bans on Nano fertilizers in UP and Maharashtra are holding back volumes.
Crop Protection export pricing: AI prices are firmer, but export demand is cautious and NACL revenue fell on price moderation.
Whether industry production and imports can hold through the next two months to build rabi carryover inventory.
506395|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the non-fertilizer businesses (Crop Protection, Retail, Specialty) but cautious and repeatedly pressing the government on fertilizer subsidy. Management was evasive on a few specifics (CP export/domestic mix, Dhaksha numbers, NACL stake increase), deferring them to follow-up.
key_quotes: Overall, we have delivered a resilient performance in a challenging operating environment marked by delayed monsoons, elevated raw material costs and pressure on fertilizer margins.
These rates do not fully compensate for the increase in global raw material costs, which happened subsequent to Middle East crisis.
Given the Phosphoric Acid price of $1,700, at least we want $800 of sulphur.
So I would put a normal sustainable capex of INR300 crores would be the number we'll look at.

506401|2026-03.headline: Deepak Nitrite Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 13% YoY to INR383 crore, margin 18%, with PAT INR220 crore; management guides Q1 FY27 better than Q4.
506401|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,127 crore, down from INR2,202 crore a year earlier but up from INR1,983 crore in Q3, while EBITDA rose 74% QoQ and 13% YoY to INR383 crore. Phenolics EBIT reached INR287 crore at a 20% margin, and Advanced Intermediates EBIT rose to INR34 crore. Management attributed the gains to favourable pricing, feedstock bought on dips before the Middle East disruption, and integration benefits. The nitric acid plant ran at about 45% utilisation in Q4 because of technical issues, so the expected INR90-100 crore EBITDA addition is delayed.

financial_highlights.change: -3% YoY vs INR2,202 crore; +7% QoQ vs INR1,983 crore
+13% YoY vs INR339 crore; +74% QoQ vs INR219 crore

segments.name: Advanced Intermediates
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR708 crore vs INR654 crore in Q4 FY25 and INR652 crore in Q3; EBIT INR34 crore vs INR15 crore in Q3. Gains came from stable volumes, end-product pricing and product mix, while exports slowed on logistics disruption.

segments.name: Phenolics
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,429 crore; EBIT INR287 crore vs INR239 crore in Q4 FY25 and INR145 crore in Q3, a 20% EBIT margin supported by spreads and downstream demand.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 expected to be better than Q4 FY26 on both standalone and consolidated basis, and better than Q1 FY26.
FY27 expected to show stronger margins for standalone business vs FY26, driven by new downstream products that management calls significantly margin accretive.
Feedstock inventory bought on dips expected to support costs until price stabilisation, perhaps end-Q2 FY27 or mid-Q2.
New products and fluorinated molecules expected on regularised commercial production from Q3 FY27, in time for export customers' CY2026 requirements.
MIBK/MIBC plant expected to be commissioned around end-Q1 or early Q2 FY27.
Polycarbonate project expected to be commissioned by June 2028; PC resin and Phenol expansion may be offset by about a quarter.
capex_capacity: Nitric acid plant ran at about 45% utilisation in Q4 FY26 due to technical issues; under repair with technology and equipment suppliers; the earlier INR90-100 crore EBITDA addition target is pending stable operations.
Nitration and hydrogenation facilities at Deepak Chem Tech, Dahej, commissioned and stated as operating at expected productivity.
Multipurpose agrochemical intermediates and MIBK/MIBC projects: mechanical completion near; pre-commissioning next, commissioning around end-Q1 or early Q2 FY27.
Polycarbonate resin project (India's first fully integrated PC facility) targeted for June 2028 commissioning; total announced project around INR11,000 crore.
Praxair India to build, own and operate a dedicated on-site HyCO plant at Dahej under a build-own-operate model, reducing upfront capex for Deepak.
Funding: 60:40 debt-equity; bank debt tied up; equity contribution ongoing, with debt drawdown after 25% equity infusion.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as relatively stable across automotive, infrastructure, pharma, electronics and polymers; management says it is passing through raw material cost increases where possible, an ongoing exercise.
Advanced Intermediates realisations were lower than in earlier years, per management; capacity was reported as running full.
Phenol: domestic buyers' ordering pattern is mixed, with some back to normal buying and others still need-based. Management cited a China-India price spread but declined to comment on it.
China anti-involution and safety curbs on nitration chemistries seen as a structural tailwind for nitration products (DASDA, OBA-linked); management said this has already started on the ground.
Sulfur and sulfuric acid cost increases are a global headwind; management expects no significant net impact if India prices stay at par with international prices.
Management declined to give IPA or phenol production volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What was nitric acid utilisation in Q4 and is the INR90-100 crore EBITDA addition still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant was at about 45% utilisation in Q4 due to technical issues; the balance was bought from the market. Target achievable once stable, but no timeline given. Concentrated nitric acid plant operating normally.

qa_highlights.question: Phenolics feedstock availability and China-India spread outlook for Q1-Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance was preponed by about 10-11 days in early April; intermediate stock covered supply. Management guided Q1 profitability higher than Q4 and expects no propylene constraint. Declined to comment on other companies' spreads.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new products and fluorinated molecule add to FY27 standalone performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Validation batches are supplied or in transit to customers; commercial production on a regular basis from Q3 FY27. Management did not anticipate customer approval concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it moved some customers to dealership and CSA models to secure outstanding amounts amid volatility, and said realisations, not capacity utilisation, are the lower metric in Advanced Intermediates.

qa_highlights.question: Is the China nitration tailwind already visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the CCP-led safety and transport audit is a structural tailwind, not tied to a specific province or product, and that it has already started happening.

qa_highlights.question: How will the polycarbonate project (about INR11,000 crore) be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Upadhyay: debt tied up with banks at 60:40; equity is being infused, and debt will be drawn after 25% equity per the bank condition. Management said funding is not an issue and cash generation is sufficient.

risks_watch: Nitric acid plant reliability: utilisation was about 45% in Q4; repairs and the timing of stable operations remain open.
Feedstock cost volatility (benzene, xylene, toluene, propylene); inventory bought on dips is expected to support costs only until around mid-Q2 FY27.
Working capital: receivable days rose, and some customers have moved to dealership and CSA models.

Execution risk on MIBK/MIBC commissioning (around end-Q1 or early Q2 FY27), new products (Q3 FY27), and the polycarbonate project (June 2028, possible quarter mismatch between PC resin and phenol expansion).
Sulfur and sulfuric acid cost increases; pricing gap between India and international markets.
Geopolitical risks in the Middle East and the US tariff and China policy environment.

We are expecting it to be commissioned by June 2028.

It has already started happening.

506401|2026-06.headline: Deepak Nitrite Q1 FY27: record consolidated EBITDA of INR 554 crore (21% margin) and PAT of INR 345 crore, up 207% YoY.
506401|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 35% YoY and 22% QoQ to INR 2,592 crore, with EBITDA up 159% YoY to INR 554 crore and margin at 21% versus 11% a year ago. Phenolics delivered record EBIT of INR 418 crore at a 24% margin, while Advanced Intermediates EBIT was INR 67 crore at an 8% margin. Management said April was disrupted by a maintenance shutdown, propylene shortages and gas curtailment, so the phenol run rate of about 1 lakh tonnes applies to parts of the quarter rather than the full period. Debt funding for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project has been closed, and the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.27x.

segments.name: Phenolics
segments.commentary: Record revenue of INR 1,775 crore and EBIT of INR 418 crore (24% margin), supported by stronger realisations, sustained demand and high utilisation. Management said the business is almost entirely domestic.

segments.name: Advanced Intermediates (AI)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR 804 crore and EBIT of INR 67 crore (8% margin), helped by better realisations, higher operating rates and product mix. AI export mix is about 40-50%; raw material costs stayed high for some products.

guidance_outlook: MIBK and MIBC to be commissioned with acetophenone in August 2026; the remaining projects (multipurpose agrochemical intermediates facility, etc.) are due in Q2 FY27, with commercial volumes from January.
Management aims to reach 4 lakh tonnes of phenol in the existing Deepak Phenolics asset in the short to medium term, with about INR 70-odd crore of debottlenecking capex.
Polycarbonate commissioning targeted for H2 FY28-29 and BPA a couple of months later; propylene from the PDH project is expected to support phenol volumes.

Capex: about INR 1,200 crore spent to date, another INR 1,000-1,600 crore in FY27 (figures varied in the call), and about INR 3,000 crore in FY28. Peak debt estimated at INR 8,000-8,500 crore including working capital, with D/E below 1.
capex_capacity: Ammonia-to-amines integration chain (nitric acid plant, nitration and reduction) completed and stabilised; the company says it now runs 8 products simultaneously.

Phenol capacity is about 3.5 lakh tonnes, and management says it is debottlenecking toward 4 lakh tonnes through advanced process controls. Run rate reached about 1 lakh tonnes per quarter in parts of Q1, but was not sustained through the full quarter.
MIBC pre-commissioning runs reportedly exceeded design capacity; management said it can ramp above 100% once demand comes in.
Debt for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project is closed, funded 60:40 debt to equity, with the 25% equity already contributed.
demand_pricing: Management said phenol demand in India is roughly balanced with no new global capacity, and some supply is short. Imports were duty-free for most of Q1 until the government reimposed the duty.
Raw material costs were high in April, but procurement secured feedstock for continuous operations. Management said feedstock costs are competitive domestically and globally.
Freight and insurance costs rose. The company responded with CIF to FOB shifts, larger parcels, and a product reformulation for a Middle East customer that changed its hazard class.
Consolidated export mix is about 20%. AI is roughly 50-50 domestic to export; Phenolics is almost entirely domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Did phenol run rate reach 1 lakh tonnes per quarter, and how is propylene covered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1 lakh tonnes was a run rate reached in significant periods, not the full quarter, because of raw material sourcing and a short maintenance shutdown. Debottlenecking is aimed at the 4 lakh tonne mark in the short to medium term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Phenolics spread in Q1 and outlook for Q2-Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose spreads and said Deepak buys feedstock below international index levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the phenol capacity now exceed earlier maturity assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main change was confidence. Advanced process controls, costing about INR 80-100 crore cumulatively, enabled higher throughput, with INR 70-odd crore more planned for debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: Is the phenol supply-demand balance sound?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no new capacity, China is largely self-sufficient, demand is balanced and India is short of supply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak debt and capex plan for the INR 11,500 crore project?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,200 crore has been spent. Peak borrowing is about INR 6,800 crore plus working capital, for total peak debt of INR 8,000-8,500 crore. Management said D/E will stay below 1x.

qa_highlights.question: Could you quantify incremental revenue and EBITDA margin from the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, but said the margin profile of new products is in line with or above the AI average.

risks_watch: Phenol throughput depends on propylene and feedstock availability; April showed how a shutdown and raw material shortage can cut volumes.
Ramp-up timing for the Q2 AI projects and the MIBC run rate; management said the alkylation and multipurpose plants slipped because of manpower and gas shortages.
Polycarbonate and BPA commissioning (H2 FY28-29) and the debt drawdown schedule.
Freight and insurance costs and the reimposed phenol import duty could change domestic realisations.
Management declined to give Phenolics spreads, AI product-level margins, and the MIBK/acetone ratio, so these remain unverified.

506405|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose to INR 177 crore from INR 150 crore QoQ, mostly raw-material pass-through; FY26 revenue INR 582 crore.

Sulfur supply was constrained by Middle East/Hormuz disruption, and the Roha plant ran at about 60% capacity for roughly 15 days in March before supply was restored. Working capital and short-term borrowings rose substantially on higher inventory, debtor and advance-payment requirements for boron, at about 8.75-9% interest. segments.name: Sulfur / sulfuric acid (bulk chemicals)
