Fillers market in India is estimated at about INR200 crore. Management aims to move from number 2 to number 1 in toxin plus fillers within 3-5 years.

International: aims to raise margins from 40-50% under distributor models to 15-20% higher with its own field force in Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia. Recruitment of a regional team happened in Q1.
CHAI partnership for liposomal amphotericin B gives access to more than 100 markets; bioequivalence study due by August-September, followed by WHO PQ filing.

Employee additions are mainly at Indore (around 50-60 for domestic expansion), with international headcount capped at 20-25. Management says the previous-year contract-to-payroll conversion was one-time.

qa_highlights.question: Is Gufic participating in GLP-1 (semaglutide) under its own brand, and has third-party CMO revenue started?
qa_highlights.answer: Pranav Choksi said GLP-1 is purely a CMO role for Hetero, which got permission in May 2026, so Q1 revenue was residual. CMO traction is expected to build from Q2, with the main contribution in Q3; about 30% of capacity is for domestic CMO and about 70% for international use, where Hetero and Gufic have filed in more than 22 countries. No front-end role is planned in India or abroad.

qa_highlights.question: How does the shift in international model (distributor-led to own-registration, field-force led) change economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is moving to own field force in Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia once registrations and scale allow, aiming to lift margins from 40-50% under distributor models by 15-20% or more. A regional team was recruited in Q1 (one person in Mexico, one in the Philippines, two in Mumbai); the company also says it is building IP and trademarks in these markets.

qa_highlights.question: When will Indore get EU certification and does margin expansion follow, and is 18% the new normal margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Navsari already holds EU certification. The Indore EU certificate is awaited, with feedback expected in about one to two months; a US partner has also filed from the site. Indore utilisation was 18-22% last year, 20-25% the year before, and close to 30-35% this year, targeted at 40-45% by year-end. Management said the 18% margin is the start of an improvement trend rather than a new normal, and that the earlier 18% period had Indore costs, depreciation and interest capitalised.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fillers (Revanesse tie-up) scale, and how big is the opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: The Indian filler market is estimated at about INR200 crore. Launch is expected around December-January, after registration in Q2 or mid-Q3. Management gave no first-year revenue number and aims to move from number 2 to number 1 in toxin plus fillers within 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15-20% growth conservative, and can growth go beyond 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15-20% year-on-year company growth is a bare minimum, with efforts aimed at growing beyond it. Some low-yielding product mix is being squeezed out, and it was not conservative in that guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential from current capacity without further capex (analyst cited about INR2,700 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Roonghta first put FY27 expected revenue at about INR1,100 crore, with 15% annual growth taking it to about INR1,600 crore on existing facilities. Pranav Choksi said Navsari is capped at about INR800 crore, with toxin and penem not saturated, and Indore could add INR800-1,200 crore on about INR300 crore capex. The combined no-capex figure was cited as INR1,600-1,800 crore, and the total maximum as INR1,600-2,000 crore. The INR2,700 crore figure was not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned employee addition strategy, and what productivity metrics are used?
qa_highlights.answer: Most additions are at Indore, with about 50-60 people for domestic expansion, while international headcount is capped at 20-25. The previous year's increase reflected contract staff moving to payroll in Indore and Navsari for quality roles, which management called a one-time step. Employee cost growth is in line with the company's overall growth.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating leverage from Indore's product mix start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects operating leverage to start around mid-FY28. Indore has 6 lyophilisers (4 at 100,000-vial and 2 at 44,000-vial capacity). Target mix is about 20% liquid, 50-60% lyophilisation and 20-30% complex injectables, with the liquid line targeted at about 80% utilisation within 3 years.

risks_watch: Indore EU certification is still pending, and margin expansion depends on it; the US partner audit timing is also uncertain.
GLP-1 CMO ramp is back-ended (Q2 traction, Q3 main contribution) and depends on Hetero's approvals; a 5-day plant shutdown is planned for visits.
Average realisation per vial is INR80-100 today; the INR300-500 per vial target depends on depot, liposomal and complex injectables launching on schedule.
Toxin plant is WHO Phase 1 with limited capacity; global registrations are deferred to after next year pending cash flow.
Filler launch (Revanesse) timing depends on registration in Q2 or mid-Q3; first-year revenue was not quantified.
Management's peak revenue figures were inconsistent during the call (INR1,600 crore, INR1,600-1,800 crore, INR1,600-2,000 crore), so the capacity-revenue framework needs clarification.
Rising employee count, with 50-60 domestic and 20-25 international additions, needs productivity tracking against operating leverage.
key_quotes: Yes. And I'm sure Roonghta sir explained this in the last 2 calls also because in the period which you have mentioned, at that time, the total expense of Indore as well as the depreciation and the interest were being capitalized.
But 15% to 20% is what we commit to you that would be a bare minimum.
So our traction of their revenues was residual in the Q1.
Our current facility is only WHO Phase 1 with limited capacity.
509079|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on Indore's operational progress, the 15-20% growth floor and the margin trajectory, but cautious on timelines, deferring the EU certificate, global toxin registrations and any margin uplift from exports until approvals come through. Answers on revenue capacity were less precise and at times reconciled on the fly.

509152|2026-03.headline: GRP Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell to INR 94 million (7% margin) from INR 331 million as EPR income, exports and raw-material costs weighed.

FY26 total income fell about 3% to INR 5,380 million and EBITDA dropped to INR 429 million from INR 694 million, with adjusted PAT of INR 46 million after a INR 14 million Labour Code charge. Export volumes fell about 15% while domestic volumes grew nearly 10%, and raw-material inflation reached 43% in certain SKUs. Management said the Pyrova (pyrolysis) and rCB platforms are still stabilising, and that the revised pricing from April 2026 passes through the full raw-material impact.

qa_highlights.question: How much one-time loss came from Polymer Composite in Q4?

qa_highlights.question: Did pyrolysis oil realisations improve with high crude prices, and will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Some benefit in March; Q1 FY27 realisations are marginally above Oct 2025-Feb 2026, but road-construction demand is weaker, so volumes are affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the recovery trend in exports and order inflows, and have RM costs stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: North American direct volumes are largely recovered and the order book is stronger than most of FY26. Revised pricing from April 2026 captures the full raw-material cost increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 capex breakup, and what is the feedback on TPO and the new reclaim technology?

qa_highlights.question: How much EPR income will pyrolysis and rCB generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Pyrolysis EPR accrual awaits PCB approvals, expected within weeks, with retrospective accrual in Q1 or Q2 FY27. Credits accrue at about 0.8 weightage with about 1.5x conversion; the mix of crumb, char and TPO is not yet disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised EBITDA margin after Pyrova stabilises, and how will capex be funded?

Recovery of indirect US-linked volumes via Southeast Asia, and the status of US tariff revisions.
Chinese virgin PP imports continuing to erode recycled PP competitiveness in packaging.
Gross margin of 46% in Q4 versus 54% in FY25; the EBITDA trajectory needs to recover toward FY25 levels.
509152|2026-03.management_tone: Management was candid about a weak FY26 and attributed the decline to tariffs, raw-material inflation and start-up costs, while expressing confidence in the Pyrova and reclaim-rubber expansion. key_quotes: FY '26 represented an important transition year for GRP.

509152|2026-06.headline: GRP Q1 FY27: EBITDA up 60% to INR174 million, margin 11% (+233 bps), PAT more than doubled to INR42 million on 26% total income growth.

EBITDA grew 60% to INR174 million with margin up 233 bps to 11% despite sharp raw material inflation. Management re-segmented into Rubber Recycling and Others, and for the first time gave a directional FY27 outlook of close to 20%+ revenue growth. Pyrova cleared a 25-day monthly continuous run threshold in July 2026, and the rCB plant is slated for commissioning by October 2026.

segments.name: Others (Engineering Plastics, Repurposed Polyolefin, Windmill, residual polymer composite)

FY27: reclaim rubber volumes to grow close to 20%; management hopes to hold double-digit volume growth for the year.
Reclaim rubber, mid-term: mid-teen volume growth over 3 years, double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin from ~9-10% toward 10-14% after Pyrova synergies.
Pyrova: capacity to 45,000 tons, then +30,000 tons in FY28; EBITDA margin to 18-20% after rCB is mature (later described as 15-20%); FY28 seen as maturity year.
Plastics: over 20% growth in FY27, mid-teen growth through FY30, EBITDA margin 10-15%. Management said current margin is not one-time and should keep improving.
FY27 capex INR90-100 crore; FY28 capex decision in 2H FY27. Remaining ~INR100 crore of the INR250 crore plan still to be deployed.
capex_capacity: Pyrova: two more pyrolysis lines to take capacity to 45 KTA; longest continuous reactor run achieved; July 2026 met threshold of 25-day monthly run with 4-day shutdown.

Reclaim rubber debottlenecking capex included in FY27 plan.

Engineering plastics growth driven mainly by automotive OE demand, with early appliance approvals contributing; polyolefin volumes flat as customer selection tightened.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rCB project status, including customer trials, expected revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The first pyrolysis phase was commissioned in October 2025 and stabilised by March 2026. The rCB plant starts commissioning in August 2026 and is targeted for October 2026. Meaningful contribution is expected from Q4 FY27. Pyrova can reach 18-20% EBITDA margin once rCB is mature, subject to customer approvals; FY28 is seen as the maturity year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 27% growth in engineering plastics volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was mainly automotive OE demand for nylon, with early appliance approvals from Q4 FY26 contributing some commercial volume. Polyolefin revenue grew but volumes were flat because customer selection was tightened, with a push into specialty polyolefin sectors.

qa_highlights.question: How much has rubber inflation risen over the past year, and when will prices stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to predict how long rubber inflation will last. Revenue grew about 30% against 12% volume growth, so the balance is price, largely passed to customers with a lag because contracts reset quarterly, half-yearly or annually. Prices are not expected to reverse soon given El Nino and oil-linked synthetic rubber.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 capex plans, and what is the deleveraging plan?

About INR100 crore of the INR250 crore plan remains. Deleveraging timing is not in management's control, and there are no firm plans, though it would be needed to accelerate the Gujarat expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers shifting toward sustainability-led material solutions rather than buying on price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a combination of value and sustainability. Reclaim is increasingly considered an alternative to virgin rubber given synthetic rubber and carbon black supply-demand mismatches. In plastics, regulation drives conversion and cost drives adoption.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the recovery is demand normalisation versus share gains, and is the export order book back to pre-tariff levels? What is the sustainable EBITDA margin, and when does Pyrova become EBITDA positive?

qa_highlights.question: Is volume growth at risk from price increases?

segments.commentary: Over 900 corporates served; management cited a 95.62% CAGR. Named clients include Accenture, Siemens, EY, Zoho, Tech Mahindra and, recently, Adani.

segments.name: Retail / leisure
segments.commentary: Card business declined in FY26 on lower US student traffic and competition from rupee credit cards; leisure market down about 25% since March. Management described this as a calibrated, value-led push with a minimum margin per transaction.

segments.name: Prepaid cards
segments.commentary: Four products (three plastics and one digital-only, Uni-Z launched last month). Switch Card supports 30 currencies; Xplorer Metal card is by invitation. Samsung Pay and Google Pay tokenisation planned this year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 to be a challenging, linear quarter with leisure travel down roughly 25% from March, and expects the next one to two months to remain tough.
Trade remittances expected to become a material business in 12 to 18 months; family maintenance (about $3 billion market) to be a growth area.
FXC network expected to expand through the model over the next 12 to 15 months, with Spice Money group network and NBFC/retail partners as possible distribution.
Trade remittance margins expected 20-30 bps, below current blended levels, as competition rises.
Target to raise digital/automated share of transactions from about 60% to 80% this year.
Management did not give numerical FY27 targets for cards or revenue; it said Q2 to Q4 are peak months and FY27 mix will change materially.
capex_capacity: Network kept lean at 21+ branches (down from 35 when the CEO took over, 16 in COVID); expansion planned mainly through FXC appointments rather than owned branches.
Company is evaluating whether to apply for a PA-CB licence.
Working on multiple payment rails for faster, holiday-enabled remittances and a student fee-remittance platform.
Smart Agent Platform, FPaaS, Smart Corporate Platform and consumer app run on a unified payments stack.
demand_pricing: Q4 traffic hit in March by the US-Israel-Iran conflict; leisure market contracted about 25% from March to May 2026 per management.
Rupee credit cards with zero cross-currency markup and lounge perks have taken a large share of international spend (management estimate about 60%), with credit card spend outside LRS and TCS.
Management says it will not price at a loss; pricing uses interbank rates with a small card fulfilment fee on the Switch card.
B2B and corporate make up about 80-85% of business; partner commissions and referral fees are a larger share of costs.
Retail customer lifetime value is quoted at about INR1,000 of annual income per traveller versus high digital CAC.
Management expects more competition after the RBI circular, with margin pressure; trade remittances may run at 20-30 bps margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new RBI circular affect volumes, revenue and margins over the next one to two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said scope has expanded to trade and non-trade current account transactions, with no negative impact from the circular itself, but competition will pressure margins. Trade remittance margins are expected at 20-30 bps; current net margin is 0.6-0.8%.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will be most affected by the new regulations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split out the impact by segment. It said the new trade and family maintenance categories open new growth areas, and that retail/leisure faces the most pressure from credit cards.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company compete with low-priced small players on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay competitive but will not work at a loss per transaction, citing a minimum margin policy and a digital platform for each segment. It acknowledged its retail pricing may not be the lowest.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise FY26 revenue, volume, customer and new-product breakdown; agent commissions versus branch revenue; CAC; card KPIs and FY27 targets
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave only broad-based answers: B2B and corporate are 80-85% of business, partner commissions are higher as a B2B company, and digital CAC is high. It declined to give specific numbers and said detailed data would be shared through the company's written channel.

qa_highlights.question: How does Scapia (bank-sponsored card) compare, and how are rupee credit cards affecting forex cards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said credit cards hold a regulatory arbitrage (no LRS or TCS), that around 60% of international spend has moved to credit cards, and that the association has represented to RBI for parity. Forex cards are positioned on rate certainty for multi-currency travel; corporate and student segments do not use credit cards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TCS cut to 2% for education remittances doing to the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2% TCS mainly hit own-fund students, while loan-funded students are growing; it called the change a relief and said zero TCS would be better for the priority-sector segment.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and payables increase?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Pooja Mishra said the rise in current assets and liabilities reflects card-program customer wallet balances on both sides of the balance sheet. Capital turnover improved to 4.4x from 3.8x, and short-term borrowings are fixed-deposit-backed working capital lines, not structural debt.

risks_watch: Leisure and card volumes down about 25% since March; Q1 FY27 expected to be linear and challenging.
Rupee credit cards eroding forex card share in leisure; RBI parity representation is pending with no timeline.
Margin pressure from new AD-II entrants and FFMC-licensed competitors; trade remittance margins guided at 20-30 bps.
Execution risk on FXC network rollout and trade/family maintenance scope, which management said still has open clarifications.
Management was evasive on FY27 numerical targets, segment-wise volumes, card KPIs and PA-CB licence decision.
Customer service complaint raised on a Delhi branch; management promised corrective action.
511147|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the regulatory opportunity and long-term structure, but cautious and evasive on near-term numbers: Q1 FY27 was flagged as challenging and specific FY27 targets and segment KPIs were withheld. Management was defensive when discussing credit card competition and pricing.
key_quotes: Revenue crossed around INR111 crores for the first time. Revenue grew 26% significantly ahead of GTO growth, good business profitable mix.
We are happy to say we are increasing our market share year-on-year while the business has -- overall market has contracted by 20%.
So, from our perspective, we are clearly focused on forex cards, how to bring out the merits of the forex card and it's up to the customer's choice to take a forex card or credit card.

511196|2026-06.headline: Can Fin Homes Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 29% YoY to INR 2,609 crores, but rundown of INR 1,857 crores absorbed the AUM gain.
511196|2026-06.overview: Disbursements of INR 2,609 crores beat the INR 2,500 crore internal plan and grew 29% YoY across all six zones. Book rundown rose to INR 1,857 crores (from INR 1,730 crores in Q4), mainly from part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crores after the annual-to-quarterly reset, so net AUM growth was about 10.8% YoY. Yield held at 9.81% and cost of borrowing fell to 6.98%, lifting spread to 2.83% and NIM to 3.81%. Management reaffirmed 14% AUM growth and a 10 bps credit cost for FY27, while ROA slipped to 2.39% on higher opex and an IT project rollout is underway across 250 branches.

segments.name: Housing loans
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 1,650 crores, up 28% YoY; accounted for about 63% of Q1 disbursements.

segments.name: Non-housing / LAP
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 958 crores, up 32% YoY; about 37% of Q1 disbursements.

segments.name: Self-employed (SENP)
segments.commentary: Disbursements up 44% YoY; current NPA around 1.45-1.5% vs about 0.6-0.63% in salaried, per management.

segments.name: Karnataka / Telangana
segments.commentary: All six zones grew; Karnataka grew 18% YoY (lowest zone), Telangana slightly higher. IT-sector exposure about 6% of customers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target INR 13,000 crores with 14% AUM growth; management may push to INR 13,200-13,400 crores if needed to offset higher rundown.
Q2 FY27 disbursement target INR 3,000 crores; quarterly path then steps up to INR 3,500 crores and INR 4,000 crores in Q3 and Q4 per prior plan.
NIM to be maintained at 3.81% plus; Q2 incremental bank borrowing at 7.25-7.5% expected to add only marginal cost, on new loans only.
Credit cost guided at 10 bps for FY27; management sees no challenge to this.
Cost-to-income ratio around 19.5% for FY27, trending back toward 18% over about three years.
Remaining 245 branches to move to new IT platform by end of Q2, in tranches at month-end (July, August, September); update expected around September.
Opex: about INR 40 crores of further IT-related costs yet to come; no other major surprises expected.
capex_capacity: New LOS/LMS/report-generation platform live in 5 pilot branches from 8 July 2026, with sanctions, disbursements, NACH, BBPS collections and closures processed.
Rollout to remaining 245 branches (250 total) planned within Q2 FY27, migrating month-end data in tranches.
Management expects about six months for new branches to stabilise on the new system; staffing benefits expected this year with sales additions from existing headcount.
APF (apartment finance) approvals up to 331 projects; per-project exposure capped at 10% of the book per project.
demand_pricing: No demand slowdown seen across geographies; partner banks willing to sanction, including a couple of large sanctions.
Bank borrowing rates for new loans now 7.25-7.5% vs about 6.95% last year; existing loans unchanged.
Special-rate threshold raised from INR 20 lakh to INR 25 lakh loans, to offset higher incremental borrowing costs.
Customer pricing range about 8.4% (best, salaried, CIBIL above 725, INR 25 lakh+) to about 12.5% (non-salaried, non-housing, S3); blended yield 9.81%.
Competition: LIC and Bajaj Housing are the main rivals in branches; Bajaj growing around 25-30% per analyst comment, with its technology edge cited.
Best rate gap to banks widened from 55 bps to over 100 bps after repo cuts; management says it cannot close the gap cheaply.
82% of loans now have CIBIL score above 700 (vs about 75% earlier); 80% of business sourced via DSA.

financial_highlights.change: +29% YoY vs INR 2,015 crores; ahead of INR 2,500 crore plan

Flat through quarter; vs 9.82% last year

qa_highlights.question: Macro, underwriting and asset quality outlook for next 3-6 months, and any changes to norms or customer filters (salaried vs self-employed rejections)?
qa_highlights.answer: No demand slowdown across geographies; 60 APF projects added in Q1 (271 to 331 approved). Rates for new bank loans are 7.25-7.5% vs 6.95% last year. Special-rate threshold moved from INR 20 lakh to INR 25 lakh, customer re-rating parameters and EWS/OTMS monitoring added, and 82% of loans now have CIBIL above 700 (vs about 75% earlier). Expect some indirect rise in rejection ratios; 80% of business comes via DSA.

qa_highlights.question: Status of IT rollout (LOS, LMS, report generation) and any impact on disbursement targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Pilot in 5 branches went live on 8 July 2026 using 30 June data, processing sanctions, disbursements, NACH, BBPS and closures with only minor teething issues. Remaining 245 branches to move in month-end tranches (July, August, September), with a further update around September; INR 3,000 crore Q2 target unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and blended yield by segment; are there trade-offs by ticket size?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended yield 9.81% (9.82% last year). Best rate about 8.4% for salaried, CIBIL above 725, loans of INR 25 lakh plus; highest about 12.5% for non-salaried, non-housing, S3 customers.

qa_highlights.question: Housing vs non-housing and salaried vs self-employed growth; number of loans; run-rate going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Housing disbursements INR 1,650 crore (+28% YoY) and LAP INR 958 crore (+32%); salaried +21%, SENP +44%. Management gave amounts only, not loan account counts. FY27 disbursement target INR 13,000 crore unchanged, with a possible push to INR 13,200-13,400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the IT-sector hiring slowdown in Bangalore affecting home loan offtake or policy?
qa_highlights.answer: No major impact seen so far: Karnataka grew 18% YoY and Telangana slightly more (partly base effect). IT-sector customers are about 6% of the base, with top IT employers barely represented. Karnataka NPA was lower in absolute terms at March 2026 vs March 2025, with only a marginal June increase.

qa_highlights.question: Any opex surprises in FY27 and how far is APF exposure per project capped?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 40 crore of further IT-related cost to come, with AMCs and depreciation starting; salary, rent and other costs in line with last year. Cost-to-income about 19.5% for FY27, trending toward 18% in about three years. APF exposure capped at 10% of the book per project.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the book rundown elevated for four quarters, and is the 4% level the new normal? Also, how does the best-rate gap to banks affect pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crore (vs INR 976 crore) drove the rundown, as borrowers under change-in-tenure kept EMIs constant and paid down principal. BT-outs were INR 408 crore (vs INR 400 crore), and other closures INR 377 crore (vs INR 360 crore). Best rate gap widened from 55 bps to over 100 bps; management is exploring deposit conversion and bureau alerts for retention.

qa_highlights.question: Can ROA of about 2.4% and ROE of about 18% be achieved in FY27 given higher opex and the soft Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 ROA was 2.39% (2.53% last year) and ROE 18%+. Management said the cost impact is already visible and expects to manage ROA, with NIM and spread on track and credit cost not a concern. Q1 NPA rise was only INR 17-18 crore vs INR 45 crore last Q1 FY26.

risks_watch: Book rundown: part-prepayments of INR 1,857 crore in Q1 (INR 1,072 crore part-prepay) mean FY27 disbursements may need to exceed INR 13,000 crore to hold 14% AUM growth; Q2 target is INR 3,000 crore.

IT rollout: 245 remaining branches migrate in month-end tranches through September; update expected around September. Management noted 50-100 branches will need more handholding than the 5-branch pilot.
Cost of funds: new bank loans priced at 7.25-7.5% vs 6.95% last year; NIM guidance of 3.81%+ depends on incremental-only pass-through and yield mix shift.
Competitive pricing gap: best rate spread to banks/larger players widened to over 100 bps from 55 bps; LIC and Bajaj Housing (growing about 25-30% per analyst) are main rivals.
Asset quality: SENP current NPA about 1.45-1.5% vs about 0.6-0.63% for salaried; IT-sector and Karnataka exposure monitored with early-warning signals; credit cost guided at 10 bps.
Opex: cost-to-income moved from about 18% to 19%+ in Q1, FY27 guided near 19.5%; about INR 40 crore of further IT costs yet to come.
key_quotes: So against INR 2,500 crores, which was what was planned and what was projected, we have achieved INR2,609 crores.
So, we are confident that the NIM will be maintained at 3.81% plus and we should not have a problem in that.
And so the 10 bps that we have been talking about, definitely doesn't look to be a challenge this year.

The major challenge or the major portion from where our run down is happening is actually amortization and more importantly, part prepayment where customers are making more payments every month, and but the loans are still with us.
511196|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on disbursements, asset quality and the 14% AUM growth target, but cautious on the higher book rundown, the widened pricing gap to banks and the IT rollout's business impact. Management was candid about the rundown and competitive pressures, and it deferred on new product launches, saying the Board has not yet deliberated.

511196|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 disbursements fell to INR2,375 crore as Project Tejas IT migration hit branches; FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore held.
511196|2026-09.overview: Can Fin Homes completed the full go-live of Project Tejas (IT transformation) across all branches, with the final ~93 old branches and new branches moving live from 1 October 2026. Disbursements for the quarter were INR2,375 crore, net of about INR29 crore of NHB-mandated cancellation netting, and management attributed the shortfall to one-time migration and process changes plus a Telangana Section 22 verification issue. Management held FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore and AUM growth of 13-14%, and guided FY28 disbursement of INR16,000 crore with 15%+ AUM growth. Prepayments eased to INR1,795 crore from INR1,857 crore in Q1, and the company passed on a 10 bps housing rate hike effective 8 October 2026.

segments.name: Branches live on new system (Project Tejas)
segments.commentary: Rollout in phases: 11 branches in July (5 old, 6 new), 89 in August (75 old, 14 new), 77 old in September and 98 in October (93 old plus 5 new). Disbursements at branches during their go-live month dropped about 70-75%, recovering to 80-90% of prior run-rate the following month.

segments.name: Branches not yet migrated (93-branch cohort)
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursement was INR435 crore in Q1 and rose to INR454, INR458, INR424 and INR481 crore in the months of July-September per management's slide 20 data (management's figures; not independently verified).

segments.name: Sales team channel
segments.commentary: Sales team headcount about 90 now, targeted at 150 by year-end and 250 in FY28; management expects INR1,500-1,600 crore from sales in FY27 versus INR560 crore in H1.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Disbursement has stabilised at INR230-250 crore per period, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement guidance held at INR13,000 crore (20%+ growth over INR10,500 crore in FY26); Q3 target about INR3,500 crore with the shortfall to be recovered in Q4.
FY27 AUM growth guidance of 13-14%, closer to 14%; management said the 15% AUM growth figure for FY28 is a resultant of disbursement and rundown.
FY28 disbursement internal target INR16,000 crore (about 22% growth), implying 15%+ AUM growth, closer to 15.5%.

Spread and NIM guidance of 2.75% and 3.75% maintained; management said it will pass through rate hikes, with about 12-13 bps of liability cost increase on the full book from the 25 bps repo hike and 10 bps passed on so far.
FY27 credit cost guidance of 10 bps maintained; gross NPA expected to fall in H2.
Plans to draw NHB refinance earlier, from Q3 if sanctions are higher, to benefit from lower rates; exploring an additional refinance limit.
capex_capacity: Project Tejas fully live: LOS and LMS live across all branches as of 1 October 2026; modules including risk, ALM, borrowings (by September 2025 onward) and deposits/DMS (January) implemented per management.
25 of 28 branches planned for FY27 are already operational with staff; these are expected to contribute in Q3 and Q4.
Branch expansion: about 12 branches added in UP in the last year, per management.
About 129 staff who were deployed on the IT project are being redeployed to branches and departments, with some support retained for 1-2 months.
demand_pricing: Management said underlying demand is robust with no change, and attributed the Q2 shortfall to process changes (about 8-10 additional OTPs per borrower and co-borrower), a 5-day post-month data handover lag, and a new Telangana Section 22 sub-registrar verification requirement.
Housing loan rate raised by 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 (new customers from 12 October); about 87% of floating book is on quarterly reset, about 12-13% on annual reset.
Management expects a 25 bps repo hike to translate into about 12-13 bps on the book, with plans to pass on about 15 bps next time.

Prepayment rate was about 15.5-16% historically and about 17-17.5% recently; management said a 100 bps rise could narrow the rate gap by around 60 bps, reducing prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.
Higher-ticket (INR30 lakh+) loans have grown, and the company is also looking at AHF-linked INR15-25 lakh loans as NHB AHF share rises.
PMAY 2.0 uptake described as slow relative to CLSS-1, with limited presence in the high-need states (Odisha, Bengal, Bihar, UP).
Management said the sales team contributed INR560 crore in H1 FY27 and targets about 20% of disbursement from sales in FY28.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 was INR2,600 crore per management; Q2 shortfall vs planned INR3,000 crore
vs INR1,857 crore in Q1 FY27
vs INR40 crore in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Above 100% (regulatory minimum 100%); management cited range of 135% to 250%

FY26 full-year sales team contribution INR868 crore

qa_highlights.question: Why did the liquidity coverage ratio rise well above the 100% regulatory minimum, and what is a steady level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to lower short-term borrowings, now about 12% of borrowings versus 26-27% in March 2023, plus smaller bulk borrowings. LCR range cited as 135% to 250%; HQLA held at roughly INR2,300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Does a rising rate cycle affect home loan demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 25-50 bps move is a non-event for demand because EMI impact is limited on 15-year tenors. Rates of 7.15-8% are among the lowest seen, so customer behaviour is not expected to change much.

qa_highlights.question: Is there risk to FY27 disbursement target from the South monsoon or drought, and to asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is early to assess; drought has been declared in parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka, but the company lends mainly in Tier 1-2 areas. If industry slows, it could hit disbursement, and it may use LAP or construction top-ups as short-term levers.

qa_highlights.question: How will operational efficiency from Project Tejas play out in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited manual processes now automated, native AI features, auto form filling, and a digital sourcing channel expected to reach about 10% of business. Sales headcount to rise from about 90 to 150 this year without adding branch staff.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rate pass-through and prepayment outlook after the repo hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Housing rates rose 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 against a 25 bps repo hike, which translates to about 12-13 bps on the book. Management said a 100 bps rise could cut the rate gap by about 60 bps and reduce prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How reset timing works for bank borrowings and the loan book, and whether spread is at risk in a rising cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Repo-linked bank borrowings reprice from 1 November; T-bill-linked ones reset quarterly. About 87% of the floating book is on quarterly reset and 12-13% on annual, with roughly one-third repricing each on 1 November, 1 December and 1 January. Management said it will pass on hikes to protect spread and NIM.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management in the H2 disbursement ramp (about INR3,500 crore per quarter) and the FY28 AUM outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was INR2,600 crore against a planned INR2,500 crore, so the INR100 crore buffer was used; Q3 target is INR3,500 crore with about INR400 crore shortfall recovered in Q4. FY28 disbursement target of INR16,000 crore implies AUM growth of about 15-15.5%, with 15% described as a resultant figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the productivity ramp for new branches and the pipeline status?
qa_highlights.answer: New branches take about 18 months (range 18-24) to reach 5 cases per staff per month. Management said sanctioned-but-not-disbursed rose about INR118 crore quarter on quarter, and that some pipeline was lost during the migration.

risks_watch: Q3 disbursement delivery against the INR3,500 crore target, and whether the INR400 crore shortfall is recovered in Q4 as guided.
Spread and NIM protection: liability cost rising about 12-13 bps on the full book against 10 bps passed on so far; management plans a next hike of about 15 bps.
Asset quality: SMA-0 uptick attributed to a daily versus month-end overdue computation change; gross NPA is expected to fall in H2 and credit cost is guided at 10 bps against about 9 bps in Q2.
Monsoon and drought risk to construction activity and demand in Maharashtra and Karnataka, plus Telangana Section 22 verification delays.
Sales channel ramp from about 90 to 150 staff (and 250 in FY28) to deliver INR1,500-1,600 crore in FY27 versus INR560 crore in H1, and the digital channel target of 10%.
Liability mix: NCD pricing around 8.3-8.35% versus bank term loans at about 7.65%, and special-rate T-bill-linked borrowings that reset at varying times.
Prepayment trend (INR1,795 crore in Q2 versus INR1,857 crore in Q1) after the housing rate hike, and the NHB refinance draw (INR1,350 crore sanctioned, expected at about 6.6-6.7%).
key_quotes: The month in which the implementation has happened, the disbursements, they have dropped in that particular branches by about 70% to 75%, and then the next month, again, it pushes back and it comes back to almost 80% -90% of the old disbursement.

Basically, in terms of the demand or in terms of the business per se, there has been no change, but for the impact of the IT transformation, which is mainly on account of the understanding, or rather the change in the flow, the additional processes that have been incorporated.
We will be looking at a 20% plus growth in terms of the disbursement, which consequently should become a 13%- 14% AUM growth this year and a 15% plus AUM growth in the next year.
Basically, our endeavor will be to ensure that our NIM and spread and NIM stays protected.
511196|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the full-year guidance and long-term benefit of Project Tejas, while openly attributing the Q2 shortfall to one-time migration issues. Management was more hedged on the Telangana verification issue and monsoon risk ("it's a little early"), and it was evasive on the exact timing of the sales ramp and branch productivity.

511218|2026-06.headline: Shriram Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose 59.79% YoY to INR3,444.56 crores, with NIM at 9.04% and disbursements up 19.51% YoY to INR49,974 crores.
511218|2026-06.overview: Shriram Finance reported strong Q1 FY27 numbers, with PAT of INR3,444.56 crores (up 59.79% YoY, up 14.3% QoQ) and NII up 33.67% YoY to INR8,055.70 crores. Growth was supported by fresh equity of about INR39,600 crores, which cut the leverage ratio to 2.14x from 3.82x in March and funded repayment of borrowings. Management reiterated the FY27 AUM growth guidance of 18% but said it will reassess after Q2, and guided credit cost around 2% and operational NIM around 8.5% in the medium term. Asset quality was broadly stable, with gross Stage 3 at 4.64% against 4.58% in Q4 FY26. Management said the company will now deploy surplus liquidity into growth and return to borrowing, including securitisation, towards the end of the quarter.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 PV disbursement INR11,018 crores. Management cited industry PV sales growth of 25.9%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 MSME disbursement INR6,184 crores. Management targets MSME rising from about 15% to about 20% of the book, with growth expected to exceed the overall book.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 gold disbursement INR5,153 crores; gold is about 2.5% of the book, targeted at about 5% in three years, with about 2,200 branches gold-ready.

segments.commentary: Personal loans INR2,773 crores, 2-wheelers INR3,548 crores, construction equipment INR792 crores (about INR1,000 crores for five quarters), farm equipment INR947 crores.

Operational NIM expected around 8.5% in the medium term (2-3 years); current NIM of about 9% expected to hold for the next two quarters as surplus liquidity is deployed.
Credit cost guided at around 2% in the near and medium term.
Cost-to-income ratio to remain stable; about 150 branches to be added in FY27 without a material rise in cost.

511754|2026-03.headline: Shalibhadra Finance FY26 AUM rose 25% to ₹220 crore and PAT grew 21.67% to ₹19.48 crore; FY29 target is ₹500 crore AUM.

The company is moving from two-wheeler and vehicle finance into micro-LAP, LAP and home loans under its "Shalibhadra 2.0" strategy, with a branch expansion from 61 toward 100 branches. Management guided to lower ROA (about 7% within two to three years) and a rising share of nationalised bank borrowing to cut funding costs.

Management targets 10-15% overall growth over the next two to three years, described as a big achievement given uncertainty.
No major capex foreseen over the next two years; Hyderabad pet food plant awaits DPR and government approvals before construction.
Feed price increase to be announced within about 10 days of the call, to offset steep raw-material cost increases.
capex_capacity: Shrimp processing capacity is about 26,000-28,000 MT on paper, but the business is seasonal and utilisation is constrained by raw-material availability.
Management said it is not planning major capex in the next two years, but will raise capacity utilisation and add value-added products.
Pet food: land near Hyderabad converted to non-agricultural use; land development in progress, final designs and DPR under preparation, construction to start after government approvals.
Ecuador investment made in partnership with a local party (per management).
demand_pricing: Fish meal consumption price rose to INR 130/kg in Q4 FY26 from INR 117 in Q3 and INR 91 a year earlier; purchase price now INR 230/kg. Management said fish meal doubled from INR 100 to INR 240 over May and June.
Soya bean meal rose to INR 55/kg in Q4 FY26 from INR 44 in Q3 and INR 41 a year earlier; current purchase price INR 72/kg. Wheat flour eased to INR 31/kg from INR 32 in Q3.
A feed price increase was taken in February 2026 but had only one month of impact; a further increase is planned.
Frozen shrimp exports in FY25-26 were 7,92,647 MT worth USD 5,624.48 million; USA imports fell 17.9% in volume, while China rose 24% and EU 36%.
Company shrimp exports rose to 16,976 MT in FY26 from 14,149 MT in FY25.
Management said about 75% of India's fish meal output is exported, driven by price and government incentives; it is lobbying for export limits and to allow soya bean meal imports.

qa_highlights.question: Why does FY27 feed offtake of 11-12 lakh MT imply flat demand, and how will the feed division perform?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a price increase is being worked out against market acceptance, with a specific figure expected in about 10 days; farm economics are described as good and the second quarter is key.

qa_highlights.question: What is the quantum of the Q4 price hike and how will feed margins move in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the February price increase had limited Q4 impact, and another increase is planned to offset the steep fish meal and soya bean meal rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 export target of about 19,000 MT conservative versus peers and FTA benefits?
qa_highlights.answer: Executive director Nikhilesh said growth must be step by step given the business's build-up needs, citing quality and food-safety requirements for EU access.

qa_highlights.question: Is any major capex planned over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no big capex is foreseen in the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and cash burn of the pet care business?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume has risen from 53 to about 100 tonnes, with 31 distributors in 13 cities; own manufacturing is needed before cost benefits show, so the current focus is brand building.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US IEEPA tariff refund size and who is the importer of record?
qa_highlights.answer: Avanti Frozen Foods is the importer of record; refund claims are estimated at about USD 15-20 million, with processing expected to take time as anti-dumping reviews complete over 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there capacity headroom and why not expand faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Installed capacity is about 26,000-28,000 MT, but seasonal raw-material availability limits utilisation; management is focused on raising utilisation rather than adding capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the value-added shrimp mix changing, and will processing EBITDA margins rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said value-added products (ready-to-eat, breaded, Japanese preparations) are a larger share than 10 years ago and yield margins above the market average, though they reduce factory output.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and profit growth is expected over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 10-15% overall growth, but said it cannot yet give a firm FY27 budget due to uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioned versus Ecuador, the largest exporter?
qa_highlights.answer: India is the number two exporter; management is positive on the US and Europe markets after the tariff changes.

512573|2026-06.headline: Avanti Feeds Q1 FY27 consolidated PBT fell 37% YoY to INR 157 crore despite 19% higher gross income, as feed raw-material costs squeezed margins.
512573|2026-06.overview: Consolidated gross income rose 30% QoQ to INR 1,966 crore but PBT fell 15% QoQ to INR 157 crore and 37% YoY. The Feed division's gross income rose 27% YoY to INR 1,615 crore on 28,287 MT higher volume, yet PBT dropped 45% YoY to INR 114 crore as fish meal and soya bean meal prices surged. Feed PBT margin fell to 7.06% from about 13% in Q4 FY26 and 17% in Q1 FY26. Shrimp Processing and Export gross income fell 7% YoY to INR 350 crore, while PBT rose to INR 45 crore on better realisations and forex. Management took a roughly 10% feed price hike in June 2026 and said industry and government are working on a raw-material price mechanism.

segments.name: Shrimp Feed (standalone Feed division)
segments.commentary: Gross income INR 1,615 crore and PBT INR 114 crore on 1,93,852 MT of sales; PBT hit by higher fish meal (INR 153/kg avg vs INR 123 in Q4 and INR 93 in Q1 FY26) and soya bean meal (INR 58/kg vs INR 49 and INR 40).

segments.name: Shrimp Processing & Export (Avanti Frozen Foods)
segments.commentary: Gross income INR 350 crore, down 22% QoQ and 7% YoY on 15-16% lower volume; PBT INR 45 crore helped by better selling prices, favourable forex and higher other income. Realisations fell in Q4 after reciprocal tariffs were withdrawn from 24 February 2026.

segments.name: Pet food (Avant Furst, Avanti PetCare)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 180 lakh in Q1 FY27 vs INR 151 lakh in Q4 FY26; distribution in Tier 1 cities expanding to Tier 2/3, available on Amazon and Supertail. Land purchased near Hyderabad for a plant, about INR 25 crore spent of an estimated INR 175 crore.

guidance_outlook: Company feed sales estimated at about 5,85,000 MT in FY27, against 5,62,060 MT in FY26; analyst noted this implies roughly 5-6% annualised growth.
Shrimp exports estimated at about 19,000 MT in FY27, against 16,976 MT in FY26.
Management expects raw-material prices to stabilise in coming months as fresh crops arrive and monsoon eases El Nino effects, but called FY27 a challenging season for aquaculture.
On the Q2 question, management agreed that Q2 could be another weak quarter before the benefit of the price hike and any government intervention plays out.
Shrimp production estimated at 8-9 lakh MT in calendar 2026, with feed consumption estimated at 11-12 lakh MT.

Pet food capex estimated at about INR 175 crore in total, of which about INR 25 crore spent on land so far.
No feed capacity, utilisation or new feed plant commentary was given in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Arjun Khanna (Kotak MF) asked how farm-gate shrimp prices are trending given global protein inflation and rupee depreciation, and why shrimp prices have not moved up like other proteins.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said farm-gate prices balance global prices against processor/exporter economics and farmer affordability, and are fixed from time to time. It gave no specific reason for the lack of upward move; prices move with domestic availability and global demand.

qa_highlights.question: Khanna asked whether further feed price hikes are envisaged given rising input costs and margin pressure.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said any hike requires balancing farmer affordability and feed-industry sustainability, with the Andhra Pradesh government having a say. A government-formed committee with a big-four consultant is working on the pricing approach, and no further hike was committed.

qa_highlights.question: Khanna asked for an update on the US reciprocal tariff refund, where USD 15-20 million had earlier been mentioned.
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said refunds are stuck because the ADD/CVD review entries are under suspension and CBP will not process reciprocal tariff refunds until that is lifted. The company has declared the entries as its legal counsel and customs broker advised.

qa_highlights.question: Ronak Shah (Equirus) asked how farmers view current shrimp activity, given the 17% YoY feed volume growth and the 5-6% annualised growth implied by the FY27 target of 5.85 lakh MT.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shrimp culture is going well with favourable climate and good culture progress, with farm-gate prices up. The only concern is feed cost, and it hopes for raw-material price stabilisation in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Shah asked whether a price hike was taken in the last three to four months, whether more is planned, and whether formulation changes are being evaluated to mitigate ingredient volatility.
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed a price hike of around 10%, taken on 19 June 2026 and effective around 10 July. It is also working on formulation and quality to reduce raw-material usage without compromising feed quality or FCR.

qa_highlights.question: Shah asked for confirmation that Q2 could be another weak quarter before the price hike and government intervention play out.
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed with the summary, answering yes.

qa_highlights.question: Shah asked about the pet food capex cycle and investment to date.
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated about INR 175 crore total pet food investment, with about INR 25 crore spent so far on land.

risks_watch: Feed margin compression: Feed PBT margin at 7.06% vs about 13% in Q4 FY26 and 17% in Q1 FY26, with management conceding Q2 may be another weak quarter.
Price hike of around 10% (June 2026) may not offset raw-material costs; further hikes are subject to Andhra Pradesh government committee outcome and farmer affordability.
US reciprocal tariff refund (USD 15-20 million previously mentioned) on hold until ADD/CVD review suspension is lifted; timing unclear.
Shrimp export volumes: US volumes down 17.9% YoY in FY26 and FY27 export target of about 19,000 MT vs 16,976 MT; realisations hit after reciprocal tariffs were withdrawn from 24 February 2026.
Pet food capex of about INR 175 crore pending Consent for Establishment approval for the Hyderabad plant; construction timing depends on approval.

Monitor next quarter: fish meal and soya bean meal price trend (spot INR 225/kg and INR 71/kg), feed volumes against the 5.85 lakh MT FY27 target, and whether the Shrimp Processing segment sustains its PBT of INR 45 crore.
key_quotes: The PBT during the quarter stood at 7.06% on revenue as compared to about 13% during Q4 FY 26 and 17% during Q1 FY26.
The government has, in fact, constituted a committee with one of the big four consultants.
Around 10%, we have taken.
We are estimating around INR 175 crores investment in a pet food.

513023|2026-03.headline: Nava standalone PAT rose 116% to INR 911 crore in FY26, driven by overseas dividends and buyback proceeds, while consolidated profit was hit by a non-cash deferred tax charge at Maamba.
513023|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a strong year, with standalone PAT up 116% YoY to INR 911 crore on upstream dividends from overseas investments and buyback proceeds. Consolidated profitability was weighed down by a non-cash deferred tax charge at Maamba Energy Limited (MEL), driven by about 32% appreciation of the Zambian Kwacha. Q4 consolidated EBITDA fell QoQ, mainly on INR 18 crore lower other income and a planned shutdown at the Maamba plant. The board declared a record dividend of INR 8.50 per share.

segments.name: Power (Maamba Energy, Zambia)
segments.commentary: Management expects a higher PLF this year after Singareni coal prices fell around September 2025, letting the Telangana plant run year-round. Q4 had a planned Maamba shutdown that raised manufacturing and maintenance costs. Zambian receivables are being collected on time; about 10% of receivables still pending from ZESCO, expected within six months.

segments.name: Ferro alloys (Silico manganese)
segments.commentary: Pricing is under pressure from Indian surplus exports diverted to the domestic market after EU safeguard duties. About 40% of production is under yearly contracts with two Japanese mills and another 40-50% under quarterly fixed-base contracts with private steel producers. Ferro silicon has been discontinued. Next-year silico manganese volume guided at about 130,000 tons; capacity at full utilisation is about 160,000 tons.

segments.name: Agro (avocado and sugar)
segments.commentary: First commercial avocado harvest of about 150 tons this year; first sale of about 1,000 tons expected next year, doubling yearly until 2034. Peak agro revenue guided at about $22 million, with peak expected post-2032. Plantation Division D growth completes around FY-end.

segments.name: Solar (Maamba, 100 MW)
segments.commentary: Commissioning to start July 2026 at a tariff of $0.078 per unit. Expected incremental revenue of $20-22 million and EBITDA of $6-7 million. Equity contribution for solar is fully made; about $30 million of debt remains to be drawn.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 35-40% for the coming year, subject to Phase 2 ramp-up and loss of Phase 1 tax holidays.
Power realisation guided at about INR 5.50 per unit for the current year.
Maamba Phase 2 (300 MW expansion) commissioning expected early January 2027.
Solar 100 MW commissioning to begin July 2026.
Silico manganese production expected slightly up; pricing not expected to fall below prior-year levels as of now.
Management advised investors to model annual rather than QoQ performance.
Remaining $1.3 million of old receivable provision to be reversed next financial year.
capex_capacity: Phase 2 at MEL: 300 MW expansion, commissioning early January 2027; a large equity tranche still to be contributed.
Solar 100 MW: commissioning from July 2026; equity fully contributed, about $30 million debt still to be drawn.
Group equity commitment about $130 million, of which about $100 million is for Agri and about $17.5 million for Maamba Phase 2.
Agri-side debt of about $100 million to be raised; total incremental debt of about INR 1,200 crore across Agri and solar.

Africa mining: manganese exploration in Ivory Coast on a 360 sq km allocation; exploitation permit targeted within about one year. Lithium exploration in Zambia on hold pending a ministry review of a contested licence.
demand_pricing: India peak power demand expected to reach 277 GW; power exchange prices down 13% YoY, so the company is relying on bilateral contracts with better net realisations.
Ferro alloy prices track steel; surplus Indian supply and EU safeguard duties are pressuring prices, with a rebound possible if European and Middle East conditions improve.
Zambian Kwacha appreciation of about 32% created a non-cash deferred tax charge; management says the cash position is unaffected.
Zambia requires local employee pay and contracts in Kwacha by statutory instrument, though power assets remain USD-based; coal sales are in Kwacha, partly offsetting employee cost increase.
Employee cost increase attributed to ESOPs, the labour code and normal wage hikes; management said the increase is sustainable subject to increments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned use of the INR 1,347 crore financial assets and the remaining equity and debt needs?
qa_highlights.answer: Assets are mainly in liquid mutual funds and debt products, earmarked for agro projects funded from Indian corpus. Group equity commitment about $130 million; agri debt about $100 million; solar debt about $30 million; Maamba Phase 2 equity about $17.5 million.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tariff and NBEIL FY26 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar tariff is $0.078. NBEIL FY26 revenue INR 442 crore, PBT INR 80 crore, PAT INR 59 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated EBITDA margin fall QoQ, and what margin should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower other income of INR 18 crore and a planned Maamba shutdown raised costs. Management guided 35-40% EBITDA margin, citing Phase 2 and Phase 1 tax holiday loss.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for silico manganese volumes and ferro alloy pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Next-year silico manganese volume guided at about 130,000 tons versus 134,000 tons last year; ferro silicon discontinued. Prices remain fluid but management sees no fall versus prior year as of now.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs jump and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by ESOPs, labour code changes and wage hikes. Management said the increase is sustainable, subject to normal increments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the land monetisation plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Nacharam (Telangana) and Dharmavaram land under review; options include sale or JV with a third-party adviser. Management declined to give a value range.

risks_watch: Consolidated profit hit by non-cash deferred tax on Kwacha appreciation; reversal depends on FX movement.
Zambian elections in August 2026 could affect the operating environment.
Ferro alloy spot pricing pressure from surplus supply and EU safeguard duties; about 10-15% of volumes exposed to spot.

Lithium licence in Zambia is contested and on hold pending ministry review.
Roughly INR 1,200 crore of new debt needed for Agri and solar projects.

513023|2026-06.headline: Nava Q1 FY27 consolidated total income hit an all-time quarterly high of INR1,269 crore; Phase 2 thermal (MEL) slips to Q2 FY28-29 commissioning.
513023|2026-06.overview: Management reported record consolidated total income of INR1,269 crore for Q1 FY27, with standalone total income at a record INR689 crore, helped by lower coal and manufacturing costs and dividend income from Nava Global. The 300 MW MEL plant ran at an 89.3% PLF. Phase 2 thermal commissioning has been pushed by a couple of months to around July 2027 (Q2 FY28, per management wording) due to logistics delays on critical equipment linked to the geopolitical conflict. A 100 MW solar project is slated for commissioning by end-September 2026. Management did not disclose consolidated profit or margin figures in the call.

segments.name: Energy (MEL 300 MW, Zambia)
segments.commentary: MEL 300 MW plant operated at 89.3% PLF. Zambia energy sustainable EBITDA margin cited at 45-50%, with recent decline attributed to lower reversal of ECL credit.

segments.name: Metals (manganese/ferro-alloys)
segments.commentary: Nikhil Devineni said quarterly sales dipped as the Orissa unit was under long-term maintenance shutdown; it resumed operations on 1 August 2026. Spot pricing up about 5-10% QoQ; around 70% of production committed under long-term or quarterly contracts.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.commentary: Consolidated EBITDA expected at 35-40% of segment EBITDA after intersegment eliminations. Zambia reported on 100% consolidation basis.

guidance_outlook: MEL Phase 2 thermal (2 units): full commissioning by Q2 FY28 (around July 2027); first unit slightly earlier; no material capex impact stated.
MEL Phase 2 expected revenue about INR200 million; project cost INR400 million, funded INR300 million debt and INR100 million equity.
100 MW solar project to be commissioned by end-September 2026; management expects it to open a new niche and further investment in solar.
Sugar plant (Zambia) commissioning targeted Q4 FY28, with revenue of INR55-60 million per annum.
Expected return on equity on the new 300 MW phase about 15%; no tax holiday currently for Phase 2, company pursuing one with government.
Metals margins expected to be stable or slightly higher; no downward trend seen until end of FY27.
Dividend policy of at least 30% of PAT (stated as Nava Global policy).

100 MW solar project: commissioning by end-September 2026.
Zambia projects in implementation: thermal energy, renewable energy, avocado and sugar; some expected to yield revenue shortly.
Exploration: lithium (Zambia) slowed by elections; manganese concession of 360 sq km with detailed exploration on only 2 sq km, now moving to exploitation licence.
Management said Phase 2 Maamba commissioning is later than originally envisaged but no material impact on capex.
Maamba bi-annual maintenance shutdown scheduled in the current quarter.

Management described metals as volume-driven rather than margin-driven; sales were lower in Q1 due to Orissa shutdown.
Zambia operations reported as fine with no power disruptions from West Asia crisis.
Management flagged significant challenges from geopolitical and supply-chain disruption and said remedial actions are being taken.

qa_highlights.question: Expected commissioning and revenue from thermal Phase 2 expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Full commissioning of both units by Q2 FY28 (around July 2027); Phase 2 revenue about INR200 million; margins not disclosed, with tariff described as attractive.

qa_highlights.question: Why are land assets carried at historical cost and what is their current value?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Accounting Standards allow historical cost; management has engaged a third party to study current asset values and options, and declined to give a number.

qa_highlights.question: Is funding available for new power projects (solar, wind, SMR) and is Zambia spin-off planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all current projects are adequately funded from equity and cash, with no need to sell assets. Nava Limited is 100% ultimate owner of Nava Global; Zambia assets were always under Nava Global.

qa_highlights.question: Why was consolidated deferred tax high and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Deferred tax INR40 crore this quarter vs INR163 crore prior quarter, linked to Kwacha-USD rate; CFO said it may reverse depending on exchange rate on reporting date.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Zambia energy EBITDA margin declined and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower reversal of ECL credit; sustainable EBITDA margin around 45-50%.

qa_highlights.question: How is consolidated EBITDA derived from segment EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Intersegment transfer pricing (power-metals and coal from mines) is eliminated; consolidated EBITDA is around 35-40% of segment EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is Phase 2 finance cost capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, finance cost on Phase 2 is capitalised, as required under Ind AS and IFRS.

qa_highlights.question: Why is metals sales flat and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Orissa unit shutdown reduced Q1 sales; unit resumed on 1 August 2026. Margins expected stable or slightly up through FY27.

513097|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12.3% to ₹570.9 crore and EBITDA margin expanded ~250 bps to 22.9%, with a PAT of ₹95.8 crore (+24.8%).
513097|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as a shift toward value-added components, assemblies and OEM/Tier-1 engagement, with consolidated EBITDA up 26.0% to ₹130.7 crore. Standalone revenue grew on broadly flat volumes, which management attributed to better realisation (shunt component mix moving from ~55% to ~65%, ~10-12% realisation uplift). Contacts (silver-based) grew sharply, but management said only about 30-31% of the ~54-60% growth was underlying volume, with the rest from silver price pass-through. 513228|2026-03.headline: Pennar Q4 FY26 PAT rose 14.91% to INR41.04 crores on total income of INR933.7 crores; management commits to 20% PAT growth in FY27.
513228|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income rose 2.26% to INR933.7 crores while EBITDA grew 15.27% to INR114 crores and PAT grew 14.91% to INR41.04 crores, with PAT margin at 4.44% versus 3.9%. FY26 was a record year: total income INR3,666 crores (up 12.33%), PAT INR138.83 crores (up 16.22%), PAT margin 3.83% versus 3.7%. Management attributed the Q4 revenue slowdown to revenue slipping into Q1 and a solar hit in diversified engineering, and blamed labour shortages for PEB India underperformance in FY26. Working capital rose to 82 days, and gross debt-to-equity rose to 0.98x, both of which management is targeting to reduce.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Vriddhi savings flow-through to P&L?

A&P spend more than doubled year-on-year, which management said front-loaded investment and weighed on quarterly profitability. Renewables is now reported as a separate segment and is growing rapidly, while switchgear sales fell about 4% YoY with margin erosion of around 260 bps.
