532175|2026-03.headline: Cyient Semiconductors signed a definitive deal for INR300 crore external funding at INR4,650 crore equity valuation (~$500M), first tranche, from EAAA Alternatives.
532175|2026-03.overview: Cyient Semiconductors, the carved-out unit of Cyient Ltd, signed a definitive agreement for INR300 crore of funding from EAAA Alternatives (formerly Edelweiss Alternatives), described as the first tranche of an external raise. Management said the deal is a combination of INR200 crore debt and INR100 crore equity, and that the valuation is about 6-7x revenue on FY26 or FY27 revenue. The company completed the ~$85 million Kinetic Technologies acquisition in March/April 2026, funded through debt raised at a Singapore entity, and now carries about $100 million of semiconductor-level debt (about $80M foreign currency, $20M Indian). Breakeven guidance for the unit is late FY27 to early FY28, with management signalling possible slippage of a quarter or two in favour of growth investment. The call was a management-led Q&A focused on funding structure, valuation and product mix rather than reported quarterly financials.

segments.name: Power ASSP (incl. Kinetic)
segments.commentary: Management says Power ASSP including Kinetic is roughly 50-60% of business; ASSP gross margin expected at 50-60%, the highest of the three segments. ASSP revenue share expected to rise over 3-4 years given 2-3 year R&D cycles.

segments.name: Custom ASIC turnkey
segments.commentary: Remainder of business is split between services and ASIC turnkey, with ASIC expected to grow fastest near term. ASIC pipeline is ~$100 million of qualified opportunities, mainly industrial and medical; primarily on TSMC 180nm.

segments.name: Semiconductor design services
segments.commentary: Remaining share of revenue with the lowest gross margin of the three segments, per management ranking. No separate figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Breakeven still targeted at late FY27 to early FY28 (EBIT basis); management may come back after investor conversations and flagged a quarter or two of slippage is acceptable.
PAT profitability timing not given; management said EBIT comes first.
Parent committed to total ~$100 million investment in Cyient Semiconductors; ~$70 million remaining, to be deployed case by case, including possible co-investment in design.
FY27 focus: execution at scale, integrating Kinetic, accelerating ASSP roadmap, converting ASIC and ASSP into sustained revenue growth, and higher sales-channel spend.
Management expects semiconductor-level debt rather than further equity for now, and flagged a possible future spin-off path.
capex_capacity: Funds to be used for R&D, lab infrastructure and working capital, per management.
Kinetic is described as a fully operational fabless platform with ~250 products and ~100 IP/patents.
Seven GaN products launched in India with Navitas, primarily 650V class.
Four patents filed in FY26 on high-voltage DC architecture for AI data centres.
Custom ASICs primarily on TSMC 180nm Gen2; some 40/55nm microcontroller work at TSMC, with transition to GlobalFoundries planned.
demand_pricing: ASIC and ASSP pipeline of ~$100 million of qualified opportunities, mainly industrial and medical end markets.
Selected as L1 bidder on SCL semiconductor modernisation initiative (India government programme).
Power semiconductor addressable market cited at ~$8.5 billion.
Management cites data centre power share rising from 2% (2025) to 8% (2030), without quantifying Cyient's share.

Valuation benchmarks cited: listed semiconductor peers 5-15x revenue; recent M&A upwards of 10x revenue; listed Indian services company ~7x. 800V architecture work is at early OCP stage with no order visibility.

qa_highlights.question: Is there Navitas or NVIDIA-related business expected this year or next?
qa_highlights.answer: Navitas is on the NVIDIA board reference design; Cyient is working with Navitas on GaN in India, and 800V architecture work is early, with no specific orders given.

qa_highlights.question: Distribution route for Navitas parts in India?
qa_highlights.answer: A new India sales head (ex-Arrow and TI) was hired last week and is evaluating distributors; expected to be resolved in about a month.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue mix and margins across the three segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Power ASSP incl. Kinetic is ~50-60% of business; ASSP gross margin ~50-60%, then ASIC turnkey, then services. ASIC expected to grow fastest near term.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kinetic fully fabless and how is the funding handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Kinetic is fully fabless. Parent has put in ~$30M of the $100M commitment; more funding possible, with a preference for Semicon's own capital structure.

qa_highlights.question: Is breakeven still FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Still late FY27 to early FY28, but management may shift a quarter or two to prioritise growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt rate and split, and how was Kinetic funded?
qa_highlights.answer: INR200 crore debt and INR100 crore equity; rate not disclosed as deal not closed. Kinetic was funded entirely by debt raised at the Singapore entity.

qa_highlights.question: Will short product cycles hurt ASIC and ASSP revenue durability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said close customer ties give visibility about 9-11 months ahead, and continued R&D investment is needed to keep pace.

qa_highlights.question: Currency split of the ~$100M semiconductor-level debt?
qa_highlights.answer: About $80M foreign currency (Kinetic acquisition debt) and $20M Indian rupee (new transaction).

risks_watch: Breakeven timing may slip beyond late FY27/early FY28 as growth investment continues.
Dilution and valuation: INR4,650 crore valuation rests on IP and roadmap, not current revenue; further partners are under discussion.
Leverage: ~$100M debt at the semiconductor unit, with a portion at unspecified rates; interest cost and cash burn not disclosed.
Product cycle risk: fast chip generations (6-9 months, per analyst) could erode ASIC/ASSP revenue.
Execution: Kinetic integration, India distribution set-up, and conversion of L1 SCL bid and $100M pipeline into orders.
Dependence on Navitas and GaN roadmap for 650V and 800V products.

Management was openly flexible on breakeven timing.

We're not in a rush, and we're not going to dilute for the sake of dilution.

532175|2026-06.headline: Cyient Q1 FY27: DET revenue $162.5M, down 0.5% QoQ in constant currency, while DET EBIT margin rose to 13.2% and the 15% target slipped to H1 FY28.

Management pushed out its 15% EBIT target from Q4 FY27 to around H1 FY28 because revenue ramp-up is lagging, and it said mid-single-digit FY27 growth is now hard to achieve. Group revenue was $219M (+4.5% QoQ, +9.1% YoY in constant currency), with Kinetic Technologies consolidated for the first time.

segments.commentary: Revenue $162.5M, -0.5% QoQ cc, with normalized EBIT margin of 13.2% (+79 bps QoQ). Transportation & mobility grew 3% QoQ and 14.8% YoY cc, while strategic units fell 8.2% QoQ on energy weakness.

segments.name: Cyient DLM
segments.commentary: Management said the quarter closed with its highest-ever order book and book-to-bill above 1.5, with double-digit EBITDA margins for four consecutive quarters. No DLM financial figures were given on the call.

segments.name: Semiconductor
segments.commentary: Combined revenue $17.9M including Kinetic ($10.4M). Organic business $7.5M (+5% QoQ). Management expects breakeven only in FY28, with about $3M per quarter of Kinetic-related amortisation to cover.

guidance_outlook: 15% DET EBIT target now expected about H1 FY28 rather than Q4 FY27, because revenue ramp-up is behind plan while cost levers are on track.
No formal revenue guidance; management said mid-single-digit growth for FY27 will be challenged and it is 'hopeful' of meaningful growth returning in H2 FY27.
Full-year DET effective tax rate expected at 27-28%.
Semiconductor breakeven expected in FY28; high-voltage/high-power ASSP development to consume cash for at least the next four to five quarters.
TAO Digital Solutions closing expected by August 2026 (late Q2); TAO revenue expected at roughly $40-50M, with consolidation from about late Q2.
Investor Day scheduled for 25 August 2026 in Mumbai.
capex_capacity: DET capex was higher in Q1 due to a cyclical IT system refresh and project ramp-up.
Management chose not to cut investments, including in the high-power semiconductor ASSP program, which it says is funded organically and absorbs most of the cash flow.
Semiconductor: seven new GaN-powered chips launched on Navitas technology; custom ASIC pipeline above $100M.
Share buyback completed: 6.4M shares at Rs 1,125 (Rs 720 Cr, about 5.76% of paid-up capital), settled after the quarter ended.

Existing-business renewals were weak because of project completions, delayed restarts of discretionary projects and customer hesitancy, which management described as timing rather than structural.

Energy: the prior large single project has completed; management expects one to two more quarters before growth rebounds, with cross-selling into North America under way and nuclear engineering wins expected in one to two quarters.
Telecom/connectivity: fibre build-out capex is seen as visible, but Q1 was affected by delayed program starts and fiscal-year seasonality.
Aerospace: no impact yet on business-as-usual work, but flying-hour concerns from the West Asia conflict have stopped some discretionary projects.
Management did not disclose or quantify pricing changes; it cited customer rate increases as one lever for margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is Strategic Units at the bottom after two quarters of decline, or is there more impact from delayed discretionary spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Energy is the one market still soft; management expects one or two more quarters before growth rebounds and aims to narrow the gap or make it flat next quarter. Other strategic-unit verticals are delivering adequate results.

qa_highlights.question: Is Transportation & Mobility growth driven by a single project or a broader sector trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Not one project. Aerospace, rail and automotive each grew QoQ and at double digits YoY, so growth is broad-based.

qa_highlights.question: How will semiconductor breakeven come through, including PAT, given Kinetic acquisition debt, and what is growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven expected only in FY28. High-voltage ASSP development will consume cash for at least four to five more quarters, and about $3M per quarter of Kinetic-related amortisation must be covered. Growth expected to stay strong, with custom ASIC pipeline above $100M.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the energy vertical lost momentum versus peers that are winning deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier growth was built on one very large project, now completed. Management cited three fixes: a rebuilt go-to-market team, prioritised offerings, and a broader service portfolio, with a multi-year digitalisation deal with a large energy OEM as an example.

qa_highlights.question: Will DET revenue growth turn positive from Q2 and accelerate through FY27? Also, when will the 15% EBIT margin be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth will build slowly over the quarters. On margin, cost levers are on track but absorption from growth will come late. Management expects 15% to be reached around H1 FY28, a couple of quarters into next year, and wage-hike decisions will be taken at the start of H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue outlook for FY27, including TAO once consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: There was no formal guidance; the aim was mid-single-digit growth, which is now challenged. Management is hopeful of meaningful growth in H2 FY27 but gave no landing figure. TAO is expected to close in late Q2 with revenue of about $40-50M.

qa_highlights.question: Why was existing-business renewal weak despite strong order intake?
qa_highlights.answer: Project-based work ended (mostly planned), discretionary restarts were delayed, and customers were hesitant to commit. Management called this timing rather than structural.

NIM expected at 3.65-3.70% over the next few quarters as cost of deposits rises about 5 bps; long-term view 3.70-3.75%.
Cost of deposits guided at 5.60-5.70%; borrowing cost of about Rs 94 crore per quarter for the next two quarters.

AI-led automation invested in operations; management expects it to lower cost further.

Business enterprise (non-MSME, no Udyam registration) loans at Rs 18,827 million; large-industry book fell from Rs 22,500 million (Dec-25) to about Rs 15,000 million then rose to Rs 19,000 million on exits and yield pressure.

Term deposit rates expected to rise on high demand; FCNR window brought in fresh deposits of Rs 150 crore.
SMA-0/1/2 at 1.20%/0.70%/0.90% (total 2.85%), down from 7.12% in June 2025 and 10.78% in September 2024. Domestic consumption said to be insulated from West Asia stress.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins move beyond the near-term cost-of-funds increase (FY27-FY28 levers), given stagnant lending yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to MSME, gold and retail secured yields (agri gold ~10-10.5%, non-agri 11-11.5%, LAP 9.60-9.70%, MSME 9.30-9.40%) and a low-cost deposit franchise; long-term NIM view 3.70-3.75%. The Q1 cost-of-funds decline was attributed to better repricing and lower borrowing cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is MSME growing about 15% when system MSME growth is above 20%? Is utilisation falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Rs 900 crore monthly repayments, MSME utilisation down to 70% from a 73-74% norm, and slightly more cautious pricing. Guidance is MSME growth 2-3% above system, with MSME at 55-60% of book.

qa_highlights.question: What slippage and credit cost levels are sustainable over one to two years?

qa_highlights.question: How will the bank reach 25-30% higher growth with the mix intact (gold 31-32%, MSME 55-60%, retail 10%), and what is the MSME outlook?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in cost of funds despite lower deposit costs, and what is the treasury and borrowing cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing cost rose to Rs 94 crore from Rs 72.5 crore in 4QFY26; treasury gains were Rs 52.54 crore vs Rs 29 crore in 4QFY26. Borrowing cost is guided at about Rs 94 crore per quarter for the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How is the bank participating in ECLGS, and how is the ECL provisioning assessed?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 800 crore disbursed to date (Rs 200 crore last quarter); total expected Rs 2,000-2,500 crore. ECL provision about 0.45% of loan book, with CAR consumption capped at 0.65%; flow impact described as negligible given the secured book.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income decline and how will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income was down about 15% YoY (analyst cited 19% in one comparison). Management expects catch-up in Q2-Q4 from processing fees, suit recoveries and insurance income; non-treasury other income was Rs 243 crore in Q1 vs roughly Rs 300 crore in Q4 last year.

risks_watch: Utilisation trend in MSME (70% in Q1 vs 73-74% norm) and whether the European trade-agreement recovery in textiles materialises.
Cost of deposits moving to 5.60-5.70% and the ~5 bps NIM hit; NIM guided 3.65-3.70%, below the 3.78% reported in Q1.
Cost-to-income rising to 47-48% for FY27 from 45.42% as staff hikes start from July; exit ROA 1.60-1.65% depends on fee income recovery.
Gold loan pricing: management ruled out rate hikes, so growth is supported only by volume; agri gold LTV around 62% with sensitivity to gold price drops.
West Asia stress and SMA trends (SMA-0/1/2 total 2.85%) and ECLGS-linked disbursements that may affect future asset quality.
Large-industry book volatility (Rs 22,500 million in Dec-25, down to ~Rs 15,000 million, then ~Rs 19,000 million) and the non-MSME business enterprise book of Rs 18,827 million.
key_quotes: For 1QFY27 as well, we have achieved 25% credit growth quarter-on-quarter, the highest growth rate in June-to-June and our advances had increased to Rs. 67,645 crores from Rs. 54,020 crores in 1QFY26.
So, the trend of recovery more than slippages continues, and we are confident of maintaining recovery more than slippages for the next quarter as well, which is the current quarter.

It was cautious on margins, cost-to-income and fee income, and deflected on the MSME utilisation decline and gold pricing rather than offering new numbers.

532218|2026-06.headline: South Indian Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 17% YoY to INR378 crore, with record NII of INR1,025 crore and NIM of 3.23%.
532218|2026-06.overview: Net profit grew 17% YoY to INR378 crore, and net interest income hit a record INR1,025 crore, up 23% YoY and INR110 crore QoQ. NIM recovered to 3.23%, up 28 bps QoQ and 20 bps YoY, helped by repricing of high-cost deposits, CASA growth and a 50% cut in bulk deposits. Gross advances grew 17% YoY and gross NPA fell to 1.38%. Non-interest income was soft: core fees fell to INR179 crore from INR191 crore in Q4, and management called this a one-off. Management said the call was the last for MD and CEO P.R. Seshadri, who is leaving.

segments.name: Business loans (MSME)
segments.commentary: Business loans rose to INR14,391 crore from INR12,660 crore; growth was 18% excluding a INR554 crore charge-off. Management said MSME growth was muted versus expectations this quarter.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book reached INR24,930 crore, up 43% YoY, with average LTV of 65.25% and average ticket size of INR2.94 lakh. QoQ growth was only about 0.8% because co-lending and portfolio purchases of about INR270 crore ran off after an RBI circular effective April 1.

segments.name: Mortgages, home and auto loans
segments.commentary: Mortgage loans grew 34% YoY, home loans 19% and auto loans 34%, excluding IBPC/DA impact.

segments.name: Corporate book
segments.commentary: Corporate lending grew in Q1 as pricing hardened on short-tenor facilities. Corporate is about 40% of the loan book against a stated long-run target of about 30%.

guidance_outlook: NIM: no numeric guidance. Management believes the rate cycle has turned, so NIM should harden as repo changes pass through on a T+1 basis. Management also said the sharp deposit-repricing gains are unlikely to repeat.
Opex: management expects full-year opex growth of about 5-6% and aims for positive operating leverage for the full year. Q1 did not have positive operating leverage.
Fees: management called the fee decline a one-off. Trade and FX platform is expected to go live by end-September 2026.
Slippage: management expects FY27 slippage of INR500-750 crore, with INR800 crore as the maximum even with West Asia stress. Recoveries are expected at INR800-1,000 crore.
Credit cost: management said the 9 bps Q1 cost is probably generous and could moderate.
ROA: management said ROA should move from 100-110 bps toward 120-125 bps over time. No explicit ROE target was given, and the CEO declined a firm multi-year number.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion restarting on a small scale after about 3 years of freeze; branch count had fallen slightly and is being rebuilt in key locations.
Trade and FX digital platform targeted to go live by end-September 2026, covering FX bookings, LCs, guarantees and export/import bill settlement.

Capital: management plans to grow the balance sheet at market growth plus about 2%, shifting mix toward higher risk-weight retail and MSME assets. Risk density is expected to rise, so CRAR will fall from 19.62% over time.
demand_pricing: Deposit costs fell as high-rate deposits repriced down 40-60 bps between January and June 2026. Average CASA grew 19%, and bulk deposits were cut about 50% YoY.
Asset yields rose 5 bps, helped by mix shift, T-bill-linked corporate pricing and firmer corporate pricing on short-tenor loans. Retail pricing did not move up.

FCNR(B) deposits grew about 6% QoQ. Management expects a large share of inflows in August and September before the scheme closes on September 30. Inflows are unlevered because the bank has no external credit lines or GIFT City entity.
Recoveries of INR179 crore in Q1 against slippages of INR128 crore. Q1 is seasonally weak for recoveries.
SMA-1 and SMA-2 rose about INR80 crore QoQ. Management called it seasonal and said the constituents are reversible.
ECLGS: limit of about INR400 crore, disbursed about INR238 crore, with utilised book of about INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp fall in cost of deposits and the yield rise on advances, and what is the NIM outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: High-rate deposits repriced 40-60 bps, CASA grew, and bulk deposits were halved. Yield gains came from mix shift and T-bill-linked corporate pricing. Management gave no numeric NIM guidance, but expects NIMs to harden if the rate cycle has turned.

qa_highlights.question: Will opex and hiring rise for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Branch rollout is restarting in key locations. Opex growth is expected at about 5-6% for the year, with positive operating leverage targeted for the full year after Q1 lacked it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income soften, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Core fees fell to INR179 crore from INR191 crore, partly from a product renewal fee-charging error that will be fixed. Treasury income fell to INR44 crore and Q1 FY26 PSLC sale income of about INR60 crore did not recur. Management called this an aberration.

qa_highlights.question: Why is corporate share about 40% against a 30% target?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate pricing improved and liquidity was available, so the bank added short-tenor, high-quality corporate loans. Management still intends to reduce corporate exposure over the long run.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost run rate, and what about SMA-1/2 and ECL?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost was 9 bps. Management called that generous and expects moderation. FY27 slippage is seen at INR500-750 crore. Management expects no material NII impact from ECL effective-interest changes.

qa_highlights.question: Is FCNR(B) growth sustainable after June, and what is the landed cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflows are strong and expects most in August-September. Pricing matches domestic rupee liquidity levels. Landed cost was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for excess capital and the ROA and ROE path?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance sheet to grow at market growth plus about 2%, with mix shifting to higher risk-weight retail and MSME. ROA target path is 100-110 bps moving toward 120-125 bps; no firm ROE guidance was given.

risks_watch: Leadership transition: the MD and CEO is leaving, and management declined to commit to multi-year ROA or ROE targets that would bind a successor.
NIM tailwind may fade: management said the sharp deposit-repricing benefit is unlikely to repeat at the same scale.
Corporate exposure at about 40% of the book, above the 30% target, with West Asia uncertainty cited.
Gold loan QoQ growth was only about 0.8% after the RBI circular, and bulk-deal run-off is ongoing.
FCNR(B) inflows depend on the Dubai rep office permissibility and on foreign bank credit lines that have not yet materialised.
SMA-1/2 rose about INR80 crore QoQ; management attributes this to seasonality, but the trend needs monitoring.
Fee income recovery: management has to show that core fees rebound from INR179 crore and that the trade/FX platform goes live by end-September.

key_quotes: And so now we are in a position where our belief is the rate cycle has switched. So it's more likely to increase than to reduce.
We think that the 9 basis points that we currently have is probably on a generous side.
So with respect to fees, my own view is that it's a one-timer. We shouldn't read this as something that is going to last forever.

532218|2026-09.headline: South Indian Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 21% YoY to INR426 crore, with NIM at 3.33% and gross NPA at 1.24%.
532218|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 net profit was INR426 crore, up 21% YoY from INR351 crore, the bank's highest quarterly profit as stated. Deposits grew 19% YoY to INR1,37,279 crore and gross advances grew 19% to INR1,09,517 crore (about 20% excluding the INR1,163 crore technical write-off last year). NIM rose 10 bps QoQ to 3.33%, ROA was 1.08% and ROE 14%. Management said credit cost rose to 0.14% from a conservative top-up in account-level provisions, not a specific one-off, and that the current-account jump was partly one-off IPO-related inflows. The call also covered the new MD and CEO transition from P.R. Seshadri, the 15-16% growth guidance and the medium-term ROA and NIM targets.

financial_highlights.change: +19% YoY from INR92,286 crore; about 20% excluding technical write-off
Analyst calculated about 60 bps on a different basis

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate share of advances fell to 39% from 40%. Management targets about 35%, and corporate loans are priced off repo and T-bills, with new bookings up 25-30 bps over three months.

segments.name: Retail, agri and MSME
segments.commentary: Now 61% of advances. Retail, MSME and agri disbursements are growing faster than wholesale. Retail is targeted to grow faster than corporate.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about INR26,000 crore (INR15,000 crore retail, INR10,000 crore agri), growing about 41%, with 25% of advances. Blended yield about 10%; retail yields at most 25 bps above agri. Target is 30-32% of advances in the first phase, then 35%.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: Miscellaneous income of INR190 crore includes INR73 crore recovery from technically written-off accounts and bancassurance income of INR30-35 crore per quarter. Core fees are about INR198 crore and treasury forex about INR80 crore.

demand_pricing: Current account balances rose 20% QoQ, partly from one-off IPO-related inflows at quarter end; management expects some slippage in CASA.
Bulk deposit growth reflected cheaper bulk rates after FCNR(B) inflows. Deposit repricing is expected to be limited in the next two quarters because rates are lower than a year ago.
Around 43% of the book is EBLR-linked (20-23% repo or T-bill linked), with MCLR about 5% and fixed about 47%. EBLR loans reprice on repo changes almost immediately.
Repo rate was raised by 25 bps. New corporate bookings reflect this, but gold loan spreads have not been raised yet.
Third-party distribution is about 5-7% of fee income, so the IRDAI bancassurance draft circular has limited impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise and was there any floating or contingent provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no specific one-off. The higher provisions were account-based and conservative, with no floating or contingent provisions. ECL impact is expected to be modest given low SMA and NPA levels.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 20% QoQ rise in current account balances?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly one-off IPO-related inflows at quarter end. Some slippage is expected, though core CASA growth is stable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15-16% growth guidance be met and can the bank outpace the system?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will aim for the higher end of 15-16% and grow faster than the market if it is above the market. Retail is to grow faster than corporate, with corporate share targeted down to about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank planning to raise capital?
qa_highlights.answer: No capital raise is planned at 19.40% CAR. The Board has approved INR500 crore of Tier 2 bonds, and capital needs will be reassessed once growth picks up.

qa_highlights.question: Can opex growth stay in single digits while the bank expands branches?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth will be lower than loan growth, not substantially higher. Cost-to-income is targeted at about 50%, with income growth expected to absorb the added branch and hiring costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rate sensitivity of the investment book?
qa_highlights.answer: Each 1 bp move in yields changes MTM by about INR1-1.1 crore. NII benefits from repo hikes through EBLR loans and new gold loans at higher rates.

key_quotes: And definitely, our endeavour will be to move towards 3.40% to 3.50% in the medium to long term horizon.
But there is no major technology overhaul or anything -- any of that things are required.

Cost-to-income targeted at about 50%; opex growth to remain below loan growth, with no substantial opex rise despite about 11 branches opened in H1 FY27.
Corporate share of advances targeted at about 35% (from 39%), with retail growing faster than corporate; gold loans targeted at 30-32% of advances in the first phase and then 35%.

Recovery from technically written-off accounts expected at INR50-55 crore per quarter for the current year, declining over 4-6 quarters as the stock of recoverable NPAs is exhausted; bancassurance income expected at INR30-35 crore per quarter and sustainable.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion: about 11 branches opened in the first two quarters of FY27; management said opex will grow with hiring and branch additions but more slowly than loans.
IT spend: no major technology overhaul required; management described ongoing refinement, with added focus on AI-led process efficiency.
Capital: CAR 19.40% and Tier 1 18.71%. Board approved INR500 crore of Tier 2 bonds; no equity raise planned at present, with capital needs to be reassessed once growth picks up.
Gold loan book about INR26,000 crore (INR15,000 crore retail, INR10,000 crore agri), growing about 41%; management aims to raise its share of advances to 30-32% first, then 35%.
risks_watch: Current account balances rose 20% QoQ on one-off IPO-related inflows at quarter end; management expects some slippage in CASA balances.

ECL transition: management said the impact is not substantial, but has not yet decided whether to take the glide path.
Gold loan spreads have not been raised despite the 25 bp repo hike; management said it would act if needed. Repricing of deposits expected to be limited for the next two quarters.
Fee recovery from technically written-off accounts is expected to decline over time, which will weigh on miscellaneous income.

532221|2026-06.headline: Sonata Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10.6% YoY to Rs 3,279.1 Cr, but PAT fell 17.1% QoQ to Rs 108.6 Cr on Rs 35.4 Cr forex hit.
532221|2026-06.overview: International services revenue was flat QoQ in constant currency (+0.1%) at $82 million, while EBITDA margin fell to 15.4% from 20.2% as utilisation dropped to 88.5% on a delayed large-deal ramp-up, a one-time compensation benefit reversed, and AI talent investments rose. Domestic revenue was Rs 2,505.6 Cr with gross contribution up 4.2% QoQ and 14.5% YoY, and management said an OEM direct-billing risk has been partly reversed through contract renewals. Management reiterated an AI-native, engineering-led strategy and an AI order book of $21.4 million, but declined to give a steady-state EBITDA margin or formal guidance.

segments.name: International services
segments.commentary: Revenue $82M, flat QoQ cc and +2.1% YoY cc; EBITDA 15.4% vs 20.2% in Q4 on utilisation drop, one-time Q4 compensation benefit (~2 pts), ~50 bps forex hit and AI talent investments. Headcount 6,293 (vs 6,283), attrition 13%, offshore mix 70%.

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 2,505.6 Cr and gross contribution Rs 78.5 Cr (+14.5% YoY). SMC and corporate software business grew ~82% YoY. DSO rose to 65 days from 47 days, which management attributed to seasonality.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA to show positive traction each quarter this year, with some one-time items normalising in coming quarters; it declined to give a steady-state EBITDA margin as guidance.
Large-deal ramp-up expected to complete in Q2 FY27; management said margin trajectory should turn positive from next quarter.
Domestic management expects financial performance to keep improving in Q2 and the rest of the year.
Normalised effective tax rate guided at about 25%; Q1 benefited from a one-time US state R&D tax credit.
Medium-term: management expects gradual improvement in revenue and EBITDA, supported by AI pipeline.
capex_capacity: Utilisation at 88.5% vs 91.8% in Q4; attributed to delayed large-deal ramp-up and AI capability incubation.
Forward deployed engineer pool being expanded to about 100 people by August 2026.
Sonata University has trained 93% of workforce in AI.
Workbench agentic AI service delivery platform launched in the quarter; several clients have shown interest.
demand_pricing: AI order book $21.4M (18.2% of total order book) vs $16.9M in Q4; AI-led pipeline $340M; AI-led order wins +27% QoQ and AI-led pipeline +21% QoQ.

About seven new international customer wins in the quarter, including a three-year multimillion-dollar modernisation and managed services deal; a global beverage brand deal (800+ locations, 11 countries) was also won.
Top 10 clients were 51% of international revenue; management declined to disclose absolute top-10 revenue, which an analyst said declined QoQ.
Clients above $5M run rate: 12 (flat QoQ); $3-5M: 9 (flat QoQ); clients above $10M run rate: eight.
Management said 21% of engagements are output-based; cloud share of revenue reported at 62% vs 53% a year ago (per analyst question).
Domestic: some customers in the probable direct-billing list were retained through contract renewals after an OEM moved to direct billing with large customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the domestic business confident of sustaining double-digit YoY gross contribution growth, and how are the nine micro-verticals and six value pools defined?
qa_highlights.answer: Management (Jagannathan) said it is confident domestic growth momentum will continue as past issues are behind it. Rajsekhar said the six value pools are customer engagement and ops transformation, agentic AI, legacy modernisation, AI-ready data, resilient AI backbone and AI-native service delivery; micro-verticals include payments, mortgage and lending, healthcare, clinical ops, logistics and retail manufacturing, and are sharpened existing areas rather than new ones.

qa_highlights.question: Top-10 client revenue fell about 6% QoQ and has been weak for six quarters; is productivity pass-through the cause, and what is the absolute top-10 figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan attributed the lower top-10 share (51%) to growth in the 11-20 client bucket and new wins, with no discounts or productivity pass-through and no major top-10 account declining. He declined to disclose absolute top-10 revenue, citing risk of exposing top-5 client revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BFSI/retail and manufacturing vertical revenue decline QoQ, and when will they recover; what is the outlook for TMT?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan said the BFSI share grew beyond expectations, so R&D as a percentage of revenue fell; this is not a standalone R&D issue. Rajsekhar said TMT growth will come from hyperscalers and enterprise product and packaged software organisations, with early pipeline signs from new leadership.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the international margin drop and how will the outcome/output-based model keep margins on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajsekhar said the large-deal ramp-up is largely behind, billing/paperwork delays were one-time, and AI advisory and forward-deployed engineer investments will continue for a couple more quarters; he expects a positive margin trajectory from next quarter. Jagannathan said the top-five accounts appear stable with no major threat, with growth expected in a few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net cash fall QoQ, and what is the cash conversion picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan said the decline reflects domestic vendor payouts tied to turnover and deal completions, with gross cash about Rs 565-567 Cr vs Rs 605 Cr and net cash about Rs 65 Cr vs Rs 30 Cr. He said there was no one-time payment and international collections and DSO were stable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state international EBITDA margin, and what is the domestic large-deal margin view?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan declined to give a steady-state EBITDA margin, saying it would become guidance; he said margin will move positively in coming quarters. For the domestic large deal, management measures success by absolute gross contribution, which is positive and accretive, not by percentage margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised tax rate and does the R&D tax credit affect cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan said the normalised ETR is about 25%; Q1 benefited from a one-time US state R&D tax credit that reduces the cash tax liability.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any LME-linked alumina term contract for FY27?

532259|2026-03.headline: APAR Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 26.7% YoY to INR6,603 crores; PAT of INR254 crores was INR285 crores before INR31 crores of one-offs.

Growth led by Public Services (+12% YoY) and Retail & CPG (+10.1% YoY); six of seven verticals grew YoY. Added one $100M client, six $50M, 11 $20M and 31 $10M clients YoY.
Geography YoY: USA +2.9%, Europe +0.1%, ROW +10.8%, India +16.9%.

BFSI growth attributed to AI-native approach and wallet share gains with top financial services clients; Life Sciences and Healthcare declined on lapse of medical device regulatory work and US healthcare stress.

Management sees divergence: AI-native and AI-amplified services growing strongly, AI-disrupted commoditized work being optimized further by automation. Revenue per employee up 3.3% YoY, rising for five consecutive quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What limits raising guidance given record Q1 bookings and the early-July mega deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the band is broad and only Q1 is done; the mega deal transitions over a couple of months with steady state only by April 2027 and negligible FY27 revenue impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the AI datacenter investment look like a colocation-cost build (about $7M per MW), and what further commitments follow?
qa_highlights.answer: INR3,500 crore is only an initial fraction of the long-term 50 MW plan; it is a full-stack play, not colocation, with further investment tied to free cash flow and funded via partners, client commitments, hardware financing, and equity/debt mix.

qa_highlights.question: Token costs: will they collapse or stay high, and what does that mean for services revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said token prices may fall but total token consumption will rise, so total cost rises; tiered architecture with enterprise SLMs creates a new engineering services wave in data work and training.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 18-19% soon, perhaps in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 margins were near 18% excluding restructuring; FY27 guidance is 17.5-18.5% including 40-50 bps restructuring; FY28 margin guidance will be given next year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ER&D decline and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Decline was in Tech and Telecom and Media & Entertainment, from sharp discretionary cuts at two large US telcos flagged last quarter, plus a high base in tech; no explicit outlook for further declines was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter datacenters now, and how does this differ from the cloud cycle? Also, what about GPU oversupply risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued private AI stacks and SLMs differ from the cloud cycle, that megawatts are an anchor and value lies in wrapped services, and that the market remains GPU-starved; no explicit utilisation or tenancy assumptions were given.

qa_highlights.question: Does the margin guidance include amortization from M&A, and is the services outlook tougher than at the start of the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is organic and excludes acquisitions including Jaspersoft and CTG; macro view is unchanged since March and management will revisit after Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How big will Jaspersoft be, and when does CTG close?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaspersoft is expected to add about $10-15M per quarter with seasonality, consolidated from Q2; CTG expected to close later in Q2.

risks_watch: Revenue guidance (1-4%) was held despite the strongest Q1 bookings; any Q2 change in tone is flagged by management as possible after Q2 results.
ERS revenue is under pressure from telecom and media discretionary cuts; further sequential declines are possible.
AI datacenter entry (INR3,500 crore initial, 50 MW long-term) carries capex, funding and utilisation risk; no committed-consumption figures or return metrics were disclosed.
Margin pressure from AI investment and restructuring (40-50 bps in FY27); FY28 margin view deferred.
Declining healthcare and life sciences revenue, with management attributing it to regulatory work ending and US healthcare stress.
Telecom client headwinds and a high-tech base effect; attrition 12.7% LTM and headcount down 3,292 QoQ.
Pending CTG acquisition closing and Jaspersoft integration; guidance excludes both.

So we are not putting this entire investment in the balance sheet in a single year.

532281|2026-09.headline: HCLTech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.3% QoQ to $3,724M and EBIT margin hit 18.2%, while FY27 revenue guidance was narrowed to 2.5%-4%.
532281|2026-09.overview: Services grew 3% QoQ and 4% YoY in constant currency, led by Advanced AI revenue of $219M (up 28.4% QoQ, 78% YoY). New bookings were $3.3B (up 27% YoY, 35% QoQ), the second-highest quarter ever. HCLSoftware revenue fell 5.8% QoQ and 11.2% YoY to $294M, though ARR rose 7.8% YoY to $1.134B (2.6% ex-Jaspersoft). EBIT margin was 18.2%, up 131 bps QoQ, and FY27 EBIT guidance of 17.5%-18.5% was maintained.

LTM payout INR60, 88.6% of net income
+261 bps YoY; Services 49.4% (+411 bps), Software 19.2% (-264 bps)

segments.commentary: Grew 4.1% QoQ and 2.1% YoY in constant currency.

segments.name: HCLSoftware
segments.commentary: Revenue of $294M fell 5.8% QoQ and 11.2% YoY, mainly from fewer multiyear license renewals (multiyear subscription revenue $39M vs $81M in Q2 FY26). ARR grew 7.8% YoY to $1.134B.

guidance_outlook: FY27 company revenue growth (constant currency) guidance narrowed to 2.5%-4%, including 87 bps inorganic contribution; organic midpoint broadly unchanged.
FY27 Services revenue growth guidance 3%-4%, including 62 bps inorganic contribution.
FY27 EBIT margin guidance unchanged at 17.5%-18.5%.
Management expects Services to land slightly above the guidance midpoint; Q3 expected to be strong with a Software step-up.
Mega deal won in the quarter will not contribute revenue in Q3 or Q4; expected to start in Q1 FY28.
Management's desired medium-term EBIT band is 18%-19%, but it declined to commit to this given industry change.
capex_capacity: First AI data center planned in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, in partnership with Sarvam and the Government of Odisha.
Global Technology Center announced in Bhubaneswar; new Global Technology Center opened in GIFT City, Gujarat for financial services clients.
Advanced semiconductor lab launched in Bengaluru with an investment of INR185 crore (post-silicon engineering, testing, validation and failure analysis).
Completed acquisition of HPE's Telco Solutions Group (2 months consolidated in Q2, about $21M revenue); Jaspersoft fully consolidated (about $15M).
Announced intent to acquire Robotiq.ai, a Croatia-based enterprise RPA platform provider.
demand_pricing: Pipeline described as strong and balanced across service lines, verticals and geographies; healthy demand toward end of quarter, but management remains cautious given a fluid environment.
Large AI deals were largely single-sourced through partners; competition came mainly from boutique providers and from service providers in agentic AI build, semiconductors and inferencing.
Management said IP and platform revenue carries gross margins upwards of 70%; AI services margins are at least 7%-10% higher than traditional services.
Top-client buckets: +1 client in $100M+, +8 in $50M+, +10 in $20M+, +33 in $10M+ on a YoY basis. Three top-20 clients ramping down (two telcos, one manufacturer) were already factored into guidance.
Geographic growth YoY: USA +3.5%, Europe -0.3%, Rest of World +11.4%, India +21.8%. Retail and CPG +14% and Financial Services +7.1% led verticals; 5 of 7 verticals grew YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How is value shared between frontier AI labs and managed services, and how will it look in steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its value sits mainly in the FDE motion and services around OpenAI and Anthropic platforms, with a long tail of work once inside an enterprise. Pricing for some offerings includes token cost, making the economics non-linear rather than headcount-linked.

qa_highlights.question: Who is HCLTech competing with in Advanced AI deals?
qa_highlights.answer: The two largest AI deals were single-sourced via partners. Competition came from boutiques, and from service providers in agentic AI build, semiconductors and inferencing; IP platform monetization (e.g., AI Force line items) is now included in large deals.

qa_highlights.question: When will FCF-to-net-income conversion return to the 3-4 year average?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Shiv Walia said two one-time items (a bilateral advance pricing agreement tax payment and a contribution to an external gratuity trust) depressed LTM conversion; he expects it to revert to 100%+ as they roll out of LTM.

qa_highlights.question: Why not raise the top end of guidance given strong Services growth and a seasonally strong Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the environment remains volatile (citing the Middle East conflict) and it does not want to raise guidance; it expects Services slightly above the midpoint and a Q3 Software step-up.

qa_highlights.question: Are the AI engagements with OpenAI/Anthropic under T&M or fixed price, with meaningful TCV?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a mix: change management and operating model transformation engagements have some fixed-price deals, while agentic implementation on Google and similar platforms is largely time-and-materials.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ramp-downs in top-20 clients behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact from the three ramp-downs was already in guidance, though discretionary spend at the two telco clients could still weigh. Upselling to existing clients has kept the client buckets growing.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Software margin expand while revenue declines, and how do Services margins look?
qa_highlights.answer: Software Q1 had a one-off restructuring cost; excluding it, lower employee costs and lower amortization drove the QoQ margin gain. Services margins benefited from Project Ascend and the higher Advanced AI mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic decline in Software and how long can ARR-to-revenue disconnect last?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue fell about 15% YoY on an organic basis while ARR rose 2.6% ex-Jaspersoft. Management attributed the gap to upfront recognition of multiyear licences and perpetual licence timing, expecting renewals to return in FY28 and FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in HPE Telco Solutions (Aruba TS) revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only two months were consolidated and extrapolating to three months should be right; there may be small seasonality but nothing major.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q3-Q4 Services sequential growth expected to decelerate versus Q2 organic growth of about 2.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the mega deal not contributing until Q1 FY28 as the main outlier, and said it is being conservative given uncertainty, with Services likely above the midpoint.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from ecosystem partners, and what is the impact of frontier-lab partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not track partner-channel revenue reliably, much of it is influenced rather than direct. It is a small but growing professional services partner for hyperscalers and frontier and GPU companies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term margin range?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the earlier aspiration of 18%-19% remains the desired band, but he would not commit to it now, preferring to invest in capability and differentiation.

risks_watch: HCLSoftware: revenue declined 11.2% YoY; the gap to ARR growth depends on multiyear renewals returning in FY28-FY29.
Discretionary spending pressure at two telco top-20 clients, plus a steep budget-driven ramp-down at one manufacturing client.
Free cash flow conversion (LTM FCF to NI 87%) depressed by BAPA tax payment and gratuity trust funding; watch for reversion to 100%+.
Mega deal revenue begins only in Q1 FY28; H2 FY27 Services sequential growth looks slower than Q2.
Macro and geopolitical volatility (Middle East conflict cited) and US PERM program suspension (management says immaterial).
Limited disclosure of partner-channel and AI revenue split; AI pricing and token-cost pass-through economics still evolving.

key_quotes: I think our value here is largely in the FDE motion, the services around it.

But 18% to 19% is our desired band, but I wouldn't want to kind of comment on it now, because the industry is changing significantly
We are seeing a good environment, and we hope it will continue. For Services, we feel confident to be slightly above the midpoint.

532285|2026-06.headline: Geojit Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR160.4 crore and PAT to INR19.8 crore, but management guided to continued cost pressure and no hiring for several quarters.
532285|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR160.40 crore, up 11% YoY, with PBT of INR25.99 crore (up 4% QoQ) and PAT of INR19.83 crore (up 14% QoQ). Employee cost rose INR18 crore on sales force expansion, DIFC hiring, tech team additions and higher incentives, though management said employee cost would normalise after a lower insurance-incentive quarter. Customer assets reached INR1.11 lakh crore (up 15% QoQ), mostly from market appreciation, with recurring assets at INR26,000 crore. Management said margin benefits from FY26 investments would take a couple more quarters, and that hiring has been paused except for replacements due to Middle East conflict and market conditions. Leadership succession was also confirmed, with Jones George becoming MD from 1 October.

qa_highlights.question: Are the FY26 investments starting to show up in financial performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some productivity gains are visible, but covering costs will take longer because most recurring MF, PMS and AIF revenue is trail-based.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall from the previous quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the March quarter carried high insurance incentive payouts, while April-June had lower insurance income, so employee cost normalised; fresh hiring is slow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East outlook and the GCC contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: GCC AUM is a little under USD 1 billion. Middle East investment decisions are on hold, and no expansion is planned until stability returns.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net cash levels and buyback plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is about INR1,000-1,100 crore, with about 70% deployed in MTF/NBFC lending and trading. A buyback is being considered but has no timeline; consolidation opportunities may take priority.

qa_highlights.question: Why do investors choose Geojit given weak PAT over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Geojit focuses on delivery and MF trail income rather than F&O. It expects margins to improve in coming quarters, not immediately.

risks_watch: Profitability is still under pressure: employee cost is up INR18 crore and no near-term breakeven timeline was given for new hires.
SIP and new-client momentum has slowed, and productivity of the expanded sales force is still unproven.
Middle East and GCC NRI business faces conflict and FCNR-related outflows, with no expansion planned.
Customer asset growth was mostly market-driven, so flows need to be tracked against market moves.
Buyback and capital allocation remain undecided, with consolidation as a possible alternative use of cash.

532286|2026-06.headline: Jindal Steel Q1FY27 consolidated adjusted EBITDA INR 2,667 crore, INR 11,937/ton, with ASP up INR 7,500/ton despite 15% sequential volume drop.
532286|2026-06.overview: Q1FY27 revenue fell about 8% QoQ on a plant maintenance shutdown (BOF refractory change), with sales volume down 15% sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 2,667 crore (INR 11,937/ton, up INR 1,843/ton), while PAT was INR 844 crore and finance cost rose to INR 548 crore as Q4FY26 expansion assets entered the P&L. qa_highlights.answer: Priorities: utilise 15.6 MT capacity and shift mix to value-added grades; growth funded from earnings at INR 7,000-10,000 crore capex per year, with no commodity capacity additions and no new borrowing to expand.

qa_highlights.question: Current NSR movement and Q2 price outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Flats about INR 7,000/ton higher QoQ and longs about INR 4,500/ton higher QoQ; recent HRC about INR 800/ton lower and TMT about INR 8,000 lower, expected to recover post-monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 volume fall and what is the FY27 volume outlook?
