segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: JSOL (100% subsidiary) turnover and EBITDA are rising as major projects commission; Mozambique coal EBITDA improved YoY on better coal prices.

guidance_outlook: Net steel production target of about 6 MT in H2 FY27 (about 3 MT per quarter, planned at 0.96 MT per month); gross steel about 11 MT for FY27.
Record production expected in Q3 FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026), with Q4 to exceed Q3.
FY27 sales volume guidance lower end of about 10.5 MT; management says 9-9.5 lakh saleable tons per month is needed and that they are comfortable.
Coking coal cost increase of USD 20-25/ton expected for Q3; a possible further USD 20/ton from diesel and oil if the West Asia conflict prolongs.
Slurry pipeline (192 km, Barbil to Angul) commissioned; commercial supply from about 2-3 days from 23 Oct, saving about INR 700/ton on freight at 20,000 tons per day.
Blast furnace at Angul (about 10,000 tons per day) to ramp to 10,500 in about 7 days, 11,000 in November and 12,000 in December.
Coal gasifier expansion (3 more gasifiers, 35,000 NM3/hr each) and DRI-2 (2 MT) targeted for commissioning by June 2027.
Utkal B2 coal mine clearance expected in FY27; Roida iron ore mine restart expected by about December 2026 to January 2027.
Annual growth capex guided at INR 7,500-10,000 crore; net debt-to-EBITDA to stay below 1.5x through the cycle.
capex_capacity: Blast furnace at Angul ramping to about 10,000 tons per day, targeting 12,000 tons per day by December 2026.
Slurry pipeline: 192 km, commissioned, first iron slurry dispatched, continuous operation planned.
Captive coal mines: about 15 MT total capacity across Raigarh and Angul; captive coal meets about 50-55% of requirement, targeted at 65-70%. Gare Palma about 4 MT.
Kasia iron ore mine at 22,000 tons per day, ramping to 30,000 tons per day.
Coal gasification: 3 additional gasifiers (105,000 NM3/hr combined), over 95% indigenous content, commissioning by June 2027.
Total capex plan of about INR 47,000 crore with INR 8,000-9,000 crore remaining, including DRI-2 and performance-linked payments.
demand_pricing: Average HRC moved from INR 51,000 to INR 60,000/ton during Q2; TMT from INR 52,000 to INR 59,000/ton; structurals INR 60,000-65,000; rails above INR 70,000.
Spot prices around INR 60,000/ton for HRC and TMT as of late October.
Coking coal cost rose about USD 12-15/ton in Q2, within prior guidance; management says prices are stable now.
Propane to coal-gas switch saves about INR 70/kg in reheating furnaces (propane about INR 100/kg vs syngas about INR 30/kg). Management says the company will not revert to propane.
Q2 is seasonally weak for TMT; Q3 expected to be stronger on festive-season construction demand.
Europe steel deficit of about 28 MT cited; EU CBAM and quota remain open issues for exports.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4.8 MT H1 production run-rate achievable and will flat mix stay at 70:30 in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of about 3 MT per quarter; mix target is 65:35 flat to long, not 70:30, to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How much freight saving does the slurry pipeline give, and any extra cost?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 700/ton on freight with no additional cost; around 500 of 700 daily iron ore trucks to be removed.

qa_highlights.question: Coking coal and West Asia cost impact for Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Coking coal up USD 20-25/ton expected in Q3 by Sandeep Modi; West Asia impact on fuel about USD 4-5/ton, steady. Another USD 20/ton possible if conflict prolongs.

qa_highlights.question: Water availability from Brahmani for Angul at higher volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Only 31 MLD being used against 59.1 MLD sanctioned; usage to fall at least 15% next year as Barbil slurry supplies water.

qa_highlights.question: Power sales and their EBITDA contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said power sales are miniscule relative to the INR 1 lakh crore revenue ambition; no figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Pellet plant and merchant pellet sales?
qa_highlights.answer: No merchant pellet sales now; all 33,000 tons/day consumed in-house. New pellet plant commercial production by June 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation and spot price detail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined exact spot prices, citing policy; gave approximate ranges as above.

risks_watch: Coking coal and diesel cost pressure from the West Asia and Russia-Ukraine supply disruptions; management flagged possible USD 20-25/ton in Q3.
Execution on the Angul blast furnace ramp, Roida mine right-of-way, and Utkal B2 approvals.
Possible delays to DRI-2 and coal gasifiers, which management says could slip from June 2027 due to imported equipment.
Other expenses rose about 13% QoQ on freight and power/fuel; management expects normalisation in Q3.
Water availability at Angul given the Brahmani river reservoir level, though management says consumption will be lower.
EU quota and CBAM outcomes that determine export access.
532286|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and expansive on production ramp-up, cost savings and balance sheet, with management repeatedly describing the company as cash surplus. Evasive on exact ASP, spot prices, power sales and subsidiary-level numbers, which it declined to quantify on the call.
key_quotes: So, we are quite confident that we'll be in a position to achieve these 3 million tons per quarter.
And INR 700 per ton will be saving on freight and no additional expenses.
So, we don't want to invest money unless we reach to our 100% capacity utilization.
So, the steel scenario is very good. I think it is now around 10% Y-o-Y basis, there's a growth.

532300|2026-03.headline: Wockhardt FY26 revenue INR3,373 crore, EBITDA about INR630 crore (~51% growth); Zaynich US FDA approval is the key catalyst, with peak sales guided at $1.5-2 billion globally.
532300|2026-03.overview: Management hosted an investor meet on 4 June 2026 (disclosed 11 June) after the US FDA approval of Zaynich (cefepime-zidebactam), described as the first Indian-discovered research product approved by the FDA. FY26 revenue was INR3,373 crore, EBITDA about INR630 crore (margin about 18.6%, up from about 5.4% three years earlier) and profit before tax INR238 crore. Management framed the next phase as scaling growth: US launch of Zaynich via an operationally light model, India and emerging-market launches, and biosimilar diabetes expansion. Most numbers were given verbally; no quarterly figures or formal guidance were disclosed in the presentation.

segments.name: Pharma core (India, UK, Ireland)
segments.commentary: About 75% of business; UK is top-five with 18% covered-market share and focuses on specialty injectables. India driven by diabetes, orthopedics, pain and regenerative medicine (Emrok, Miqnaf).

segments.name: Biosimilars / biotech (diabetes)
segments.commentary: Grew 27% in FY26; human insulin output scaled 2x and glargine 1.5x. Two products commercialised, five in pipeline (aspart, RN 30/70, degludec, degludec aspart, semaglutide); registered in 30 emerging markets.

segments.name: Novel antibiotics (Zaynich, Emrok, Miqnaf, Odrate)
segments.commentary: Specialty (biosimilars plus novel antibiotics) is 23% of business. Zaynich has US FDA and CDSCO India approvals; US launch planned with leadership hired and a commercial operating partner; European approval expected by end of calendar 2026.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: 28% of turnover, growing 35%, supported by partnerships in Brazil, Thailand, Algeria and Malaysia. Plans to launch Zaynich in seven to eight high-carbapenem-resistance markets within 18 to 24 months.

guidance_outlook: Zaynich global peak sales of $1.5-2 billion per year, with US roughly 40% of global revenue; country-wise split not given.
Revenue ramp expected to be slow initially (hockey-stick pattern), with breakeven in 12 to 18 months in the Zaynich business; first 12-18 months may see a slight loss, per the Chairman.
Zaynich US price expected at roughly $1,200-1,500 per day, with India pricing about 75-80% below US; Europe and US pricing described as price-neutral versus existing antibiotics.
Long-term target of about 20-25% share of resistant cases globally; India possibly higher.
Biosimilar business expected to double in 24-36 months; capacity to double in 12-15 months; five pipeline products to launch about two years out.
Capex of INR200-300 crore over next three years, primarily for biologicals capacity; R&D spend to stay at similar percentage of sales.
Foviscu DCGI filing expected in two to three months; approval timing not predictable. Odrate is about four years away and Phase 2 waiver not expected.
capex_capacity: Planned capex of INR200-300 crore over the next three years, mainly for biologicals capacity.
Biosimilar capacity to double within 12-15 months.

Zaynich manufacturing: US supply from an FDA-approved European site; India supply from Indian facility; emerging markets to be supplied from either India or Europe depending on timelines (Europe could save six to nine months).
Company has 11 manufacturing facilities and two R&D centres in-house.
Management said US, Europe and emerging markets filings are submitted or in progress, with European approval expected by end of 2026.
demand_pricing: US cUTI is the largest of about 1.2 million US gram-negative hospital infections (about 600,000 cUTI cases); management cited about 20-25% readmission rate for cUTI.
India: about 600,000-700,000 gram-negative infection patients, with 35-45% estimated carbapenem resistance (ICMR surveillance caveated by regional variation).
Phase 3 vs meropenem: composite cure rate 96.8%, about 20% higher than meropenem per management.
Management said new anti-infectives in the US market total about $1 billion; the company does not plan to create new demand but to take share, with price neutrality.
Competition: cefiderocol (Fetroja) cited as the closest competitor; management claimed Zaynich has a better efficacy and safety profile, without numerical head-to-head data.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue from Zaynich over the next 6 to 24 months, and capex and commercial costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman expects slow initial revenue growth, a hockey-stick curve after 12-18 months, INR200-300 crore capex over three years, and no capex for sales build-out, only revenue cost. Breakeven expected in 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Does Zaynich qualify for the 10% PLI and what is the China strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Government funding recognised but immaterial versus R&D spend. China: Chinese patients in trial were insufficient; a small China study is ongoing and a partner may be sought.

qa_highlights.question: Will Zaynich be made in Europe for the US and in India for emerging markets?
qa_highlights.answer: US supply from an FDA-inspected European site as a de-risking step; India supply from India; emerging markets from India or Europe depending on timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Wockhardt exit US generics and will it re-enter?
qa_highlights.answer: US generics were about 5% of the portfolio and loss-making, amid the 2012-13 FDA import alert. Management said it is re-entering with innovative products sourced from European manufacturers, with India production for India.

qa_highlights.question: Patent life and exclusivity for Zaynich, Emrok and Miqnaf?
qa_highlights.answer: Zaynich patent runs to 2038 in India with further filings planned; Miqnaf patent to early 2033 in India. QIDP status gives five extra years in US; minimum 10-year market exclusivity in US and Western markets.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and patient targets for FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: US price about $1,200-1,500 per day, typically $10,000-15,000 per course; India priced about 75-80% below US. Long-term share of 20-25% of resistant cases, with no FY28-29 patient numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Peak sales of Zaynich?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $1.5-2 billion per year globally at peak, not cumulative, with US around 40% of global revenue.

risks_watch: Commercial execution: a new US sales model for antibiotics with a commercial operating partner, 6,000 US hospitals to segment, and a first-time anti-infective launch for the company.
Losses or breakeven in the first 12-18 months from US launch costs; Chairman's comments on profitability were clarified as Zaynich-only.
Regulatory timing: European approval expected by end-2026, emerging market filings to follow; DCGI approval for Foviscu not predictable.
Label scope: US approval is for cUTI; HAP/VAP and other indications need a further trial, so off-label use is a question.
Zaynich Phase 2 waiver for the aztreonam combination (Odrate) not expected; Odrate timing about four years.
Hospital segment profitability and ROCE targets were not answered (hospitals deemed out of scope; ROCE question deflected).
532300|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on Zaynich and the R&D pipeline, with forward-looking claims (peak sales, market share) given without detailed assumptions. Evasive or deflective on ROCE, hospitals, Foviscu timing and China specifics, and on country-wise revenue split.
key_quotes: Wockhardt, as you know, in the last few days, is now the first Indian company to have an Indian research product approved with the US FDA, Zaynich.
So, it is in your financial terms you say investment, I mean, asset-light and capital-heavy.
We will stick to only antibiotic research for next 10 years.
Peak sales per year.

financial_highlights.change: about 35% in last year per Q&A

532305|2026-06.headline: Ind-Swift Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 2.85x YoY to ₹33.32 crore, a 17.91% margin, with management guiding to 20%+ from Q3.
532305|2026-06.overview: Operating income grew 21.16% YoY to ₹186.08 crore and operating EBITDA reached ₹33.32 crore (17.91% margin, up 1258 bps). PAT excluding exceptional items was ₹24.68 crore (13.26% margin vs 4.99%). Management attributed the step-up to exit of litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business after the merger, and to a higher own-brand export mix. CDMO contracts with Viatris, Manx and Arrotex were commercialised in the quarter but contributed only about ₹5-6 crore so far, with ramp-up expected from Q2 and Q3. Management reiterated FY27 export sales of about ₹750 crore and ₹1200 crore revenue by FY29, and declined to revise targets at this stage.

segments.name: Export own-brands
segments.commentary: 57.20% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 48% in Q1 FY26; management cites this mix shift as a key margin driver. Export gross margin was stated at about 55%.

segments.name: Export contract manufacturing (CDMO)
segments.commentary: 26.64% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 29% a year earlier. Viatris, Manx and Arrotex partnerships commercialised in the quarter, with about ₹5-6 crore booked from Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) so far.

segments.name: Domestic segments
segments.commentary: Branded generics 6.41%, ethical 6.14% and domestic contract manufacturing 3.61% of Q1 FY27 sales, all lower than a year ago. Management describes these as a stable cash-generation base; domestic sales are seasonal.

segments.name: Product portfolio
segments.commentary: Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin was about ₹25 crore in Q1 FY27 per management, partnered with Tiffen-Becker. FY26 revenue: Atorvastatin ₹85.50 crore, Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin ₹80.78 crore, Fexofenadine ₹74.32 crore, Quetiapine ₹19.75 crore, Famciclovir ₹18.64 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 export sales target of about ₹750 crore, with roughly 45% from CDMO (per management).

FY29 revenue target of ₹1200 crore; management said it is not revising this yet and will revisit by year-end. Mentioned FY27 expectation of about ₹900 crore and a longer-term aspiration of ₹1500 crore revenue and ~₹200 crore net profit by FY30.
EBITDA margin of 18% described as sustainable; management expects to move above 20% from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally targeted), potentially 21-22% with sequential sales growth.
Viatris CDMO volumes expected to double in Q2 versus Q1; Arrotex Macrogol push expected in Q2, and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules to contribute in Q3-Q4.
Medium-term growth of 20-25% CAGR referenced, with EBITDA margins above 18% (management answered 'yes').
Dossiers to reach 400+ additions, taking the total from 2,100 to about 2,500 by Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: About ₹250 crore of cash to be deployed in capex over roughly 2 to 2.5 years across a new warehouse, capacity enhancement at the existing facility, and the Jammu facility (EU-GMP/PIC/S audit under way).
Samba facility upgrade to EU-GMP and PIC/S standards in progress as planned.
Capacity utilisation for Ibuprofen and granules about 70% in Q1 per management; management expects 90% utilisation of planned FY29 capacity over time.
Capex for a potential new CDMO customer deal estimated at ₹50-75 crore, with revenue of ₹150+ crore expected.
R&D working on 5-6 molecules for FY27-29; capex to follow only after filings are completed. New R&D land bought in Panchkula area.
demand_pricing: CDMO economics: Viatris paid about USD 2 million for development work, to be reimbursed through orders.
Selection criteria for new products include a minimum 50-55% gross margin and customer confidence in R&D delivery. Candidate molecules include Rosuvastatin, Mirabegron, Sitagliptin and Empagliflozin.
Tiffen-Becker arrangement: transfer-priced supply with about 43% of the customer's margin shared with Ind-Swift.
Management expects no dearth of capacity for the planned growth; new partnerships under discussion with 3-4 existing overseas customers, not expected to contribute this year.

qa_highlights.question: What was the CDMO contribution in Q1 and what growth to expect from the Viatris partnership over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Gagan Aggarwal said Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) booked only about ₹5-6 crore in Q1, with growth reflecting in Q2 and Q3. He said about ₹100-130 crore is expected from these two products, not the full ₹200 crore in year one, and that it would build over about two years.

qa_highlights.question: What are export margins for CDMO and own-brands, and how will the ₹250 crore cash and Synthimed stake be used?
qa_highlights.answer: Export gross margin is about 55%. The ₹250 crore cash will be deployed as capex over about 2.5 years (warehouse, existing capacity, Jammu). No plans to divest the Synthimed stake this year; Synthimed budgeted EBITDA is about ₹750 crore and Q1 results are on track.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18% EBITDA margin sustainable, and could it rise further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 18% is fully sustainable and could reach 21-22% if sales grow quarter on quarter. It denied calling Q1 a turnaround, citing litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business for about 1.5 years that are now over.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY29 revenue guidance of ₹1200 crore not being raised, and when does growth come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will not revise at this stage and will revisit by year-end. Growth is H2-weighted via Arrotex Macrogol in Q2 and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules in Q3-Q4. FY27 expectation is about ₹900 crore, with export sales of about ₹750 crore, roughly 45% from CDMO.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the API business sold and what R&D capability was retained?
qa_highlights.answer: The API business was sold to Synthimed in FY24 for net about ₹2000-2100 crore, used to repay group debt of about ₹1250-1300 crore. Retained R&D in Panchkula handles regulatory compliance, tech transfer and global filings, with new land bought for a further R&D facility.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and will there be a capacity shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Ibuprofen and granules ran at about 70% in Q1 on pilot batches. Management expects 90% utilisation of the FY29 plan over time and sees no capacity dearth. Capex for new molecules will follow only after filings are complete.

risks_watch: CDMO ramp-up timing: Viatris volumes are guided to double in Q2 from a ₹5-6 crore base, and Arrotex Macrogol and Ibuprofen and granules contributions depend on Q2-Q4 execution.
Margin trajectory: management targets above 20% EBITDA margin from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally), against 17.91% in Q1; a shortfall would challenge the 21-22% view.
Capacity and capex: ₹250 crore capex over about 2-2.5 years, Jammu and Samba EU-GMP/PIC/S audits in progress, and the new CDMO deal needs ₹50-75 crore capex; delays could cap FY28-29 revenue.
Revenue guidance: FY27 about ₹900 crore and FY29 ₹1200 crore; management says it will revisit by year-end, so the next quarter's run-rate matters.
Synthimed stake: ~7.8% holding, no divestment planned this year, tag-along right on any PE exit; monetisation timing is open.
Customer concentration and unnamed partners: two new overseas CDMO deals and 3-4 existing customers are under discussion but not named; 'the war' is cited as slowing signings.
Several questions were deferred (market size, Q1 capacity utilisation, new registrations, packaging differentiation), so follow-ups via IR are pending.
key_quotes: Yes, yes, 18% is fully sustainable and we plan if the sales we are able to increase quarter-on-quarter they might go up to 21 to 22%.
Sir, not at this stage. Maybe after if we are able to achieve our, overachieve our results this financial year, we may revise this.
So that ₹250 crores will be deployed in capex over a period of 2.5 years approx.
We don't want to spend a single penny in R&D before we sign off any agreement with our customers.
532305|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins and the export mix, stating 18% EBITDA margin is fully sustainable and describing the quarter as an excellent start. Cautious on guidance, declining to revise the ₹1200 crore FY29 target and avoiding firm commitments on the 20% margin timing, the new partnerships and the CDMO revenue split. Evasive on several detailed questions, including market size, Q1 capacity utilisation, partner names and new registrations, which were deferred to follow-up.

532309|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 PBT from continuing operations hit INR 119 crore, but one-offs (incl. ~INR 44 crore BHEL ECL reversal) drove much of it; underlying FY26 EBITDA margin 11%.
532309|2026-03.overview: GE Power India reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 316 crore (up from INR 266 crore YoY) and FY26 revenue of INR 1,269 crore (up 21%), led by Core Services (+14%) and Upgrades (+24%). Profit before tax and exceptional items from continuing operations was INR 119 crore in Q4 versus a loss of INR 15 crore a year earlier, and INR 340 crore for FY26 versus INR 22 crore, with management flagging sizeable one-offs in both periods. Order intake fell sharply to INR 877 crore for FY26 from INR 2,183 crore, and order backlog declined to INR 1,628 crore from INR 2,662 crore, mainly due to termination of FGD-EP contracts. Management is pushing a service-led, short-cycle strategy, has settled with BHEL and Jaypee, and has signed a Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy, with a recommended dividend of INR 7 per share (70% of face value).

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 14% YoY and core orders rose 32% YoY; Core Services order backlog up about 40% YoY. Management says about 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book executes in FY27 (12-month cycles).

segments.name: Upgrades
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 24% YoY, driven by upgrade volumes in Q4; Vindhyachal and Wanakbori complex upgrade orders of INR 591 crore were booked in FY25.

segments.name: New Build / FGD EPC (AQCS)
segments.commentary: In close-out mode; FGD-EP contracts of Jaypee Bina and Nigrie (INR 775 crore) were terminated, driving backlog decline. Seven operational acceptances and four unit completions achieved in FY26.

segments.name: Durgapur manufacturing (discontinued)
segments.commentary: Being demerged to JSW Energy; asset of about 660 acres, reported losses in recent quarters. Five-year JSW supply and capacity agreement signed to protect core services manufacturing needs.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give numeric FY27 guidance; CFO said the FY26 underlying EBITDA base (11%) is set and FY27 margins should be at par or better, without a range.
About 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book (INR 1,628 crore) expected to execute in FY27, implying roughly INR 1,380-1,470 crore; this is a management estimate from the call, not formal guidance.
Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy: filed with NCLT; target completion in calendar 2026, and within 12 months of 31 Mar 2026 at the latest.
Core Services target addressable fleet of about INR 3,500-4,000 crore; company holds about 18% share and aims to grow it before considering other areas.
Management says the ECL impact from the BHEL settlement is fully recognised as of 31 Mar 2026, so no similar reversal is expected in FY27.
capex_capacity: Durgapur manufacturing facility to be demerged to JSW Energy; a five-year agreement with JSW covers reserved manufacturing capacity and supply for core services boiler components.
Management aims to build an alternate supply chain for boiler components within about 18 months to become independent of JSW after the five-year agreement.
Three PG tests completed for key new-build units and multiple synchronisations and facility closures achieved in FY26.
Eighteen new first-of-its-kind service products ordered during FY26; first-time generator repairs, turbine upgrades and control system solutions delivered.
demand_pricing: Management says thermal plant PLF and availability are rising, increasing services demand; target addressable market quoted at INR 3,500-4,000 crore.
Q4 order intake of INR 254 crore was below the prior-year INR 285 crore (which included INR 52 crore O&M); FY26 orders fell 60% YoY on the FY25 FGD-EP and complex upgrade wins.

FGD mandate: per the July 2025 notification, Category C plants (over 200 GW) were removed and Category A (about 8 GW, mainly Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra) must install FGD; Category B is optional with no tariff pass-through if they opt in. Management says the mandate has limited near-term order impact.
Management is pursuing 13 countries for boilers, including Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Indonesia, while stating its perimeter remains India-only for GEPIL and non-GEPIL assets.

qa_highlights.question: Does GEPIL participate in gas turbine, HRSG or combined-cycle business?
qa_highlights.answer: Puneet Bhatla said no; HRSG and gas-plant business belong to GE Vernova's gas business and fall outside GEPIL's objects, which are steam and thermal only.

qa_highlights.question: Of the order book, how much is executable in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Aashish Ghai said short-cycle orders typically complete within 12 months, so about 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book is expected in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will backlog grow after the current book runs off, and is the business widening beyond core?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is new-build close-out. Core backlog is up about 40% YoY; the company plans to grow its 18% share of the INR 3,500-4,000 crore fleet before expanding to other areas.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 450 crore loan and what yield does it earn?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said it is surplus cash lent to a promoter-group cash pool benchmarked to HSBC, with rates of 5.5-6.35% in FY26, about 0.25% above commercial bank deposit rates. Lending is board-approved, shareholder-approved and audited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope of the FGD opportunity and the margin range?
qa_highlights.answer: Roshan Singh outlined the notification: Category A (about 8 GW) must install FGD, Category B is optional, and Category C was removed. He said the mandate has limited weight for GEPIL unless utilities act proactively. No margin range was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR 880 crore net cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Puneet Bhatla said the cash is under evaluation for deployment into growth in services, with no specific plan disclosed yet and shareholder value as the stated priority.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Durgapur demerger timeline and benefit to minority shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said the NCLT petition is filed, creditor and shareholder approvals and tax/bank NOCs are required, and completion is targeted for this calendar year and within 12 months of 31 Mar 2026. Shareholders receive entitlement shares in the resulting company.

qa_highlights.question: Will the demerger affect manufacturing needed for core services?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said no, because a five-year JSW Energy agreement reserves manufacturing capacity at pre-set schedule and price. An alternate supply chain is targeted within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the underlying EBITDA margin excluding one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said FY26 normalised entity-level EBITDA was 11%, with Q4 at about 18%. He declined to give a numeric margin range for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will ECL-related reversals continue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said no; the BHEL settlement is fully executed, with the final tranche received in March 2026, and the ECL impact is complete as of 31 Mar 2026.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR 266 crore in Q4 FY25 (about 19% YoY as stated in the call)

financial_highlights.metric: PBT before exceptional items, continuing ops (Q4 FY26)
financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR 15 crore in Q4 FY25; includes ~INR 44 crore BHEL ECL reversal (CFO later said ~INR 41 crore with other benefits)

financial_highlights.metric: PBT before exceptional items, continuing ops (FY26)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR 22 crore in FY25; includes ~INR 116 crore BHEL ECL reversal, ~INR 22 crore Solapur EoT/LD settlement, ~INR 18 crore insurance claims (Solapur and Sipat fire)

532482|2026-09.overview: Management, at an IIFL-hosted "Granules India 2.0" webinar, framed FY27 onward as a shift from building capabilities to scaling them, after a return to growth in FY26. Four growth engines were named: controlled substances, complex generics/early market entry, oncology, and peptide CDMO (Senn Tides). The CFO said the company is now in a consolidated net cash position following September 2026 preferential warrant proceeds, and plans about 2,000 crore of organic capex over three to four years. Management was candid that gross margin gains (about 15 pp over four years) have not yet fully flowed to EBITDA, and that the peptide business is currently loss-making. No quarterly financial figures for Q2 FY27 were given in the call.

532493|2026-03.headline: FY26 turnover of INR1,157 crores in line with guidance; order book INR2,141 crores standalone and FY27 top-line growth reaffirmed at 15-20%.
532493|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 turnover of INR1,157 crores, in line with the start-of-year guidance, with operating cash flow of INR370 crores versus minus INR99 crores a year earlier. Q4 billing was INR490 crores (up 16% YoY) and Q4 fresh orders were about INR530 crores, taking the standalone order book to INR2,141 crores at 31 March 2026. Management reaffirmed FY27 top-line growth of 15-20% and guided to roughly INR1,600 crores-plus of orders in FY27, with a board-approved in-principle demerger of the space, meteorology and hydrology business. The call leaned heavily on a long-range "near-triple turnover in 4.5-5.5 years" narrative, with proprietary IP products and the Su-30 upgrade positioned as upside rather than included in the numbers.

financial_highlights.change: vs minus INR99 crores in FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR2.40 per share (about 120% of face value)

financial_highlights.change: Analyst figure, not confirmed by management
FY26 JV share of profit about INR8 crores after tax

financial_highlights.value: Orders INR546 crores; sales INR360 crores

segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 60% of FY26 revenue and is expected to be about 45% of FY27 orders/mix. Shipborne radar systems were handed to DRDO for final testing.

segments.name: Space and meteorology
segments.commentary: Contributed about 16% of FY26 revenue and is expected to be about 25% of FY27 orders. Management said space is about 10-15% of sales, and defence satellite subsystems were completed in Q4.

segments.commentary: Expected to be about 25% of FY27 orders, driven by Su-30 EW DCPP role (Angad) and active seekers for couple of missiles, with orders expected in 2-3 years.

segments.commentary: FY26 orders INR546 crores and sales INR360 crores. Management targets at least 50% growth in both orders and sales in FY27, with INR200 crores of FY27 order visibility and sales above INR600 crores expected.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth reaffirmed at 15-20%, with potential for much stronger growth over coming years.

Roughly 25% of FY27 expected orders from R&D programmes, balance from production orders.

Management expects to nearly triple turnover in 4.5-5.5 years (around FY30-FY31) driven by about five or six programmes (QRSAM, Uttam radar, Su-30 Virupaksha, Su-30 Angad, JV business and electronic mines), excluding export and IP-product upside.
Capex to remain around INR40-50 crores per year; no incremental capex beyond normal run-rate expected; working capital needs to rise with volumes but are expected to be met within sanctioned limits.

Management indicated FY26 margin (about 55% as stated, likely gross margin) should be sustained; JV EBITDA guided at 18-20% with at least about INR20 crores share of profit on INR600 crores JV revenue.
capex_capacity: Annual capex of about INR40-50 crores to augment existing capacity; no additional capex beyond normal run-rate expected for the 3x plan.
Demerger of space, meteorology and hydrology business approved in principle by the board; detailed scheme expected within weeks.
Miniaturisation work underway for radars using in-house components; digital array radar and photonics radar subsystems delivered to DRDO.
First NCNC demo of proprietary product planned within the current quarter; multiple Astra-branded IP products targeted before Diwali.
demand_pricing: Management cited about 75% of India's defence capital acquisition budget allocated to domestic companies and FY26 defence exports above INR38,000 crores.

Export margins: exports to ARC are RF content of SDRs co-developed with Rafael; management said gross margin on these is about 40-45%, versus single-digit margins on build-to-print (BTP) business, which the company has exited.
Uttam radar order: negotiations with HAL at final stage; order expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27.
QRSAM: BEL expects its contract by about June 2026; Astra has started receiving small quantities for FOPM; production orders expected 3-4 months after BEL's main contract.
Su-30 radar (Virupaksha AAAU): development to complete in next 2-3 months; DRDO qualification possibly FY28, then user qualification and about 2-3 years to production orders.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins sustain given rising space and export mix, and what are the exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are to wholly owned subsidiary ARC with higher value add (RF portion of SDRs co-developed with Rafael), with gross margin near 40-45%. Space subsystems for a defence satellite contributed decently in Q4 and similar orders are expected from ISRO and defence. Management said margins are a function of order mix and may vary.

qa_highlights.question: How much more capex is needed for the 3x revenue target, and will working capital improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR40-50 crores a year with no additional capex beyond normal run-rate. Working capital will rise with volumes but should be funded within sanctioned limits; receivables realisation is expected to continue, so finance cost should be similar to FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Given space order book share has shrunk, how does margin mix look?
qa_highlights.answer: Space is about 10-15% of sales, so a lower space order share should not hurt overall margins. Management said FY26 margin was about 55% and the aim is to sustain it, with guidance at the top end and margin numbers possibly slightly lower to avoid disappointment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MMIC dependency and sourcing position?
qa_highlights.answer: No issues encountered in MMIC production or development. Most active devices in subsystems are sourced from the in-house MMIC division, and the company is now promoting MMICs to domestic and international customers.

qa_highlights.question: Has the total addressable market (about INR28,000 crores FY26-FY28) changed?
qa_highlights.answer: The total accessible market is unchanged, but programme timing has slipped, so the opportunity window moves from FY28-FY29 to FY30-FY31 due to budget and priority delays.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and business scale for the Su-30 upgrade programmes?
qa_highlights.answer: Radar qualification likely in FY28 with user qualification about one more year; EW (Angad) development expected to complete in about one year; production orders are expected 2-3 years after that, with DRDO timing not controlled by Astra.

qa_highlights.question: Why was JV profit only about INR1 crore and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR1 crore figure was for Q4; full-year JV share of profit was about INR8 crores after tax. Around $2 million of forex provision and ongoing R&D weighed on profit. JV EBITDA is projected at 18-20%, implying at least about INR20 crores share of profit on INR600 crores revenue, with management calling INR20 crores a minimum.

risks_watch: Programme timing slippage from DRDO and government-driven budgets; the TAM window has shifted to FY30-FY31.
Su-30 radar and EW programmes are still in development; production orders depend on DRDO and user qualification and may take 2-3 years after qualification.
Quarterly margin variability depends on order mix; management warned of possible variations.
Working capital needs will rise with volume growth despite improved receivables realisation.
ARC profitability hit by forex provision (about $2 million) in FY26; JV profit conversion is well below the earlier 10-12% PBT framing.
Consolidated vs standalone order book distinction (INR2,600 crores vs INR2,141 crores) and the demerger structure need clarity when the scheme is published.
Uttam (HAL) and QRSAM (BEL) order timing (Q2-Q3 FY27 and post June 2026) are key near-term catalysts.
532493|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term strategy and the three-fold growth narrative, but cautious and hedged on specific timing of DRDO and Su-30 orders, repeatedly noting that delays are possible. Management also described the INR20 crore JV profit as a minimum and guided margins to the top end with some caution.
key_quotes: We are very much a tier-1 systems company.
not a single rupee from these future proprietary IP-led opportunities has been factored into our near threefold growth aspiration over the next five years.
the margins delivered by the company in the current year is about 55%.
This is probably as best as it gets, if I may say so.

532493|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue was modest at INR182 crore, while a INR2,205 crore HAL Uttam Radar order lifted the total order book to about INR4,300 crore.
532493|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 as modest on revenue and profitability, blaming customer approval delays and last-stage technical issues that it expects to normalise in coming quarters. Q1 order inflow was INR185 crore, in line with guidance. The July receipt of the INR2,205 crore HAL Uttam Radar subsystem order (about INR1,870 crore ex-GST) roughly doubled the order book. Management reiterated FY27 revenue of about INR1,350 crore (guided as more than 15-20% growth) and flagged a planned demerger of the Space and Weather divisions from April 1, 2027.

financial_highlights.change: Described as modest; no YoY figure given in call

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone order book at quarter end
Consolidated order book at quarter end

financial_highlights.metric: Order book after July HAL Uttam Radar win (as stated)

segments.name: Defence (Uttam Radar, HAL)
segments.commentary: Largest order in company history: about INR2,205 crore from HAL for critical subsystems for Uttam Radar, with a 5-year execution window. Phase 1 of 12 numbers due by September 2027, about 14 months from order date.

segments.name: Space, Metrology and Hydrology
segments.commentary: About 34% of the standalone order book. Management guided INR120-150 crore of FY27 revenue from space. Space and Weather is to be demerged as a separate listed entity, with first-year standalone revenue guided at INR300-plus crore and at least 18-20% PBT margin.

segments.name: Joint venture (Astra Rafael Comsys)
segments.commentary: Order book INR836 crore; FY27 booking target INR360 crore. Management expects INR500-750 crore of further ARC orders over the forecast period.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target about INR1,350 crore, plus or minus INR25 crore; growth stated as more than 15%, with 15-20% given in Q&A.
FY28 revenue about INR1,600 crore, plus or minus INR50 crore, with growth of 15-18%.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR1,600 crore, excluding the Uttam order; management said it may be improved over the next few quarters.
Over 5 years, management expects at least 6-7x FY26 revenue. It sees order intake of INR8,000-9,000 crore over 3-4 years, excluding chip sales, counter-UAV, EM wall, exports and BrahMos NG.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be similar to FY26, with a positive delta increase; no long-term margin guidance given.
Management said it expects the Q3 and Q4 working capital position to be broadly similar to FY26, and it has no plan to dilute equity for working capital.
capex_capacity: Uttam Radar: Phase 1 of 12 numbers due by September 2027; roughly 25+ numbers per year thereafter; management said total quantity could be executed by FY31.
Own satellite to be launched within the first 6 months after the Space and Weather entity lists; part of a planned satellite constellation.
Management said production lines and teams are fully ready for large-scale execution; investment in automated process engineering and infrastructure is ongoing.

Su-30 upgrades (Virupaksha, Angad): Tier 1 radar and Tier 2 EW role; management expects about INR3,000 crore of orders over the forecast period.
QRSAM: expects INR700-800 crore of orders for the first 3 regiments; part of the existing INR4,300 crore book is expected before year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Which top-line growth target is correct: 10-15% (press release) or 15-20% (presentation)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the correct target is in excess of 15%, i.e. 15-20% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the year-end order book target?

qa_highlights.question: Is EW (Tejas, Su-30) and LCH content in the order inflow projections?
qa_highlights.answer: Angad and some LCH subsystems are included in the 4-year projections. Tejas Mk1A is additional, around INR500-600 crore. Management said none of the EM wall or counter-UAV revenue is in its numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to positive cash at the end of FY26, which kept overdraft utilisation in Q1 minimal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Uttam execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall execution is about 5 years, with total completion before FY32 and possibly by FY31; Phase 1 of 12 numbers is due by September 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What margin guidance is available for new products?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 6-7x five-year revenue target based on the defence business only?

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue decline and was there deferred revenue?

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital moderate further in FY27?

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 revenue of INR182 crore was described as modest; management attributes shortfall to inspection, specification-proof, development-cycle and supply-chain delays and expects Q3 and Q4 to carry the year, so watch whether H2 execution delivers the INR1,350 crore FY27 target (+/-INR25 crore).

Execution load on the INR2,205 crore Uttam Radar order: Phase 1 of 12 numbers due by September 2027 and roughly 25+ numbers per year thereafter; supply chains are stretched and management flagged cross-border supply risk.

Working capital: management expects Q3 and Q4 pressure to build and no significant change versus FY26; it ruled out equity dilution for working capital, so monitor receivables and operating cash flow at the end-Q3 update.

Order inflow visibility rests on unawarded programmes (AMCA AAAU where the company is L1 with contract expected in about a month, QRSAM, Su-30 Virupaksha/Angad, Tejas Mk1A EW, P-75I); none of the EM wall, counter-UAV, chip, export or BrahMos NG upside is in numbers.

Space and Weather demerger from April 1, 2027: details on leadership, plans, satellite launch and the INR300-plus crore first-year revenue guidance remain to be shared over the next few quarters; watch for structure and shareholder-ratio clarity.

Long-term 5-year 6-7x revenue ambition and INR8,000-9,000 crore order intake ambition were questioned by analysts (ICICI Securities on cumulative execution); management said it would clarify one-to-one, so treat as unverified until tracked.

532497|2026-06.headline: Radico Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 1,684 crore and EBITDA Rs 348 crore (20.7% margin, record); P&A volumes up 36%.
532497|2026-06.overview: Radico reported record quarterly IMFL volume of 10 million cases (up 3% YoY), revenue of Rs 1,684 crore and EBITDA of Rs 348 crore. Premium and above (P&A) volumes grew 36%, while regular volumes declined on a higher base after the Andhra Pradesh route-to-market change and policy changes in Maharashtra and Karnataka. Gross margin rose 610 bps YoY to 49.1% and EBITDA margin rose 536 bps YoY to 20.7%. Management reiterated about 20% EBITDA margin for FY27 and raised P&A volume growth guidance to over 25% from 20%, and said it is on track to become net debt free by Q2 FY27.

Maintenance capex Rs 150 to 170 crore; management said acquisitions are unlikely and growth will stay organic.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be sustained at 20% EBITDA and how does ENA cost exposure matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 20% EBITDA margin for FY27 and said more clarity will come later in the year. Mix shift to P&A is expected to support margins, reducing ENA sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20.7% margin sustainable, and what are IMFL and non-IMFL margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-IMFL margin is about 11% to 11.5% and IMFL is 23%+. Non-IMFL margins historically ranged 8% to 11%, fell to 6% to 7% during inflation, and management considers current levels sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan once debt free?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance capex is Rs 150 to 170 crore; the remainder is for the Board to decide. Acquisitions only if they make sense for shareholders; management says Radico has always grown organically and sees no brand acquisition opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Magic Moments 43% growth a trade-loading one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied trade loading, citing strong credit control, and said the growth is tertiary-driven, with month-on-month traction continuing.

qa_highlights.question: How will the India-UK FTA affect pricing and competition in luxury?

qa_highlights.question: Will A&P spend increase given P&A growth well ahead of peers?

532504|2026-06.headline: Navin Fluorine Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 44% YoY to INR1,044-1,045 crore, with EBITDA up 73% and PAT up 108% to INR243 crore.
532504|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 44% YoY to about INR1,045 crore, with operating EBITDA of INR357 crore (34.2% margin, up 566 bps YoY) and PAT of INR243 crore. Advanced materials adoption capex (INR90 crore) to be done in two phases, first phase around mid-Q4 FY27 for commercial-scale qualification; not included in any return projections.

qa_highlights.question: Advanced materials: end-use applications, and growth beyond FY28 given current capex?

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR90 crore adoption capex a pilot or commercial scale, and what is the payback?

qa_highlights.question: R32 pricing and India capacity additions versus quota start in Jan 2028?

qa_highlights.question: Why did subsidiary (NFASL) margin fall about 12 pp QoQ?

532505|2026-06.headline: UCO Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 8% YoY to Rs 656 crore despite a Rs 1,237 crore one-time DTA charge; operating profit up 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore.
532505|2026-06.overview: UCO Bank reported Q1 FY27 with advances up 21.18% YoY to Rs 2,72,768 crore and deposits up 11.28% to Rs 3,32,315 crore. Operating profit rose 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore, helped by Rs 1,018 crore of technical write-off recoveries, of which about Rs 800 crore is from a few accounts management does not expect to recur. Net profit was held to Rs 656 crore by total tax of Rs 1,919 crore, including a one-time Rs 1,237 crore DTA remeasurement on the shift to the new tax regime. Management said most asset-quality and margin metrics were within guidance, and that it would review credit growth guidance only after Q2.

segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 30% YoY; gold loans are cited as a growth driver.

segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 25.27% YoY and make up 64.5% of the book, within the 62-65% guidance; management aims to hold around 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Can management give full-year guidance on cost of funds, cost of deposits, cost-to-income, RAM and corporate advances, ROE and ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds fell to 4.36% as deposit repricing completed; expected to stay stable. NIM 3.05% vs 2.8-2.9% guidance, aim to stay above 2.9%; yield on advances moved about 3 bps. Cost-to-income 37.49% in Q1 but flattered by about Rs 800 crore from few TWO accounts; FY27 target around or below 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank shifting away from IBPC and low-yield government lending, and where is the rebalancing?

qa_highlights.question: What upside does UCO get from West Bengal's investment climate, given its Kolkata head office?
qa_highlights.answer: About 400 branches in West Bengal across five zonal offices; opportunities seen in steel, railway-related and infrastructure projects. Pan-India network of 3,421 branches.

qa_highlights.question: What would ROA have been under the old tax regime, and what are NIM, ROA and EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No figure given; the shift to the new regime is statutory. Management said ROA could have been above 1% excluding the Rs 1,237 crore charge, a rough estimate. ROA of 0.68% now, seen near 1% by year-end; NIM guidance 2.8-2.9%.

qa_highlights.question: Where is competition coming from (PSU, private, NBFC)?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition from PSBs, private banks, RRBs and NBFCs; management would not quantify the split and views the market as expanding. Digital balance sheet about Rs 35,000 crore at 30 June vs Rs 25,000 crore at 31 March; 70% of FDs booked digitally.

qa_highlights.question: Should the 12-14% credit growth guidance be raised given 21% actual growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance kept at 12-14% for now; the bank aims to grow above industry and will review only after Q2 FY27 results. Rs 15,000 crore sanctioned pipeline awaiting disbursement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECLGS sanction and disbursement, and is any MSME stress visible?
qa_highlights.answer: ECLGS sanctions about Rs 2,150 crore, of which Rs 1,700 crore disbursed, under 50% of eligible customers' loans. SMA-1 book (Rs 1 crore and above) fell to Rs 1,009 crore (0.36%) from Rs 1,125 crore (0.43%) in March; slippage 0.63%.

qa_highlights.question: How much ECL provision is already held versus the requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Assessment done on the 1 April transition date; about 60% of the requirement already provided as buffer over and above mandatory provisions. Remaining 40% to be built over the next 4-5 quarters before ECL starts.

qa_highlights.question: Retail loan pricing trends and corporate pricing; was there JP Associates interest recovery in TWO income?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail rates held as they are repo-linked; MCLR raised 5 bps to 8.80% in July 2026. Corporate pricing held, with demand shifting to loans as bond yields limited. No interest recovery from JP Associates in interest income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise QoQ, why did fee income from loan processing fall, and what drove other commission?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of deposits rose slightly due to reclassification of deposits and borrowings; overall cost of funds still lower. Advance-related fees fell as renewal charges are now recognised on actual basis; other commission rose on PSLC sale of about Rs 2,000 crore earning Rs 55 crore.

Corporate book growth driven by working-capital limit drawdowns; sustainability of demand and yield on the corporate book to watch.
ECLGS and MSME stress: management sees none, but the ECLGS 5.0 disbursement pace and SMA-1 trend need monitoring.

532505|2026-09.headline: UCO Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 26.77% YoY to Rs 786 crore; advances grew 24.70%, well above the 12-14% guidance.

Global advances grew 24.70% to Rs 2,87,690 crore, while deposits grew 14.36% to Rs 3,49,590 crore and CASA ratio slipped to 36.77%. Gross NPA fell 60 bps YoY to 1.96% and net NPA to 0.18%, both within guidance. Management said the quarter's slippage rise was mainly agriculture crop-loan marking done half-yearly in September, and that the June quarter had a one-off Rs 785 crore recovery that did not recur.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit rates be raised, and with what lag?
qa_highlights.answer: No immediate need to raise deposit rates; current term deposit rates maintained. Any hike would apply only to new deposits and renewals, decided later based on deposit requirement.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a change in corporate stance, and will the bank raise its credit growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate advances grew 24.15% YoY; RAM share crossed 65% (guidance 62-65%) and is expected to hold around 65%. Corporate sanctioned but undisbursed pipeline is about Rs 10,000 crore, dependent on lending rates and capex. Guidance of 12-14% kept; management aims to exceed it but will not revise mid-year.

Estimate not materially changed from three months earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating expenses rise by about Rs 160 crore, and is it one-off?

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost and cost-to-income outlook for the full year?

Cost-to-income was 50.39% (about 45% excluding the June one-off effect); expected around 50% for FY27 and possibly below 50% next year.

qa_highlights.question: Second-hand car loan growth and yield, and housing ticket size?
qa_highlights.answer: Second-hand car loans are not tracked separately and are a small share of car loans; management will work out numbers. Average home-loan ticket rose from about Rs 35 lakh to about Rs 45 lakh, with growth from both volume and ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Is NII growth enough to offset treasury stress, and what NIM is expected in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said repo-linked NII growth (about 66% of advances) would more than offset treasury stress, and that FVTPL exposure is small. Global NIM was 3.00% and domestic 3.19%, against guidance of 2.80-2.90%; management expects to sustain NIM above guidance.

532508|2026-06.headline: Jindal Stainless Q1 FY27: revenue up 10.5% YoY and PAT up 7.7%, but finished-goods volume fell 7.3% on gas shortages; FY27 volume guidance held.

Management kept FY27 volume guidance (8-10% growth) and the INR 18,000-20,000/t H1 EBITDA guidance, deferring any revision to the next quarter. Indonesia melt shop (1.2 MTPA) has started ramping up; the Jindal Stainless Indonesia structure changed from subsidiary to associate effective 1 July 2026.

Group EBITDA was INR902 crore at a 21% margin, and reported net profit before exceptionals was INR145 crore (up 245% YoY) as interest cost fell 23% YoY to INR213 crore. Biosimilars grew 16% to INR2,855 crore, while generics grew 21% to INR760 crore with EBITDA margin recovering to 7%. Management said the second half should be stronger, driven by new launches (Aflibercept in the US, denosumab in Europe) and insulin capacity from the Malaysia second drug product line. Working capital and net debt rose sequentially on inventory build ahead of the H2 ramp.

qa_highlights.answer: Kiran Mazumdar Shaw said Bicara is no longer significant, the holding is small, and monetisation is not being contemplated at present.
