qa_highlights.question: Opex growth of 8-9% vs balance sheet growth above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost growth is driven by staffing new branches from day one; cost-to-income is 36-38% and guided below 40%. Branches opened three or more years ago have all turned profitable, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did treasury profit jump to INR266 crore and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury included a one-time SR of INR104 crore, with part of the payment possibly coming in later quarters; no treasury profit targets are set.

qa_highlights.question: SMA-2 jump from INR56 crore to INR208 crore; is MSME stress rising?
qa_highlights.answer: A single government entity account of INR87 crore moved into SMA-2 and is expected to regularise. SMA-1+2 stands at 1.34%, down 5 bps YoY.

risks_watch: Cost of deposits rose 5 bps QoQ to 4.38% and retail term deposits are growing faster than total deposits; watch the QoQ trend.
Thin CASA growth in Q1 (current account balances fell sharply QoQ) and reliance on refinance (about INR19,000 crore) and possible CDs as deposit growth lags loan growth.
Agri gross NPA at 7.58% and the debt-waiver haircut timing; the Rs 87 crore government account in SMA-2 needs to regularise.
Agri and MSME gross NPA rose QoQ (MSME 1.60%); watch for stress from geopolitical conditions (West Asia).
NIM pressure from MCLR resets, with the yield on advances down 71 bps YoY to 8.57% globally; the rate-hike benefit depends on repo-linked share at 53%.
Equity raise of INR5,000 crore pending government approval; treasury gains include a one-time item of INR104 crore.
ECL provisioning of about INR125 crore per quarter through March 2031 against net worth.
532525|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and asset quality, with repeated emphasis on keeping guidance unchanged. Management was evasive on the NII-versus-loan-growth gap and the cost-of-deposit trajectory, answering both with qualitative points rather than numbers.
key_quotes: We are committed to the guidance numbers that we have shared.
Gross NPA is maintained at the March level 1.45% against our guidance of maintaining it below 2%.
So refinance, again, why we decided not to go for high-cost bulk deposits, the blended cost that we have experienced while we go for refinance is in the range of 6% to 6.5%.
The mantra is very clear. It has to be a profitable growth and no compromise on the quality.

532525|2026-09.headline: Bank of Maharashtra Q2 FY27: business up 25% YoY, advances up 30%, ROE 26.98%, GNPA down 47 bps to 1.25%.
532525|2026-09.overview: Management said all FY27 guidance metrics were met in Q2, with business crossing INR7 lakh crore and advances growing 30% YoY (23% ex-IBU). Operating profit rose 31% and net profit 41% YoY, lifting ROE 440 bps to 26.98% and NIM 12 bps to 3.97%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 1.25% and NNPA at 0.12%, helped by write-off recoveries and lower NPA provisions, while INR500 crore of ECL provisions was booked in the standard asset line. Cost of deposits fell 4 bps YoY to 4.38%, though management acknowledged a QoQ rise tied to FCNR(B) and OFCB raises of about $1.65 billion.

financial_highlights.metric: Cost of deposits / cost of funds

segments.name: Advances / large credit
segments.commentary: Large credit up 38% YoY to INR36,000 crore, of which INR18,000 crore from GIFT City IBU and INR18,000 crore domestic (19% growth). Domestic credit ex-IBU grew 23%, with RAM, retail, agri and MSME each above 20%.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Deposits up 22% YoY, or 19% ex-FCNR(B); CASA up 12% YoY with INR19,000 crore CASA added over the last FY.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri book INR44,000 crore, up 34% YoY (about INR11,000 crore). Agri gold loans INR18,600 crore vs INR6,500 crore in Sep-25; agri stress down 35 bps to 3.51%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Total gold loan outstanding INR33,000 crore; MSME gold loan about INR2,000 crore. Retail gold declined QoQ as loans were reclassified to agri/MSME under RBI norms.

guidance_outlook: Management said all FY27 guidance metrics across growth, profitability, asset quality and capital were met in H1.
Domestic credit guidance is 18%; management sees no challenge sustaining above 18% with INR23,000 crore pipeline and INR10,000 crore expected to be disbursed by March 2027.
Recovery target from written-off accounts of INR1,300-1,500 crore annually for the next 4-5 years; FY27 recovery so far INR1,023 crore.
ECL: total assessed requirement INR2,500 crore over 4 years; INR750 crore already provided (INR250 crore earlier plus INR500 crore in Q2), which management says covers more than 1 year.
Maharashtra debt-waiver government receivable (about INR2,700 crore of eligible INR3,500 crore): about INR1,200 crore received to 30 Sep; SLBC timeline for balance is 31 March 2027.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion: about 200 branches planned annually; 77 branches made functional in H1 FY27.
Employee strength raised to 17,500 from about 13,000 two years earlier, driven by branch expansion and specialist hiring (treasury, IBU, IT).
IT budget: INR900 crore in FY25 and INR985 crore in FY26, with a large share on cyber security.
Pipeline sector mix: infra power about 18%, roads/HAM about 12%, renewables about 10%, metals and others about 10%; data centres cited as a niche growth area.
demand_pricing: Credit growth ex-IBU of 23% YoY; IBU book INR18,500 crore funded partly by about $560 million of FCNR(B) leverage. The FCNR(B) special window has closed.
Repricing: management raised rates on several MCLR-linked state PSU facilities (several thousand crore, about 25 bps on some) in Q1, contributing to NIM gains.
Global yield on advances 8.86%, domestic 9.02%; IBU yield not disclosed on the call.
Gold loan pricing tiers: agri lowest, MSME about 50 bps higher, non-priority retail highest.
EBLR-linked loans are 47% of the loan book.

qa_highlights.question: Provisioning: standard/restructured provisions rose to INR603 crore from INR76 crore; what is the ECL preparedness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NPA provisions fell from INR580 crore a year ago to INR120 crore this quarter, helped by recoveries. Standard-asset provisions rose to INR603 crore including INR500 crore of ECL; total ECL assessed at INR2,500 crore over 4 years, with INR750 crore already provided.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit growth sustain after the FCNR window closes, and will write-off recoveries continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IBU leverage was about $560 million from FCNR(B) and the window is closed; domestic growth is 23% and the INR23,000 crore pipeline supports growth above the 18% guidance. Write-off recovery target is INR1,300-1,500 crore a year for 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FCNR(B) is fixed at 6.51%, OFCB at 6.11%, and 1-year CDs at about 7.75-7.9%. About $1.65 billion was raised via FCNR(B) and OFCB against a $1.5 billion plan, with 5-year fixed-cost borrowings and a 3x oversubscribed MTN issue; YoY cost of deposits fell 4 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the 30 bps QoQ rise in yield on advances despite IBU mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to repricing of MCLR-linked state PSU accounts (about 25 bps on several thousand crore), a one-off write-off recovery impact of about 2-3 bps on NIM, and a 3-4 bps ITR refund. Only INR30 crore of the INR125 crore recovery has gone to interest income so far.

qa_highlights.question: Drought exposure and restructuring under SLBC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no visible agri stress; special SLBC restructuring applies at 33-50% crop loss (1-year moratorium, up to 3-year tenor) and above 50% loss (5-year tenor including 1-year moratorium). Farmer applications open till February 2027; past experience suggests 10-15% take-up, with about 5% provisioning on the restructured amount.

qa_highlights.question: Agri gold and retail gold trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri gold loans rose to INR18,600 crore from INR6,500 crore YoY. Retail gold declined QoQ because loans were reclassified to MSME/agri under RBI norms; total gold outstanding INR33,000 crore and MSME gold about INR2,000 crore.

risks_watch: Drought and El Nino: Maharashtra drought could trigger SLBC restructuring; management estimates 10-15% take-up and says no visible stress yet.
ECL transition: INR2,500 crore total assessed; management said the number may fall; surplus provisions of INR1,600-1,800 crore (COVID, global uncertainties INR200 crore) can be used.
Cost of deposits: QoQ increase from high-cost FCNR(B)/OFCB/CD raises; FY28 impact on margin depends on deployment.
Maharashtra debt-waiver balance of about INR1,500 crore receivable; management does not count on it and timing depends on state process (deadline 31 March 2027).
Pace of IBU growth after the FCNR(B) window closed; IBU yield not disclosed.
Cyber and DPDP compliance; management deferred detailed answer.
532525|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and profitability, with frequent emphasis on guidance delivery. Cautious on agri and drought stress, and evasive on IBU yield and October SMA data, which were deferred to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: And I'm happy to share that each one of those guidance numbers have been met, and this is getting consistently met also is one good feature.
So I don't see a challenge at all to maintain a pace above our guidance of 18% in credit in future also.
Our total assessment was that INR2,500 crores is our ECL provisioning to be done in 4 years.

532527|2026-06.headline: Ramkrishna Forgings Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 1,217 crore (+19.8% YoY), PAT Rs 46.9 crore (~4x YoY), EBITDA margin 17.96%.
532527|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was flat QoQ at Rs 1,217 crore and up 19.84% YoY, with EBITDA excluding other income at Rs 218.47 crore (up 47% YoY, 5% QoQ). EBITDA margin rose to 17.96% from 17.11% in Q4, while management said energy and shipping costs were not fully passed on. Net debt fell about Rs 100 crore QoQ to around Rs 1,900 crore, and management reiterated a Rs 500 crore leverage reduction target for FY27. Management guided to strong export growth, a wheels JV and rail trial ramp-up, and a multi-year non-ferrous (aluminium, titanium, Inconel) push.

financial_highlights.change: from 17.11% in previous quarter (+85 bps QoQ)
Up ~535 bps QoQ per analyst question; management said it is sustainable
Down ~Rs 100 crore from Rs 1,990 crore last quarter
Per analyst question; not stated by management

segments.name: Automotive (order wins)
segments.commentary: Secured Rs 278 crore of business with a four-year program life; ~82% passenger vehicle and ~18% two-wheeler, all domestic. Passenger vehicle split roughly 50:50 ICE vs EV per management.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Won Rs 15 crore of Metro orders from Indian Railways. Rail wheel JV (RKTR) trial production has started; first 300 sample wheels to be submitted in August.

segments.name: Mexico
segments.commentary: Production started; about Rs 6 crore of revenue booked this quarter, with significant revenue expected from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Aluminium / non-ferrous
segments.commentary: Bulk supplies of aluminium forgings have started. Management says meaningful contribution from aerospace/semiconductor/robotics is 12-18 months away, with Inconel/titanium 8-10 quarters away.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated ROCE targeted at 12-15%; FY28 target 20%.
Exports expected at about 35% of consolidated revenue for FY27 and growth of 'almost 20% plus' in exports; management called it possibly the highest export revenue ever.
Net debt reduction of at least Rs 500 crore in FY27 (implying ~Rs 1,500 crore by year-end), per management.
FY27 capex guidance around Rs 350 crore, plus Rs 20-30 crore further investment into the rail wheel JV.
Turnover target of Rs 8,000 crore now pegged to FY29 (one year later than earlier), implying 22-25% CAGR.
Working capital: internal target of 15-20 days improvement across debtor, inventory and creditor days, with management suggesting roughly 10 days per year.
Cold forging capacity utilisation expected above 70% by Q3 FY27; sustainable utilisation of 75-80% before next capex.
Rail wheel plant: bulk production targeted for Sept/Oct 2026 with full contractual supply to Railways thereafter.
capex_capacity: Majority of strategic capex is complete; focus shifted to utilisation and asset turn. Management cited asset turn of 2.5x on ~Rs 3,700 crore net block implying ~Rs 9,000 crore sales at 100% utilisation, though it said 75-80% is the practical ceiling.
Ring rolling capacity at 127% utilisation; management said no plans to add ring rolling capacity and expects peak utilisation for two to three years.
A new press line is being added; it will take four to five quarters to reach about 80% press utilisation.
Casting plant capitalised in Q4 FY26; integration substantially complete and capacity ramp-up expected over the next three quarters.
Aluminium forging capability in place; Inconel/titanium capex limited to about Rs 10-20 crore for heating arrangements.
Wheel JV: 80,000 confirmed Railway wheel order plus about 25,000 wheels from JV partners (~1,10,000 total), covering production until end FY28. Major new capex to be announced only by end FY28.
demand_pricing: Management described the order book as strong, with healthy domestic demand, and expects the next half (after monsoon, around September) to be exciting domestically.
Export growth driven by Europe and North America, with new orders from existing and new customers; customer names not disclosed.
Steel is passed through with a one-quarter lag; gas, energy and shipping costs are not fully passed on. No hedging available for steel.
Currency is passed through every quarter on all contracts, per management, so rupee depreciation (1-1.5% in quarter) gives no net benefit.

Domestic realisation rose QoQ on better mix, higher utilisation and product choice. Casting realisations declined QoQ due to one-off components run during capacity ramp-up; management expects recovery.
Management said it would not guide on profitability or a full-year margin range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin rise only 85 bps QoQ when gross margin rose ~535 bps? Is it only price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied it was only price, citing product mix. It said energy and shipping costs have not been passed on, which limited EBITDA margin gains; improvement should follow once costs stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Are there target ROCEs for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 ROCE of 12-15% and FY28 target of 20%, with ROCE returning to historical levels.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 278 crore auto order be domestic or export?
qa_highlights.answer: Entirely domestic: ~82% passenger vehicle and ~18% two-wheeler; the two-wheeler business is crankshafts from the Gurugram machining facility. Management says the PV order is EV, which is domestic-brand supply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV vs ICE mix in passenger vehicles and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: PV order book is about 50:50 ICE and EV. Export sales have so far been more EV-led, with bulk ICE supply starting.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt fall to Rs 1,000 crore in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No target given; management said it is not aiming for a zero-debt company but will keep leverage under check while growing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the Rs 8,000 crore turnover target?
qa_highlights.answer: Target moved to FY29 (one year later), implying 22-25% CAGR from last year's turnover of about Rs 4,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 margin improving given market conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: No improvement in market conditions yet. Management said energy and shipping costs will not moderate unless geopolitical issues are resolved.

risks_watch: Energy and shipping costs not yet passed on; management said they will not moderate unless the geopolitical situation (West Asia) is resolved, so EBITDA margin gains depend on cost relief.
Steel passes through with a one-quarter lag and cannot be hedged; a sharp steel move could swing quarterly margins in either direction.
Working capital pressure from shipping delays and longer transit times; management gave internal targets of 15-20 days improvement but no firm timeline.
Execution on new ventures: aluminium forging bulk supply started, aerospace/semiconductor/robotics revenue 12-18 months away, Inconel/titanium 8-10 quarters away; zero aerospace order book currently.
Mexico revenue ramp (about Rs 6 crore this quarter, significant revenue from Q3 FY27) and rail wheel JV bulk production targeted Sept/Oct 2026 are timeline commitments to track.
Casting realisations fell QoQ due to one-off components during ramp-up; management expects recovery next quarter. Ring rolling at 127% utilisation with no capacity addition planned.
key_quotes: So, we would not like to guide the market in terms of profitability.
No, I think we have not seen any improvement in terms of market conditions.
No, I think this margin is sustainable margin and you will see improvement on it going forward.
I think it is at least 12 months to 18 months before we have a significant revenue or product lines from this section.
532527|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and export outlook, but cautious and evasive on margins: management refused to give a full-year margin range or profitability guidance and said Q2 market conditions had not improved. Deliberately vague on timelines for working capital targets and the non-ferrous ramp.

532528|2026-06.headline: Datamatics Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore, with EBITDA margin up 343 bps to 19.7%.
532528|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore and EBITDA rose to INR 101.1 crore at a 19.7% margin, with the margin gain attributed to cost discipline and operational excellence. Digital Operations drove growth (revenue up 16.1%, EBIT margin 19.3%), while Digital Technologies grew 6.1% at an 8.9% EBIT margin and Digital Experiences declined 5.3%. Management reiterated high single-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance, citing softness from geopolitical uncertainty, and said about 60% of FY27 deals won were AI-led or AI-driven. The TNQTech integration into Lumina Datamatics was completed in the quarter, and a INR 200 crore TNQTech payout was made in Q1.

segments.name: Digital Operations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 296.8 crore, up 16.1% YoY; EBIT margin 19.3%. TNQTech is integrated here, per management.

segments.name: Digital Technologies
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 153.1 crore, up 6.1% YoY; EBIT margin 8.9%. Carries the company's AI R&D spend of about INR 40-50 crore a year, which management says depresses the margin.

segments.name: Digital Experiences
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 64 crore, down 5.3% YoY; EBIT margin 11.7%. Management said several good-sized deals were signed this year and the practice is seeing an upswing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of high single digits, maintained despite market softness.
Full-year EBITDA margin expected to rise about 0.5 percentage point, to close to 20%; management later said 19-20% at year end.
AI R&D spend to stay at about the same level (INR 40-50 crore) in FY27; FY28 budget not yet decided.

Management cited a roughly 3-year target of about INR 3,000 crore revenue, versus about INR 2,000 crore now, to be a mix of organic and inorganic growth; it was described as starting in the current year.
Annual salary increments effective April 2026 are already reflected in Q1 numbers.
M&A dialogue is ongoing but no deal has matured to disclosure stage.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were discussed.

AI platforms cited as growth drivers: KAiBRE and KAiSDLC for legacy modernisation, KAi underwriting for insurance, agentic claims processing, and SuperCX for contact-centre and front-office automation.
Legacy modernisation projects reportedly compress timelines from about three years to about six months; first underwriting-product revenue has been booked with one customer.
demand_pricing: Customers are choosing Datamatics for AI capability; recent wins include SBI Life Insurance (TruAI underwriting), a US pet and veterinary provider (AI voice agent) and a US consumer products company (KAiBRE/KAiSDLC).
About 60% of deals won this fiscal were AI-led or largely AI-driven, per management.
Deal sizes are rising but are increasingly shorter (3-9 month) AI projects rather than multi-year annuity contracts; management said margins are not shrinking.
Competition is increasingly from well-funded local AI start-ups, GCCs and captive tech teams, not from larger listed IT peers.
Top 5, 10 and 20 clients contribute 30%, 41% and 54% of revenue. Education and Publishing is 29%, technology and consulting 20%, BFSI 19%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for AI R&D spend, and is there any plan for buybacks or M&A with the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: AI R&D stays at about INR 40-50 crore this year. Cash of INR 710 crore predates the INR 200 crore TNQTech payout, and management is in M&A dialogue but nothing has matured; no buyback was mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 revenue growth consistent with the full-year guidance, given the strong Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained high single-digit FY27 growth guidance and cited market softness from the war and uncertainty. The CFO clarified that 43% growth refers to PAT, while revenue grew 9.9%.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Digital Technologies grown slowly with margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to traction in KAi underwriting, KAiSDLC and KAiBRE, with legacy modernisation projects starting. It said the segment carries the AI investment, so removing it would give a much healthier margin.

qa_highlights.question: How has the competitive landscape changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not compete much with large listed IT players. Competition comes from funded local AI start-ups, GCCs and in-house tech teams.

qa_highlights.question: What are the risks to the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Key risks are customers automating in-house instead of outsourcing, captive/GCC setups, and geopolitical softness.

qa_highlights.question: What is the five-year blueprint and what are the revenue drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about INR 3,000 crore over roughly three years from about INR 2,000 crore now, with organic growth from AI platforms and bolt-on acquisitions.

risks_watch: Customer insourcing to automation and GCC/captive setups could reduce outsourcing budgets, per management.
Geopolitical uncertainty (the war) is cited as softening demand; management said it needs to settle.
Shift toward shorter AI projects (3-9 months) rather than multi-year annuity deals could affect revenue visibility.
Digital Experiences declined 5.3% YoY and Digital Technologies margin is 8.9%; watch for recovery.
Whether AI R&D spend (INR 40-50 crore) remains flat next year is undecided.
532528|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on AI-led deal wins, margins and the INR 3,000 crore ambition, but cautious on near-term demand, which management said remains soft due to the war. Management was vague on TNQTech's standalone contribution and on the FY28 AI spend.
key_quotes: So, we have projected a high single-digit growth in our guidance. We are maintaining that.
We are seeing strong market validation of our AI-first strategy.
So, a project that will take three years can be probably done in six months now.

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash and investments (net of debt)
financial_highlights.change: As of 30 June 2026, before INR 200 crore TNQTech payout in Q1

532531|2026-03.headline: Strides FY26 revenue rose 6.4% to INR48,587 mn and EBITDA 15% to INR925 crore at 19% margin; Q4 US revenue weak at $70 mn as flu season failed to materialise.
532531|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 6.4% YoY to INR48,587 mn, held back by a weak second-half US flu season and donor-funding pressure in access markets; management says underlying growth was about 10% excluding access markets. Ex-US revenue grew 21% and reached about 50% of Q4 revenue, while EBITDA margin expanded 140 bps to 19% for the year. Q4 EBITDA rose 10% YoY to INR240 crore (18.1% margin), with about INR20 crore of logistics and air-freight cost pressure. Operational PAT crossed INR500 crore for the first time at INR518 crore, and the Board recommended a dividend of INR5 per share.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue $284 mn and Q4 $70 mn, hit by a weak second-half flu season; 6 launches in the year, 9 products exited, and some molecules faced higher competition, with leading positions in 37 of 70 products. Controlled substances from the Chestnut Ridge ANDA acquisition are in their first full year, with 4 products launched and quota allocations below expectations.

segments.name: Ex-US (total)
segments.commentary: Grew 21% in FY26 and reached about 50% of Q4 revenue, with a 3-year CAGR of about 19%. Quarterly ex-US revenue rose from about $40 mn in Q1 FY24 to about $70 mn in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Other regulated markets (ORM)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue rose from about $31 mn in Q1 FY24 to a $52 mn exit run rate in Q4 FY26, with traction in Europe, UK, Australia and the Nordics.

segments.name: Africa / growth markets
segments.commentary: Focus is shifting toward branded business, with Francophone Africa growing faster than the underlying market. The Sandoz product acquisition (announced Feb 2026) is expected to contribute from H2 FY27 and to lift the branded portfolio more than 1.5x.

guidance_outlook: Long-term aspiration: EBITDA margin upwards of 20% and gross margin in the 58%-60% range; Q&A reiterated a 18%-20% margin range for the near term.
US aspiration of $375-400 mn by FY28, described as a full-year FY28 target rather than an exit run rate; management said about 8 quarters remain.
Sequential growth expected from Q4 to Q1 FY27; Q4 sequential growth stated at 11% (14% excluding institutional business).
US growth expected to pick up from H2 FY27; FY26 seasonality was roughly 50:50 H1:H2 versus the usual 45:55.

Sandoz portfolio expected to contribute from H2 FY27; R&D spend to be $20-25 mn a year over the next 2 years; tangible and intangible investment run rate about INR300 crore; nasal sprays, patches and films expected to contribute mainly from FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: FY26 total investment INR418 crore: INR236 crore tangible (including nasal spray capacity, ex-US capacity and a UK office) and INR182 crore intangible (global product rights and SAP HANA ERP upgrade).
Tangible capex is nearly complete beyond maintenance; a run rate of about INR300 crore across tangible and intangible is expected, including possible acquisitions of global rights.
Capacity sufficient for the next 2 years; no major additional capacity needed in the next 1-2 years apart from growth capex.
Chestnut Ridge facility (acquired from Endo) is capable of manufacturing nasal sprays and controlled substances; second nasal spray filed in May 2026, with commercialisation about 12 months away.
Patches and thin films: filing expected in 12-18 months.
demand_pricing: US flu-season demand did not recover in H2 as it had in prior years, and wholesaler discipline also contributed.
Marginal US pricing pressure, offset by COGS improvements; gross margin held in the 58%-60% range for 8 quarters.
Intense competition in a few molecules led to market-share rationalisation; management prioritises profitability over volume.
Q4 logistics and air-freight costs of about INR20 crore hurt margins; price increases are being negotiated with customers.
Access markets are facing donor-funding challenges, which management describes as tactical.

qa_highlights.question: What is happening in the US, including discontinuations and delayed launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the missing flu season, controlled-substance quota timing, and a policy of not launching until market conditions are attractive. It said 150 products are in the portfolio and launches will continue through FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Are controlled substances and nasal sprays structurally higher-margin, and how big is the controlled substances opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said controlled substances are an in-US-for-US strategy and margins will be similar to the current profile, not dramatically different. It declined to give revenue potential, saying the company needs more DEA quota first, and the company has gone back to the DEA for additional quota.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q4 SG&A and freight spike persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SG&A will stay around the current range, with Q4 freight costs elevated. It said a discount factor should be applied to Q4 when modelling.

qa_highlights.question: What are the nasal spray and new modality timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: One or two nasal products could launch earlier, but bulk revenue is expected in FY28-FY29. Patches and thin films filings are expected in 12-18 months, with about 5-6 additional third-party nasal programmes added.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sandoz deal's impact and the R&D outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The Sandoz deal is expected to close in H2 FY27 (October-March). R&D spend is expected to be $20-25 mn over the next 2 years.

risks_watch: US growth depends on a recovery in H2 FY27 and on the controlled-substance quota outcome from the DEA; no timeline was given.
Gross margin needs to stay in the 58%-60% range amid logistics, fuel, raw material and FX cost pressure.
Working capital: cash-to-cash cycle is 124 days, with inventory up 21 days and payables stretched in Q4, which management expects to normalise.
Competition in several US molecules and a 2-year wait before new nasal spray and modality revenue.
Access markets exposed to donor-funding challenges; Sandoz integration timing.
532531|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on ex-US growth, profitability and balance sheet, but cautious and evasive on US timing, quota and controlled-substance sizing. Management repeatedly deferred US recovery to H2 FY27 and declined to quantify the controlled-substance revenue potential.
key_quotes: Ex-U.S. markets have emerged as the most important highlight of our performance.
We are reporting an operational PAT of INR518 crores crossing the INR500 crores mark for the first time.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the new 4W EV plant revenue potential and how much of the 1.85 lakh capacity is booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Booked share was not disclosed; the 1.85 lakh figure is eventual capacity and will be built as business is won. Khed (INR 400 crore+) and the new plant (INR 550 crore) plus about INR 300 crore CSN casting total about INR 1,200 crore capex, with revenue above 2x, at least INR 2,500 crore and up to about INR 3,000 crore at peak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin impact from the labour and commodity pressures, and how does pass-through work?

Pass-through cycles are set by each customer (3 or 6 months, with 1-2 customers annual), not by commodity. Management is seeking monthly or quarterly adjustments. The 11% plus/minus 50 bps guidance includes known start-up costs.

qa_highlights.question: What are the alloy wheel penetration levels and the 2W alloy wheel and 4W alloy wheel capacity post expansion?

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin down about 1%, and how large is the trading drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin fell about 1% YoY. Management attributed this to newer lower-margin businesses and commodity impact. The EV-related trading business is about INR 40-45 crore and too small to matter. Exports from India were about INR 600 crore in FY26 and are expected to cross INR 1,500 crore in the next few years.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the Denso JV infotainment (IVI) order and how does it reflect in consolidated numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: The IVI order has annual peak value of about INR 600 crore, with SOP in Q3 FY29 and about 70% of current JV revenue of INR 846 crore. It sits in the Denso JV and is excluded from consolidated revenue, appearing only as share of JV profit. No further new business timing was committed.

risks_watch: Commodity (aluminium) and labour cost spikes (Haryana up about 35%; labour impact about INR 200 crore for Haryana and Gujarat) hit coming quarters, and pass-through cycles of 3-6 months (1-2 customers annual) lag the cost increase.

Start-up costs and execution load as about 7 of 11 projects commence or ramp in FY27, including Khed EV powertrain (H2 FY27), sunroof (end FY27) and CSN/Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar plants; the 11% plus/minus 50 bps EBITDA guidance must absorb these.
Alloy wheel penetration softening (4W mix shift to entry models, 2W programmes switching to steel wheels) could weigh on casting growth.
Capex of about INR 1,750 crore in FY27 and possible additional land at CSN, Hosur and Gujarat; net debt rose to INR 2,179 crore, partly from the INR 200-odd crore FRIWO-linked acquisition.
Q4 debit/credit note adjustments were not quantified, so the underlying Q4 margin base is harder to assess; monitor Q1 FY27 margin and the pass-through reset to monthly or quarterly.
Revenue visibility on the new 4W EV plant is not disclosed; booked share of the 1.85 lakh capacity and revenue timing remain open.

532539|2026-06.headline: Uno Minda Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% YoY to INR 5,557 crores; EBITDA margin 10.3%, with FY27 guidance of 11% ±50 bps held.

qa_highlights.question: Is green mobility near group profitability, and what is the capex plan for FY27 and FY28?

FY27 capex remains about INR 1,750 crores; FY28 guidance will be given with the annual outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How fast will margins recover toward 11%, and can wage and commodity costs be passed through?

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation fall QoQ in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Casting uses the WDV method, so new capacity starts from a lower base and Q1 depreciation tends to be lower than Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential of the 4W seating capex and the timing of export and sunroof ramps?

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the China Inovance JV and is e-axle import at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Press Note 3 approval is in hand, but China approval is pending after recent regulatory tightening; Inovance is seeking clarification. There is no current restriction on e-axle imports, and more clarity is expected in about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export growth outlook and the gross margin trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports rose to INR 228 crores from INR 141 crores, and new business of about INR 400 crores is in the pipeline. Gross margin is diluted by commodity pass-through (~0.4%) and lower-margin electronics, but EBITDA margin is expected to hold given better asset turns.

532540|2026-06.headline: TCS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% YoY to ₹72,275 crore, but operating margin fell 130 bps QoQ to 24% on wage hikes.

Operating margin fell to 24% (down 130 bps QoQ), with a 170 bps hit from annual salary increments partly offset by 40 bps of currency benefit and efficiencies. qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 16% YoY dollar increase in SG&A?

qa_highlights.question: Is AI-driven productivity deflating revenue, and how much has been passed through?

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall sharply across segments, and when will they recover?

Print drove the result, with advertising revenue up 10% in Q4 on higher ad yields, while volumes were broadly flat. Radio revenue fell on a high events base, and management surrendered six loss-making radio frequencies and exited the OTTplay subscription business effective 1 April 2026. Net cash remains above INR 1,000 crore, though other income fell about INR 50 crore on mark-to-market losses on treasury holdings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HMVL's Print segment revenue for the prior year change by about INR 6 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Pervez Bajan said it is an intersegment revenue elimination for OTTplay advertising in print, reclassified because OTTplay moved to discontinued operations; the amount was written off with a matching PBIT impact.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further exceptional losses from radio or OTTplay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further closure losses are expected. A possible statutory charge from the new labour codes could hit exceptional items.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall about INR 50 crore, and why invest INR 22 crore in Assetvault?
qa_highlights.answer: Mark-to-market losses on treasury holdings as yields rose to record highs; the 10-year is near 7%. Management plans to hold to maturity. Assetvault is an AFE investment with no cash outflow.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ad yield sustainable, and what is the cash plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly sustainable, but competitor reactions are a risk. Management aims to keep deals at or above current levels. The Board is investing the cash pile in core and digital and has no current capital return plan.

Radio sector pressure despite portfolio cleanup; management will review on a close basis.
Residual OTTplay servicing costs through September 2026 and cash outflows from contract exits.
Possible statutory exceptional charge from the new labour codes.
Other income volatility from treasury mark-to-market as bond yields move.
532662|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on Print pricing and margin delivery, and candid about the exit from radio and OTTplay. Evasive on specific yields, copy share and cash deployment, citing competitive sensitivity and no forward guidance.
key_quotes: The lever for the growth in revenue is primarily yields, volumes have been by and large flat, which have tracked the industry.
The simple answer is no. But even if you break down the exceptional items in this year, one of the big items which is sitting is consequent to the new labour codes.

532662|2026-06.headline: HT Media Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15% to INR 497 crore and EBITDA nearly tripled to INR 90 crore, while a preferential issue drew shareholder pushback.
532662|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY to INR 497 crore, with EBITDA up nearly 3x to INR 90 crore (margin up about 12 points) and PAT of INR 47 crore (9% margin). Print drove growth, with advertising up 15% to INR 295 crore and operating revenue up 16% to INR 376 crore, and management credited yield improvement. Digital operating revenue fell about 28% with EBITDA of negative INR 3 crore, as the portfolio was deliberately reset, and Radio was flat with negative INR 3 crore EBITDA after surrendering licences for non-viable stations. The board approved a preferential issue of equity to HT Media and Digicontent Ltd (not HMVL), priced at the SEBI formula (around INR 24-25 per share), which drew sharp objections from minority shareholders on dilution and pricing.

financial_highlights.change: from INR 111 crore a year earlier

segments.name: English Print
segments.commentary: Advertising revenue grew 12% YoY to INR 156 crore; circulation revenue grew 14% to INR 13 crore (about INR 1.5 crore absolute change, mostly pricing and mix).

segments.name: Hindi Print
segments.commentary: Advertising revenue rose YoY to INR 139 crore; circulation revenue flat.

segments.name: Radio
segments.commentary: Topline flat YoY; operating EBITDA negative INR 3 crore. Licences surrendered for certain non-viable stations.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Operating revenue down about 28% YoY; operating EBITDA negative INR 3 crore (margin -12%) after deliberate portfolio reset; OTTplay decision taken around 31 March 2026 per management.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal revenue or earnings guidance; said it is 'very hopeful' of sustaining good numbers.

Newsprint (25-40% of print bill of materials) at about USD 650-700 per tonne is the highest since COVID; management believes prices have peaked and will plateau before easing, but acknowledged no forward market exists.
Q2 newsprint expected slightly higher than Q1; Q1 Print margin of about 13% offered as a modelling baseline, with downside if dollar and newsprint rise further.
Preferential issue proceeds to retire 30-50% of the debt at HT Media and Digicontent; management says it is EPS-accretive and will improve interest coverage and credit rating.
Government ad and circulation rates were raised in November 2025 after seven years, so the price benefit continues for the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Preferential issue at HT Media and Digicontent Ltd (DCL), priced on the SEBI formula (higher of 10-day or 90-day VWAP); promoters subscribing on the same terms, up to their regulatory maximum; ongoing vote, with a shareholder voting against.
Radio footprint reduced by surrendering licences for non-viable stations.
Cost right-sizing: consolidated employee cost fell to INR 99 crore from INR 111 crore YoY.
HMVL cash (where most of the INR 922 crore net cash sits) to be deployed at HMVL board's discretion; no preferential issue at HMVL.
demand_pricing: Commercial print revenue held on volume with yield improvement as the main driver; government revenue grew on both volume and the November 2025 rate increase.
Management stated that a substantial part of the 15% revenue growth came from pricing, not volume.
Cover price hikes seen as difficult: Hindi papers are already well priced and prior commodity-driven hikes were taken.
Circulation held steady market by market to protect copy share in English markets.
Other operating income at HMVL roughly doubled to about INR 20 crore (from about INR 10 crore), mainly job work and scrap sales.
Competitive environment described as likely to remain as is for circulation.

qa_highlights.question: Why use a preferential issue at about INR 24 per share, below book value of about INR 70, rather than a rights issue, given INR 922 crore net cash and a 15% dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all the net cash sits in HMVL, while HT Media and DCL are net debt companies. Preferential issue is faster (2-3 months), gives more certainty of raising the amount and avoids underwriter risk; pricing follows the SEBI formula with no premium. Proceeds will retire 30-50% of debt.

qa_highlights.question: Given the 15% dilution, the valuation and the moral/reputational issue, will the company withdraw the preferential issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not agree to withdraw. It said price-to-book is below 0.5x, the promoters are subscribing on the same terms, and it is raising capital to retire debt and improve EPS. A shareholder said he voted against the resolution.

qa_highlights.question: Is the debt position consistent with earlier statements that the company was debt-free?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt has built up at HT Media over the last 3-4 years post-COVID (Print English and Radio); the combined net cash figure hides this, and the number is not new.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of HMVL's other income jump, and is it MTM?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury gains from mutual funds (NAV-based) plus realised profit on sale of assets; no MTM on investments. Treasury gains depend on yield curve movements and are not predictable.

qa_highlights.question: How will newsprint costs affect Print margins, and can prices be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Newsprint is 25-40% of the bill of materials. Management expects a plateau at current levels, so Q1 Print margin of about 13% can be used as a baseline if prices don't rise further; cover price increases are difficult.

qa_highlights.question: What drove ad revenue growth at Print, and what share is government revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly commercial yield improvement with volumes holding; government revenue grew on volume and pricing. Management did not disclose the government share and called it 'substantial' but smaller than commercial.

risks_watch: Newsprint at about USD 650-700 per tonne, the highest since COVID, with no forward market; Q2 newsprint guided slightly higher than Q1, and a weaker dollar adds to cost pressure on the 13% Print margin.

Preferential issue at HT Media and Digicontent: ~15% dilution at roughly INR 24-25 per share versus book value of about INR 70; shareholder voting is ongoing and at least one minority holder has voted against, so approval and final pricing remain open.
Debt at HT Media and DCL: management said 30-50% of debt will be retired from the issue proceeds; the net cash of INR 922 crore sits in HMVL, and the consolidated figure masks standalone net debt.
Other income at HMVL (treasury gains and profit on asset sales) is not predictable and depends on yield curve movements, so the Q1 profit level may not repeat.

Digital operating revenue down about 28% with EBITDA of negative INR 3 crore after the portfolio reset; Radio EBITDA negative INR 3 crore. Track whether these turn profitable next quarter and whether the Q1 earnings step-up holds once government rate benefits cycle out after two quarters.
key_quotes: So, a substantial part of that revenue growth of 15% is driven by our pricing .
We believe that the prices have peaked and should plateau at this level before they start coming down.
Debt has been building in HT Media for the last 4-5 years post-COVID because of the Print English operations and Radio operations, etc.
Treasury gains is basically mutual funds and the NA V based process and not a MTM valuation-based process.
532662|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operating performance, pricing and cost discipline, and on the preferential issue as a faster, certain route to cutting debt. Cautious and defensive on newsprint and dollar costs, and evasive on the debt history and share pricing, where answers repeatedly deflected to HMVL or the SEBI formula. No formal guidance was given.

532663|2026-06.headline: Sasken Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to ₹339 Cr, with software services margin up 240 bps to 30.6% while Product Solutions margin fell to 5.9%.
532663|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 24% YoY and 1.6% QoQ to ₹339 Cr, led by Software Services at ₹219 Cr (+24.3% YoY). Product Solutions revenue was ₹120 Cr (+23.6% YoY, -3.9% QoQ) after a strong Q4, with memory availability and component pricing pressure. Gross margin was 21.9% (₹74 Cr), and EBIT margin was 6.3%, while PAT was ₹23 Cr (6.9% margin) and was hit by normalisation of Q4 other-income one-offs. Order booking was US$47 million TCV, including US$34 million of new deal wins, with five new logos added.

financial_highlights.change: -310 bps QoQ (Keshav Sureka cited 12.8% prior period)
Sequential decline from Q4 one-off other income and lower FX gains

segments.name: Software Services
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹219 Cr, up 24.3% YoY and 4.8% QoQ; gross margin expanded 240 bps to 30.6% on utilisation, cost discipline and scale. Management says the segment grew more than 20% YoY.

segments.name: Product Solutions (incl. Borqs)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹120 Cr, up 23.6% YoY but down 3.9% QoQ; gross margin fell to 5.9% from 9.0% in Q4 (per the 310 bps decline) due to memory cost pass-through, lower incremental margin and silicon productization mix. Management expects margins to stabilise over the full year.

Breakeven for Borqs at about US$12 million quarterly revenue, per CFO.

capex_capacity: Inaugurated Sasken Silicon Incubation Center in Hubballi to build semiconductor talent.
Opened a new centre of excellence in Hyderabad.
Global headcount 2,658 (about 2,400 engineers), attrition 9.8%, utilisation 85%.
Inventory build in Q1 to manage memory shortage contributed to negative cash flow; some silicon products ship through the year.
Silicon business is shifting toward productization; capacity expansion requires working capital.
demand_pricing: Order booking US$47 million TCV (US$34 million new), ACV about US$40 million (US$24 million new); the TCV is not total backlog, and management targets a 9–10 month revenue carry.
Five new logos; 93 active customers vs 79 a year ago; top-five customer share ~56% (vs ~52% previously).
Two hyperscaler engagements (different hyperscalers): a multi-year capability engagement and an OS sustenance engagement, plus an AI and automation deal covering agentic AI and LLM validation.
CSAT 4.5 out of 5 vs industry benchmark 3.75.
Revenue mix: North America 30%, EMEA ~25%, India 26%, APAC ~20%.
Automotive: Borqs instrument cluster module ready but Chinese-sourced modules remain price-competitive; no commercial order yet.
Memory pricing and component costs are being passed through to customers, but incremental margin is not recovered.
532663|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, customer wins and Software Services margins, but cautious and non-committal on Product Solutions margins and cash flow. Management declined to give margin guidance, disclosed no project-level detail, and deferred on specific partnership and order-level questions.
key_quotes: We will make sure that we will maintain our margins while we maintain our growth momentum.
So, we do not want to give any guidance on the margins at this point in time, but as Rajiv mentioned, right, so we are constantly making sure that we are driving efficiencies in how we are doing.
So, it is a function of how the customer does the offtake of some of these products.

qa_highlights.question: What pipeline of accounts could cross the US$4 million run-rate threshold in FY27, given customer count rose from 79 to 93 and top-five concentration rose to about 56%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody said the 60x4x3 target (US$4 million run-rate for 93 active customers within three years) is still the goal; the three-year timeline is metaphoric and may stretch one or two more years. Specific FY27 target accounts were not named, and sales bandwidth is being added.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Product Solutions gross margin drop from 12.8% to 5.9%: memory pricing or something else?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said memory cost pass-through removes incremental margin even though costs are passed on, and the silicon business shifting toward productization changed mix. Some products ship through the year, so margins should be read on a full-year basis and are expected to stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Are the two hyperscaler engagements with the same hyperscaler or different ones?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody confirmed they are different hyperscalers.

qa_highlights.question: Headcount rose about 9% QoQ while cost rose only about 3%; how will sales and senior analog/RF leadership headcount evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody said at least five to six more sales heads will be added in the rest of the year, with some growth delivery-led. Priyaranjan said cost mix includes lateral and fresher hires and Q4 had non-recurring bonus catch-up; utilisation improved. Anup Savla said the teams are independent and senior niche analog/RF/mmWave skills are grown in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 60x4x3 target of US$4 million run-rate be reached if extended by a couple of years, and at what growth drivers, with growth at the expense of margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody said the company may take one more year, not a commitment to a number, and cited silicon, specialised silicon, devices (China-plus-one and Make in India) and full-stack software services as the three vectors. On margins, he said Software Services margins went from about 2-3% to 11.5-12% EBIT over six quarters and the company will maintain margins while growing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue stay flat for years and then grow suddenly in software services?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan cited four changes: working closer to customers, empowering teams to own growth, investing in capability, and filling white spaces such as the Borqs and silicon acquisitions for end-to-end engagement.

qa_highlights.question: Why has operating cash flow been negative for two years despite profit growth, and will FY27 be cash-flow positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said cash outflow reflects investment in working capital and fixed assets, not collection problems; a large cash consumption is expected this year, Q1 included inventory build for memory shortage. Funding will come from internal accruals and external funds, and the cash-flow positive timeline is work in progress.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Borqs break-even point still hold at the earlier US$60-70 million top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said break-even is now about US$12 million of quarterly revenue, after which the business adds to the bottom line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of GlobalFoundries and Intel IP certifications and the formal TSMC relationship?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Savla said all three are in progress with substantial progress, leading to more design activity, but no announcements can be made yet due to the non-public nature of the work.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RF and mmWave projects and when will revenue from these niche technologies show up?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Savla said projects span connectivity, automotive interfaces and power, and revenue mix already reflects such implementation, though project details were not disclosed. Hareesh Ramanna said the Borqs instrument-cluster module is ready but Chinese-sourced modules remain price-competitive, so no commercial order is yet in hand.

risks_watch: Product Solutions gross margin at 5.9% (down 310 bps QoQ) with memory cost pass-through leaving no incremental margin; watch whether margins stabilise over FY27 as management expects.
Negative operating cash flow for two years; management expects large cash consumption in FY27 and has not given a timeline to cash-flow positive. Watch working capital and any external funding.
The US$4 million run-rate per-customer target has slipped in timing by one to two years beyond the three-year goal; the 60x4x3 timeline and the 93-customer base remain unproven.
Top-five customer concentration rose to about 56% from about 52%, and the sales team is being expanded by only five to six heads.
Borqs automotive instrument-cluster module has no commercial order yet, facing price competition from Chinese-sourced modules; the TCV-to-revenue conversion (9-10 month carry) also needs tracking.

532667|2026-03.headline: Suzlon delivered a record 830 MW in Q4 FY26 and 2,456 MW for the year, with FY26 revenue up 54% to INR16,679 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will order inflow decline for a few quarters in FY27, given muted Q4 orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book closed at 5.9 GW versus 5.0 GW opening. The shift to EPC contracts takes longer to close, but EPC closures are expected to be announced from June.

qa_highlights.question: Can Suzlon help clients manage risk if the wind DSM (deviation settlement) rules tighten?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CERC moved wind DSM bands from plus or minus 15% to plus or minus 10%. Suzlon is testing a scheduling and forecasting model at plus or minus 10% and plans to offer it as a paid service, including to existing clients.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any non-moving orders in the 5,892 MW backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are currently no non-moving or slow-moving orders in the backlog.

qa_highlights.question: What drives FY27 deliveries, and is about 2,500 MW the most likely outcome?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, pointing to leading indicators and the FY24-26 trend (700 MW, 1,550 MW, 2,456 MW) instead.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for price hikes to protect margins given rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said WTG margins should not materially decline, citing pass-through clauses and cost management. Management said pricing on new contracts would reflect current exchange rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope of the Andhra Pradesh FDRE project and the DevCo model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 775 MW will be converted to FDRE under a PPA, with clients possibly taking over the PPA and Suzlon supplying full FDRE. The remaining 1,325 MW will be converted into turnkey EPC contracts from June.

risks_watch: Free cash flow was US$135M, held back by rebadged-deal ramp-up; management expects normalisation next quarter, and DSO rose four days QoQ to 88 days.
Effective tax rate of 29.9% included a one-time prior-period adjustment; underlying rate was 26.6%.
AI-driven deflation in effort-based fixed-price and managed services contracts could pressure revenue, and management acknowledged ADMS renewals carry productivity expectations that may mute growth.
Comms revenue is highly concentrated among a few clients, adding volatility.
European automotive weakness in Manufacturing, with a further sequential headwind in Q3.
AI revenue disclosure methodology is still being defined and will start in H2 FY27.
Growth in BFSI remains below the company's aspiration; leadership changes made.
532755|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and AI, with management repeatedly stating the quarter was strong and the margin target near. key_quotes: We delivered a very strong quarter with broad -based growth across the business.
We do expect, as a result of the specific AI toolchain, we're building for each and every single service line, to be able to release head count across our fixed-price projects
We don't believe for a moment that the gross margin opportunities in the business have been fully tapped out

532762|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 total income rose 15% QoQ to INR1,021 crore, but FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 18.33%; management plans 9-10% price hikes to offset 11-14% cost inflation.
532762|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as the company's best ever revenue quarter, with total income of INR1,021 crore (up 15% QoQ, 5.58% YoY) and EBITDA of INR163.7 crore (16% margin). FY26 total income was flat at about INR3,395 crore, with EBITDA up about 4% to INR622 crore and PAT up 5.4% to INR425 crore. Other income was negative in Q4 on mark-to-market losses on surplus-cash investments, and March brought West Asia-driven steel and crude cost inflation. Management is taking staged price increases and has withheld annual guidance until the middle of Q2.

segments.name: Cranes, metal handling and construction equipment
segments.commentary: FY26 income over INR2,946 crore with an 18.6% margin and INR548 crore profit; management called FY26 a normalisation year after the pre-buying ahead of the emission transition in FY25.

segments.name: Agri division
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 9% to around INR251 crore in FY26, with margins at about 1%.

segments.name: Others (miscellaneous exports)
segments.commentary: Separately reported line of about INR76.55 crore; management said it is mainly miscellaneous exports, including some construction equipment, and no volume figure is available.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27: management expects growth of 15-20% or slightly more, helped by a low base in Q1 FY26; no full-year guidance given until the middle of Q2.
Pricing: 1-1.5% hike in January, about 4% from 1 May, and a further 5% from 1 June (total 9-10%); management sees total cost inflation of 11-14% and may take another 3-4% later in Q2.
Margins: target EBITDA ex-other income of 15-16%; management said expanding margins beyond about 17-18% including other income would hurt market share.
Other income expected to recover to INR20-35 crore in Q1 FY27 if markets hold or improve, after partial April recovery of March mark-to-market losses.
Defense: execution of about INR200-220 crore in FY27 (5-6% of revenue vs about 3% last year); about INR575 crore order book; rough terrain forklift/telehandler execution to start next quarter.

Long-term: INR6,000-6,200 crore revenue target by FY29 (worst case FY30) implies adding about INR700-800 crore a year; exports plus defense targeted at 10-15% of the segment, with about 11-13% expected in FY27.
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation for cranes, metal handling and construction equipment is about 60%.

FY27 capex about INR200 crore: about INR130-135 crore for a land parcel contracted about 1-1.5 years ago, INR40-50 crore for a new defense and new-product plant within the existing complex, and INR20-25 crore maintenance.

Proposed new tower crane factory with capex upwards of INR400 crore; 12-18 months to build; decision to start this year is need-based, and management expects only about INR150 crore to be spent in FY27 if it starts.
Tower crane capacity is about 950-1,000 units a year versus about 680-690 units produced in FY26 (FY25 comparison not given).
demand_pricing: Tower crane order books are full; demand is strong into the start of Q1, with slowdown usually beginning mid-to-late June during monsoon.

Hydra-type cranes (about 60% of the market) shrank in FY26 on emission-norm skepticism and are recovering since January-February; management expects higher volumes in backhoe loaders and construction equipment.
Price realisation per unit rose on a mix shift to higher tonnage cranes; emission-transition costs added an estimated 5-7% to blended cost per unit.
About INR40-50 crore of Q4 revenue was lost to Middle East-bound export shipments stuck in India and March delivery deferrals.

Competition: Chinese players are absent from pick-and-carry cranes (below 30-35 tonnes) and compete in slew/heavy cranes (40-50+ tonnes), offering 1-2 year credit terms; competitor segment margins are about 8-9% versus about 18-19% for ACE.
Anti-dumping duties of 25-52% on Chinese cranes were recommended by DGTR in September 2025 but not notified by the Finance Ministry; the 90-day window has lapsed.

qa_highlights.question: Status of LD implementation and Chinese competition in pick-and-carry cranes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Chinese players do not make pick-and-carry cranes; they compete in heavy slew cranes (40-50+ tonnes). The anti-dumping order was not notified, and the 90-day window has lapsed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are non-current investments large and what is their size?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus cash is invested in secured, listed bonds with 1-3 year tenures, classified as non-current under accounting rules but saleable; the amount is about INR700-750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR76.55 crore 'others' revenue and the impairment line?
qa_highlights.answer: 'Others' is miscellaneous exports, reported separately by the auditors. Impairment is a prudent expected-credit-loss provision on slightly delayed receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Mark-to-market losses on investments at March month-end; partly recovered in April. Management expects INR20-35 crore of other income in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will volumes grow 10%+ in FY27 and what are price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 growth of 15-20% or more is possible on a low base; annual guidance is deferred to mid-Q2. Price hikes total 9-10% with another 3-4% possible, against 11-14% cost inflation (steel about 65% of cost, up 20-22% since January).

qa_highlights.question: What is the KATO JV revenue potential and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue of about INR300 crore in 3-4 years under current conditions, potentially INR700-800 crore if anti-dumping duties are imposed. Chinese imports are priced 25-30% below Indian-made costs, aided by credit terms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and tower crane factory timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR200 crore; a INR400 crore tower crane factory is need-based, with a 12-18 month build.

risks_watch: Steel (about 65% of cost) up 20-22% since January; the price pass-through lags 2-3 months and may not fully recover 11-14% inflation.
Anti-dumping duty notification remains pending; the outcome determines JV scale and Chinese pricing pressure.
Other income is volatile due to mark-to-market exposure on treasury investments (INR700-750 crore).
Demand is capital-goods-linked; management flagged geopolitical risk, rupee depreciation, and a possible monsoon slowdown from mid-June.
Other expenses are largely fixed, so margins are sensitive to volume shortfalls; volumes fell about 18-20% in FY26 (about 13,300 to 10,800 units by the analyst's count).
ROCE fell from about 40% to 32% over two years; capex timing is tied to demand before the tower crane factory is approved.
532762|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on near-term demand and pricing power, but evasive on full-year numbers, which were deferred to mid-Q2 FY27 citing turbulence from the West Asia conflict. Management was candid about cost pressures and the lapsed anti-dumping order, and it framed margin protection as the first priority over market share.
key_quotes: Despite these geopolitical headwinds, we responded with agility and operational discipline to deliver our best ever revenue performance in quarter 4 last year with sustained operating margins to fortify our balance sheet.
Our focus remains on driving volume-led competitive growth with right balance on pricing.
So our competition at segment level, I think they are at 8%, 9% margin, whereas we are close to 18%, 19% margin.

532762|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 total income rose about 19% to INR836 crore and EBITDA rose 19.66% to INR170.58 crore at a 20.40% margin, with management guiding no margin expansion.
532762|2026-06.overview: Management called Q1 FY27 its best-ever first quarter on revenue and profit, with total income up about 19% YoY to INR836 crore and PAT up 22.47% to INR118.59 crore. Segment revenue for Cranes, Construction Equipment and Metal Handling rose about 22% to INR738.37 crore, while Agri Equipment booked INR42.67 crore. Commodity inflation (steel up nearly 20%, plus rubber, tyres, plastics and freight) compressed gross margin by about 140 bps YoY, which management is offsetting with price hikes totalling about 10% so far. Management declined to give a full-year revenue growth number until end-September, citing demand unpredictability and price resistance.

financial_highlights.change: up 19.66% YoY; margin up 12 bps YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Cranes, Construction Equipment & Metal Handling revenue
financial_highlights.change: up about 22% YoY from INR605.43 crore; volumes up 17.25% YoY

financial_highlights.value: INR42.67 crore revenue; INR4.34 crore margin

financial_highlights.change: contracted about 140 bps YoY per analyst; management attributed to commodity costs

segments.name: Cranes, Construction Equipment & Metal Handling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR738.37 crore (up about 22% YoY), volumes up 17.25%, margin INR134.09 crore (up 24.35%). Backhoe loaders run at about 150-160 units per quarter.

segments.name: Agri Equipment
segments.commentary: Revenue INR42.67 crore with margin INR4.34 crore (about 10% margin). Management expects agri at about 6-7% of FY27 revenue.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: About 5% of Q1 revenue. Management expects 5-6% of FY27 revenue; the big defence order execution starts in August, and a repeat order above INR100 crore is expected in 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 3% of Q1 revenue, held back by shipping issues and Middle East (Saudi Arabia) shipments pending since March. Management expects 6-7% or more of FY27 revenue.

guidance_outlook: No full-year revenue growth number yet; management will give guidance by end-September 2026, after the price actions play out.
Management expects Q2 FY27 to be better than Q2 FY26 and similar to Q1 FY27. Historically 40-45% of revenue comes in H1 and 55-60% in H2.
Management aims to maintain operating EBITDA margin of about 15% (FY26 was a little over 15% on an operating basis) in Q2 and possibly Q3, with no planned margin expansion.
Cost inflation expected at 11-12% in total; about 10% price increases already booked; about 2% more may be needed depending on August-September commodity moves.
Capex for FY27 guided at INR200-250 crore, including about INR130-140 crore for land takeover, INR40-50 crore for Plant 9, and INR50-60 crore for upgradation, robotics and maintenance.
KATO JV to be functional by end-July 2026. Revenue contribution from Q3 FY27, with meaningful revenue from FY28.
capex_capacity: KATO JV with Japan's KATO Works: total investment about INR200 crore, of which INR100 crore cash from KATO and INR100 crore in kind from ACE (machine models, technology, infrastructure). Upgraded Indian models with KATO technology from about Q4 FY27; dedicated KATO export models in 1-2 years, with localisation targeted at 50-60%.

Plant 9 (defence-dedicated, special machines plus new products): INR40-50 crore investment, functional by end-December 2026 (Q3 FY27 to early Q4). Management expects turnover capacity of about INR500 crore. Uses the last meaningful land parcel (about 100 acres) in the existing complex.

Tower crane capacity expansion: plans ready, but start deferred. Decision in September 2026 on starting in October or deferring by 6 months. Current capacity was raised to about 1,000 cranes a year via minor rearrangements and a rented small factory about 4-5 km away.
Rough terrain forklift manufacturing started in Q1 FY27 for defence.
demand_pricing: Demand was strong till May-June 2026, and softened in the monsoon. Management says it expects growth in Hydra crane volumes (price increases and technology change had suppressed them in FY26).

Pick-and-carry mix: Hydra about 60% and new generation (NG) about 40% in FY26; management expects a return to about 60:40 in FY27, eventually settling near 50:50. Realisation expected to rise on higher tonnage models (18, 20 and 25 tonne).
Price actions: about 1-1.5% in January, 3-4% in March, and 5-6% in June (still being implemented, due to complete in July). Cumulative about 9-10%, with another 2% possible.

Commodity inflation: steel up nearly 20%, plus tyres, belts, rubber and plastics. Management estimates Q1 raw-material inflation at about 5-6% (7-8% flowed through per Sorab Agarwal), with more to hit Q2.
Competition: intensity unchanged according to management. Biggest challenge is inflation and customers' resistance to price hikes.

Predictability is the main issue; management cites the Iran/West Asia war, US tariffs and erratic monsoon. A deficient monsoon could cut Tier 2 and rural demand by 5-10%, with the effect showing in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much did defence and export orders contribute to Q1 revenue, and what is the visibility for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Export was about 3% and defence about 5% of Q1 revenue. For FY27, management expects exports 6-7% or more and defence 5-6%, so the combined share will be about 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Can you update on the KATO JV?
qa_highlights.answer: Formalities are complete and the JV should be functional by end-July. Revenue from Q3 FY27, with meaningful revenue from FY28. Upgraded models are expected from about Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the defence order target of about INR200 crore still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to exceed it by 10-15%. A repeat order of more than INR100 crore is expected in 1-2 quarters. Small orders of INR1-5 crore come in monthly.

qa_highlights.question: What commodity inflation did you see in Q1, and what is expected in Q2? Will margins expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Inflation is expected at 11-12% in total, with about 10% booked. Management says there is no plan for margin expansion, only cost recovery. Price increases and inflation are expected to align by July-August.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gross margin down about 140 bps YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to commodity cost increases. Steel is up nearly 20%, and all other inputs have risen, with pricing actions taken to protect full-year margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the new tower crane facility and the Plant 9 facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Tower crane expansion will be decided in September (start October or defer 6 months). Plant 9 is due by end-December, with turnover of about INR500 crore, and capex for the year is INR200-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What was the anti-dumping duty status on Chinese cranes?
qa_highlights.answer: No leads so far. Management believes the DGTR recommended the duty, but the Finance Ministry did not implement it, and says it is still hopeful.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation: management expects 11-12% in total with about 2% more to come, and any further escalation in West Asia would add to costs.
Price resistance: about 10% price increases in 6 months may slow Q2 volumes, particularly in the seasonally weak monsoon period.
Export shipments to Saudi Arabia and the Middle East were delayed by shipping issues, with about 3% of Q1 revenue at risk of further slippage.
Anti-dumping duty on Chinese cranes was not notified, leaving import competition unaddressed.
Monsoon risk: a deficient monsoon could cut rural and Tier 2 demand by 5-10% in H2 FY27.

key_quotes: Against this backdrop, our company registered its best -ever Q1 performance with continued focus on disciplined execution, operational excellence and maintaining a healthy balance between growth and profitability.

532768|2026-03.headline: Fiem FY26 revenue rose 16.04% to INR2,790.65 crore and PAT 24.36% to INR253.87 crore, with EBITDA margin at a record 14.09%.
532768|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 net sales were INR744.35 crore, up 17.44% YoY, with EBITDA of INR109.18 crore (14.67% margin, up from 13.22%) and PAT of INR70.59 crore, up 22.36%. For FY26 the company reported record revenue, PAT and EBITDA margin, and the Board recommended a final dividend of INR40 per share. Management reiterated 15-20% revenue growth for FY27 and a roughly 14% EBITDA margin, and gave the first explicit 4-wheeler revenue range after the CEO's exit. Receivables rose because the company stopped discounting bills with its two major customers, not because of any change in payment terms.

segments.name: Automotive lighting (LED)
segments.commentary: LED share of automotive lighting was 63% in FY26 versus 60% in prior years; management says its pipeline is almost 100% LED and the share will keep rising, with 1-2% gains each quarter.

segments.name: 4-wheeler
segments.commentary: Current 4-wheeler business guided at INR100-150 crore for FY27, rising to INR200-250 crore in FY27-28; Mahindra & Mahindra orders start this year, and Mercedes is at testing and validation stage.

segments.name: Rear-view mirrors and plastic moulded parts
segments.commentary: Share of revenue is slipping slightly, but management says absolute amounts are growing, though more slowly than lighting; these are ancillary products sold to the same lighting customers.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 15-20% a year for FY27 and beyond, ahead of industry growth, despite possible El Nino or weak-monsoon moderation.
EBITDA margin guidance of around 14% or more, including the 4-wheeler business; 4-wheeler expected to be margin-neutral over the next 2-3 years.
4-wheeler revenue: INR100-150 crore in FY27, INR200-250 crore in FY27-28; management says impact is limited this year and more meaningful from next year.
Capex of about INR200 crore over the next two years at company level; no greenfield project envisaged.
Commodity and INR-depreciation cost pressures are treated as pass-through to customers, with a lag of a quarter at times.
Borrowing not needed given healthy cash; insurance premiums to be renegotiated at next renewal.
capex_capacity: Current capacity utilisation about 75%; FY26 capex of about INR108 crore went mainly to debottleneck lines.
Projected capex of about INR200 crore over the next 2 years, which includes the 4-wheeler initiatives.
Solar and open-access renewable energy rollout across plants; Hosur plant gets about 65% of energy from solar and a further 20% from wind, with the model to extend to other plants.
An in-house EMI/EMC validation lab is being installed to cut product development time and reduce reliance on outside test agencies.
R&D spend is more than 2% of revenue (around 2%) in FY26.
demand_pricing: Industry: 2-wheeler production grew about 12% to a record roughly 26.7 million units in FY26, above the FY19 pre-pandemic peak.

Customers: TVS (iQube, Jupiter, Moped, motorcycles), Honda (Activa EV and new models), Royal Enfield (Classic, EV initiatives), Suzuki and Yamaha (healthy growth; 8-9 models in development), Hero (two recent launches running well, and a new EV platform approved).
4-wheeler RFQs of about INR700 crore; about 70% converted into business now under development (management said this does not equal fixed orders).
Pricing: commodity and currency-driven price changes are passed through to customers in both directions.
LED products cost about 3-4x conventional halogen lighting setups, depending on the product.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables jump this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company stopped discounting bills with two major customers, TVS and one other, because cash flow is now strong; payment terms are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other expenses rise faster than revenue, and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost was 13.80% of sales in FY26 versus 13.62% earlier, with part of the rise from recently notified labour-cost increases. Capex is about INR200 crore over two years at company level, and no greenfield project is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CEO exit a sign of a delay in the 4-wheeler strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet Sahni left after a three-year term to pursue other interests. Rahul Jain and Rajesh Sharma now lead 4-wheeler, and management says there is no derailment and a detailed strategy will follow.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still looking for a new 4-wheeler CEO?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management says there is enough bandwidth in-house and Rahul Jain, with Rajesh Sharma, will personally oversee 4-wheeler growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will 4-wheeler be margin-accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business is too small to judge separately and will be margin-neutral, with overall EBITDA guidance kept at around 14%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the other automotive lighting (non-LED) growth a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the non-LED share is declining and the chart cited covers the whole company, including rear-view mirrors, not just automotive lighting; it offered to clarify offline.

risks_watch: 4-wheeler execution: order book is still small, Mahindra and Mercedes timelines are not fixed, and the CEO has left.
Demand moderation risk from weak monsoon or El Nino on 2-wheelers.
Cost pass-through lag on commodity and INR-depreciation pressure, including imported LED chips.
Receivables trend after bill discounting was stopped.
Insurance premium increase after the Tapukara fire, to be negotiated at renewal.
Timing of new-product launches (POC stage; regulatory norms for touch and laser technology still awaited).

segments.name: EV lighting
