EBITDA rose 29.1% to Rs 15.7 crore at a 7.8% margin, and PAT rose 50.2% to Rs 8.3 crore. Management said a price hike taken in April was largely passed on to trade through extra schemes, so realisations did not capture it. Management guided to 10-12% revenue growth and a 9-10% EBITDA margin for the coming quarter, with a further price hike planned for August.

financial_highlights.metric: Modern trade including e-commerce share of revenue

financial_highlights.value: About Rs 21 crore, about 10.5% of revenue

segments.name: Athleisure
segments.commentary: Q1 declined 5-7% YoY after a strong Q4; management targets at least double-digit growth from Q2 and more than double-digit for the full year.

segments.name: Women's wear (Softline, Macroman)
segments.commentary: Women's share was about 8% in Q1 and has run at 8-10% on an annual basis. Softline is undergoing a brand and font change, with new fabrics and a new team being built.

segments.name: Thermal (winterwear)
segments.commentary: Management described the order book as sound and expects FY27 thermal sales to be better than last year, but this depends on how the winter unfolds.

segments.name: E-commerce and modern trade
segments.commentary: Management targets 20-25% e-commerce growth, with senior heads appointed and warehousing, inventory and IT infrastructure being built.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 10-12% expected in the coming quarter (Q2 FY27).
EBITDA margin expected to stay in the 9-10% range in the coming quarter.
A further price hike of 4-5% is planned to be implemented from August, dependent on competitor behaviour.
Advertising and marketing spend to be rationalised from about 10.5% of revenue to 6-7%, which management says will support the EBITDA margin target.
Athleisure expected to grow at least double digits from Q2 and more than double digits for the full year; e-commerce targeted at 20-25% growth.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed on the call.
Management said a DMS (distributor management system) is being rolled out state by state, with a hands-on presence expected in a year or two; ARS is described as in place but dependent on DMS.
demand_pricing: Q1 price hike of 4-5% was largely passed to trade through extra schemes because of intense competition, so realisations did not reflect it; growth was volume-led.
Gross margin slipped 30 bps YoY to 37.4%.
Yarn prices are rising, which management sees as a favourable pricing environment, but competitors are offering extra discounts and extended sale periods to gain share.
Old inventory across the industry is described as now largely exhausted, with fresh stock at higher prices, which management expects will allow the new rate to stick from August.
Management said competition is mainly from organised players and that Rupa is taking share, but via higher discounts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall short of the 9-10% guidance given last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said advertising and marketing spend was about 10.5% of revenue in Q1 and would be rationalised to 6-7%, which should help achieve the desired EBITDA level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the April price hike not show up in realisations, and when will it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intense competition led to extra schemes that passed the hike on to trade. A new rate is expected from August, and it is yet to be implemented.

qa_highlights.question: What is the thermal order book outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sound and healthy order book; management expects thermal to contribute better than last year, but this depends on how the winter season unfolds.

qa_highlights.question: Will further price hikes be taken to offset yarn cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, a further hike is planned, but it depends on how competitors behave.

qa_highlights.question: What were the athleisure and women's trends, and what is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Athleisure fell 5-7% YoY in Q1 and is targeted at double-digit growth from Q2. Women's share is about 8%, and Softline is being rebranded and gets a new team and fabrics.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ROCE/ROE decline structural, and is there room to cut costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the returns are not desirable and blamed the tough competitive environment. It cited the shift from wholesale to secondary-led sales, LFS, e-commerce and other channels. Cost efficiency is an ongoing process with no fixed target.

risks_watch: Competitive intensity from organised players continues to drive extra schemes, so price hikes may not stick (the April hike was largely passed on).
Whether the planned August price hike is implemented and reflected in realisations.
Thermal sales depend on the timing and severity of the winter season.
Women's wear and athleisure both declined or underperformed in Q1; the recovery is not yet proven.
Management guided 9-10% EBITDA margin last quarter but reported 7.8%; the cut in ad spend to 6-7% of revenue needs to show up next quarter.
533552|2026-06.management_tone: Optimistic on volumes, channels and pricing outlook, but cautious and hedged on price realisation, thermal and women's wear. Responses on competition and returns were often open-ended and deferred to coming quarters.
key_quotes: So, from August onward, we are quite hopeful the new rate will be implemented.

533553|2026-03.headline: TD Power Systems FY26 standalone PAT rose 42% to INR2.18bn; FY27 revenue guided at INR24bn-plus, with a Turkey LD penalty dragging Q4 margins.
533553|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone total income rose 35% to INR17.37bn and PAT rose 42% to INR2.18bn; consolidated PAT rose 36% to INR2.36bn. Full-year order inflow was INR22.38bn (+51%), with exports at 79%, and the manufacturing order book stood at INR19.73bn at year-end. Q4 consolidated gross contribution margin fell about 3 points below the 33-34% historical average because of a one-off Turkey contract penalty after components shipped from India were delayed about 1.5 months. Management revised FY27 revenue guidance to INR2,400-plus crore and flagged a large-generator capacity expansion (rotors, machining up to about 200 MW) with details deferred about 2-3 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance revised to INR2,400-plus crore (about INR24bn), with management signalling an extremely high probability of raising it further to match order inflow.

Q1 FY27 execution expected to beat Q4 FY26.

Large-generator capacity complete by calendar 2027; large ramp-up in calendar 2028 (FY29); commitments made to the market from FY29.

Nuclear: NPCIL ordering is slow and choppy, and competition includes BHEL, Crompton and imports.
Management said some customer prices are not yet in effect, creating a lag in price recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross margin contract, and will it revert?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated gross contribution margin averages 33-34% (about 34%); Q4 was about 3 points lower because a Turkey contract was delayed about 1.5 months by components stuck on a shipment from India, and a high LD penalty was paid. Management expects a return to historical levels.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity and currency impact on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Copper price increases are running off hedges and customer price increases are only partly in effect; rupee depreciation is expected to offset this. Management expects broad neutrality for 2-3 quarters but said a further 20-30% commodity rise would need a response.

qa_highlights.question: Large-generator capex, end markets and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed capacity expansion in rotors and large machining; quantum and ramp-up to be disclosed in about 2-3 months. End markets are mainly export: power generation, AI data centres and combined-cycle applications. Full capacity is earliest in calendar 2027, with the big ramp in calendar 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Execution risk from turbine OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the opposite: turbine and engine customers monitor deliveries twice weekly and take machines immediately, so the pressure is on TDPS execution. No machines are waiting in the shop on the gas side.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the outstanding amount of about INR700 crore that was due has been fully covered. Working capital is building for growth, and the company expects conversion to improve as inventory turns into cash next quarter. Management said retained earnings are going into working capital.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue and FY28 capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance is INR2,400-plus crore. Current and planned capacity covers about INR30-32bn through FY28, which management calls conservative. Order book growth of 20-25% is expected in FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed a new CEO, Deepak, joined as number two, and is not only for the large-generator business. He previously was at L&T Mitsubishi and GE. Deepak did not join the call.

533573|2026-03.headline: Alembic Q4 FY26 revenue rose 4% YoY to INR1,838 crore; FY27 guided to low double-digit consolidated top-line growth with Pivya launch drag of 100-150 bps.
533573|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR1,838 crore, up 4% YoY, with core EBITDA margin near 25% (vs 24%) and gross margin at 71%. Reported PAT was INR203 crore, helped by a one-time INR101 crore tax adjustment, after a INR24 crore exceptional item. R&D rose to INR209 crore (11% of revenue) on peptide development and higher filings. For FY26, revenue grew about 10%, EBITDA before R&D was INR1,846 crore (25% of revenue), and reported PAT grew 16% to INR675 crore. Management guided FY27 to low double-digit consolidated growth, with R&D of INR750-800 crore and capex of INR300-350 crore.

Management attributed the margin fall to a higher domestic mix, export deliveries deferred by freight costs rising 3-4x, a near-zero-margin NTPC CO2 energy storage project, and legacy orders priced before commodity inflation. Order booking rose 6.1% to ₹5.68 bn, led by exports and aftermarket, while domestic and product bookings declined.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹2.4 bn, up 27.4% YoY, but domestic order booking fell 35.4% YoY and domestic enquiries declined. Management says the domestic market is broadly weak across industries.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹2.03 bn (48.8% share). Export orders were 68% of Q1 bookings (vs 47%), up 53.4% YoY; exports are 57% of closing order book. Growth is led by Southeast Asia, Africa, Europe and the US.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: 39% of Q1 order booking (vs 27%), growth of 54% in orders; 29% of closing order book. Driven by geothermal and utility contract wins plus refurbishment.

segments.name: Product
segments.commentary: Product order booking fell 11.6% YoY in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of top-line and bottom-line growth for full-year FY27, but growth will be back-ended into H2.
Roughly ₹175 mn of NTPC CO2 project execution remained at end-Q4; management said about 40% falls in Q1 and Q2 with the rest in Q3, while the commissioning is expected around end-Q2 or early Q3.
Management reiterated that a PBT margin above 20% is sustainable in the medium to long term; no specific H2 margin number was given.
US subsidiary is targeted to break even in FY27; product sales from the US are expected to be executed mainly in FY28.
Management expects lumpy quarterly results for a couple more quarters, both positive and negative.
capex_capacity: US facility utilisation in FY27 will be adequate but not high; significant Q1 losses at the US subsidiary were attributed to the absence of an order book.
Execution cycle guidance: under 15 MW about 7-8 months; 15-45 MW about 9-12 months; 30-45 MW about 14-15 months; about 18 months for 100 MW.
Management indicated it is ready to manufacture up to 250 MW class sub-critical packages if NTPC introduces such a policy; participation not yet decided.
Heat pump plus MVR combined solution is in early customer deployment with a demo unit and initial MVR orders in execution; ORC enquiries rising, including in the Americas.
demand_pricing: Export share of Q1 order booking rose to 68%. Management attributed the export execution delays to freight rates rising 3-4x and reduced vessel availability; FOB contracts mean freight is borne by clients.
Domestic enquiries declined. Management said order finalisation is taking longer as customers wait and watch; gestation is 6-12 months.
Bought-out items range 30%-70% of order value depending on the order; all contracts are fixed-price, so commodity inflation during execution is absorbed by Triveni.
US data centre demand is rising as gas turbine lead times extend to 3-5 years; US enquiries have been converted slowly (more than 12 months), with product orders expected first.

Management said the domestic margin decline came from legacy orders booked when commodity prices were volatile and competition was intense, and from lower pricing on the current execution mix. Management expects higher order-booking margins going forward and a rupee benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What was the impact of the NTPC CO2 energy storage order on Q1 margins and quantum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was taken at negligible or near-zero margin to validate technology, so it adds nothing to profit; about 40% of the roughly ₹175 mn balance is expected in Q1 and Q2, with the rest in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic enquiry trend and reason for the slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give quarterly enquiry numbers, cited weakness in India across industries, flat-to-declining conversations, and longer order gestation periods. Green shoots in Europe and strength in the US and Southeast Asia were noted.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin decline comes from bought-out components and cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Lalit Agarwal said bought-out content varies by order from 30% to 70% of the balance of the order value, and contracts are fixed-price, so commodity increases during execution were absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable margin should be expected for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a specific number, but reiterated that a PBT margin above 20% is achievable over the medium to long term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the US aftermarket and product business?
qa_highlights.answer: The US aftermarket contributed less than 10% of the figure implied by analysts because of state-level certification. US product enquiries are closer to commercial discussions, with product sales expected to lead, followed by refurbishment.

qa_highlights.question: How long are execution cycles for different order sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Under 15 MW about 7-8 months; 15-45 MW about 9-12 months; 30-45 MW about 14-15 months; about 18 months for 100 MW.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on H2 execution of legacy orders and on the rupee and new orders with higher margins; Q1 PBT margin was 15.7%.
Domestic order booking fell 35.4% YoY and domestic enquiries are declining; the 6-12 month gestation means the effect may appear in later quarters.
Freight costs and vessel availability could defer more export dispatches into Q2 and Q3.
The US subsidiary is loss-making with break-even targeted in FY27; the US product conversion timeline is more than 12 months.
The CO2 energy storage project (with NTPC) is a technology-validation order that has limited profit potential in the early years; commissioning is expected around end-Q2 or early Q3 FY27.
533655|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on full-year growth and H2 recovery, but cautious and somewhat defensive on Q1 margins. Management gave few numbers on enquiries, margin guidance and US timelines, and attributed the weakness to geopolitics, freight and legacy pricing.

financial_highlights.change: Export share 48.8% vs 49.3% in Q1 FY26

key_quotes: So the softer order mix of H1 FY 2026 has carried through to Q1 FY 2027 profitability.
This of course, was taken at negligible and near zero margins. And so that does not contribute to profitability at all.
But I think that this lumpiness will continue for a couple more quarters, both on the positive and negative side.
So, we will have a double whammy going down.
we believe that a PBT margin of over 20% is something that we can maintain in the medium and long -term.
The exact number is going to be less than 10% of the number that you would have suggested.

533758|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 volume fell ~20% QoQ to 745,000 tons, but EBITDA per ton held near INR5,500 and management reiterates 20% FY27 absolute EBITDA growth.
533758|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 volume of 745,000 tons was below expectations, down roughly 20% QoQ, driven by the UAE disruption (about 25,000 tons lost QoQ), weak SG Premium volumes against secondary steel, an energy crisis hitting rust-proof pipes and roofing (25,000-30,000 tons), and destocking after steel prices rose. Gross profit per ton rose INR1,000 QoQ as management held prices, and EBITDA per ton was flat at above INR5,500. Management says July volumes were up about 20% MoM at over 300,000 tons, and it reiterated 15-20% volume growth and above 20% absolute EBITDA growth for FY27. Working capital days remain below zero and cash was about INR14 billion at June end versus INR15 billion in March 2026.

segments.name: Apollo branded products
segments.commentary: Management targets EBITDA of INR6,000-7,000/ton for Apollo and roofing products combined; the company is at that range currently. Primary and secondary volumes were hit by high prices and channel destocking.

segments.name: SG Premium
segments.commentary: Priced about 6-7% below APL Apollo brand at around INR58,000/ton; EBITDA spread INR0-1,000/ton depending on micro-market. Volumes fell due to the primary-secondary price gap (INR10-12/kg currently).

segments.name: UAE operations
segments.commentary: Dubai volumes fell to 5,000-6,000 tons/month during the disruption; July output was 10,000-12,000 tons, with a target of 16,000-17,000 tons in August and 24,000-25,000 tons in September. About 70,000 tons of inventory is in transit, but raw material for 70,000 tons is not yet lined up. Management expects UAE EBITDA to reach INR5,000-6,000/ton if ramp-up succeeds.

segments.name: Roofing products
segments.commentary: Hit by the energy crisis in India (25,000-30,000 tons lost). Management says roofing EBITDA is currently INR6,000-7,000/ton, with a roofing line starting in APL adding about 20,000 tons of ramped-up volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guidance of 15-20% reiterated; management says 15% is achievable with confidence and 20% needs tailwinds.
FY27 absolute EBITDA growth of 20% or more; FY27 EBITDA per ton expected in the INR5,000-5,500 range.
Quarterly targets: Q2 about 1.0 million tons, Q3 about 1.05 million tons, Q4 about 1.2 million tons. Monthly targets: August 325,000-335,000 tons, September 350,000-360,000 tons.
Q2 expected to be better than Q1 in volume and absolute EBITDA; H2 expected to outperform H1.

Long term: value-added share to rise from about 65% to 75-80% by Q4 FY28; EBITDA per ton target of INR6,000 for the 8 million ton base over the next 2-3 years; ROCE target to return to 30% and then 40%.

Gorakhpur (200,000 tons) expected to start around September 2026; Siliguri (300,000 tons) in Q4 FY27; Malur (about 1 million tons, value-added, EBITDA target INR8,000+/ton) in July-October 2027; a 0.5 million ton plant planned in Maharashtra or North Karnataka. About 2 million tons of new capacity is due over about 2.5 years, plus 1 million tons via debottlenecking.
capex_capacity: Total capex plan of 7 million tons. Gorakhpur 200,000 tons (start around September 2026), Siliguri 300,000 tons (Q4 FY27), Malur about 1 million tons (July-October 2027), a 0.5 million ton plant in Maharashtra or North Karnataka, plus 1 million tons from debottlenecking.
The Bhuj plant was dropped; the Mumbai plant is being shifted fully to exports. A new 500,000-ton plant near the Pune corridor is planned to cut freight to INR200-300/ton from INR1,100-1,200/ton.
Current capacity is about 5 million tons, with full operation targeted in Q4 FY27.
Solar segment: management expects 4-5% of total volume from solar products within 2-3 years, versus a low current contribution.
demand_pricing: Q1 disruption drivers: UAE loss (~25,000 tons QoQ), SG Premium share loss to secondary steel, energy crisis in India, and destocking by channel partners after steel prices rose INR7,000-8,000/ton in Q4 FY26.
July demand recovered as the price correction ended; dealers returned to normal stock positions and July volume was over 300,000 tons (about 20% MoM).
Pricing: management says it held prices, passing on steel price increases plus INR100-200/ton. Price cuts of INR100-200/ton were applied to about 15-20% of the portfolio to gain volume.

Competition: management says it is not losing share, targeting 60-65% share of its market, and sees Tata's planned 4-5 million ton pipe capacity as unclear by segment. Primary steel capacity additions (Lloyd, AM/NS, JSW, Tata, JSPL) are expected to narrow the primary-secondary gap over 1-3 quarters.
PEB segment: about 20% of PEB structure weight is steel pipe; APL holds a 65-70% share with large PEB players.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 volume guidance of 15-20% and EBITDA growth of 20%+ still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15-20% volume growth and 20%+ EBITDA growth; 15% is considered confident, and 20% needs tailwinds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UAE outlook and how will the company participate in reconstruction demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Dubai volume recovered to 10,000-12,000 tons in July, with a target of 24,000-25,000 tons in September. About 70,000 tons of inventory is in transit, but raw material for 70,000 tons is not yet lined up.

qa_highlights.question: How is competitive intensity with Tata and others evolving, and how is market share protected?
qa_highlights.answer: No share loss seen so far; the target is to hold 60-65% share. Tata's pipe plans are not clearly defined by segment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA per ton path beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads expected to be INR5,000-5,500/ton in FY27, improving INR100-200/ton a year, with a target of INR6,000/ton at 8 million tons in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per ton rise YoY despite lower volume?
qa_highlights.answer: The January 2025 repositioning of APL Apollo brand raised prices by about INR500/ton, which lifted spreads from Q4 FY25 through FY26 and into Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What were the segment-level EBITDA targets, and why were segment margins no longer disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: Apollo and roofing are targeted at INR6,000-7,000/ton, SG Premium at about INR500/ton, and UAE at INR5,000-6,000/ton if ramp-up succeeds. Management stopped segment margin disclosure to avoid competitor scrutiny.

risks_watch: Volume ramp-up: H2 needs about 3.5-4 lakh tons per month, and any shortfall would make the 15% volume target difficult.
Primary-secondary steel gap: if it persists for 1-3 more quarters, SG Premium and secondary-linked volume stays under pressure.
UAE: raw material shortage for about 70,000 tons, high demurrage costs, and pricing hits in the post-disruption recovery.
Gorakhpur (September) and Siliguri (Q4 FY27) timing; Malur (July-October 2027) execution risk on the 7 million ton capex plan.
Possible pricing pressure from the 15-20% of the portfolio where prices were cut; the EBITDA per ton could drop INR100-200 in some quarters.
Employee cost step-up in Q1 that management says will reverse once volumes recover.
Management declined to give FY28 guidance and disclosed no segment EBITDA going forward, reducing visibility.
533758|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the full-year guidance and the recovery in July, but cautious on quarterly volume, which management says is hard to forecast. Answers on UAE, segment margins, and FY28 were less specific, and management said it would not give FY28 guidance.
key_quotes: So, we chose to focus on profitability and as a result, you would see that our gross profit per ton increased by INR1,000 on quarter-on-quarter basis.
So, we do expect that our EBITDA spreads will remain in range of INR5,000 to INR5,500 per ton throughout the year.
Now the run rate was around 250,000 tons per month for the quarter one.
Our target is to maintain our 60% to 65% market share.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR15 billion in March 2026; similar level
attributed to low per-ton production and annual increment

533758|2026-09.headline: APL Apollo Q2 FY27 volume hit 960,000 tons with EBITDA near Rs 6,000/ton; management guides FY27 EBITDA up 20%, with the 15% volume target conditional on Dubai and steel supply.
533758|2026-09.overview: Management called Q2 FY27 its best quarter on volume, EBITDA and net profit, with volume of 960,000 tons despite UAE operations being disrupted, steel shortages in the domestic market and container disruption affecting exports. Growth came from the APL Apollo brand and roofing sheets, where pricing and EBITDA spreads improved, while low-margin SG Premium and export volumes were deliberately not pursued. Management guided FY27 EBITDA growth of about 20% on an absolute basis and said Q2 EBITDA per ton of about Rs 6,000 is sustainable. Working capital days were stated as zero, and cash rose 15% QoQ to Rs 16 billion. Several answers on Dubai, SG Premium and volume guidance were non-committal.

segments.name: APL Apollo brand
segments.commentary: Management says brand products get better pricing and EBITDA spreads; APL Apollo and roofing volume grew about 20% YoY in H1, with double-digit growth expected in H2. Analysts were told the brand targets 15-20% YoY growth.

segments.name: Roofing sheets
segments.commentary: Capacity cited at 7 lakh tons per year (about 175,000 tons per quarter); Q1 volume was about 135,000 tons and the target for the current quarter is 175,000 tons. Mix is 50% housing, 25% commercial/industrial and 25% other industrial; thickness 0.4-3.5 mm; no commission paid to third parties.

segments.name: SG Premium
segments.commentary: Low-margin product; management declined to give volume guidance due to steel shortage and low margin. Management said it can sell about 200,000 tons if steel prices fall and that absolute EBITDA would rise as volume increases.

segments.name: UAE (Dubai) operations
segments.commentary: Volume at about 40% of past levels; current run rate about 100,000 tons per year against about 300,000 tons capacity. Brownfield expansion to about 500,000 tons by March 2027, with EBITDA of Rs 8,000-10,000/ton expected on new mills. Management says no losses there.

segments.name: Defence, aerospace and specialised tubes
segments.commentary: New specialised tube mill can produce up to 250x250 mm with 16 mm thickness; samples sent to agencies, with results expected in 2-3 months. Development items for ISRO and DRDO are in progress.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA growth of about 20% on an absolute basis by March 2027; management says it may beat this if UAE operations recover in H2. Management said absolute EBITDA should cross Rs 2,200 crore this year (one analyst cited Rs 2,200-2,300 crore; Shaleen Kumar's Rs 2,400 crore reference was given by management as possible if Dubai performed).

Apollo brand and roofing volume growth of about 15% for FY27 (about double-digit in H2); management also cited 15-20% YoY growth for these two segments. Company-wide volume guidance not committed due to Dubai and SG Premium uncertainty.
Q3 FY27 EBITDA per ton expected to be above Rs 6,000; October described as good and above guidance.

Management said FY28 EBITDA could reach about Rs 2,500 crore; in response to an analyst's Rs 3,000 crore scenario, management agreed it is achievable if Dubai, domestic steel supply and container freight stabilise. Management said that if it targets Rs 6,000-6,500/ton, it will update guidance after another quarter of evidence.
Capex target of 7 million tons greenfield plus brownfield capacity and 1 million tons de-bottlenecking within two years. Capex outflow in H2 expected to be about Rs 200 crore.
Net cash of about Rs 1,600 crore expected to rise to about Rs 2,300 crore; Rs 200-300 crore of this is earmarked for capex, and management will decide the use of the remainder later.
capex_capacity: Target of 7 million tons greenfield plus brownfield capacity and 1 million tons de-bottlenecking within the next two years (per management).
Current run-rate of 960,000 tons per quarter; utilisation about 70-75%.
Dubai capacity about 300,000 tons, rising to about 500,000 tons by March 2027 with two new mills; run-rate about 100,000 tons per year.
H1 FY27 capex Rs 400 crore; H2 capex expected to be low (about Rs 200 crore).
Greenfield additions described as small, limiting fixed-cost impact; brownfield expansion said not to hurt existing fixed costs materially.
demand_pricing: Management said demand for APL Apollo and roofing remains strong, with no decline seen, and that order books are full despite higher steel prices causing customers to delay quotations.
Pricing: black pipe price cited at about Rs 70,000/ton vs competitors at Rs 68,000-70,000; HR coil about Rs 60,000/ton; conversion cost about Rs 10/kg; worst item margin about Rs 6,000/ton.
Discounts: July required higher discounts; August and September needed less. A demand-driven discount swing can move results by Rs 10-15 crore per quarter.
Management said steel plant shutdowns are causing shortages, with November also weak and volumes expected to recover to about 400,000 tons per month from December.

Management said Q2 margin expansion came from three sources: exiting non-profitable volumes, roofing capacity additions and cost/innovation. It declined to give product-level EBITDA; the disclosure has been discontinued.
Exports affected by very high container freight; UAE exports blocked.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised FY27 volume guidance given H1 growth of about 4% vs an earlier 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 15% guidance holds for the Apollo brand and roofing, but company-wide volume guidance is not committed because of Dubai and steel shortage; low-margin volumes are being deliberately dropped.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall QoQ, and why did the FD balance drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the other-income decline to FX gains and losses; the FD drop of about Rs 225 crore is due to reclassification of over-one-year FDs to within one year, and management said it would check the FX figure.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is Rs 6,000/ton EBITDA, and what if steel prices normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 6,000/ton is sustainable, citing the exit from non-profitable business, roofing additions, cost savings and utilisation of 70-75%. Management said SG Premium growth would dilute per-ton margin but lift absolute EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the drop in GP per ton when mix has improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said light structures carry lower realisation and GP; GP per ton fell about Rs 500/ton QoQ, and light-structure mix was about 25% in Q2 per management (analyst noted 35%).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the large volume jump from Q1 to Q2 beyond roofing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the APL Apollo brand, where the company shifted focus from SG Premium to Apollo branding and got better pricing, with Q3 seen as strong so far.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 EBITDA outlook, including Dubai recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 2,400 crore is achievable this year if Dubai performs, and agreed Rs 3,000 crore for FY28 is possible if Dubai, domestic steel supply and container freight stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Will falling rainfall affect housing demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said housing demand remains intact; any impact would be 2-4% at most, and order books and enquiries are strong.

risks_watch: Dubai/UAE operations remain largely shut: run-rate about 100,000 tons vs about 500,000 tons capacity after expansion, and management cannot commit on timing.
Steel shortage and plant shutdowns; November expected to be weak, with recovery from December.
Sustainability of Rs 6,000/ton EBITDA if HRC falls to Rs 55,000-60,000; management said it wants to see another quarter before raising FY28 guidance.
Adding about 2 million tons of capacity over the next one to one-and-a-half years with unclear fixed-cost impact.
Opacity: product-level EBITDA disclosure discontinued; SG Premium and heavy/super-heavy mix not quantified; a figure in slide 18 (H1 EBITDA per ton of about Rs 11,000) was acknowledged as a typo.
Freight and container disruption affecting exports; power cost at Rs 6.2-6.3/unit vs Rs 5 target.

It was evasive on company-wide volume guidance, Dubai timing, SG Premium volumes and product-level EBITDA, repeatedly saying it could not commit or that the matter was outside its control.

533761|2026-03.headline: GPT Infra FY26 consolidated revenue rose 8.6% to INR1,290 crores, below guidance, while consolidated EBITDA grew 28.5% to INR174.2 crores; FY27 revenue growth guided at 27-30%.
533761|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 1.3% YoY to INR373.9 crores, while consolidated revenue grew 8.9% to INR414.7 crores; management attributed the March shortfall to West Bengal elections and labour migration. Margins improved, with standalone Q4 EBITDA up 27% to INR53 crores at 14% margin and consolidated Q4 EBITDA up 53% to INR59.2 crores, helped by the Ghana factory. The Alcon signalling EPC acquisition (INR151.83 crores cash) closed in the quarter and is being merged into GPT Infra with an appointed date of April 1, 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 27-30%, order inflow of about INR3,000 crores and consolidated EBITDA margin of around 14%.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Contributed more than 90% of FY26 revenue; key executing projects include Prayagraj Ganga Bridge, Kona Expressway and Raniganj. Alcon signalling will be reported within the infra line item.

segments.name: Concrete sleepers
segments.commentary: Management said the segment was profitable in FY26 on domestic demand and African operations. Q4 was loss-making in South Africa, Namibia and Ghana, which management attributed mainly to currency mark-to-market effects; Ghana production has started.

segments.name: Signalling (Alcon, acquired)
segments.commentary: Margin of about 20% vs 13-14% for traditional infra; FY27 revenue expected at INR120-130 crores. Order book is about INR90-100 crores; FY27 order inflow expected at INR150-200 crores against about INR500 crores of bids.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 27-30%, subject to Middle East war-related economic headwinds; long-term revenue growth target above 20%.
FY27 order inflow guidance of about INR3,000 crores across infra, signalling and sleepers.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at about 14% for FY27, with long-term standalone and consolidated margin above 13%.
West Bengal catch-up expected: April subdued again due to elections, Q1 not fully caught up, but first half expected to recover the shortfall.
Average capex of about INR70-75 crores a year for the next couple of years including the HAM equity share of INR55-60 crores; equipment purchases of INR40-50 crores a year.
Alcon and GPT merger (appointed date April 1, 2026) expected to complete in FY27, subject to regulatory approvals.
capex_capacity: Acquired Alcon Builders and Engineers (New Delhi EPC signalling) for INR151.83 crores cash; wholly owned subsidiary from January 1, 2026.
First HAM contract (elevated bypass, Jodhpur, NHAI), contract value about INR669 crores; GPT holds 51% in the SPV, which is already incorporated.
Steel girder fabrication factory at Singur, West Bengal, started during the year with about 10,000 tonnes per annum capacity; further expansion under review.
Ghana facility commercially operational, with first supply and invoice raised in March 2026.
demand_pricing: Order inflow of INR2,422 crores in FY26, and about INR500 crores of Alcon signalling bids in the last two months; Alcon contracts of INR70-80 crores individually.

Major wins: Northern Railway rail-cum-road bridge over Ganga at Varanasi, INR1,201 crores total (GPT share 40%, about INR481 crores); MCGM LBS Marg flyover, INR1,805 crores total (JV share 26%, about INR470 crores).
Price escalation formulas in all contracts, linked to SAIL/RINL steel, WPI for cement and fuel; NHAI and MoRTH moved to monthly escalation payments and allowed a 4-month force majeure extension.
Management said about 40% of revenue comes from West Bengal, and migrant labour returning from there was disrupted in March and April.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract assets rise from INR336 crores to about INR514 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR60-65 crores is from Alcon (retention, unbilled revenue, escalation), with the rest from EPC milestone-based billing; contract assets are typically 6-8 months old and are targeted to fall to 3-4 months of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Where did the QIP proceeds go, given limited debt reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt was cut by about INR125-130 crores from March 2024 to March 2025; FY26 debt rose on EPC working-capital drawdowns and internal accruals used for the Alcon purchase, with debt expected to return to the earlier level.

qa_highlights.question: Did West Bengal elections cause the revenue guidance miss, and does Alcon's INR140 crores contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed March execution was hit by elections and labour migration; the Alcon contribution in FY26 was only Q4 numbers of about INR30 crores, since it was consolidated from January 1.

qa_highlights.question: Is labour back and is there execution risk to FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: April was again subdued by elections, but May execution is strong and labour is back on site; new contracts won in December and January are expected to contribute heavily in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material inflation from the war affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts carry escalation formulas; NHAI now pays escalation monthly, so a lag is possible, but management expects full-year margins to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and is Alcon consolidated separately?
qa_highlights.answer: Average capex about INR70-75 crores a year including the HAM share; Alcon is consolidated and, after the merger, will report within the infra segment rather than as a separate line.

533941|2026-03.overview: Thomas Scott reported Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 78 crore (+63% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 11 crore (14.14% margin) and PAT of Rs 6 crore (7.71% margin), its 10th consecutive quarter of revenue growth. For FY26, revenue was Rs 255 crore (+58%), EBITDA Rs 33 crore (13.1% margin, +105 bps) and PAT Rs 19 crore (+51%). Management said some own-brand sales shifted to outright wholesale sales to marketplace distributors at 30-40% below retail, lowering reported revenue per unit while EBITDA margin was said to be neutral. Working capital, short-term borrowings and receivables drew the most scrutiny, with management attributing much of the stretch to a fire-related inventory loss and March-clustered sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did own-brand revenue fall QoQ in Q4 and how will the revenue mix look?

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be funded and what is the sustainable debt level?

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still on track for prior revenue run-rate and margins in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets unchanged: same growth rate as the last few years and healthy margins, with margin improvement sought while reserving margin for growth investment.

Margin guidance: EBITDA at least 6.5-7% and PAT 6-6.5%.

Awards guided at INR 20,000-25,000 crore this year (including Supertech about INR 10,000 crore, J&K about INR 3,500 crore, Rajasthan Mandapam about INR 3,500 crore), against an earlier INR 30,000-32,000 crore target.
GPRA 5 colonies (Lodhi Colony, Andrews Ganj, DIZ, Lakshmi Bai Nagar) order of about INR 30,000 crore expected; management says cabinet approval is pending.
Redevelopment fund generation of INR 30,000-35,000 crore expected this year, sale-linked and construction-linked, with cash collected over about two years.
capex_capacity: Phase 2 Amrapali is awarded and in execution, with one tower at the 20th floor using Mivan shuttering and others at the 13th floor; Phase 1 has 23 of 24 projects completed.

Dubai: 66 housing units under construction on a purchased land parcel; developer licence in hand; construction tender expected in October.
Goa redevelopment: four packages ordered, site mobilised and work started; two more packages pending tender.
demand_pricing: Africa Avenue auction for 262 residential units drew about 2,900 participants; auction postponed on a technical issue and expected in August. Vinayak Mandir auction targeted for September and Palanji area for September-October. Management expects INR 5,000-6,000 crore from Africa Avenue sales.
Amrapali: about 8,800 units in total, with roughly 4,000-4,500 sold; management expects to sell about INR 4,000-5,000 crore of inventory.

Pipeline: Supertech tender to be floated this quarter (16 projects in Noida and Greater Noida, about INR 10,000 crore); J&K infrastructure tender of about INR 3,500-4,000 crore to be floated this month after an initial INR 100 crore package drew about 15 bidders; MAHAPREIT (about INR 25,000 crore) expected in Q3; Naveen Nagpur infrastructure tender after DPR approval.

International: Seychelles has awarded a further 1,000 houses after about 2,000 in Maldives; management cites prospects in Australia, Saudi Arabia and Fiji, none included in projections.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins move over the next two to three quarters, and by how much?

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA rise sharply while work and consultancy expenses fell from INR 3,412 crore in Q4 FY26 to INR 1,536 crore in Q1 FY27 (standalone)?

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone and PMC revenue growth look slow, and what are the FY27-FY29 targets?

qa_highlights.question: What is the CPSE REIT plan, timeline and investment needed?

qa_highlights.question: Why have big awards (J&K, MAHAPREIT, Supertech) slipped, and is funding the constraint?

Management cut 2026 award guidance to INR 20,000-25,000 crore from INR 30,000-32,000 crore.
FY27 revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore against standalone Q1 revenue of INR 1,823 crore; analysts questioned the run rate and Q3 Delhi GRAP construction curbs.
Earnings quality: Q1 EBITDA gain driven partly by one-off marketing fees from Bharat Business Park; FY27 PAT guidance of INR 1,100-1,200 crore needs roughly 2x the Q1 run rate of INR 151 crore.

534392|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% to INR486 crore and EBITDA reached INR68 crore (INR10,760/ton), with PAT at INR41 crore.
534392|2026-06.overview: Sales volume was 59,000 tons, up 6.5% YoY, with revenue up 12% on higher volumes and OEM price revisions tied to input cost increases. EBITDA was INR68 crore (INR10,760/ton, management says excluding treasury income from Aichi surplus funds, the figure is near INR10,700/ton), and PAT was INR41 crore versus INR34 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR20 crore a year ago. Management said demand exceeds what it can supply, the 3 lakh ton licensed capacity is the binding constraint, and it has applied for an increase to 3.6 lakh tons. Forging project with Aichi Steel is tracking on schedule with capex now below the INR475 crore estimate, and the greenfield 5 lakh ton plant scope and cost are being revised upward.

financial_highlights.value: INR10,760/ton (INR10,700 excluding treasury income from Aichi surplus funds)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR34 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR20 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Automotive steel (core)
segments.commentary: Volumes were good and prices were revised upward on cost pass-through; Q1 settlement is complete with some OEMs and pending with others, where the price is expected to rise further. Maruti is about 10% of business.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Direct exports are about 6-7% of sales and indirect exports via the Aichi trading arm about 5%; management guides total exports to 7-8% (max about 10%), with Aichi roughly 40-50% of exports.

segments.commentary: Ingot casting is due in Q3 FY27 and to stabilise in Q4; die steel production is expected to be regular in FY28. Die steel imports into India are about INR1,000 crore a year, and die steel sells at about INR2.5 lakh/ton (non-ESR) versus average realisation of about INR85,000/ton.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target about 255,000 tons; FY28 target above 270,000 tons, rising to about 290,000 tons if the environmental approval for 3.6 lakh tons comes through, and 330,000-340,000 tons in FY28-29 with new capex.
EBITDA/ton range is INR8,000-11,000 currently; management intends to move to INR8,000-12,000 for next year and to INR9,000-12,000 after the new solar plant and value-added products ramp up (FY28-29).
Q2 FY27 realisations are expected to be higher than Q1 after a 1 July price increase request; Q3 is expected broadly flat to slightly up or down depending on raw material prices.
Rolling mill has reached 3 lakh tons input capacity and is expected to reach 330,000 tons of input, about 10% higher, within the current licence constraint.
Forging project with Aichi Steel: commissioning by Q4 FY28, with 6-12 months to fill; revenue from around end FY29 to FY30; capex below INR475 crore estimate (more than 10% saving).

New greenfield steel plant (about 5 lakh tons, to be enlarged): commissioning on track for FY29-30; land and machinery to be finalised by mid-September 2026; cost likely a little higher than earlier per ton due to metals inflation and rupee depreciation.
capex_capacity: Existing licensed capacity is 3 lakh tons; application for 3.6 lakh tons (360,000 tons melting) is pending with the Environment Ministry, with approval expected in about 3-4 months but not assured.
New reheating furnace has stabilised; new NDT (testing) line and new peeling line to be commissioned September-October 2026 to remove bottlenecks and reduce job work.
Solar: about 50% capacity addition planned in roughly 1-1.5 years; savings will be lower than phase one because local cell manufacturing rules raise panel cost.

Greenfield plant being reconfigured (scrap preheating, extra continuous testing and automatic testing lines), so capacity and cost will rise; a refined project is due at the next Board meeting, with details in next quarter.
Funding: internal cash is in hand; a capital raise is planned in FY28 with commitments from Vardhman Group and Aichi; Punjab government support is assured.
demand_pricing: Demand is strong and the company is turning away orders; there are no long-term orders, all business is repeat, and customer volumes drive supply.
Next volume lift comes from commercial production for import substitution for Maruti, expected from Q4 FY27.
Tie-ups with Aichi and Toyota Kirloskar (TKM) support approvals; TKM's new Aurangabad plant needs green steel, where the company claims to be the only Indian player with the approvals.
Price revisions follow raw material cost changes; OEMs can reverse or move prices, and the company operates within a band.
Non-auto product mix is a planned margin lever; die steel is high-price, low-volume and carries higher heat-treatment cost.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue is from exports, and how is business concentrated by customer?
qa_highlights.answer: Direct exports are about 6-7% and indirect exports via Aichi's trading arm about 5%; Maruti is about 10% of sales, and management says there is no concentration risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the 3 lakh to 3.6 lakh ton expansion and the 5 lakh ton greenfield plant?
qa_highlights.answer: The EC application is filed and approval is expected in 3-4 months; the greenfield land and machinery are to be finalised by August end to mid-September, and the plant will be larger than 5 lakh tons with cost likely a little higher.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the EBITDA/ton range rising from INR8,000-11,000 to INR8,000-12,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites higher volumes spreading fixed costs, lower operating costs, reduced job work from Q3 FY27, and the new solar plant; the range floor is to move to 9,000 after the solar addition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume target and what drives growth beyond the licence limit?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is about 255,000 tons, FY28 above 270,000 tons; growth beyond that needs the EC approval and new capex, and non-auto products (ingot casting, die steel, railway axles, windmill shafts) are the next growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aichi forging project cost and timeline on track?
qa_highlights.answer: The project is on schedule for commissioning by Q4 FY28, cost is more than 10% below the INR475 crore estimate, and revenue begins around end FY29 with a 6-12 month fill-up period.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a partner for the advanced metals / aerospace JV?
qa_highlights.answer: No partner is selected; management is talking to several parties, the JV will be a separate company that is not Aichi, and it is expected to take a couple of years, so the numbers are outside the forecast horizon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book and realisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has no formal order book and says it is fully booked; Q2 realisations are expected to be higher than Q1 after a 1 July price increase, while Q3 is expected broadly flat.

risks_watch: Licence cap at 3 lakh tons constrains volume; the 3.6 lakh ton EC approval is pending and not assured.
Pending OEM price settlements for Q1 and Q2 realisations depend on OEM acceptance and raw material costs.
Greenfield project cost is rising (metals inflation, rupee depreciation, added testing lines), and the refined project and cost are due in the next Board meeting and next quarter.
Solar savings in the next phase will be lower because of local cell rules, which affects the planned EBITDA/ton uplift.
The reported EBITDA of INR68 crore includes treasury income from surplus Aichi funds; management excluded it to get INR10,700/ton, so the operating figure should be tracked separately.
Direct export share was over-estimated earlier; the company will start estimating indirect component exports from next quarter.
534392|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and the Aichi forging project, with clear timelines and cost savings; more cautious and hedged on the EC approval, greenfield plant cost, and pricing, which management repeatedly says will happen "when it happens".
key_quotes: We closed a good quarter.
Demand scenario is good. We are, in fact, finding it difficult to meet the requirements of the customers.
But -- and cost per ton is going to be lower than what we had estimated in the new plant.
So, the new plant is 5 lakh tons, not 5 million.

534425|2026-03.headline: Speciality Restaurants Q4 FY26 revenue up 13.65% YoY and PAT up 44.20%, with SSG of 2.25% for the quarter and 11.57% in April.
534425|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue growth of 13.65% YoY and PAT growth of 44.20%, helped by 2.25% same-store sales growth and gross margin expansion from 69.1% to 70.4%. Full-year SSG was 1.49%, and April SSG reached 11.57%, which management attributed to higher dine-in covers and refurbishments of older restaurants. Management guided to about 15% top-line growth in FY27 and about 15-16% EBITDA growth on revenue, with 32 new outlets planned. On the cost side, the company took a 4% price increase and moved 78% of its kitchens off LPG/PNG to induction, targeting 100% within 20 days.

financial_highlights.metric: Profit after tax growth (Q4 FY26, YoY)

segments.name: Mainland China / Asia Kitchen / Gong (Asian brands)
segments.commentary: Mainland China AOV is INR 1,200-1,300 per cover; Asia Kitchen INR 1,000-1,100; Gong INR 2,500-3,000, with a Bandra launch and Pune and Delhi (Vasant Kunj) openings planned. Management sees Asia Kitchen and Mainland China reaching about 50 restaurants within 5 years.

segments.name: Haka (digital QSR, delivery-first)
segments.commentary: Haka operates from hybrid sites, with about 40-50% of new Mainland China stores co-locating a Haka and Oh! Calcutta cloud kitchen. Management expects Haka to reach a 'decent number' within two quarters; no figure was given.

segments.name: Walters and Sweet Bengal
segments.commentary: Walters AOV is about INR 700 and Sweet Bengal about INR 400 per cover. Plans include 15 new Walters (to 20 total) and 10 new Sweet Bengal outlets in FY27, with Sweet Bengal rebranding and FMCG packaging planned.

segments.name: Siciliana (Italian)
segments.commentary: Newer chain; management cited an average spend of about INR 1,200-1,300 per cover, equal to Mainland China, per the answer on Siciliana's pricing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of about 15%, implying revenue near INR 600 crores; management said 'maybe more' and suggested about INR 700 crores by FY28 at a slower pace.
EBITDA to grow about 15-16% for each percentage of revenue growth, as front-end costs of new restaurants weigh over the next 2 years.
Restaurant-level EBITDA of about 15% post-rent (22% pre-rent) for a 2,500-3,000 sq ft store generating INR 8-9 crores revenue; breakeven in 4-6 months.
FY27 capex of INR 40 crores for renovations and new stores; 8 new restaurants (INR 32 crores) and QSR/confectionery (about INR 5 crores) for a total of INR 37 crores.
Planned 32 new outlets in FY26-27 (8 restaurants, 15 Walters, 10 Sweet Bengal), taking touch points from 121 at 31 March to about 150 by year-end.
Management expects double-digit SSG going forward after renovations of older restaurants.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex of INR 40 crores for renovations and new store openings; INR 37 crores is earmarked for 8 new restaurants and QSR/confectionery.
Restaurant capex of INR 12,000-13,000 per sq ft for Mainland China and Asia Kitchen; lower for small Walters and Sweet Bengal stores.
Renovations started at Andheri West, then Pune and Bangalore; about 4 restaurants refreshed by April.
Walters commissary set up in Maharashtra, geared for 20-25 stores.
Induction conversion: about INR 1.12 crores spent on induction woks since 4 March; 78% of the restaurant chain off LPG/PNG, with 100% targeted within 20 days.
Average occupancy is about 2 times installed cover capacity on an average basis, according to management.
demand_pricing: April 2026 SSG of 11.57%; management said there was no sign of consumer slowdown as of late May, citing a planned redemption-coupon scheme (for example INR 200 or INR 150 off a INR 1,000 meal) launching at the end of May.
Price increase of 4% taken in FY26, with management stating it would not take more than 4% and is not seeking extra margin from price.
Management said there is no significant reduction in spend historically during high inflation or domestic shocks other than COVID, and none currently.
Franchisees: 11 earlier, 7 remaining, each paying 6% of revenue as royalty with no capex by the company; management said Indian partners need 'skin in the game'.
Competition: management sees Panda Express as a fast QSR format different from Mainland China, so no threat to the business.

qa_highlights.question: What were same-store sales growth for Q4 and FY26, and why is the company lagging peers like Barbeque Nation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 SSG was 2.25% and full-year FY26 was 1.49%. Management said April SSG was 11.57%, driven by more dine-in covers, and blamed slow growth on unrenovated restaurants, with refurbishments now under way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the restaurant-level economics for top brands?
qa_highlights.answer: For a 2,500-3,000 sq ft store, revenue is INR 8-9 crores a year with 22% restaurant EBITDA before rent. Rent is about 20-21% of revenue (revenue-share triggers at 17-18%), leaving about 15% post-rent EBITDA. Breakeven takes 4-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company managing LPG and fuel supply, and what does induction cost?
qa_highlights.answer: The company started the transition on 4 March and imported wok-based induction sets (around 300). It has 78% of the chain off fuel, targeting 100% in 20 days. Management said induction cost is the same or lower, with a 6% saving in a pilot restaurant from avoiding pilot-flame wastage.

qa_highlights.question: Why not focus on fewer brands, given that the bottom 8 brands contribute under 10% each?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed seven focus brands (Mainland China, Asia Kitchen, Haka, Gong, Siciliana, Walters, Sweet Bengal). Other brands are profitable and will not be shut, but no further expansion is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is a buyback under consideration, given the cash pile and the share price correction?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the question would be taken up by the Board and it was too early to say.

qa_highlights.question: How can FY26 cash flow (about INR 80 crores CFO less about INR 50 crores rent) reconcile with a 15% EBITDA margin claim?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the 15-16% figure is at restaurant level after rent. Cash-flow EBITDA is after corporate costs, which fell to about 4% of revenue from 6-7% as the company resumed expansion.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (fuel, energy, freight) with only a 4% price increase taken so far; management said it is not seeking extra margin from pricing.
Consumer wallet pressure on discretionary dining if inflation or geopolitical uncertainty deepens; management reports no current impact.
Same-store sales growth of 1.49% in FY26 is weak; the 11.57% April figure needs to be sustained through FY27.
Execution risk on 32 new outlets, Gong expansion in Pune and Delhi, and Haka scaling.
Corporate cost and new-store front-end costs may slow EBITDA growth to about 15-16% against revenue growth of about 15%.
Management's FY27 revenue of about INR 600 crores and FY28 of about INR 700 crores are forward-looking and dependent on macro conditions.
Gross margin and EBITDA reconciliation: an analyst said cash-flow-implied EBITDA margin was about 7-8%, against management's 15-16% restaurant-level figure; this gap was not fully resolved.

The leader holds the price line. So we continue to believe in that right from the beginning, and we've not taken more than 4% at this point.

qa_highlights.question: How was margin expanded despite cost pressure, including gas shortages?

qa_highlights.question: Is the delivery mix growth deliberate, and does it hurt margins?

qa_highlights.question: How many stores are planned, and what are the constraints?

qa_highlights.question: How will the two Inox Green acquisitions contribute to EBITDA and when will they be consolidated?

qa_highlights.question: What was the FY26 working capital position against the INR5,000 crore guideline?

qa_highlights.question: What was actual MW execution in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give megawatt execution, saying the company guides on revenue only, and reiterated this stated policy.

qa_highlights.question: Will equipment supply shift raise margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins stay at about 20% or higher, with equipment supply carrying less risk and more upfront cash; O&M at about 50% margin would add a higher-margin bias.

qa_highlights.question: Other income of INR61 crore at Inox Green: how much is recurring and how much is treasury?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR40 crore relates to the two acquisitions (debt-linked, net of deferred tax, roughly INR25-26 crore at PAT level), INR10 crore is value-added services and INR10 crore is treasury income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Inox Green revenue fall QoQ from about INR78 crore to INR69 crore?

Credibility: FY26 revenue of INR4,500 crore was below the INR5,000 crore target and Q4 revenue was flat YoY; management declined to disclose MW execution.

539118|2026-03.headline: VRL Logistics Q4 FY26 total income rose 6% YoY to INR859 crore, with tonnage back to 3% YoY growth and EBITDA margin at 21.4%.
539118|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR859 crore, up about 6% YoY and 3% QoQ, helped by better realisation, new clients and return of previously lost accounts. Realisation per ton was about INR8,147, up roughly 3% YoY, and daily tonnage crossed 11,500 tons. EBITDA margin was about 21.4%, down about 190 bps YoY from an exceptional Q4 FY25 (23%+) but up about 48 bps QoQ. FY26 total income was about INR3,245 crore, profit INR237 crore (up about 29%), and EBITDA margin 20.8%. Management guided to FY27 tonnage growth of 6-7% and kept an EBITDA margin of around 20%+ despite fuel cost pressure, which it plans to pass on via selective rate hikes and fuel surcharges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume growth outlook and what efforts drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least 6-7% full-year tonnage growth and about 2% sequential growth per quarter, driven by completed rate rationalisation, marketing, new branches and new customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will fuel-driven price hikes hurt volumes, and how is fuel cost passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume pressure is from weak petrochemical-linked demand, not fuel prices. Hikes were applied on selected routes, with fuel surcharges in contracts; April 2026 YoY volume grew about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of lower bulk fuel purchase?
qa_highlights.answer: Some basis points of margin impact; management said it is flexible to hold EBITDA around 20% and the bulk purchase facility has already been lost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lorry hire charges rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Fleet fell from about 6,100 to 5,900 vehicles while tonnage grew, so outside hired vehicles were used to carry the extra volume, plus higher lorry hire rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new branch contribution and depreciation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: New branches contributed about 1-1.5% of Q4 growth; FY27 branches expected to add 2-3%. Depreciation is not expected to rise much, as land is a large share of new investment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the business mix and competitive positioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix is about 80% spot (TO PAY/PAID), 15-16% account, 6-7% FTL; door-to-door about 38-40%. Rates are at a premium to unorganised players and comparable to organised players.

Reliance on hired vehicles (lorry hire cost rose) while owned fleet shrinks.

qa_highlights.question: Why have trade receivables risen so fast (₹162 cr vs ₹115 cr), and is DSO a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the rise to higher ad revenue and a large Dhurandhar booking at March end. DSO was 147 days vs 121 in FY25 and about 134 in FY19; provisioning is adequate. Management agreed to show DSO for periods above 120 days in future.

qa_highlights.question: Is UFO losing pricing power as ad-sharing with theatres rose to about 59.5% from 33%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied losing pricing power. It cited multiplex mix, rental-linked minimum guarantees and aggregated inventory where UFO did not invest. It expects the ratio to decline as revenues scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue per screen fall in CDC and VPF in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said February was almost blank and blockbusters like Dhurandhar and Border drew wide releases, so other films avoided the window. Full-year CDC and VPF revenue still rose, and management says the business has stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of software, footfall monitoring and off-screen or activation initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: Footfall and ProCAT are used to market the network to advertisers. Activation and off-screen advertising work has started but is at an early, phased stage.

qa_highlights.question: What was free cash flow, and why does debt rise while cash improves?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO did not give an FCF figure. Net cash rose from ₹48.3 cr to ₹59 cr despite about ₹15 cr tied in working capital including TDS. Debt is raised for theatre equipment via LC-to-loan conversions, and the company keeps both cash and debt by policy.

risks_watch: Receivables and DSO (147 days) could stay elevated if Dhurandhar-type year-end releases recur; watch for the new >120-day DSO disclosure.
Q4 EBITDA fell 13% QoQ and net profit fell 30% QoQ, so momentum is uneven quarter to quarter.
Ad-sharing ratio near 59.5% compresses margins; the company expects it to moderate as minimum guarantees are exceeded.
Employee costs rose to ₹94.7 cr; management says cost optimisation is ongoing.
Dependence on blockbuster timing: February was nearly blank and CDC/VPF per-screen revenue fell in Q4.
Q1 FY27 started mixed; success depends on the named Peddi, Welcome to the Jungle and Cocktail 2 releases.

Management credited a 33% YoY jump in advertisement revenue to the spillover from "Dhurandhar" and to annual advertisers onboarded around it. Product sales declined YoY, driven by roughly ₹7 crore lower international sales because Dubai imports were delayed by the regional war; management says these orders remain in hand.
